endorsements.quote: For the proposed AI, compare the same task and workload against the rule baseline, document the relevant system boundary and assumptions, measure energy or carbon where feasible, and avoid generic per-query estimates as product evidence.

evidence.title: Technology-mediated screening interviews for youth mental health: content validation, randomized controlled trial, and expert evaluation
evidence.outcome: Patient satisfaction and expert ratings of chatbot and robot interviews versus psychiatrist-led interviews
evidence.effect: Psychiatrist-led interviews had higher satisfaction, especially communication quality; willingness to repeat did not differ; expert ratings comparable across modalities except alignment with other assessment methods favoring psychiatrists over robot.
evidence.quote: Psychiatrist-led interviews achieved higher satisfaction scores, particularly for communication quality, while willingness to repeat screening did not differ significantly across modalities.

evidence.title: SymptomAI: Toward a Conversational AI Agent for Everyday Symptom Assessment
evidence.outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy of AI agent versus independent clinicians given the same dialogue
evidence.effect: SymptomAI DDx were significantly more accurate than independent clinicians (OR = 2.56, p < 0.001) in a blinded randomized comparison.
evidence.quote: SymptomAI DDx were significantly more accurate (OR = 2.56, p < 0.001) than those from independent clinicians given the same dialogue in a blinded randomized comparison.

evidence.title: Evidence-grounded AI for longitudinal clinical management in musculoskeletal care
evidence.outcome: AI performance compared with orthopaedic physicians across the care pathway
evidence.effect: OrthoPilot surpassed experts with 25 years of experience in diagnostic reasoning, clinical decision-making and management planning in a reader study with 81 physicians.
evidence.quote: In a reader study, OrthoPilot was compared with 81 orthopaedic physicians across the complete care pathway, surpassing experts with 25 years of experience in diagnostic reasoning, clinical decision-making and management planning.

evidence.title: Comparing the Acceptability and Quality of Intervention Modalities for Suicidality in the Emergency Department: Randomized Feasibility Trial
evidence.outcome: safety plan quality
evidence.effect: H=0.60, P=.74 comparing chatbot to in-person and telehealth clinicians
evidence.quote: The safety plans created across all 3 modalities were high-quality (H=0.60, P=.74).

evidence.title: Real-time machine learning-assisted sepsis alert enhances the timeliness of antibiotic administration and diagnostic accuracy in emergency department patients with sepsis: a cluster-randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance (AUROC) of ML model versus rule-based tools for early sepsis identification
evidence.effect: ML AUROC significantly higher than qSOFA, SIRS, and MEWS for early sepsis identification.
evidence.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of ML in early sepsis identification was significantly higher than qSOFA, SIRS, and MEWS.

evidence.title: A deep-learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection on CT angiography images in China: a stepwise, multicentre, early-stage clinical validation study
evidence.outcome: AI versus clinician patient-level diagnostic sensitivity on external validation cases
evidence.effect: External patient-level sensitivity was 0·943 [0·921-0·961] for AI vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672] for clinicians; p<0·0001.
evidence.quote: The AI model in the internal dataset achieved a patient-level diagnostic sensitivity of 0·957 (95% CI 0·939-0·971) and a higher patient-level diagnostic sensitivity than clinicians (0·943 [0·921-0·961] vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672]; p<0·0001) in the external dataset.

evidence.title: A randomized controlled trial of a WeChat-based artificial intelligence agent for postoperative care in orthopedic patients
evidence.outcome: AI agent response speed, quality and accuracy compared with physician communication
evidence.effect: AI responded faster (0.5±0.6 vs 358±47.5 min, p<0.05) with higher perceived quality but slightly lower accuracy (93.9% vs 98.1%, p<0.05).
evidence.quote: The AI system responded far more rapidly (0.5 ± 0.6 vs. 358 ± 47.5 min, p < 0.05) and provided feedback of higher perceived quality, though with slightly reduced accuracy (93.9% vs. 98.1%, p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Evaluating and Validating Large Language Models for Health Education on Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: 2-Phase Study With Expert Ratings and a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: performance differences among models
evidence.effect: Significant differences found in accuracy, richness, fluency, understandability, and DISCERN scores among the 4 evaluated LLMs.
evidence.quote: There were significant differences between the 4 LLMs concerning accuracy, richness, fluency, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials Understandability, and DISCERN (P<.05).

evidence.title: A community-codesigned LLM-powered chatbot for primary care: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.outcome: primary care quality scores
evidence.effect: AI outperformed usual care in diagnosis (4.13 vs 2.86) and test ordering (4.27 vs 2.68)
evidence.quote: P&P Care (e-learning plus variant) significantly outperformed both usual care and telemedicine across all domains ( P < 0.001; Fig. 5b ), with marked improvements in diagnosis (4.13 ± 1.15 versus usual care: 2.86 ± 1.05; telemedicine: 2.30 ± 1.17) and test ordering (4.27 ± 1.13 versus usual care: 2.68 ± 1.17; telemedicine: 2.29 ± 1.23; Extended Data Table 5 ).

evidence.title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
evidence.outcome: Agreement between candidate-model screening ranks and downstream coding performance
evidence.effect: Intrinsic screening ranked BioMistral highest (44.1% selection probability). Downstream fine-tuning preserved model ordering, with BioMistral achieving F 1 -score = 0.78 and win rate = 69.2%.
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 4 , the relative ordering of models was preserved after fine-tuning: BioMistral achieved the highest downstream performance (F 1 -score = 0.78; win rate = 69.2%), followed by MedLlama2 and Mistral.
evidence.sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

evidence.title: A bimodal large language model reduces misalignment in patient education: A double-blinded randomized trial
evidence.outcome: Emotion recognition accuracy and semantic consistency of Dolphin versus a matched text-based LLM and human educators
evidence.effect: Dolphin outperformed the text-based LLM in emotion recognition accuracy (0.886 vs. 0.713) and semantic consistency (84.9% vs. 82.1%; both adjusted p < 0.001), and received higher expert ratings than the LLM and human educators (all p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Dolphin outperformed the text-based LLM in emotion recognition accuracy (0.886 vs. 0.713) and semantic consistency (84.9% vs. 82.1%; both adjusted p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (randomized trial); 64,200 utterances from 16,583 cases in the misalignment analysis

evidence.title: Full end-to-end diagnostic workflow automation of 3D OCT via foundation model-driven AI for retinal diseases
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with expert ophthalmologists on abnormality detection and multi-disease diagnosis
evidence.effect: FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), with better efficiency.
evidence.quote: In human-machine comparisons, FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), while demonstrating better efficiency.

evidence.title: Prospective validation of machine learning models predicting Gram negative bacteremia in ICU versus clinical scores
evidence.outcome: ML model discrimination for Gram-negative bacteremia compared with established clinical scores in ICU
evidence.effect: Several clinical scores were significantly associated with bacteremia. ML models showed modest discrimination overall, improving to AUROC ≈ 0.70 with higher sensitivity in a post-hoc subgroup of cultures from ICU days 4-10.
evidence.quote: While ML models demonstrated modest discrimination in cohort, performance improved to a moderate level (AUROC ≈ 0.70) with higher sensitivity in a post-hoc subgroup analysis of cultures obtained between ICU days 4 and 10.

evidence.title: Prospective Evaluation of Machine Learning for Public Health Screening: Identifying Unknown Hepatitis C Carriers
evidence.outcome: HCV carriers identified per number screened, ML-targeted outreach versus concurrent USPSTF-eligible testing
evidence.effect: ML outreach: 477 screened, 38 active carriers, NNS 10. USPSTF-eligible testing: 53,403 tested, 38 carriers, NNS 1029. Over 100-fold greater efficiency.
evidence.quote: Among the 53,403 USPSTF screening–eligible members who were tested over the same period, 38 were found to be active HCV carriers, yielding an NNS of 1029.
evidence.sample_unit: members screened for HCV antibodies in prospective outreach

evidence.title: AUPA: weakly supervised approach for streamlining breast cancer diagnostic workflow by WSI histological type classification for efficient IHC triage
evidence.outcome: AUPA performance compared with expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models
evidence.effect: AUPA performs competitively against expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models, especially in distinguishing in situ from benign cases.
evidence.quote: Compared to expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models, AUPA performs competitively, especially distinguishing in situ from benign cases.

evidence.title: Prospective Validation of the EAC+ Algorithm for Surgical Timing in Multi-System Trauma: A Multicentre Pragmatic Trial
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, AUROC, precision and recall of EAC+ versus standard practice, EAC thresholds, logistic regression, decision tree
evidence.effect: EAC+ achieved the highest accuracy (91.4%), AUROC (0.94), precision (0.89), and recall (0.92) versus comparators; also shortened ICU stay by 1.6 days and lowered 30-day mortality.
evidence.quote: EAC+ achieved the highest accuracy (91.4%), AUROC (0.94), precision (0.89), and recall (0.92), while reducing unnecessary surgical delays, shortening ICU stay by an average of 1.6 days, and lowering 30-day mortality.

evidence.title: Audited large language model triage for systematic review screening in national clinical guideline production: validation and prospective deployment
evidence.outcome: LLM triage versus blinded human consensus screening on audited records
evidence.effect: All 38 final retained records were AI flagged, while locked blinded human consensus missed seven.
evidence.quote: Across 600 randomly sampled AI-excluded records from the migraine and dementia programmes, none was confirmed as a final false negative after post-unblinding adjudication; across the completed 680-record audit, all 38 final retained records had been AI flagged, whereas locked blinded human consensus missed seven.

evidence.title: A ‘Silent Trial’ Assessing the Accuracy of Large Language Models for Assisting Community Health Workers in Low-Resource Settings
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two LLMs and CHWs on referral accuracy using the same encounters
evidence.effect: o3 performed similarly to CHWs (97.9%); Gemini 2.5-Flash accuracy was 47.3% (95% CI 42.6-52.1), so choice of LLM is a critical design decision.
evidence.quote: In conclusion, the choice of LLM appears to be a critical design decision.

evidence.title: Physician gestalt compared with AI model to predict intubation in critically ill patients
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of Vent.io versus intensivist gestalt for predicting intubation within 24 hours
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 0.190 (physicians) vs 0.714 (Vent.io); specificity 0.960 vs 0.673. Vent.io OR 18.68 for correct when intubation needed; physicians OR 24.80 for correct when not needed.
evidence.quote: Vent.io had significantly greater odds of being correct when patients required intubation compared to physicians (OR 18.68; 95% CI 1.87-186.31; p=0.013).

evidence.title: A Machine Learning Model Integrated with the Clinical Workflow Detects Sepsis Early with High Sensitivity and Specificity
evidence.outcome: False positive rate of new sepsis model versus existing commercial model in same health system
evidence.effect: Post-deployment false positive rate 6% versus 30% for the commercial model; sensitivity 91% and specificity 94% after deployment.
evidence.quote: Notably, the post-deployment false positive rate of 6% represents a substantial reduction compared to the currently deployed commercial model in the same health system, which exhibits a false positive rate of 30%.

evidence.title: Multicenter Development and Prospective Validation of eCARTv5: A Gradient Boosted Machine Learning Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: eCART discrimination compared with MEWS and NEWS on same data
evidence.effect: eCART AUROC 0.835 (95%CI 0.834, 0.835) vs NEWS 0.766 (0.766, 0.767) and MEWS 0.704 (0.703, 0.704) in retrospective validation.
evidence.quote: In retrospective validation, eCART had the highest AUROC (0.835; 95%CI 0.834, 0.835), followed by NEWS (0.766 (95%CI 0.766, 0.767)), and MEWS (0.704 (95%CI 0.703, 0.704)).

evidence.title: Enhancing Real-World Data Extraction in Clinical Research: Evaluating the Impact of the Implementation of Large Language Models in Hospital Settings
evidence.outcome: Data extraction accuracy of ChatGLM and LLaMA versus manual input on free-text forms
evidence.effect: Initial manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, ChatGLM extraction accuracy 77.13%, and LLaMA 43.86%.
evidence.quote: The initial manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, the ChatGLM data extraction accuracy was 77.13%, and the LLaMA data extraction accuracy was 43.86%.

evidence.title: Development and Prospective Implementation of a Large Language Model based System for Early Sepsis Prediction
evidence.outcome: Sepsis prediction performance of COMPOSER-LLM versus standalone COMPOSER on same encounters
evidence.effect: COMPOSER-LLM had sensitivity 72.1%, PPV 52.9%, F-1 61.0%, and 0.0087 false alarms per patient hour, outperforming standalone COMPOSER; prospective validation yielded similar results.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on 2,500 patient encounters, COMPOSER-LLM achieved a sensitivity of 72.1%, positive predictive value of 52.9%, F-1 score of 61.0%, and 0.0087 false alarms per patient hour, outperforming the standalone COMPOSER model.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Predictive Model to Accelerate Antibiotic Therapy for Critical Ill Children with Sepsis in the Pediatric ED with Pediatric ICU Disposition
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUROC) of the local model versus vendor-developed sepsis model
evidence.effect: SEPD model AUROC 81.8% compared to 57.5% for the vendor-developed sepsis model, with better precision-recall performance.
evidence.quote: The SEPD model outperformed a vendor-developed sepsis model with an AUROC of 81.8%, compared to 57.5%.

evidence.title: Clinical value of artificial intelligence in thyroid ultrasound: a prospective study from the real world
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with senior radiologists and residents on same nodules
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 0.95, accuracy 0.84, AUC 0.753; not statistically different from experienced radiologists, superior to residents (all p < 0.01).
evidence.quote: The sensitivity, accuracy, and AUC of the AI system were 0.95, 0.84, and 0.753, respectively, and were not statistically different from those of the experienced radiologists, but were superior to those of the residents (all p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Developing and Validating a Prediction Model For Death or Critical Illness in Hospitalized Adults, an Opportunity for Human-Computer Collaboration
evidence.outcome: ML model vs clinician predictions of ICU admission or death on the same hospitalizations
evidence.effect: ML median F1 0.32, AUC 0.77 vs clinicians F1 0.33, AUC 0.64; ML more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.
evidence.quote: ML predictions were more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model to Identify Patients Before Surgery at High Risk for Postoperative Adverse Events
evidence.outcome: Mortality prediction accuracy of ML model versus NSQIP calculator on same 902 patients
evidence.effect: Model beat NSQIP: AUROC 0.945 vs 0.897 (difference 0.048); specificity 0.87 vs 0.68; accuracy 0.85 vs 0.69.
evidence.quote: The model outperformed the NSQIP tool as measured by AUROC (0.945 [95% CI, 0.914-0.977] vs 0.897 [95% CI, 0.854-0.941], for a difference of 0.048), specificity (0.87 [95% CI, 0.83-0.89] vs 0.68 [95% CI, 0.65-0.69]), and accuracy (0.85 [95% CI, 0.82-0.87] vs 0.69 [95% CI, 0.66, 0.72]).

evidence.title: Performance of CT-based deep learning in diagnostic assessment of suspicious lateral lymph nodes in papillary thyroid cancer: a prospective diagnostic study
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with senior radiologists and FNA reference in prospectively enrolled lymph nodes
evidence.effect: Ensemble model AUC 0.829, sensitivity 0.839, specificity 0.769, accuracy 82.3%; not significantly different from FNA (P=0.115) or the two senior radiologists (P=1.000, P=0.392).
evidence.quote: With FNA results as the criterion standard, the ensemble model had excellent diagnostic performance ( P =0.115), similar to that of the two senior radiologists ( P =1.000 and P =0.392, respectively).

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance, Triage Safety, and Usability of a Clinical Decision Support System Within a University Hospital Emergency Department: Algorithm Performance and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: CDSS urgency triage sensitivity compared against physician evaluations on the same patients
evidence.effect: CDSS urgent sensitivity 85% vs physicians; physician-to-physician urgent sensitivity 85%; nonurgent 19% (CDSS) vs 35% (physicians).
evidence.quote: The mean sensitivities were 85% and 35%, respectively, when comparing the evaluations between the two physicians.

evidence.title: Prospective, multicenter validation of the deep learning-based cardiac arrest risk management system for predicting in-hospital cardiac arrest or unplanned intensive care unit transfer in patients admitted to general wards
evidence.outcome: AUROC of AI early warning versus MEWS/NEWS for IHCA or unplanned ICU transfer
evidence.effect: Composite outcome AUROC for DeepCARS 0.869 vs 0.756 (MEWS) and 0.767 (NEWS); fewer alarms per 1,000 beds at same sensitivity and higher rate of appropriate alarms.
evidence.quote: In terms of the composite outcome, the AUROC for the DeepCARS™ was superior to those for the MEWS and NEWS (0.869 vs. 0.756/0.767).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection in screening mammography in Sweden: a prospective, population-based, paired-reader, non-inferiority study
evidence.outcome: Screen-detected breast cancer compared with standard-of-care double reading
evidence.effect: One radiologist plus AI was non-inferior to two radiologists: 261 [0·5%] vs 250 [0·4%] detected cases; relative proportion 1·04 [95% CI 1·00-1·09].
evidence.quote: 269 (0·5%) women were diagnosed with screen-detected breast cancer based on an initial positive read: double reading by one radiologist plus AI was non-inferior for cancer detection compared with double reading by two radiologists (261 [0·5%] vs 250 [0·4%] detected cases; relative proportion 1·04 [95% CI 1·00-1·09]).

evidence.title: Comparison of humans versus mobile phone-powered artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of pigmented skin cancer in secondary care: a multicentre, prospective, diagnostic, clinical trial
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic and management accuracy of AI versus specialist and novice clinicians on same lesions
evidence.effect: 7-class AI equivalent to specialists (1·2% [-6·9 to 9·2]) and superior to novices (21·5%); ISIC AI inferior to specialists (-11·6%); management AI inferior to specialists (-0·5% scenario A).
evidence.quote: The diagnoses of the 7-class AI algorithm were equivalent to the specialists' diagnoses (absolute accuracy difference 1·2% [95% CI -6·9 to 9·2]) and significantly superior to the novices' ones (21·5% [13·1 to 30·0]).
evidence.sample_unit: suspicious pigmented lesions (diagnostic trial; 124 patients); management trial 5696 lesions from 66 patients

evidence.title: AI Model Versus Clinician Otoscopy in the Operative Setting for Otitis Media Diagnosis
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI model versus pediatricians for otitis media
evidence.effect: Model more accurate than clinicians (90.6% vs 59.4%, P = .01)
evidence.quote: We find that the model is more accurate than clinicians (90.6% vs 59.4%, P = .01).

evidence.title: Using artificial intelligence to predict adverse outcomes in emergency department patients with hyperglycemic crises in real time
evidence.outcome: AUC for all-cause mortality prediction, AI model vs existing PHD score
evidence.effect: AI model AUC 0.796 vs PHD score AUC 0.693 for predicting all-cause mortality.
evidence.quote: The AI model performed better than the PHD score for predicting all-cause mortality (AUC 0.796 vs. 0.693).

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound with artificial intelligence-assisted assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI-assisted FoCUS LVEF with formal TTE reference on same participants
evidence.effect: Overall ICC 0.904; weighted kappa 0.83 for LVEF categories; AUC 0.98 for LVEF <50% (sensitivity 92.8%, specificity 92.3%).
evidence.quote: The overall intraclass coefficient was 0.904, and 0.921 in the novice (n = 208) and 0.845 in the experienced (n = 216) cohorts.

evidence.title: Clinical Decision Support System for All Stages of Gastric Carcinogenesis in Real-Time Endoscopy: Model Establishment and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Overall accuracy of CDSS versus experienced endoscopists on prospective real-clinic evaluation
evidence.effect: No significant difference in overall accuracy between invited endoscopists and established CDSS in prospective real-clinic evaluation (P=.23).
evidence.quote: There was no significant difference in the overall accuracy between the invited endoscopists and established CDSS in the prospective real-clinic evaluation (P=.23).

evidence.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model integrated with the clinical workflow for early detection of sepsis
evidence.outcome: False positive rate of new model versus currently deployed commercial model
evidence.effect: Post-deployment false positive rate of 6% versus 30% for the commercial model in the same health system.
evidence.quote: Notably, the post-deployment false positive rate of 6% represents a substantial reduction compared to the currently deployed commercial model in the same health system, which exhibits a false positive rate of 30%.

evidence.title: Large language models for preventing medication direction errors in online pharmacies
evidence.outcome: Near-miss events for MEDIC versus two LLM benchmarks on same expert-reviewed prescriptions
evidence.effect: Benchmarks recorded 1.51 (CI 1.03, 2.31) and 4.38 (CI 3.13, 6.64) times more near-miss events than MEDIC.
evidence.quote: On 1,200 expert-reviewed prescriptions, the two benchmarks respectively recorded 1.51 (confidence interval (CI) 1.03, 2.31) and 4.38 (CI 3.13, 6.64) times more near-miss events-errors caught and corrected before reaching the patient-than MEDIC.

evidence.title: External validation of the myocardial-ischaemic-injury-index machine learning algorithm for the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction: a multicentre cohort study
evidence.outcome: MI3 versus ESC 0/1h-algorithm sensitivity, NPV, specificity, PPV, rule-out and rule-in efficacy for type 1 NSTEMI
evidence.effect: ESC 0/1h had higher sensitivity (diff 0.88%, p=0.0082) and NPV (0.18%, p=0.016); MI3 had higher specificity (3.80%), PPV (7.84%) and rule-out efficacy (11%); ESC had higher rule-in efficacy (5.4%).
evidence.quote: The sensitivity and NPV of the ESC 0/1h-algorithm were higher than that of MI 3 (difference for sensitivity 0·88% [0·19 to 1·60], p=0·0082; difference for NPV 0·18% [0·05 to 0·32], p=0·016), and the rule-out efficacy was higher for MI 3 (11% difference, p<0·0001).
evidence.country: Switzerland, Spain, Italy, Poland, Czech Republic

evidence.title: Comparing Clinician Estimates versus a Statistical Tool for Predicting Risk of Death within 45 Days of Admission for Cancer Patients
evidence.outcome: Model versus clinician estimates on discrimination, calibration, and net benefit on same admissions
evidence.effect: Model outperformed clinicians (AUC 0.834 vs 0.753, p<0.0001); clinicians overestimated risk while the model was extremely well-calibrated; model showed net benefit across thresholds.
evidence.quote: The model performed better than the clinician estimates (AUC 0.834 vs. 0.753, p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: A 3D and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Model for Evaluation of Chronic Otitis Media Based on Temporal Bone Computed Tomography: Model Development, Validation, and Clinical Application
evidence.outcome: 3D model versus 2D baseline and clinicians on same data
evidence.effect: 3D model outperformed 2D model for COM detection (P≤.05) and cholesteatoma (P<.001); outperformed resident fellows and attending otologist (P<.05), rivaled senior clinicians.
evidence.quote: The model also demonstrated superior diagnostic capabilities over resident fellows and the attending otologist (P<.05), rivaling all senior clinicians in both tasks.

evidence.title: A Machine Learning Method for Differentiation Crohn's Disease and Intestinal Tuberculosis
evidence.outcome: Comparison of six candidate ML models, and ML versus multidisciplinary team, on the same data
evidence.effect: XGBoost performed best of six models (AUROC 0.946, accuracy 0.884); in clinical practice ML-MDT agreement was 90.7%, kappa 0.780
evidence.quote: XGBoost displays the best performance among the six ML models.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of the Offline Medios Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Detection in a Rural Tele-Ophthalmology Setting
evidence.outcome: AI vs tele-ophthalmologist agreement with glaucoma specialist diagnosis and false-positive referrals
evidence.effect: AI agreement with specialist 80.3% vs 55.3% for tele-ophthalmologist; false positive referrals 2 of 10 for AI vs 9 of 10 for tele-ophthalmologist.
evidence.quote: The agreement between AI and the glaucoma specialist was 80.3%, surpassing the 55.3% agreement between the tele-ophthalmologist and the glaucoma specialist amongst those participants who were referred to the base hospital.

evidence.title: Comparison of 1-year mortality predictions from vendor-supplied versus academic model for cancer patients
evidence.outcome: Vendor model compared against academic model on same patients for 1-year mortality AUC and PPV
evidence.effect: AUC 0.73 (EOLCI) vs 0.82 (academic); PPV 0.38 vs 0.65, showing the vendor model performed worse than the comparator.
evidence.quote: AUC for 1-year mortality for EOLCI and academic model was 0.73 (95% CI [0.70-0.76]) and 0.82 (95% CI [0.80-0.85]), respectively.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence applied to electrocardiogram to rule out acute myocardial infarction: the ROMIAE multicentre study
evidence.outcome: AMI diagnostic AUC of AI-ECG versus HEART, GRACE 2.0, troponin, and physician score
evidence.effect: AI-ECG AUC 0.878 (95% CI 0.868-0.888), comparable with HEART 0.877 and superior to GRACE 2.0, hs-troponin, and Physician AMI score.
evidence.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-ECG was 0.878 (95% CI, 0.868-0.888), comparable with the HEART score (0.877; 95% CI, 0.869-0.886) and superior to the GRACE 2.0 score, high-sensitivity troponin level, and Physician AMI score.

evidence.title: Real-world feasibility, accuracy and acceptability of automated retinal photography and AI-based cardiovascular disease risk assessment in Australian primary care settings: a pragmatic trial
evidence.outcome: Predictive accuracy of AI rpCVD score versus WHO CVD risk score for 10-year incident CVD
evidence.effect: rpCVD AUC = 0.672 (95% CI: 0.658-0.686) versus WHO CVD risk score AUC = 0.693 (95% CI: 0.680-0.707); comparable accuracy using retinal images alone.
evidence.quote: Despite this, the rpCVD system, which relies solely on retinal images, demonstrated a similar level of accuracy in predicting 10-year incident CVD (AUC = 0.672, 95% CI: 0.658-0.686) compared to the WHO CVD risk score (AUC = 0.693, 95% CI: 0.680-0.707).

evidence.title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses From Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o versus baseline Clinical Longformer on PE extraction performance, same validation set
evidence.effect: GPT-4o outperformed Clinical Longformer in 2 metrics: sensitivity 1.0 (P<.001) and F1-score 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; P<.001) on validation dataset.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o outperformed the Clinical Longformer in 2 of the metrics, achieving a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0; Wilcoxon test, P<.001) and an F1-score of 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; Wilcoxon test, P<.001) across the validation dataset.
evidence.sample_unit: operational radiology report impressions (postdeployment); 200 validation impressions

evidence.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of AI early warning score versus NEWS and MEWS on same data
evidence.effect: VC-MAES AUROC 0.896 vs NEWS 0.797 and MEWS 0.722; AUPRC 0.336 vs 0.125 (NEWS) and 0.079 (MEWS).
evidence.quote: These results indicate that VC-MAES outperformed both NEWS and MEWS in terms of both AUROC and AUPRC ( Figure 1 ).

evidence.title: Non-invasive biopsy diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease via deep learning applied to retinal images: a population-based study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity for detecting DKD, DeepDKD versus a metadata-only model, in a prospective study
evidence.effect: DeepDKD detected DKD with higher sensitivity than the metadata model (89·8% vs 66·3%, p<0·0001).
evidence.quote: In the prospective study, compared with the metadata model, DeepDKD could detect DKD with higher sensitivity (89·8% vs 66·3%, p<0·0001).

evidence.title: Behavior recognition technology based on deep learning used in pediatric behavioral audiometry
evidence.outcome: AI vs manual behavioral audiometry sensitivity, specificity, AUC by age group
evidence.effect: Ages 2.5-4: AI sensitivity 0.929 vs manual 0.900, but manual specificity 0.824 and AUC 0.901 higher. Ages 4-6: manual sensitivity 0.943, specificity 0.947, AUC 0.924 all higher than AI.
evidence.quote: For children aged 4-6 years, the sensitivity (0.943), specificity (0.947), and AUC (0.924) of artificial behavioral audiometry were higher than those of AI behavioral audiometry.

evidence.title: Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Out-patient Diabetes Care - Comparison of Two Artificial Intelligence Algorithms: RetCAD and OphtAI
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of two competing DR AI algorithms versus ophthalmologist reference on same images
evidence.effect: RetCAD sensitivity 90%, specificity 100%; OphtAI sensitivity 70%, specificity 100% for referable DR, so head-to-head comparison revealed a meaningful difference between vendors.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the second AI-based algorithm OphtAI version 2.3.4 achieved a sensitivity of 70% and a specificity of 100% for the detection of a referable DR.

evidence.title: Validation of an artificial intelligence-based algorithm for predictive performance and risk stratification of sepsis using real-world data from hospitalised patients: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: AUROC of AI sepsis prediction versus traditional scoring systems on same prospective cohort
evidence.effect: VC-SEPS AUROC 0.880, superior to traditional scoring systems; predicted sepsis on average 68.05 min before operational-definition diagnosis.
evidence.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of VC-SEPS was 0.880, indicating its superiority over traditional scoring systems.

evidence.title: Evaluating chain-of-thought prompting in a GPT chatbot for BCID2 interpretation and stewardship: how does AI compare to human experts?
evidence.outcome: Harmful or inadequate recommendations, GPT-4 chatbot vs antimicrobial stewardship program (ASP) expert recommendations
evidence.effect: Chatbot had higher combined harmful or inadequate rate (13%) than ASP (4%, p = 0.047); antibiotic therapy harmful recommendations up to 10% (p<0.05).
evidence.quote: The chatbot had a significantly higher rate of harmful or inadequate recommendations (13%) compared to ASP (4%, p = 0.047).

evidence.title: Real time machine learning prediction of next generation sequencing test results in live clinical settings
evidence.outcome: Model discrimination (AUC) compared with expert hematologist estimates for predicting Heme-STAMP results
evidence.effect: Model AUC 0.77 [0.66, 0.87] vs hematologists 0.78 [0.68, 0.86]; the model also improved calibration of human estimates.
evidence.quote: The model predicted the results of a complex next-generation sequencing test with discriminatory power comparable to expert hematologists (AUC score: 0.77 [0.66, 0.87], 0.78 [0.68, 0.86] respectively) and with the capacity to improve the calibration of human estimates.

evidence.title: Real-World Evaluation of AI-Driven Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Public Health Settings: Validation and Implementation Study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of vendor DR algorithms on same local images before selection
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 60%-80% and specificity 14%-96% across algorithms; FDA-approved algorithm excluded for low specificity; AI-3 selected (specificity 96.01%, sensitivity 68.42%, accuracy 88.43%).
evidence.quote: One Indian AI algorithm declined participation, and an Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved algorithm was excluded due to low specificity in interim analysis.

evidence.title: Real-world clinical impact of three commercial AI algorithms on musculoskeletal radiography interpretation: A prospective crossover reader study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three commercial AI tools against unaided reading on same studies
evidence.effect: Three AI tools compared with unaided reads on the same studies; no significant AUC differences, but BoneView gave larger confidence gains than Rayvolve and RBfracture.
evidence.quote: Confidence improved across tools: BoneView increased combined "very good/excellent" ratings versus unaided reads (Reader 1: 509 vs. 449, p < 0.001; Reader 2: 483 vs. 439, p < 0.001); Rayvolve (Reader 1: 456 vs. 449, p = 0.029; Reader 2: 449 vs. 439, p < 0.001) and RBfracture (Reader 1: 457 vs. 449, p = 0.017; Reader 2: 448 vs. 439, p = 0.001) yielded smaller but significant gains.
evidence.sample_unit: adult musculoskeletal studies (2,926 radiographs) read by 2 radiologists

evidence.title: Clinical validation of an AI-based blood testing device for diagnosis and prognosis of acute infection and sepsis
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of TriVerity versus CRP, procalcitonin, WBC, and qSOFA comparators
evidence.effect: TriVerity Bacterial AUROC 0.83 and Viral AUROC 0.91 exceeded CRP, procalcitonin and WBC; Severity score AUROC 0.78 reclassified risk compared with qSOFA alone.
evidence.quote: The TriVerity Bacterial and Viral scores had higher accuracy than C-reactive protein, procalcitonin or white blood cell count for the diagnosis of bacterial infection with area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) of 0.83, and viral infection (AUROC = 0.91).

evidence.title: Deep learning CT model for stratified diagnosis of pancreatic cystic neoplasms: multicenter development, validation, and real-world clinical impact
evidence.outcome: AI performance versus radiologist double-reading in prospective real-world cohort
evidence.effect: PCN-AI outperformed radiologist double-reading, providing actionable diagnostic benefit to 45.45% of patients (5/11) by identifying missed malignant PCN cases, and reduced clinical workload by 39.3%.
evidence.quote: In a prospective real-world cohort, PCN-AI outperformed radiologist double-reading, providing actionable diagnostic benefits to 45.45% of patients (5/11) by correctly identifying missed malignant PCN cases, enabling timely intervention, and simultaneously reducing clinical workload by 39.3%.

evidence.title: Safety and accuracy of AI in triaging patients in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT triage accuracy versus ED physicians against consultant gold standard
evidence.effect: ChatGPT agreed with ED physicians 85.61% (κ=0.780) but accuracy versus consultant was 42.86%; physician-consultant agreement was 63.9% (κ=0.406).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's accuracy compared to the consultant was 42.86%, with slight reliability, showing a tendency to overestimate acuity, particularly in critical cases.

evidence.title: Clinical validation of an AI-assisted system for real-time kidney stone detection during flexible ureteroscopic surgery
evidence.outcome: AI stone type prediction accuracy compared with expert surgeons
evidence.effect: AiFURS patient-level stone type accuracy of 92.2-95.3% (in vivo) and 86.8-92.2% (external) outperformed expert surgeons.
evidence.quote: In vivo and external validation of 100 and 80 cases, respectively, demonstrated diagnostic accuracy (92.2-95.3% and 86.8-92.2%, respectively) for patient-level stone type prediction, outperforming expert surgeons.
evidence.sample_unit: in vivo cases (patients) undergoing flexible ureteroscopy

evidence.title: Clinical Trial Patient Matching: A Real-Time, Common Data Model and Artificial Intelligence-Driven System for Semiautomated Patient Prescreening in Cancer Clinical Trials
evidence.outcome: Chart review workload and screening time compared with manual chart review
evidence.effect: Chart review workload reduced 10-fold; screening time reduced 41% (3.1 to 1.8 minutes per chart) for reviewed patients
evidence.quote: Implementation reduced chart review workload 10-fold and screening time by 41% (3.1 to 1.8 minutes per chart) for those patients who did undergo review.

evidence.title: Prospective validation and real-time implementation of an automated machine learning postoperative mortality prediction model
evidence.outcome: Comparison of the ML model against ASA physical status baseline
evidence.effect: ML model AUROC 0.874 vs ASA physical status AUROC 0.814 (95% CI 0.802-0.827); AUCPR 0.111 vs 0.103.
evidence.quote: By comparison, the AUROC for the 58-feature model was 0.925 (95% CI 0.900-0.947), and for ASA physical status the AUROC was 0.814 (95% CI 0.802-0.827) and the AUCPR was 0.103.

evidence.title: Real-World Integration of an Automated Tool for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection in an Unselected Cohort of Emergency Department Patients-An External Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of AI tool with first-year radiology resident on the same CT scans
evidence.effect: Resident: 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, 99.6% NPV vs RAPID ICH 87.3%, 74%, 21.3%, 98.6%.
evidence.quote: RAPID ICH showed 87.3% sensitivity, 74% specificity, 21.3% PPV, and 98.6% NPV, while the first-year radiology resident achieved 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, and 99.6% NPV.

evidence.title: Physiological foundation modeling for subclinical disease assessment: a prospective pilot
evidence.outcome: Spearman correlation with PDFF versus existing foundation models and clinical risk scores
evidence.effect: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.
evidence.quote: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.

evidence.title: Diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in premenopausal women with non-specific symptoms (ROCkeTS): prospective, multicentre, cohort study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head sensitivity and specificity of candidate risk models versus current standard test (RMI1) on same patients
evidence.effect: Versus RMI1 at 250 (sensitivity 42.6%, specificity 96.5%), IOTA ADNEX at 10% had sensitivity 89.1% (P<0.001) and specificity 75.1% (P<0.001); other tests also had higher sensitivity and lower specificity.
evidence.quote: Compared to Risk of Malignancy Index 1 at 250 threshold-the test currently used in NHS secondary care to triage women to tertiary care-most tests improve sensitivity but reduce specificity.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence risk stratification from dynamic digital subtraction angiography radiomics predicts pulmonary embolism and associates with clinical outcomes in deep vein thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study
evidence.venue: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
evidence.outcome: Discrimination for predicting pulmonary embolism, AI model versus Wells score
evidence.effect: AUC 0.88 (95% CI 0.85-0.92) for the AI model vs 0.76 (95% CI 0.70-0.83) for Wells score; P = .026.
evidence.quote: The AI model demonstrated significantly superior discriminative performance for predicting PE compared with the Wells score (area under the curve, 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.85-0.92 vs 0.76; 95% CI, 0.70-0.83; P = .026).

evidence.title: Performance of AI vs radiology residents in the detection of intracranial hemorrhage on emergency CT: a real-world analysis
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with on-call radiology residents on the same CT scans
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 84% and specificity 94.4% vs residents 96.4% and 99.6% (p-values < 0.001); AI did not offer superior performance.
evidence.quote: Radiology residents demonstrated a significantly higher performance in detecting ICH compared to the AI software.
evidence.country: Not reported (single university hospital; European journal)

evidence.title: Deep Learning and Fluid Dynamics On-Site CT-FFR Solution Compared to Off-Site FFRct and Invasive FFR
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of on-site xFFR versus off-site FFRct against invasive FFR on the same patients
evidence.effect: xFFR AUC 0.91 vs FFRct AUC 0.89 (P = 0.274); superior only for LAD (AUC 0.96 vs 0.84, P = 0.001).
evidence.quote: The overall diagnostic accuracy was comparable to FFRct (AUC: 0.91 vs AUC: 0.89; P = 0.274), superior only for left anterior descending coronary artery assessment (AUC: 0.96 vs AUC: 0.84; P = 0.001).

evidence.title: Predicting the Value of Radiology Artificial Intelligence Applications: Large-Scale Predeployment Evaluation of a Portfolio of Models
evidence.outcome: Predeployment comparison of AI versus radiologist performance on the same examinations
evidence.effect: Radiologists generally had higher PPV, AI higher sensitivity; the combined predeployment evaluation showed high agreement with real-world postdeployment value perceptions (10 of 12 tasks).
evidence.quote: A validation survey indicated high agreement between predeployment predictions and real-world postdeployment value perceptions.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-based pathological model for pan-cancer lymph node metastasis detection: a multicentre diagnostic study with retrospective and prospective validation
evidence.outcome: Additional metastasis patients detected by AI versus pathologists on same data
evidence.effect: PanCAM identified 120 additional patients with lymph node metastasis missed by pathologists in retrospective validation and 21 additional in prospective validation.
evidence.quote: At the patient level, PanCAM identified 120 additional patients with lymph node metastasis who were missed by pathologists in the retrospective validation and 21 additional cases in the prospective validation.

evidence.title: Deep learning approach for stroke volume variation estimation: retrospective modeling and prospective deployment in real-world practice
evidence.outcome: SVVNet agreement versus ABP-PWA algorithm and other DL models on external validation
evidence.effect: SVVNet had MAE 0.70 and Pearson 0.92 vs ABP-PWA MAE 1.30 and Pearson 0.80, with lower inter-individual deviation.
evidence.quote: In the retrospective external validation, SVVNet achieved higher agreement mean absolute error (MAE = 0.70, Pearsonρ= 0.92), compared to ABP-PWA algorithm (MAE = 1.30, Pearsonρ= 0.80) and lower inter-individual deviation.

evidence.title: Physician Gestalt Compared With Artificial Intelligence Model to Predict Intubation in Critically Ill Patients
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of ML intubation prediction versus intensivist prediction on the same patients
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 0.190 (physicians) vs 0.714 (Vent.io); specificity 0.960 vs 0.673. Vent.io was better when intubation was needed (OR 18.68); physicians were better when it was not (OR 24.80).
evidence.quote: Vent.io had significantly greater odds of being correct when patients required intubation compared with physicians (OR 18.68; 95% CI, 1.87-186.31; p = 0.013).

evidence.title: Transforming oncology clinical trial matching through neuro-symbolic, multi-agent AI and an oncology-specific knowledge graph: a prospective evaluation in 3804 patients
evidence.venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
evidence.outcome: Trial-matching F1 of multi-agent system versus GPT-4 baselines and manual screening
evidence.effect: Multi-agent system F1 0.82 vs GPT-4 zero-shot 0.47 and GPT-4 chain-of-thought 0.67; screening time fell from 120 min median to ~30 min.
evidence.quote: The multi-agent neuro-symbolic system achieved an F1 score of 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.81-0.83).

evidence.title: Hybrid supervised deep learning for lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis to optimize surgical strategies
evidence.outcome: subtype classification accuracy
evidence.effect: accuracy of 95.6%, outperforming manual (84.7%) and other methods (66.2%)
evidence.quote: Specifically, HSFLA achieved an accuracy of 95.6% in subtype classification, significantly outperforming manual diagnosis (84.7%) and weakly supervised learning methods (66.2% ± 3.0%).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence vs human opportunistic detection of vertebral fractures in routine CT scans: results of a pilot study
evidence.outcome: Vertebral fracture detection sensitivity of AI versus radiologists and endocrinologists against expert-panel gold standard
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 86.3% vs radiologists 50.0% and endocrinologists 68.8% (p<0.001 both); OR 6.30 (95% CI 2.90–13.58) vs radiologists, OR 2.85 (1.29–6.30) vs endocrinologists.
evidence.quote: Among 427 eligible CT scans, AI detected vertebral fractures with significantly higher sensitivity (86.3%) than radiologists (50.0%) or endocrinologists (68.8%) (p < 0.001 for both comparisons).

evidence.title: AI framework for multidisease detection via retinal imaging
evidence.outcome: Type 2 diabetes screening performance of AI versus Finnish Diabetes Risk Score in clinical pilot
evidence.effect: Pilot AUC 0.776 (0.710-0.842) and NPV 0.966 (0.946-0.983), surpassing the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score.
evidence.quote: A subsequent clinical pilot for type 2 diabetes mellitus yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.776 (0.710-0.842) and negative predictive value of 0.966 (0.946-0.983), surpassing the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score, with high acceptance from clinicians and patients.

evidence.title: Clinically-applicable prediction of hospital stay and patient similarity retrieval in paediatric cardiology using machine learning
evidence.outcome: Model length-of-stay prediction performance compared against clinician predictions
evidence.effect: Random Forest achieved the best length-of-stay prediction accuracy (0.88 ± 0.02), outperforming clinicians.
evidence.quote: Our models surpass clinician performance in length of stay prediction and show promise for case retrieval, supporting data-driven decision-making in paediatric cardiology and beyond.

evidence.title: Real-Time AI-Based Radiotherapy Planning for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: AI-generated plan quality compared with expert manual plans on same patients
evidence.effect: AI plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans in a 5-center retrospective benchmark.
evidence.quote: In the 5-center retrospective evaluation, artificial intelligence (AI)-generated plans achieved superior or comparable dosimetric quality relative to expert manual plans, despite variations in imaging, contouring, and prescription practices.
evidence.sample_unit: consecutively treated patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (prospective validation)

evidence.title: Machine learning outperforms serum creatinine for early risk stratification of hepatorenal syndrome: a prospective single-center validation
evidence.outcome: Model AUC versus serum creatinine standard for HRS diagnosis in prospective cohort
evidence.effect: ML model AUC 0.994 (95% CI 0.985-0.998) versus serum creatinine AUC 0.803; p < 0.001
evidence.quote: This represented a substantial and statistically significant improvement over serum creatinine-based diagnosis (AUC = 0.803; p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (prospective validation cohort with decompensated cirrhosis)

evidence.title: Prospective blinded clinical evaluation of a fully automated workflow for prostate radiotherapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Fully automated AI workflow compared with conventional clinical workflow on acceptability and processing time
evidence.effect: Acceptability 86% vs 95%; 'good' ratings 12/22 vs 17/22; median time 9 min vs 87 min; automated CTVs smaller (54.2 vs 68.3 cm3, p<0.001).
evidence.quote: The fully automated workflow required a median of 9 min (range 8-10) compared with 87 min (range 70-130) for the conventional workflow.

evidence.title: AI-Guided Surgical Blood Readiness: Overcoming Real-World Challenges in Prospective Validation for Safer, More Efficient Blood Preparation
evidence.outcome: Model performance compared with MSBOS and clinician RBC preordering on same cases
evidence.effect: Prospective sensitivity 0.72 and PPV 0.34, surpassing both MSBOS and clinician behavior; hybrid model MAE 12.86 vs 13.34 for MSBOS on daily RBC needs.
evidence.quote: Prospectively, the model's sensitivity was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.67 to 0.75) and its positive predictive value was 0.34 (95% CI, 0.31 to 0.37), surpassing both MSBOS and clinician behavior.

evidence.title: Expanding access to vascular care using BlueDop Vascular Expert: an artificial intelligence-driven diagnostic tool
evidence.outcome: BVE versus ABI diagnostic performance for PAD against duplex reference standard
evidence.effect: Combined 751 limbs: BVE sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 93.9%, accuracy 91.2%, κ=0.76 versus ABI sensitivity 58.3%, specificity 87.4%, accuracy 80.6%, κ=0.46.
evidence.quote: In contrast, ABI sensitivity was 58.3%, specificity was 87.4%, accuracy was 80.6%, and κ=0.46.

evidence.title: Closing the Loop: A Custom Artificial Intelligence Agent to Improve Detection of Radiologist Follow-Up Recommendations
evidence.venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
evidence.outcome: AI agent detection of follow-up recommendations compared with existing macro-based system
evidence.effect: AI flagged 6.18 times more cases than the existing macro-based system (513 vs. 83 in 10,000 studies).
evidence.quote: The AI agent achieved a balanced accuracy exceeding 97% for identifying radiologist notes requiring follow-up, correctly flagging 6.18 times more cases than the existing macro-based system (513 vs. 83 based on a sample of 10,000 studies).

evidence.title: Innovative AI-based system for precision diagnosis of childhood strabismus incorporating gaze tracking and real-time correction feedback
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus pediatric ophthalmologists and existing AI methods on same data
evidence.effect: AI achieved binary accuracy 96.8% (AUC 0.992) and multi-class accuracy 92.5% (AUC 0.983), with agreement with gold standard κ = 0.931; comparable to specialist evaluation.
evidence.quote: The diagnostic performance was compared against pediatric ophthalmologists and existing AI methods.

evidence.title: Prospective comparison of econometric, machine learning, and foundation models for forecasting emergency department boarding patients
evidence.outcome: Forecast error of candidate models versus two-week moving-average baseline on the same data
evidence.effect: VAR+XGBoost lowest RMSE, reducing forecast error by 16-42% at La Jolla and 5-19% at Hillcrest; VAR alone outperformed baseline at both sites; only 0-3% gain of hybrid over VAR.
evidence.quote: During a four-month validation period, the VAR+XGBoost hybrid achieved the lowest root mean square error-reducing forecast error by 16-42% at La Jolla and 5-19% at Hillcrest-while showing only slight gains over VAR (0-3%).
evidence.sample_unit: daily ED boarding volume forecasts at two EDs

evidence.title: Real-Time Anatomy Recognition During Single-Port Retroperitoneal Surgery: A Prospective Comparison Between AI and Operating Surgeon
evidence.outcome: AI recognition timing versus operating surgeon for key anatomical structures
evidence.effect: Surgeon was first to recognize psoas (86.7%), renal artery (86.7%), kidney (73.3%); AI rarely first (psoas 6.7%, renal vein 13.3%); median Δ-time 12.0-85.0 s, p<0.01 for most structures.
evidence.quote: The surgeon was most frequently the first to recognize anatomical structures, including the psoas muscle (86.7%), renal artery (86.7%), and kidney (73.3%).

evidence.title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
evidence.outcome: LLM Top-1 accuracy compared with specialist panel majority vote on same vertigo histories
evidence.effect: Gemini-2.5-pro and o1 reached 69.6% Top-1 vs specialist majority vote 63.9%; no LLM significantly outperformed specialists (McNemar P>.10 for all models).
evidence.quote: no LLM significantly outperformed the specialist panel majority vote (63.9%, 95% CI 57.3%-70.1%; McNemar test, P>.10 for all models)
evidence.sample_unit: outpatients with vertigo or dizziness (prospective clinical evaluation); 227 histories in history-based evaluation

evidence.title: Augmenting Head and Neck Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Recommendations With Locally Run Large Language Models: Prospective Evaluation of Real-World Implementation
evidence.outcome: LLM recommendations compared with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions on the same cases
evidence.effect: LLMs substantially improved the MDT recommendation in 1/17 cases (6%); first-line regimen matched MDT in 35% (gemma) and 41% (gpt-oss); LLMs cannot replace MDTs.
evidence.quote: In one case, 6% (1/17, 95% CI 0%-29%), the LLM was able to substantially improve the MDT recommendation by underscoring a follow-up examination that had not yet been performed.

evidence.title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
evidence.outcome: sensitivity and specificity compared to humans
evidence.effect: Sensitivity for acute coronary syndrome was 81.7% in the clinical decision support system versus 80.2% observed in humans.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity for ACS was 81.7% (95% CI 77.1% to 85.8%) in CDS versus 80.2% (95% CI 75.4% to 84.4%) observed in humans.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI-assisted surveillance of healthcare-associated infections using a standard European point prevalence study in a regional hospital, the Czech Republic, 2025
evidence.outcome: AI surveillance performance compared against manual standard-of-care PPS on same cohort
evidence.effect: HAIDI and manual PPS each detected 90.3% of combined infections and both missed seven HAI, though different ones; kappa 0.8849.
evidence.quote: The detection proportion against the combined set of infections identified by either method was 90.3% for both manual PPS and HAIDI.

evidence.title: Image-Based Diagnosis of Oral Lesions: Performance of a Vision-Language Model versus Human Clinicians
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus clinicians of varying expertise against histopathology
evidence.effect: Three-class diagnostic accuracy 94.2% for AI-Gemini vs 67.0% to 86.5% for nonsurgeon clinicians; head and neck surgeon highest for precise diagnosis (97.7% vs AI 88.0%).
evidence.quote: Three-class diagnostic accuracy was 94.2% for AI-Gemini and 67.0% to 86.5% for nonsurgeon clinicians.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Artificial Intelligence vs General Practitioners Decision-Making in Same-Day Appointments Triage: A Mixed-Methods Study in UK Primary Care
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI triage urgency scores with GP urgency ratings
evidence.effect: Spearman ρ=0.796; 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69).
evidence.quote: There was a strong correlation between AI and GP urgency ratings (ρ=0.796,  p 0.001), with 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69,  p 0.001).

evidence.title: A mixed-methods evaluation of the implementation of IOTA-ADNEX ultrasound triage in NHS secondary care ovarian diagnostic one-stop clinics
evidence.outcome: Surgery rates under IOTA-ADNEX-guided vs retrospectively calculated RMI-based triage
evidence.effect: 10% (32/334) underwent surgery under general gynaecology and cancer unit team using IOTA-ADNEX at 10% threshold vs 30% (94/334) would have under RMI triage.
evidence.quote: In comparison, 30% (94/334) would have undergone surgery under the same teams if RMI-based triage had been used.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model Integrated with the Clinical Workflow for Inpatient Discharge Date Prediction
evidence.outcome: Model F1-score compared with baseline discharge date estimates
evidence.effect: Model surpassed baseline estimates by up to 35.68% in F1-score.
evidence.quote: The model achieved a performance surpassing baseline estimates by up to 35.68% in the F1-score.

evidence.title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses from Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: A Large Language Model Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o versus fine-tuned Clinical Longformer baseline on PE extraction from impressions, same validation data
evidence.effect: GPT-4o outperformed Clinical Longformer on two metrics: sensitivity 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0; p<0.001) and F1 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; p<0.001) on validation set.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o outperformed the Clinical Longformer in two of the metrics, achieving a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI: [1.0, 1.0]; Wilcoxon test, p < 0.001) and an F1 score of 0.975 (95% CI: [0.9495, 0.9947]; Wilcoxon test, p < 0.001) across the validation dataset.

evidence.title: The Deterioration Risk Index: Developing and Piloting a Machine Learning Algorithm to Reduce Pediatric Inpatient Deterioration
evidence.venue: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and alarms per detected event of new ML model versus existing situational awareness program
evidence.effect: DRI sensitivity 53% vs 22% for existing program (p<0.001); 121 vs 276 alarms per detected event; cardiac cohort 73% vs 18%, malignancy cohort 81% vs 27%.
evidence.quote: The Deterioration Risk Index (DRI) was 2.4 times as sensitive as our existing situational awareness program (sensitivities of 53% and 22%, respectively; p < 0.001) and required 2.3 times fewer alarms per detected event (121 DRI alarms per detected event vs 276 for existing program).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Community-Based Diabetic Retinopathy Telemedicine Screening in Urban China: Cost-effectiveness and Cost-Utility Analyses With Real-world Data
evidence.outcome: Cost-effectiveness of AI grading versus manual grading in DR telemedicine screening
evidence.effect: AI model ICER US $2553.39 per year without blindness; ICUR US $15,216.96 per QALY; AI not cost-effective versus manual grading (costs $3182.50 vs $3265.40).
evidence.quote: The ICER for the AI-assisted model was US $2553.39 per year without blindness, and the ICUR was US $15,216.96 per QALY, which indicated that AI-assisted model was not cost-effective.

evidence.title: Feasibility of a deep-learning based anatomical region labeling tool for Cone-Beam Computed Tomography scans in radiotherapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy of CNN ARL versus simpler SVM baseline on same test data
evidence.effect: ARL achieved 99.2% overall accuracy on the test dataset versus 91.5% for the SVM baseline.
evidence.quote: ARL achieved an overall accuracy of 99.2% on the test dataset, outperforming the SVM (91.5% accuracy).

evidence.title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Using Smartphone-Based Fundus Photography and Deep-Learning Artificial Intelligence in the Yucatan Peninsula: A Field Study
evidence.venue: Journal of diabetes science and technology
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head sensitivity and specificity of two AI DR algorithms on same patients
evidence.effect: In 110 patients, sensitivities of Medios and EyeArt were 99% (93%-100%) and 95% (87%-99%); specificities both 88% (73%-97%).
evidence.quote: In a head-to-head comparison of 110 patients, the sensitivities of Medios and EyeArt were 99% (93%-100%) and 95% (87%-99%).

evidence.title: Real-time artificial intelligence predicts adverse outcomes in acute pancreatitis in the emergency department: Comparison with clinical decision rule
evidence.venue: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
evidence.outcome: AUC of AI model versus BISAP clinical decision rule for sepsis, ICU admission, mortality
evidence.effect: AI model had superior AUC for sepsis (0.961 vs BISAP 0.785), ICU admission (0.973 vs 0.778), and mortality (0.975 vs 0.817).
evidence.quote: Compared to BISAP, the AI model had superior AUC for sepsis (BISAP 0.785), ICU admission (BISAP 0.778), and mortality (BISAP 0.817).

evidence.title: Measuring the performance of computer vision artificial intelligence to interpret images of HIV self-testing results
evidence.outcome: AI sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV versus clients and pharmacy providers against expert panel ground truth
evidence.effect: AI: 100% sensitivity, 100% NPV, 98.8% specificity, 81.5% PPV (seven false positives). Clients/providers: sensitivity 93.2%/97.7%, NPV 99.6%/99.9%, specificity and PPV 100%.
evidence.quote: The AI algorithm demonstrated perfect sensitivity (100%), perfect NPV (100%), and 98.8% specificity, and 81.5% PPV (81.5%) due to seven false-positive results.

evidence.title: Comparison of Endoscopic and Artificial Intelligence Diagnoses for Predicting the Histological Healing of Ulcerative Colitis in a Real-World Clinical Setting
evidence.outcome: AI vs endoscopist Mayo endoscopic score diagnostic performance for histological healing (Geboes score <3.1)
evidence.effect: MES0: sensitivity 79.2%, specificity 90.6%, PPV 97.7%, NPV 46.8%, accuracy 81.2%. AI: sensitivity 74.2%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 98.3%, NPV 42.3%, accuracy 77.5%; comparable overall.
evidence.quote: The AI system performed similarly to MES for the diagnosis of GS < 3.1: sensitivity, 74.2%; specificity: 93.8%; PPV: 98.3%; NPV: 42.3%; and accuracy: 77.5%.
evidence.sample_unit: biopsy sites (52 patients with ulcerative colitis)

evidence.title: Application of artificial intelligence in lung cancer screening: A real-world study in a Chinese physical examination population
evidence.outcome: Malignant nodule and lung cancer detection rate, AI-assisted reading versus manual interpretation
evidence.effect: AI detection of malignant pulmonary nodules 97.2% vs 86.4% manual (p<0.001); lung cancer detection rate 98.9% vs 90.3% (p<0.001); AI had higher screening positive rate.
evidence.quote: Moreover, AI scanning demonstrated a markedly superior detection rate of malignant pulmonary nodules compared with manual scanning (97.2% vs. 86.4%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Using Optimal Feature Selection and Continuous Learning to Implement Efficient Model Arrays for Predicting Daily Clinical Radiology Workload
evidence.outcome: Model accuracy versus simpler models and trivial estimates
evidence.effect: Linear regression model array with three features selected over more complex models; average R2 0.83 (IQR 0.13); significantly outperformed trivial estimates.
evidence.quote: The model array had an average R<sup>2</sup> of 0.83 (IQR 0.13) across the tested radiology divisions; it significantly outperformed trivial estimates and provided an accurate daily prediction pattern.
evidence.sample_unit: days of radiology exam volume data

evidence.title: Pharmacist-led surgical medicines prescription optimization and prediction service improves patient outcomes - a machine learning based study
evidence.outcome: Comparative discrimination of candidate models predicting prescriber acceptance
evidence.effect: Among 11 models, Random Forest achieved AUC = 0.893, compared with LightGBM = 0.797, DT = 0.780, XGBoost = 0.777, and GBM = 0.773.
evidence.quote: Among the 11 ML models, the RF model had the best predictive performance in terms of AUC (AUC = 0.893), followed by the LightGBM model (AUC = 0.797), DT model (AUC = 0.780), XGBoost model (AUC = 0.777), and GBM model (AUC = 0.773) ( Figure 3A ).

evidence.title: Comparison of Initial Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Final Physician Recommendations in AI-Assisted Virtual Urgent Care Visits
evidence.outcome: Quality rating of AI recommendations versus treating physician decisions on same visits
evidence.effect: AI recommendations rated optimal more often (77.1%) than physician decisions (67.1%); quality better for AI in 20.8%, better for physicians in 11.3%, equal in 67.9%.
evidence.quote: Among the 461 weighted visits, AI recommendations were more frequently rated as optimal (77.1% [95% CI, 72.7% to 80.9%]) compared with treating physician decisions (67.1% [CI, 62.9% to 71.1%]).

evidence.title: Assessing the quality of AI-generated and physician-written discharge summaries: evaluation of an EHR-integrated tool in a Dutch academic hospital
evidence.outcome: LLM-generated vs physician-written discharge summary quality scores
evidence.effect: Total scores did not differ (14.00 vs 14.00; p=0.34); LLM lower in completeness, greater in conciseness, similar correctness.

evidence.title: Design and implementation of an end-to-end AI-driven colonoscopy recall workflow at scale
evidence.outcome: F1 for extracting colonoscopy recall recommendations: LLM versus rule-based NLP on same held-out notes
evidence.effect: GPT-4 Turbo F1 0.89 (CI 0.65-0.92) versus rule-based spaCy NLP F1 0.78 (CI 0.58-0.82), N=326 notes; confidence intervals overlap
evidence.quote: Expanded validation on a held-out set demonstrated improved F1 (0.89; CI = [0.65, 0.92], N = 326) relative to a traditional rule-based NLP approach (F1 = 0.78; CI = [0.58, 0.82]).

evidence.title: Development and Implementation of a Machine Learning Model for Prediction of Surgical Case Duration
evidence.venue: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
evidence.outcome: ML case duration accuracy vs existing scheduling, historical averages, and Epic tool
evidence.effect: Baseline MAE 35.3 min (bias -31 min); standardized workflow plus vendor-recommended Epic MAE 20.1 min; ORchestra MAE 19.8 min, bias +1.2 min. Standardization alone approached ML-level accuracy for many procedures.
evidence.quote: Notably, workflow standardization alone approached ML-level accuracy for many procedures, highlighting human-factor variability as a dominant source of error.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-guided clavicle fracture detection on plain radiographs: A retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
evidence.outcome: AI fracture detection accuracy versus experienced orthopedic surgeon on same radiographs
evidence.effect: AI on AP radiographs: accuracy 97.31%, sensitivity 95.83%, specificity 98.89%, kappa 0.95; second-plane performance similarly high and overall comparable to the experienced orthopedic surgeon.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic performance on second-plane radiographs was similarly high and overall comparable to that of the experienced orthopedic surgeon.

evidence.title: Real-world multimetric comparison of four commercial artificial intelligence solutions for intracranial hemorrhage detection
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of four commercial ICH detection AI vendors on same local CT data
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.96-0.99 and sensitivity 0.85-0.92 with no significant pairwise differences; solutions B and D had significantly higher specificity (1.00, 0.99), precision (0.90-0.98) and F1 (0.87-0.94) than others (P<0.05).
evidence.quote: In binary performance, both solutions B and D exhibited significantly higher specificity (1.00 and 0.99), precision (0.90 to 0.98), and F1 score (0.87 to 0.94) than the other solutions (P < 0.05).

evidence.title: AI-ECG Risk Stratification for Atrial Fibrillation: Real-World Performance and Explainability
evidence.outcome: AUC of AI-ECG alone versus models incorporating clinical risk scores on same patients
evidence.effect: AI-ECG alone AUC 0.64-0.69; models with CHADS2/CHA2DS2-VASc reached SVM AUC 1.00, AdaBoost 0.97-0.98, ANN 0.89-0.95; CHA2DS2-VASc was the most influential predictor.
evidence.quote: AI-ECG provides rapid, low-cost AF risk estimation from a single sinus rhythm ECG; however, its predictive performance is modest compared with clinical scores.

evidence.title: AI-based disease severity grading predicts complications in laparoscopic appendectomy
evidence.outcome: AI-derived severity compared with operative-AAST grading for predicting complications
evidence.effect: AI OR 2.76 (95% CI 1.62-4.73); after AAST adjustment OR 1.90 (1.07-3.36); AUC 0.63 vs 0.68; net benefit comparable or higher than AAST.
evidence.quote: AI-derived severity independently predicted complications (OR 2.76, 95% CI 1.62-4.73; p < 0.001), even after adjustment for operative-AAST (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.07-3.36; p = 0.028).

evidence.title: Evaluation of a National Health Service Machine-Learning Model for Hypertension Case-Finding: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Performance of the ML model versus a more interpretable logistic regression model
evidence.effect: The ML model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model, so no gain from added complexity.
evidence.quote: The model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model.

evidence.title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
evidence.outcome: comparative harm potential across systems
evidence.effect: Harm potential was not uniform; clinical AI tools outperformed generalist LLMs; multi-agent teaming improved generalist models.
evidence.quote: Harm potential was not uniform across systems, with clinical AI tools outperforming generalist LLMs, and multi-agent AI teaming further improving performance in generalist models.

evidence.title: Who Fails Where? LLM and Human Error Patterns in Endometriosis Ultrasound Report Extraction
evidence.outcome: LLM extraction accuracy compared with expert human extraction on the same reports
evidence.effect: The 20B model reached mean accuracy of 86.02%, beating smaller models. Error profiles were complementary: the LLM was better on syntactic consistency, humans on semantic and contextual interpretation.
evidence.quote: Crucially, we identified a highly complementary error profile: the LLM excelled at syntactic consistency (e.g., date/numeric formatting) where humans faltered, while human experts provided superior semantic and contextual interpretation.

evidence.title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
evidence.outcome: Comparison of AI diagnostic accuracy against physicians of varying expertise on same cases
evidence.effect: PULSE outperformed residents and junior specialists and matched senior specialists at Top@1 and Top@4.
evidence.quote: PULSE attained expert-competitive accuracy, outperforming residents and junior specialists while matching senior specialist performance at both Top@1 and Top@4 thresholds.

evidence.title: OGA-AID: Clinician-in-the-loop AI Report Drafting Assistant for Multimodal Observational Gait Analysis in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation
evidence.outcome: Error versus multimodal baselines
evidence.effect: OGA-AID outperformed single-pass multimodal baselines with low error; no numeric effect reported.
evidence.quote: Evaluated with expert physiotherapists on real patient data, OGA-AID consistently outperforms single-pass multimodal baselines with low error.

evidence.title: A Multi-Stage Validation Framework for Trustworthy Large-scale Clinical Information Extraction using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: specialty-care engagement prediction
evidence.effect: LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses were more accurate than structured-data baselines (AUC=0.80).
evidence.quote: LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses also predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines (AUC=0.80).

evidence.title: Blinded Multi-Rater Comparative Evaluation of a Large Language Model and Clinician-Authored Responses in CGM-Informed Diabetes Counseling
evidence.outcome: LLM agent vs clinician-authored responses on six quality dimensions rated by blinded clinicians
evidence.effect: CA scored higher than clinicians (mean 4.37 vs 3.58); estimated difference 0.782 points (95% CI 0.692-0.872; P<.001); largest for empathy (1.062) and actionability (0.992).
evidence.quote: The CA received higher quality scores than clinician responses (mean 4.37 vs 3.58), with an estimated mean difference of 0.782 points (95% CI 0.692-0.872; P<.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs for Inpatient Diagnosis: Real-World Performance, Safety, and Cost Across Ten Frontier Models
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and safety scores versus routine ward diagnoses and versus other LLMs on same cases
evidence.effect: All ten LLMs significantly outperformed routine ward diagnoses on average diagnostic and safety scores. LLM performance was tightly clustered (<15% variation) despite large cost differences.
evidence.quote: (ii) All LLMs significantly outperformed routine ward diagnoses on average diagnostic and safety scores.

evidence.title: Agentic clinical reasoning over longitudinal myeloma records: a retrospective evaluation against expert consensus
evidence.outcome: Concordance with expert consensus, agentic system vs simpler RAG and full-context baselines on same data
evidence.effect: Agentic 79.6% concordance vs iterative RAG 75.4% and full-context 75.8% (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007); iterative RAG and full-context did not differ (p = 1.00).
evidence.quote: The agentic system reached 79.6% concordance (95% CI 76.4-82.8), exceeding both baselines (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007).

evidence.title: Resolving the bias-precision paradox with stochastic causal representation learning for personalized medicine
evidence.outcome: AI performance compared against clinicians-in-training and large language models
evidence.effect: The method outperformed clinicians-in-training and large language models in the human-AI evaluation.
evidence.quote: In human-AI evaluation, our method outperforms clinicians-in-training and large language models, and improves clinician accuracy by 14.7% while reducing decision time, enabling interpretable, real-time clinical decision support.

evidence.title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome
evidence.outcome: Comparison of EviOSAHS against alternative prompting pipelines on same cohort and protocol
evidence.effect: EviOSAHS achieved 88.47% accuracy, 94.86% sensitivity, 93.74% F1-score, and 5.14% false-negative rate, outperforming clinical-only prompting, direct multimodal prompting, and naive two-stage pipelines under a unified protocol.
evidence.quote: EviOSAHS achieved 88.47% accuracy, 94.86% sensitivity, 93.74% F1-score, and a 5.14% false-negative rate, outperforming clinical-only prompting, direct multimodal prompting, and naive two-stage pipelines under a unified protocol.

evidence.title: Ten Headache Specialists versus Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Literature Summarization: A Critical Evaluation and Comparison
evidence.outcome: Blinded specialist ratings and preference ranking of RAG LLM summaries versus expert-written summaries
evidence.effect: Expert-written summaries were preferred over LLM summaries, though experts sometimes could not distinguish human from AI-generated summaries. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our study, comparing LLM- and expert-written literature summaries evaluated by headache specialists, showed that expert-written summaries were preferred, although experts sometimes found it challenging to distinguish between human- and AI-generated summaries.
evidence.sample_unit: headache specialist evaluators (each rating summaries for 9 of 10 questions)

evidence.title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance
evidence.outcome: Treatment recommendation and risk stratification versus guidelines and competing models
evidence.effect: HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance versus clinical guidelines (BCLC, CNLC) and competitive models including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro in 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals.
evidence.quote: In a multi-center cohort of 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals in China, HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance in treatment recommendation and risk stratification compared with clinical guidelines and competitive models, including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro.

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
evidence.outcome: Performance versus unassisted manual review
evidence.effect: F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77; kappa = 0.82 vs 0.50; review time reduced by approximately half.
