evidence.effect: Total scores: DUMS 37.96, intervention 39.52, GPT-4 36.35 (all pairwise P<.001); DUMS outperformed GPT-4 on accuracy, safety, comprehensiveness, richness.
evidence.quote: The total evaluation scores showed that the mean values of the DUMS group, intervention group, and GPT-4 group were 37.96 (SD 0.56), 39.52 (SD 0.80), and 36.35 (SD 0.89), respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT and Gemini justify brain CT referrals? A comparative study with human experts and a custom prediction model
evidence.outcome: Agreement (kappa) with human expert iGuide justification of brain CT referrals, chatbots vs custom prediction model
evidence.effect: Chatbots' performance was limited (κ = 0.3), improving for more complete referrals; the custom prediction model reached κ = 0.853 on the same referrals.
evidence.quote: The prediction model outperformed the chatbots in justification analysis (κ = 0.853).

evidence.title: Integrating blockchain technology with artificial intelligence for the diagnosis of tibial plateau fractures
evidence.venue: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus orthopedic and radiology attending physicians on external validation set
evidence.effect: Distributed AI accuracy 0.9636 vs centralized 0.9632 (p>0.05), orthopedic physician 0.9291, radiology attending 0.9175 (p<0.05). AI diagnosis time 4.99 min vs about 25-26 min for physicians.
evidence.quote: In the external validation set, the accuracy reached 0.9636 [95% CI (0.9388, 0.9762)], was slightly higher than that of the centralized YOLOv8n model at 0.9632 [95% CI (0.9387, 0.9755)] (p > 0.05), and exceeded the orthopedic physician at 0.9291 [95% CI (0.9002, 0.9482)] and radiology attending physician at 0.9175 [95% CI (0.8891, 0.9393)], with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Multimodal machine learning to predict surgical site infection with healthcare workload impact assessment
evidence.outcome: Model performance for SSI within 48 h versus clinician triage
evidence.effect: Multimodal model comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]), with excellent performance on external validation.
evidence.quote: The multimodal neural network model to predict confirmed SSI within 48 h remained comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]), with an excellent performance on external validation.

evidence.title: AI-powered prostate cancer detection: a multi-centre, multi-scanner validation study
evidence.outcome: AI compared with MDT-supported radiologists on same data for GG≥2 prostate cancer detection
evidence.effect: Per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (10% margin), AUC 0.91 vs 0.95; sensitivity 95% vs 99%, specificity 67% vs 73%.
evidence.quote: Evaluated per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (considering a 10% performance difference as acceptable), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91 vs. 0.95.

evidence.title: Improving the Real-Time Classification of Disease Severity in Ulcerative Colitis: Artificial Intelligence as the Trigger for a Second Opinion
evidence.outcome: AI accuracy compared with IBD experts and nonexperts on video severity scoring
evidence.effect: The model achieved an accuracy of 82%, with no significant differences between the experts and the AI.
evidence.quote: The model achieved an accuracy of 82%, with no significant differences between the experts and the AI.

evidence.title: GPT-4 as a Clinical Decision Support Tool in Ischemic Stroke Management: Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: 90-day mortality prediction discrimination of GPT-4 versus supervised ML models on same cohort
evidence.effect: GPT-4 AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.8077-0.9739), outperforming PRACTICE (AUC 0.70; log-rank P=.02) and PREMISE (AUC 0.77; P=.07).
evidence.quote: For mortality prediction, GPT-4 accurately identified 10 (77%) out of 13 deaths within its top 25 high-risk predictions (AUC 0.89, 95% CI 0.8077-0.9739; hazard ratio 6.98, 95% CI 2.88-16.9; P<.001), outperforming supervised machine learning models such as PRACTICE (AUC 0.70; log-rank P=.02) and PREMISE (AUC 0.77; P=.07).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT) ready to evaluate ECG in real life? Not yet!
evidence.outcome: ECG interpretation accuracy of ChatGPT-based models compared with cardiologists on same cases
evidence.effect: Cardiologists 92.52% vs GPT-ECGReader 57.94%, GPT-ECGInterpreter 62.62%, GPT-ECGAnalyzer 62.62%; differences statistically significant (p < 0.05), across all difficulty levels.
evidence.quote: Cardiologists demonstrated superior accuracy (92.52%) compared to ChatGPT-based models (GPT-ECGReader: 57.94%, GPT-ECGInterpreter: 62.62%, GPT-ECGAnalyzer: 62.62%).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT 4.0) vs. Human expertise for epileptic seizure and epilepsy diagnosis and classification in Adults: An exploratory study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and agreement of ChatGPT versus epileptologists and neurologists on same vignettes
evidence.effect: Human experts consistently outperformed ChatGPT with near-perfect accuracy and higher kappa; ChatGPT specificity was low (26.7% for epilepsy diagnosis, 33.3% for acute symptomatic vs unprovoked seizures).
evidence.quote: Human experts consistently outperformed ChatGPT with near-perfect accuracy and higher κ values.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Pediatric Differential Diagnoses in Rural Health Care: Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study Comparing GPT-3 With Pediatrician Performance
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of fine-tuned GPT-3 versus board-certified pediatricians on same encounters
evidence.effect: GPT-3 accuracy 87.3% (131/150) vs pediatricians 91.3% (137/150); P=.47, comparable. Rare diagnoses 80% (16/20) vs 85% (17/20); P=.62.
evidence.quote: The GPT-3 model achieved an accuracy of 87.3% (131/150 cases), sensitivity of 85% (95% CI 82%-88%), and specificity of 90% (95% CI 87%-93%), comparable to pediatricians' accuracy of 91.3% (137/150 cases; P=.47).

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Virtual Assistant for the Diagnostic Approach of Chronic Ataxias
evidence.venue: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI assistant versus neurologists and GPT-4 on same cases
evidence.effect: Virtual assistant accuracy 90.9% vs neurologists 18.3% and GPT-4 19.4%.
evidence.quote: The virtual assistant accuracy was 90.9%, higher than neurologists (18.3%), and GPT-4 (19.4%).

evidence.title: AI-guided precision parenteral nutrition for neonatal intensive care units
evidence.outcome: Physician blinded ratings of AI TPN recommendations versus current best-practice prescriptions
evidence.effect: Physicians rated TPN2.0 higher than current best practice in a blinded study (n = 192); Pearson's R = 0.94 versus experts.
evidence.quote: A blinded study (n = 192) revealed that physicians rated TPN2.0 higher than current best practice.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (79,790 TPN orders, Stanford training cohort)

evidence.title: Can a Large Language Model Interpret Data in the Electronic Health Record to Infer Minimum Clinically Important Difference Achievement of Knee Osteoarthritis Outcome Score-Joint Replacement Score Following Total Knee Arthroplasty?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT versus blinded orthopaedic surgeon in classifying MCID achievement
evidence.effect: ChatGPT had 97% sensitivity, 33% specificity, 65% accuracy; the surgeon had 90% sensitivity, 63% specificity, 76% accuracy.
evidence.quote: The surgeon's assessment had 90% sensitivity and 63% specificity.

evidence.title: Breaking Bones, Breaking Barriers: ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini in Hand Fracture Management
evidence.outcome: LLM management recommendations versus experienced surgeon decisions across three models (accuracy, precision, recall)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o accuracy 98.28%, recall 91.74%, precision 58.48%; DeepSeek-V3 accuracy 63.79%; Gemini 1.5 accuracy 18.97%, showing wide variation between candidate models.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated the highest accuracy (98.28%) and recall (91.74%), effectively identifying most correct interventions but occasionally proposing extraneous options (precision 58.48%).

evidence.title: Using large language models as decision support tools in emergency ophthalmology
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnosis and treatment plan quality versus ophthalmologists on same cases, Likert 1-4
evidence.effect: Human experts mean 3.72 (SD 0.50); GPT-4 3.52 (0.64); Llama-3-70b 3.48 (0.48); GPT-4o 3.20 (0.81). Only GPT-4o differed significantly from humans; GPT-4 and Llama-3-70b comparable.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 and Llama-3-70b showed performance comparable to ophthalmologists, with no statistically significant differences.

evidence.title: Accuracy of Large Language Model-based Automatic Calculation of Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System MRI Scores from Pelvic MRI Reports
evidence.outcome: O-RADS MRI score accuracy of AI strategies versus original reporting radiologists on the same lesions
evidence.effect: Hybrid model accuracy exceeded reporting radiologists (97% [153/158] vs 88% [139/158]; P = .004); hybrid also outperformed LLM-only (97% vs 90%; P = .006).
evidence.quote: For lesions with an originally reported O-RADS score, hybrid model accuracy exceeded that of reporting radiologists (97% [153 of 158] vs 88% [139 of 158]; P = .004).

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Commercial AI-based Platform in Evaluating Endodontic Treatment Outcomes on Periapical Radiographs Using CBCT as the Reference Standard
evidence.outcome: AI platform vs experienced endodontists on sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, AUC against CBCT reference standard
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity higher (67.3% vs 49.3% tooth) but specificity lower (82.3% vs 92.5%); accuracy comparable at tooth level (76.3% vs 75.3%), lower at root level (78.5% vs 81.6%); AUC 0.75 vs 0.71.
evidence.quote: The AI-driven platform demonstrated higher sensitivity but lower specificity than clinicians at both tooth (sensitivity: 67.3% vs 49.3%, P < .001; specificity: 82.3% vs 92.5%, P < .001) and root levels (sensitivity: 54.3% vs 43.8%, P = .003; specificity: 86.7% vs 94.5%, P < .001).

evidence.title: Automated computation of the HEART score with the GPT-4 large language model
evidence.venue: The American journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM-computed HEART score versus APP-computed score, each compared with blinded physician adjudication
evidence.effect: Weighted kappa with adjudicators was 0.67 for the LLM and 0.66 for the APP. The LLM's mean HEART score was higher (5.06 vs 4.69 adjudicators, 4.23 APP). No significant difference in 60-day MACE prediction (all p > .05).
evidence.quote: Among the remaining 551 participants, agreement by Cohen's weighted kappa between the LLM and adjudicators was 0.67 which was similar to the agreement of 0.66 between the APP and adjudicators.

evidence.title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
evidence.outcome: Compare LLM-RAG accuracy against clinicians on same scenarios for surgical fitness
evidence.effect: GPT4_international outperformed human evaluators (96.4% vs 86.6%, OR 4.84, p=0.016); false negative rate 25% vs 62.5% for humans.
evidence.quote: The GPT4_international model performed better than humans in evaluations of patient’s fitness for surgery (Odds Ratio (OR) = 4.84, p = 0.016).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical scenarios (3234 LLM responses vs 448 human responses)

evidence.title: [Making prostate cancer research accessible: chatGPT-4 as a tool to enhance lay communication]
evidence.outcome: comparison with original lay summaries
evidence.effect: Content quality was higher than original summaries: p=0.001 and p=0.002.
evidence.quote: Content quality was comparable between the two ChatGPT‑4 prompts (p = 0.665) but was higher than that of the original summaries (p = 0.001 and p = 0.002, respectively).

evidence.title: Cross-institutional validation of a polar map-free 3D deep learning model for obstructive coronary artery disease prediction using myocardial perfusion imaging: insights into generalizability and bias
evidence.venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
evidence.outcome: AI model compared with conventional stress TPD on same data
evidence.effect: The DL model outperformed stress TPD in both internal and external cohorts (all p < 0.001), despite lower external performance.
evidence.quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

evidence.title: The Role of ChatGPT in osteoporosis management: a comparative analysis with clinical expertise
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic and treatment recommendation accuracy and response time versus five physiatrists on same scenarios
evidence.effect: 91% of ChatGPT responses entirely accurate; 8% incomplete; mean answer time 2.3 ± 0.76 min for ChatGPT versus 5.4 ± 2.45 min for clinicians (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT exhibited a high degree of diagnostic accuracy, with 91% of responses being entirely accurate.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-large language models (AI-LLMs) for reliable and accurate cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation in obstetric practice
evidence.outcome: AI-LLM CTG interpretation quality scores compared with junior and senior doctors on same images
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o 77.86 vs SHDs 80.43 (p>0.05) and JHDs 61.57; Gemini Advanced 57.14 and Copilot 47.29 scored below JHDs.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o scored 77.86, outperforming the Gemini Advanced (57.14), Copilot (47.29), and JHDs (61.57).
evidence.sample_unit: CTG images interpreted by each of 3 AI-LLMs, 5 senior doctors and 5 junior doctors, scored by 5 blinded experts

evidence.title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: LLM versus medical students on criteria filtering and deprescribing recommendation, adjudicated
evidence.effect: LLM better at criteria filtering (80.1% vs 59.5% correct, P=.02) but worse, not significantly, at applying criteria (P=.178).
evidence.quote: However, in applying relevant criteria, GPT-4o performed worse than the medical students, though the difference was not statistically significant (McNemar test: χ 2 1 =1.818; P =.178).

evidence.title: Deep learning-based classification of lymphedema and other lower limb edema diseases using clinical images
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus human evaluators on lower limb edema images
evidence.effect: EfficientNetV2 achieved the highest accuracy of 78.6%; human evaluators' diagnostic accuracy plateaued at 62.7%.
evidence.quote: The AI system consistently outperformed human evaluators, whose diagnostic accuracy plateaued at 62.7%.

evidence.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Clinical Infectious Disease Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Analysis Among Specialists and Resident Trainees
evidence.outcome: Comparative performance of candidate LLM chatbots on the same clinical scenarios
evidence.effect: GPT-4.0 had higher composite scores than Gemini Pro (p = 0.001) and Claude 2 (p = 0.006), and was better on factual consistency, comprehensiveness, and absence of harm.
evidence.quote: Analysis showed that GPT-4.0 achieved significantly higher composite scores compared to Gemini Pro (p = 0.001) and Claude 2 (p = 0.006).

evidence.title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
evidence.outcome: AI model diagnostic performance compared with clinicians on the same Holter data
evidence.effect: Clinicians alone overlooked 13.7% of PAF patients but identified all non-AF patients; AI rarely missed PAF but misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as PAF.
evidence.quote: Conversely, AI alone rarely missed PAF patients but misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as having PAF.

evidence.title: Prospective multicenter external validation of the rib fracture frailty index
evidence.venue: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
evidence.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of RFF Index versus age for composite outcome in rib fracture patients
evidence.effect: RFF had higher discrimination (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.08-0.11 vs OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.04-0.08; p=0.04) and better calibration than age, though only in lower injury burden patients.
evidence.quote: The RFF score had higher discrimination (OR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.08-0.11 vs. OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.04-0.08; p = 0.04) and calibration performance compared with age, but on secondary analysis, higher predictive performance was limited to patients with lower injury burden.

evidence.title: Temporal validation of machine learning models for pre-eclampsia prediction using routinely collected maternal characteristics: A validation study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of ML models versus logistic regression for pre-eclampsia prediction
evidence.effect: XGBoost AUC 0.75 (0.73-0.78) and logistic regression 0.76 (0.74-0.78); random forest 0.71 (0.69-0.74); neither ML model outperformed logistic regression.
evidence.quote: During temporal validation of PE prediction models, logistic regression and XGBoost models exhibited stable prediction performance; however, both ML models did not outperform the logistic regression model.

evidence.title: Comparison of Deep Learning and Clinician Performance for Detecting Referable Glaucoma from Fundus Photographs in a Safety Net Population
evidence.outcome: DL algorithm AUROC/sensitivity/specificity versus 13 clinician graders on same test set
evidence.effect: Algorithm matched or exceeded all independent clinician graders (AUROC 0.92 with optometrist labels, 0.93 with expert panel labels); clinician sensitivity ranged 0.33-0.99, specificity 0.68-0.98.
evidence.quote: Algorithm performance matched or exceeded that of all independent clinician graders in detecting patient-level referable glaucoma based on LAC DHS optometrist (AUROC = 0.92) or expert panel (AUROC = 0.93) reference labels.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence for Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Comparison of Utilization Scenarios
evidence.outcome: performance versus no AI
evidence.effect: Only prescreener had higher net benefit than no AI; assistant had least net benefit. Prescreener sensitivity 62.9% vs 64.2%, time 143 vs 164 seconds.
evidence.quote: Among scenarios, only AI as a prescreener demonstrated higher net benefit than interpretation without AI; AI as an assistant had the least net benefit.

evidence.title: Evaluation of error detection and treatment recommendations in nucleic acid test reports using ChatGPT models
evidence.outcome: GPT error detection agreement and speed compared with senior scientists and interns
evidence.effect: GPT models agreed substantially to almost perfectly with SMLS (kappa 0.778-0.837), moderately lower with MLI (0.632-0.696), and read reports faster than both (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: GPT models exhibited substantial to almost perfect agreement with SMLS in detecting total errors (kappa [min, max]: 0.778, 0.837).
evidence.sample_unit: nucleic acid test reports (with 285 introduced errors)

evidence.title: Myo-Guide: A Machine Learning-Based Web Application for Neuromuscular Disease Diagnosis With MRI
evidence.venue: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
evidence.outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy of model versus four expert clinicians on 14 unseen MRI scans
evidence.effect: Model obtained the highest top-3 accuracy (75.0% ± 4.8%) compared to four expert clinicians.
evidence.quote: Compared to four expert clinicians, the model obtained the highest top-3 accuracy (75.0% ± 4.8%).

evidence.title: Comparison of CT referral justification using clinical decision support and large language models in a large European cohort
evidence.outcome: CT referral test justification accuracy of LLMs vs independent experts vs ESR iGuide reference
evidence.effect: Independent experts achieved highest accuracy (92.4%) for medical test justification, surpassing GPT-4 (88.8%) and Claude-3 Haiku (85.2%).
evidence.quote: Independent experts achieved the highest accuracy (92.4%) for medical test justification, surpassing GPT-4 (88.8%) and Claude-3 Haiku (85.2%).

evidence.title: Specialized Large Language Model Outperforms Neurologists at Complex Diagnosis in Blinded Case-Based Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Normalized diagnostic score of AI versus neurologists on same cases
evidence.effect: AI achieved a significantly higher normalized score (86.17%) compared to neurologists (55.11%, p < 0.001). Differential diagnosis: 85% vs 46.15%; final diagnosis: 88.24% vs 70.93%.
evidence.quote: AI achieved a significantly higher normalized score (86.17%) compared to neurologists (55.11%, p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: neurologists (plus the AI system) evaluated on 5 clinical scenarios

evidence.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease
evidence.outcome: Compared LLM-generated patient education materials against a physician-written PEM on expert and patient ratings
evidence.effect: ERNIE Bot 4.0 non-guideline PEM performed on par with physician PEM for patient comprehensibility, completeness, safety; 60% (30/50) of patients rated it as good or better than the physician's.
evidence.quote: We found that ERNIE Bot 4.0 performed on par with physicians in terms of patient comprehensibility, completeness, and safety.

evidence.title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and a Paediatric Intensive Care Specialist in Responding to Medical Education Questions: A Multicenter Evaluation
evidence.venue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
evidence.outcome: Blinded expert preference between ChatGPT-4 and PICU specialist answers to same questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p<0.001); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p<0.0001); integration of both favoured in 37%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 was preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p < 0.001), while the PICU specialist's responses were preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Predicting onward care needs at admission to reduce discharge delay using explainable machine learning
evidence.outcome: ML model discrimination compared with clinician predictions of discharge care needs
evidence.effect: ML one-vs-rest AUROC 0.915 [0.907 0.924], comparable to clinicians' predictions; each better for different care need types.
evidence.quote: The model performance (one-vs-rest AUROC = 0.915 [0.907 0.924] (95% confidence interval), is comparable to clinician's predictions of discharge care needs, despite working with only a subset of the information available to the clinician.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Diagnosing Focal Liver Lesions From CT/MRI Reports: A Comparative Study With Radiologists
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy compared with radiologists and real-world radiology reports on the same cases
evidence.effect: Two-step ChatGPT-4o 78.9% matched reports (80.0%) and junior radiologists (78.9%-82.0%) but was below middle-level radiologists (84.6%-85.5%).
evidence.quote: Regarding the final diagnosis, the accuracy of two-step ChatGPT-4o (78.9%) was higher than single-step ChatGPT-4o (68.0%, p < 0.001) and single-step Gemini (73.2%, p = 0.004), similar to real-world radiology reports (80.0%, p = 0.34) and junior radiologists (78.9%-82.0%; p-values, 0.21 to > 0.99), but lower than middle-level radiologists (84.6%-85.5%; p-values, 0.001 to 0.02).

evidence.title: Advancing emergency upper extremity care: A pilot study of ChatGPT's potential role in diagnosing and managing hand and wrist trauma
evidence.outcome: Blinded attending scores of ChatGPT versus plastic surgery residents on hand trauma vignettes
evidence.effect: ChatGPT had higher total average scores (mean = 26.6 vs. 22.7, p < 0.05) and ER management scores (9.9 vs. 6.7, p < 0.05); no notable differences in diagnosis or definitive treatment scores.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT had significantly higher total average scores (mean = 26.6 vs. 22.7, p < 0.05) and ER management scores (mean = 9.9 vs. 6.7, p < 0.05) when compared to residents.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical vignettes (16 ChatGPT and 16 resident responses per scenario)

evidence.title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
evidence.outcome: AI versus pathologist concordance
evidence.effect: At CPS ≥5, AI-pathologist κ=0.46 (95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) vs pathologist-pathologist κ=0.39 (95% CI, 0.29, 0.48); p < 0.05.
evidence.quote: At a PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 cut-off, the concordance between PD-L1 AI scores and pathologists’ manual scores was higher (Cohen’s κ = 0.46; 95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) than the average concordance among pathologists’ manual scores (Cohen’s κ = 0.39; 95% CI, 0.29, 0.48) with statistical significance ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) as well as higher than for the original IHC foundation model ( p < 0.001, Bootstrapping).
evidence.sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-based echocardiography assessment to detect pulmonary hypertension
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for PH of AI-derived versus manual TRJV measurements on same echocardiograms
evidence.effect: AUC 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.90) for automated versus 0.88 (95% CI 0.86-0.91) for manual; noninferior. ICC 0.94 (95% CI 0.94-0.95); TRJV measured in 87% of echocardiograms.
evidence.quote: Automated TRJV measurements showed equally high diagnostic accuracy for PH as manual measurements (area under the curve 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.90 versus 0.88, 95% CI 0.86-0.91).

evidence.title: Evaluating large language and large reasoning models as decision support tools in emergency internal medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM final clinical rating compared with human physician reports on same cases
evidence.effect: o1 mean final rating 3.63 vs human physicians 3.67 (p = 0.62); Claude-3.5-Sonnet 3.38 and Llama-3.2-70B 3.23 scored significantly lower (p < 0.01 vs. o1).
evidence.quote: The o1 model achieved a mean final rating (3.63) statistically indistinguishable from human physicians (3.67; p = 0.62).

evidence.title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
evidence.outcome: LLM-generated vs clinician-written notes: hallucinations and omissions on same transcripts
evidence.effect: Clinician-written notes had slightly more hallucinations but fewer omissions than LLM notes (Experiment 17); LLM best configurations had fewer errors per note than reported human rates.
evidence.quote: Interestingly, findings suggested slightly more hallucinations in clinician-written notes but fewer omissions, highlighting key differences in human vs. LLM-generated note content.

evidence.title: A Comparison of Skin Lesions' Diagnoses Between AI-Based Image Classification, an Expert Dermatologist, and a Non-Expert
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus expert dermatologist and non-expert on same images
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 93.59% and specificity 70.42% for malignant lesions; similar sensitivity and notably higher specificity than expert dermatologist and non-expert.
evidence.quote: The AI model demonstrated similar sensitivity and notably higher specificity compared to the expert dermatologist and non-expert.

evidence.title: Summarizing clinical evidence utilizing large language models for cancer treatments: a blinded comparative analysis
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of four LLMs on the same synopsis task across quality domains
evidence.effect: Claude outperformed others (accuracy 3.92 vs ChatGPT 3.25, Gemini 3.17, Llama 1.92); Llama performed considerably poorer across all domains.
evidence.quote: Llama performed considerably poorer across all the studied domains.

evidence.title: Comparative performance of large language models in structuring head CT radiology reports: multi-institutional validation study in Japan
evidence.outcome: Accuracy comparison of three LLMs across three prompt strategies on same reports
evidence.effect: Claude significantly higher accuracy than GPT and Gemini for intracranial hemorrhage (p<0.0001); Gemini significantly lower than Claude and GPT for skull fracture (p<0.0001); Claude accuracy 0.98-0.99.
evidence.quote: In many comparisons, Claude demonstrated significantly higher accuracy than both GPT and Gemini ( p < 0.0001), while no statistically significant difference was observed between GPT and Gemini.
evidence.sample_unit: head CT radiology reports (one per patient)

evidence.title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
evidence.outcome: MEWS scoring accuracy of GPT-4 models compared with nurses' manual calculation
evidence.effect: GPT-4o accuracy after prompt engineering was 96.20% vs 81.8% for nurses' manual calculation from a previous study; GPT-4-Turbo reached 100%.
evidence.quote: This is particularly notable when compared to the finding of a previous study, which indicated that the overall accuracy rate of nurses’ manual calculations was 81.8% [ 20 ].
evidence.sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

evidence.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for providing sexual health information: a consensus study using real-world clinical queries
evidence.outcome: side-by-side candidate correctness
evidence.effect: Overall correctness differed: Alice 85.2%, Azure 69.3%, ChatGPT 64.8%; p < 0.0001.
evidence.quote: Alice demonstrated the highest overall correctness at 85.2% (95% CI, 82.1-88.0%), followed by Azure at 69.3% (95% CI, 65.3-73.0%), and ChatGPT at 64.8% (95% CI, 60.7-68.7%).

evidence.title: Feasibility study of automatic radiotherapy treatment planning for cervical cancer using a large language model
evidence.outcome: LLM-generated VMAT plan quality and planning time versus manual physicist plans
evidence.effect: Qwen-2.5-max and Llama-3.2 plans took 16.3±5.0 and 9.8±2.1 min vs ~20 min manual; CI 0.929, 0.928 vs 0.926 manual; HI 0.058, 0.059 vs 0.065; OAR sparing not significantly different.
evidence.quote: The average conformity index (CI) for Qwen-2.5-max plans, Llama-3.2 plans, and manual plans on the test set were 0.929 ± 0.007, 0.928 ± 0.007, and 0.926 ± 0.007, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: cervical cancer patients (5 for prompt tailoring, 30 for testing)

evidence.title: Performance of the Large Language Models in African rheumatology: a diagnostic test accuracy study of ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Comparison of four candidate LLMs' diagnostic accuracy on same patient data against expert diagnoses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 86.41%, Claude AI 85.44%, Copilot 75.73%, Gemini 71.84%; inter-model kappa 0.43 to 0.59. Compared against each other, not against clinicians.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (86.41%), followed by Claude AI (85.44%), Copilot (75.73%), and Gemini (71.84%).

evidence.title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
evidence.outcome: questionnaire assessment scores
evidence.effect: Comparing AI to human translation revealed ChatGPT-4 scored significantly lower on readability, understandability, and appropriate language before face validation.
evidence.quote: Before face validation, the human-translated version of the questionnaire was rated at least one point higher on the parameters of readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire

evidence.title: Large language model evaluation in autoimmune disease clinical questions comparing ChatGPT 4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Gemini 1.5 pro
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy on report interpretation questions versus junior and senior doctors
evidence.effect: The performance of the three LLMs in the evaluation of autoimmune diseases significantly surpassed that of both junior and senior doctors on report interpretation accuracy.
evidence.quote: The results showed that the performance of the three LLMs in the evaluation of autoimmune diseases significantly surpassed that of both junior and senior doctors.

evidence.title: The effect of selection bias on the performance of a deep learning-based intraoperative hypotension prediction model using real-world samples from a publicly available database
evidence.outcome: Performance of DL model versus simpler MAP-only model on same data
evidence.effect: The DL model statistically outperformed the MAP-only model, but the difference was not clinically meaningful.
evidence.quote: Although the DL model statistically performed better than the MAP-only model, the difference between the two models was not clinically meaningful.

evidence.title: Enhancing responses from large language models with role-playing prompts: a comparative study on answering frequently asked questions about total knee arthroplasty
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Comparison of four candidate LLMs on the same questions rated by surgeons
evidence.effect: GPT-4 zero-shot had higher accuracy and comprehensiveness than Gemini (P=0.031, 0.009) and Claude 3 Opus (P=0.019, 0.002), and higher acceptability than Claude (P=0.006).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated significantly higher accuracy and comprehensiveness scores compared to both Google Gemini ( P = 0.031 and P = 0.009, respectively) and Claude 3 Opus ( P = 0.019 and P = 0.002, respectively).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (10 questions x 4 models x 2 prompt types)

evidence.title: External validation of cardiovascular risk scores in patients with Type 2 diabetes using the Spanish population-based CARDIANA cohort
evidence.outcome: Comparative discrimination and calibration of 18 candidate risk scores on the same local cohort
evidence.effect: Discrimination was moderate for all models. Diabetes-specific models and general-population models with HbA1c performed better; DIAL2, DIAL2-extended, SCORE2-diabetes, and ADVANCE had optimal calibration without recalibration.
evidence.quote: In our context, models derived for or adapted to diabetes patients, as well as models derived in the general population but incorporating diabetes-related metabolic measures (such as Hb1Ac) as predictors, demonstrated better performance than the others.

evidence.title: Dedicated AI Expert System vs Generative AI With Large Language Model for Clinical Diagnoses
evidence.outcome: Case diagnosis present in differential: LLMs vs traditional DDSS on same cases
evidence.effect: Without labs, DDSS 56% (20/36) vs LLM1 42% (15/36) and LLM2 39% (14/36), not significant (P=.09, P=.08). With labs, DDSS 72%, LLM1 64%, LLM2 58%.
evidence.quote: In the version with all findings but no laboratory test results, the DDSS listed the case diagnosis in its differential diagnosis more often (56% [20 of 36]) than LLM1 (42% [15 of 36]) and LLM2 (39% [14 of 36]), although this difference did not reach statistical significance (DDSS vs LLMI, P = .09; DDSS vs LLM2, P = .08).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o vs Psychiatrists in Responding to Common Antidepressant Concerns
evidence.venue: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-4o versus psychiatrists on accuracy, conciseness, readability, clarity for antidepressant questions
evidence.effect: Accuracy comparable (P = .0645); ChatGPT more concise (P = .0019); readability not different (P = .0892); psychiatrists clearer (P = .0059).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o showed comparable accuracy to psychiatrists (P = .0645) but was significantly more concise (P = .0019).
evidence.sample_unit: psychiatrists (responses compared with ChatGPT-4o answers to standardized antidepressant questions)

evidence.title: Harnessing GPT-4 for automated error detection in pathology reports: Implications for oncology diagnostics
evidence.outcome: Error detection rate, false positives, and processing time of GPT-4 versus six pathologists on the same reports
evidence.effect: GPT-4 detected 88% of errors (350/400) vs 95% (382/400) for the top senior pathologist; 4.03 s vs 65.64 s per report; false positives 2.3% vs 0.3%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 detected 88% of errors (350/400; 95% CI: [84, 91]), compared to a 95% detection rate by the top senior pathologist (382/400; 95% CI: [93, 97]).

evidence.title: Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Gatekeeping in Referrals to Specialized Care
evidence.outcome: AI model accuracy, sensitivity, specificity versus human gatekeepers against physician consensus standard
evidence.effect: AI had higher accuracy and specificity and lower sensitivity than current human gatekeeper approach; AI accuracy 0.716, sensitivity 0.542, specificity 0.801.
evidence.quote: When compared against the consensus standard, the AI model had higher accuracy and specificity and lower sensitivity than the current approach.

evidence.title: Nomograms versus artificial intelligence platforms: which one can better predict sentinel node positivity in melanoma patients?
evidence.outcome: Comparison of nomograms versus public AI platforms for predicting sentinel node positivity on same patients
evidence.effect: Only MSKCC nomogram (P=0.04) and ChatGPT (P=0.02) differed between positive and negative SNB; ChatGPT AUC 0.702, adding MSKCC gave 0.715. No concordance among nomograms or among AI platforms (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Only ChatGPT score was statistically significant for SNB positivity after univariate logistic regression (odds ratio: 1.05; 95% confidence interval: 1.004-1.108; P = 0.03).
evidence.sample_unit: melanoma patients who underwent sentinel node biopsy

evidence.title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 PEMs versus original PEMs
evidence.effect: GPT-4 PEMs had FKRE 70.8 vs 43.5 for originals (p < .001) and correctness trifecta 81/160 vs 92/160 (p = .217).
evidence.quote: The readability scores for original PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 43.5 (10.8)] were lower than for GPT-4 generated PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 70.8 (4.9), p < .001].
evidence.sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
evidence.country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

evidence.title: Mortality Prediction Performance Under Geographical, Temporal, and COVID-19 Pandemic Dataset Shift: External Validation of the Global Open-Source Severity of Illness Score Model
evidence.outcome: Comparison of GOSSIS-1 with APACHE-II, APACHE-III, and JROD on same data
evidence.effect: GOSSIS-1 calibration SMR 0.89 significantly better than APACHE-II (0.39) and APACHE-III (0.46), close to JROD (0.97); AUC comparable to APACHE-III and JROD.
evidence.quote: It also exhibited superior calibration, achieving a standardized mortality ratio (SMR) of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.88-0.90), significantly outperforming APACHE-II (SMR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.39-0.40) and APACHE-III (SMR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.46-0.47), and demonstrating a performance close to that of JROD (SMR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence vs human expertise: A comparison of plantar fascia thickness measurements through MRI imaging
evidence.outcome: Plantar fascia thickness measurement reliability of ChatGPT-4 versus experienced clinician on same MRI data
evidence.effect: Clinician ICC 0.983-0.989 vs ChatGPT-4 ICC 0.391-0.432; ChatGPT-4 mean 6.47 mm vs clinician 4.20 mm; thin fascia MAE 2.70 mm, MRE 77.17% (blinded).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated lower reliability in plantar fascia thickness measurements compared to an experienced clinician, with increased error rates in thin structures.

evidence.title: A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology
evidence.outcome: AI performance compared with clinicians on early-stage melanoma detection
evidence.effect: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis.
evidence.quote: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis, improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and enhanced nondermatologist healthcare providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 skin conditions on clinical photographs.
evidence.country: multiple (11 clinical institutions, not specified in text)

evidence.title: External validation of an AI-based preoperative frailty index using real-world data
evidence.venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of general vs service-specific frailty indices
evidence.effect: General frailty index performed comparably to or slightly better than service-specific indices across surgical specialties.
evidence.quote: The general frailty index performed comparably to or slightly better than service-specific indices across surgical specialties.

evidence.title: AI-Powered Drug Classification and Indication Mapping for Pharmacoepidemiologic Studies: Prompt Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: Acceptable ATC classification of GPT-4o vs search-based algorithm on same sample
evidence.effect: GPT-4o at least mostly correct 92.5% (185/200, 80% CI 90.1%-94.9%); search-based algorithm 82.5% (165/200) acceptable.
evidence.quote: For the search-based algorithm, 82.5% (165/200) were deemed acceptable.

evidence.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM diagnostic accuracy against physicians on the same vignettes
evidence.effect: Four of five LLMs outperformed the average physician; the all-LLM ensemble strictly outperformed 85% of physicians and outperformed or tied with 93%.
evidence.quote: This percentage was highest for an LLM ensemble incorporating all five LLMs (i.e., strictly outperformed 85% of physicians and outperformed or tied with 93% of physicians).
evidence.sample_unit: text-based medical case vignettes (40,762 physician differential diagnoses)

evidence.title: AI automated radiographic scoring in rheumatoid arthritis: Shedding light on barriers to implementation through comprehensive evaluation
evidence.outcome: AI compared against manual scorers on the same radiographs
evidence.effect: AI agreement with consensus was lower than between the two manual scorers; ICC 0.03 to 0.27.
evidence.quote: Our AI system underperformed compared to manual scoring, with lower agreement between the AI and consensus score than between the two manual scorers.

evidence.title: Whole-lesion-aware network based on freehand ultrasound video for breast cancer assessment: a prospective multicenter study
evidence.venue: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with radiologists and alternative models on same data
evidence.effect: WAUVE outperformed 2D-ResNet50, was similar to TimeSformer, and was comparable to four radiologists (sensitivity 97.39% vs 98.48%, specificity 49.33% vs 50.00%, accuracy 78.42% vs 79.34%).
evidence.quote: The WAUVE demonstrated superior performance compared to the 2D-ResNet50 model, while similar to the TimeSformer model.

evidence.title: Agent-guided AI-powered interpretation and reporting of nerve conduction studies and EMG (INSPIRE)
evidence.venue: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy detecting normal versus abnormal EDX tests, multi-agent INSPIRE versus one-shot Base-LLM
evidence.effect: INSPIRE accuracy 92.2% vs Base-LLM 62.6% (p < 0.001); INSPIRE also higher AIGERS scores in finding, clinical diagnosis, semantic concordance (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: INSPIRE achieved an accuracy of 92.2 % for detecting normal versus abnormal tests, significantly outperforming the Base-LLM model, which achieved 62.6 % (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Feasibility of Using ChatGPT to Generate Exposure Hierarchies for Treating Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
evidence.outcome: Expert-blinded ratings of ChatGPT vs expert clinician OCD exposure hierarchies
evidence.effect: Expert hierarchies rated significantly more appropriate, specific, variable, and useful than ChatGPT (ps < .05); safety/ethics not different (p = .24).
evidence.quote: However, expert human-generated hierarchies were still rated as significantly more appropriate, specific, variable, and useful, ps < .05, but not more or less safe and ethical than ChatGPT-generated hierarchies, p = .24.

evidence.title: Clinical feasibility of AI Doctors: Evaluating the replacement potential of large language models in outpatient settings for central nervous system tumors
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy versus neurosurgeons on differential diagnosis, main diagnosis, and treatment advice
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 >90% differential diagnosis accuracy, no significant difference from doctors; Doubao worse (P=0.01-0.02). Treatment accuracy 71.3-80.5%, significantly lower than doctors (P<0.05).
evidence.quote: For treatment recommendations, all models showed reduced accuracy (ChatGPT-4o: 80.5 %; DeepSeek-R1: 79 %; Doubao: 71.3 %), significantly lower than doctors (Whether in Chinese or English: P < 0.05).

evidence.title: A 3-Dimensional-Optimized Artificial Imaging Model for the Skin Tumor Burden Assessment of Mycosis Fungoides
evidence.outcome: mSWAT score agreement (ICC) of AI versus junior dermatologists on image-based scoring
evidence.effect: mSWAT-Net outperformed 3 junior dermatologists in image-based scoring (ICC = 0.917 vs 0.777); comparable with experienced cutaneous lymphoma specialists.
evidence.quote: Moreover, mSWAT-Net outperformed 3 junior dermatologists in image-based scoring (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.917 vs 0.777) and demonstrated robust performance when compared with ground truth derived from 3-dimensional patient imaging (intraclass correlation coefficient = 0.812).

evidence.title: Multicenter Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Surgical Transfusion Risk at 45 US Hospitals
evidence.outcome: Comparison of S-PATH against standard-of-care MSBOS baseline on same data
evidence.effect: S-PATH recommended type and screens for median 32.5% vs 51.6% of cases at the same sensitivity; AUROC 0.929 vs 0.857
evidence.quote: S-PATH was consistently more effective than standard care, suggesting its potential for use as a perioperative clinical decision support tool.

evidence.title: Maximizing Lung Cancer Screening in High-Risk Population Leveraging ML-Developed Risk-Prediction Algorithms: Danish Retrospective Validation of LungFlag
evidence.outcome: LungFlag performance compared with PLCOm2012 on same data
evidence.effect: LungFlag AUC 0.63 vs. PLCOm2012 0.60 in Population A; slightly higher sensitivity in Population B, minor differences.
evidence.quote: LungFlag outperformed PLCOm2012 in Population A (AUC: 0.63 vs. 0.60) and showed slightly higher sensitivity in Population B, though differences were minor.

evidence.title: Large language models versus traditional textbooks: optimizing learning for plastic surgery case preparation
evidence.outcome: Rater-scored LLM vs textbook responses on accuracy, thoroughness, usefulness, brevity, quality
evidence.effect: LLMs rated more thorough (p<0.001) but less concise (p<0.001) than textbooks; textbooks superior on contraindications (p=0.027) and complications (p=0.014); ChatGPT outperformed Gemini.
evidence.quote: LLM responses were rated as more thorough (p < 0.001) but less concise (p < 0.001) than textbook responses.

evidence.title: Multimodal Generative Artificial Intelligence Model for Creating Radiology Reports for Chest Radiographs in Patients Undergoing Tuberculosis Screening
evidence.outcome: Standalone AI report accuracy versus radiologists alone on same radiographs
evidence.effect: AI report accuracy 90.8% vs reader 1 93.4% and reader 2 91.3%; accuracy significantly lower than both readers (p<.001); localization 63.3% vs 79.8% and 77.9%.
evidence.quote: Localization performance was significantly lower (p < .001) for AI-generated reports (63.3%) than for reader 1 (79.8%) and reader 2 (77.9%) without AI-generated reports and did not significantly change for either reader with AI-generated reports (reader 1: 78.7%, p = .71; reader 2: 81.5%, p = .23).
evidence.country: Unknown (public datasets from tuberculosis screening programs)

evidence.title: A GPT-4o-powered framework for identifying cognitive impairment stages in electronic health records
evidence.outcome: Agreement of CI stage classification versus two other language models on same data
evidence.effect: GPT-4o framework weighted Cohen's kappa 0.95 and Spearman 0.93, versus weighted kappa 0.82-0.85 for two other language models
evidence.quote: Evaluated on 165,926 notes from 1002 Medicare patients from Mass General Brigham (MGB), our GPT-4o framework achieved high accuracy in CI stage classification (weighted Cohen's kappa = 0.95, Spearman correlation = 0.93), and outperformed two other language models (weighted Cohen's kappa 0.82-0.85).

evidence.title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study
evidence.outcome: AI standalone accuracy compared with radiologists on the same images
evidence.effect: AI per-examination accuracy 74.8% vs average radiologist 83.4%; AI missed 80 fractures vs 41 for radiologists.
evidence.quote: AI produced a per-examination accuracy of 74.8% [95% CI: 65.4%, 82.7%], compared to average radiologist performance at 83.4% [95% CI: 75.2%, 89.8%].

evidence.title: Applying Large Language Models for Surgical Case Length Prediction
evidence.outcome: LLM case length prediction error and accuracy versus current OR scheduling estimates on the same cases
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned GPT-4 MAE 47.64 min vs current scheduling 49.34 min (P = .10, matching); accuracy within 20% was 46.12% vs 40.92% (P < .001).
evidence.quote: Both GPT-4 fine-tuned and GPT-3.5 fine-tuned significantly outperformed current scheduling methods in accuracy (46.12% and 46.08% vs 40.92%, respectively; P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: surgical cases (evaluation set; plus 500 external validation cases)

evidence.title: Evaluating GPT-4o in infectious disease diagnostics and management: A comparative study with residents and specialists on accuracy, completeness, and clinical support potential
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o accuracy and completeness versus residents and infectious disease specialists on same questions
evidence.effect: True/false accuracy: GPT-4o 87.5%, specialists 90.3%, residents 77.8%. Specialists outperformed GPT-4o on open-ended (p = .008) and case-based (P = .02) accuracy; GPT-4o more complete than residents.
evidence.quote: In true/false questions, GPT-4o showed comparable accuracy (87.5%) to specialists (90.3%) and exceeded residents (77.8%).

evidence.title: Diagnostic efficacy of large language models in the pediatric emergency department: a pilot study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy score of LLMs versus physicians on the same 80 pediatric ED cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o scored 72.5 and Gemini 1.5 Pro 62.75, versus PED physicians 61.88 (ChatGPT-4o better, p<0.05). EM residents scored 43.75, worse than physicians and chatbots (p<0.01).
evidence.quote: The best performing chatbots were ChatGPT-4o (score: 72.5) and Gemini 1.5 Pro (score: 62.75), the first performing better (p < 0.05) than PED physicians (score: 61.88).

evidence.title: Multidisciplinary Evaluation of an AI-Based Pneumothorax Detection Model: Clinical Comparison with Physicians in Edge and Cloud Environments
evidence.outcome: AI sensitivity versus physicians of varying experience for minimal pneumothorax detection on same radiographs
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 0.93 (95% CI: 0.79, 0.97) versus 0.55 (95% CI: 0.38, 0.69) to 0.84 (95% CI: 0.69, 0.92) among human readers; outperformed junior clinicians and matched or exceeded seniors.
evidence.quote: The model outperformed junior clinicians and matched or exceeded senior physicians, particularly in detecting minimal pneumothoraces, where AI sensitivity reached 0.93 (95% CI: 0.79, 0.97) compared to 0.55 (95% CI: 0.38, 0.69) - 0.84 (95% CI: 0.69, 0.92) among human readers.

evidence.title: Machine learning versus clinicians for detection and classification of oral mucosal lesions
evidence.outcome: Model versus specialists and general dentists on classification of oral lesions in the same test set
evidence.effect: Model performed comparable to specialists (p = 0.93) and significantly better than general dentists (p < 0.01).
evidence.quote: Overall, the model performed comparable to specialists (p = 0.93) and significantly better than general dentists (p < 0.01).

evidence.title: ChatGPT as a decision-support tool for better self-monitoring of hearing
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT recommendations with 5 expert audiologists on same simulated cases
evidence.effect: Agreement scores ranged from 0.80 to 0.84; 0.99 when all 5 experts unanimously agreed.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT aligned strongly with the experts' judgments, with agreement scores ranging from 0.80 to 0.84.

evidence.title: Privacy-Preserving Generation of Structured Lymphoma Progression Reports from Cross-sectional Imaging: A Comparative Analysis of Llama 3.3 and Llama 4
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two candidate LLMs on same data for report generation
evidence.effect: Llama-4-Scout was significantly more accurate than Llama-3.3-70B for nodal (0.99 vs 0.97, p<0.001), stage (0.85 vs 0.60) and treatment response (0.88 vs 0.65).
evidence.quote: This difference was more pronounced when predicting Lugano stage and treatment response (stage: 0.85 [95% CI = 0.79-0.89] vs. 0.60 [95% CI = 0.53-0.67], p < 0.001; treatment response: 0.88 [95% CI = 0.83-0.92] vs. 0.65 [95% CI = 0.58-0.71], p < 0.001).

evidence.title: A multi-dimensional performance evaluation of large language models in dental implantology: comparison of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Grok, Gemini and Qwen across diverse clinical scenarios
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated performance of five LLMs compared on identical dental implantology questions and cases
evidence.effect: Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking scored highest (mean 21.9 in question answering, 22.2 in case analysis), significantly above ChatGPT-o3-mini (19.2) in questions and Qwen2.5-max (16.9) in cases.
evidence.quote: Gemini-2.0-flash-thinking achieved the highest overall performance, with a mean score of 21.9 in professional question answering and 22.2 in case analysis.
evidence.sample_unit: test items (40 questions and 5 complex cases)

evidence.title: Large language models for extraction of OPS-codes from operative reports in meningioma surgery
evidence.outcome: Comparing LLM coding against surgeons and professional coders on same reports
evidence.effect: Coders (100%) and surgeons (99%) outperformed LLMs in sufficient coding (GPT-4o 78%, GPT CodeMedic 89%; p<0.01); for optimal coding GPT CodeMedic (83%) outperformed surgeons (69%, p=0.03).
evidence.quote: Currently, professional coders still significantly outperform LLMs in sufficient and optimal coding.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-powered software outperforms interventional cardiologists in assessment of IVUS-based stent optimization
evidence.venue: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
evidence.outcome: AI vs interventional cardiologists on IVUS stent expansion and geographic miss assessment, same data
evidence.effect: AVVIGO+ reported lower mean expansion (70.3% vs 91.2%, p<0.0001); 25 discordant cases; identified PB ≥50% missed by IC in 12 cases; analysis time 0.76 vs 1.89 min.
evidence.quote: AVVIGO™ + consistently identified lower mean expansion (70.3 %) vs. IC (91.2 %), (p < 0.0001), primarily due to detecting frames with smaller MSA values (5.94 vs. 7.19 mm<sup>2</sup>, p = 0.0053).

evidence.title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools
evidence.outcome: Comparison of new models against existing ELTS score on same data
evidence.effect: All AUCs (ELTS and Models 1-3) were <0.68; Model 3 tended to be slightly better but the difference was not significant.
evidence.quote: Model 3 tended to be slightly more effective, but the difference was not significant.

evidence.title: Evaluating Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) models for suicide risk assessment in synthetic patient journal entries
evidence.outcome: LLM ensemble risk-stratification agreement with clinician consensus on suicide risk levels
evidence.effect: Ensemble exact agreement 65.60% vs 30.38% chance (χ2 = 86.58); 92% agreement on intervene/not intervene (Kappa 0.84); 94% sensitivity, 91% specificity.
evidence.quote: Using clinician consensus as "ground truth," our ensemble LLM performed significantly above chance (30.38%) in exact risk-assessment agreement (65.60%; χ2 = 86.58).

evidence.title: Deep Learning-Enabled Ultrasound for Advancing Anterior Talofibular Ligament Injuries Classification: A Multicenter Model Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: AI model performance compared against radiologists of different levels on same data
evidence.effect: ATFLNet consistently outperformed senior radiologists in external validation sets (all p<.05).
evidence.quote: Additionally, it consistently outperformed senior radiologists in external validation sets (all p<.05).
evidence.sample_unit: not specified (training n=2566, internal validation n=642, external validation n=717 and 493, prospective n=472)

evidence.title: The use of artificial intelligence to improve detection of acute incidental pulmonary emboli
evidence.venue: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
evidence.outcome: AI versus prospective radiologist detection of incidental pulmonary emboli on the same CT exams
evidence.effect: Radiologists detected 218 IPE prospectively; AI found an additional 36, missed 30 radiologist-detected cases, and had 94 false positives. AI had similar sensitivity but reduced PPV.
evidence.quote: Compared with radiologists, AI had similar sensitivity but reduced positive predictive value.

evidence.title: Evaluating Zero-Shot Foundation Models for Time Series Forecasting in Clinical Settings: A Simulation Study with Electronic Health Records
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Forecast accuracy of zero-shot foundation models versus optimized task-specific models on the same data
evidence.effect: Task-specific models outperformed zero-shot foundation models in accuracy across three clinical use cases; zero-shot models generalized strongly to external datasets.
evidence.quote: Across three clinical use cases, task-specific models outperformed zero-shot models in accuracy, but zero-shot models demonstrated strong generalization in external datasets.

evidence.title: GPT-4 for automated sequence-level determination of MRI protocols based on radiology request forms from clinical routine
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 MRI protocol completeness, quality, utility versus radiology residents on same requests
evidence.effect: GPT-4 comparable to R1 (each p > 0.05) but inferior to R2 for completeness and quality (p < 0.01) and utility (p < 0.001); clinically applicable in 95% vs R1 95%, R2 96%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 achieved median scores of 3 (1-5) for completeness, 4 (1-5) for quality, and 4 (1-5) for utility, comparable to R1 (3 (1-5), 4 (1-5), 4 (1-5); each p > 0.05) but inferior to R2 (4 (1-5), 5 (1-5); p < 0.01, respectively, and 5 (1-5); p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Performance of Microsoft Copilot in the Diagnostic Process of Pulmonary Embolism
evidence.venue: The western journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: PE risk discrimination (AUC) of Copilot versus Wells score on same vignettes
evidence.effect: Copilot AUC 0.713 (P<0.001) versus Wells score AUC 0.583 (P=.091); Copilot risk levels significantly higher in PE patients.
evidence.quote: Copilot demonstrated better discriminatory power than the Wells score in risk assessment of PE (area under the curve 0.713 vs 0.583), with statistical significance (P<0.001 vs P=.091).

evidence.title: AI as an independent second reader in detection of clinically relevant breast cancers within a population-based screening programme in the Netherlands: a retrospective cohort study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of single human reader plus AI versus double human reading on same screening data
evidence.effect: Combined single reading with AI recalled 5.0% (282 screen-detected cancers, 29 interval, 38 future) vs double reading 2.9%; sensitivity improved by 8.4% (95% CI 5.7-11.2, p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: Double human reading recalled 1244 mammograms (2·9%, 291 screen-detected cancers) and combined single human reading with AI recalled 2112 mammograms (5·0%, 282 screen-detected cancers, 29 interval cancers, 38 future breast cancers), improving the sensitivity by 8·4% (95% CI 5·7-11·2, p<0·0001).

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Large Language Model (ChatGPT-4) for Patients Admitted to a Community Hospital Medical Intensive Care Unit: A Retrospective Case Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-4 versus critical care physicians against blinded chart-review ground truth
evidence.effect: Accuracy 88.3% for physicians vs 85.0% for ChatGPT-4, no significant difference (McNemar p=0.249); Cohen's kappa agreement 0.57 (95% CI 0.35-0.79)
evidence.quote: The diagnostic accuracy was 88.3% for physicians and 85.0% for ChatGPT-4, with no significant difference by McNemar testing (p-value of 0.249).

evidence.title: Specialized curricula for training vision language models in retinal image analysis
evidence.outcome: AMD staging and referral F1 of VLMs compared with ophthalmologists
evidence.effect: RetinaVLM-Specialist outperformed medical VLMs and ChatGPT-4o in AMD staging (F1: 0.63 vs. 0.33) and referral (0.67 vs. 0.50), comparable to junior ophthalmologists.
evidence.quote: The resulting model, RetinaVLM-Specialist, significantly outperforms foundation medical VLMs and ChatGPT-4o in AMD disease staging (F1: 0.63 vs. 0.33) and referral (0.67 vs. 0.50), achieving performance comparable to junior ophthalmologists.

evidence.title: Surgeon, Trainee, or GPT? A Blinded Multicentric Study of AI-Augmented Operative Notes
evidence.outcome: GPT and hybrid versus clinician-authored notes
evidence.effect: Hybrid attending-plus-GPT notes had the highest average domain scores and 79% approval; GPT-only had the lowest approval rate, 23%.
evidence.quote: Hybrid notes written by an attending surgeon with GPT assistance received the highest average domain scores and the highest "as is" approval rate (79%), outperforming all other groups.

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of Diagnosis and Treatment Plan Given by Pediatric Dentists and Generated by ChatGPT: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT diagnosis and treatment plan accuracy compared with pediatric dentists on same cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 80% accuracy, equal to two dentists and lower than the 90% of the other two; no significant difference (p = 0.926).
evidence.quote: Statistical analysis revealed no significant difference between the performance of ChatGPT and the pediatric dentists (p = 0.926).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
evidence.outcome: Comparison of ChatGPT-4o versus Google Web Search on accuracy and completeness
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o was more accurate (5.83 vs 4.75) and more complete (2.88 vs 1.68; difference 1.2, 95% CI 0.96-1.44) than Google Web Search.
evidence.quote: For completeness, ChatGPT-4o’s mean score was 2.88 (SD 0.32), significantly higher than Google Web Search’s 1.68 (SD 0.69), with a mean difference of 1.2 (95% CI 0.96‐1.44).

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek for non-critical triage support using real-world conversations in emergency department
evidence.outcome: Comparison of multiple LLMs against each other and nurse KTAS gold standard on same data
evidence.effect: Eight LLMs compared on identical cases; accuracy, sensitivity and specificity differed widely (e.g., Gemini 2.5 pro sensitivity 90.9% but specificity 23.3%; GPT-4.1 accuracy 70.6%).
evidence.quote: Gemini 2.5 pro demonstrated the highest sensitivity (90.9%) and F1-score (82.4%), though with lower specificity (23.3%).

evidence.title: Comparison of a Specialized Large Language Model with GPT-4o for CT and MRI Radiology Report Summarization
evidence.outcome: Report summarization F1 and expert-rated quality, specialized LLM versus general-purpose GPT-4o on same data
evidence.effect: LLM-RadSum median F1 0.58 vs GPT-4o 0.30 (P<.001); 81.5% (1467/1800) LLM-RadSum outputs met standards vs at least 27.8% (501/1800) GPT-4o outputs needing adjustment.
evidence.quote: Overall, LLM-RadSum achieved a higher median F1 score for report summarization compared with GPT-4o (0.58 [IQR: 0.44-0.77] vs 0.30 [IQR: 0.23-0.37]; P < .001); superior performance from LLM-RadSum was observed across anatomic regions, modalities, sexes, ages, and impression lengths (all P < .001).

evidence.title: Deep Learning with Disc Photos or OCT Scans in Glaucoma Detection
evidence.outcome: AUC of OCT-based DL model versus disc photo-based DL model for glaucoma detection
evidence.effect: OCT-based DL model AUC 0.90 significantly outperformed DP-based model AUC 0.86 (P < 0.005).
evidence.quote: The OCT-based DL model achieved an AUC of 0.90, significantly outperforming the DP-based model (AUC = 0.86, P < 0.005) with superior performance consistent across demographic groups.
evidence.sample_unit: OCT and disc photo image sets

evidence.title: Comparison of Artificial Intelligence Models and Human Experts in Managing Dyslipidemia: Assessment of Adherence to Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Guideline concordance of LLMs versus clinicians of varying expertise on same cases
evidence.effect: AI correct 91.0% vs professors 82.1%/68.6%/65.7%, specialist 50.0%, residents 32.1%/21.4%; composite 10.3 vs 5.2-9.2/12; AI outperformed all human groups (p<0.01).
evidence.quote: Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons confirmed that AI models significantly outperformed all human groups (p < 0.01), professors outperformed residents (p < 0.001), and specialists performed better than residents (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Development and Validation of a Semiautomated Tool for Measuring Periorbital Distances
evidence.outcome: Reliability and correlation of automated and semiautomated tools versus manual periorbital measurements on the same photos
evidence.effect: OrbitJ ICC and Pearson >0.8 versus manual; OrbitMap ICC and Pearson >0.5 except ISS; PeriOrbitAI ICC <0.5 except MRD2 and OCD, and failed on 6 images.
evidence.quote: Reliability between PeriOrbitAI and manual measurements was low (ICC <0.5) except for MRD2 and OCD, and correlation was moderate (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.49-0.75).

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of accuracy and completeness in standardized database generation for complex multilingual lung cancer pathological reports: large language model-based assisted diagnosis system vs. DeepSeek, GPT-3.5, and healthcare professionals with varied professional titles, with task load variation assessment among medical staff
evidence.outcome: Accuracy/completeness of pathology database generation versus clinicians and general LLMs on same data
evidence.effect: Lung cancer-specific LLM outperformed nurses, residents, interns, DeepSeek, GPT-3.5 in lesion/lymph node analysis and pathology extraction for Chinese records (p<0.05); total scores slightly below chief physicians.
evidence.quote: The lung cancer-specific LLM outperformed nurses, residents, interns, and general AI models (DeepSeek, GPT-3.5) in lesion/lymph node analysis and pathology extraction for Chinese records (p < 0.05), with total scores slightly below chief physicians.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac Treatment Decision-Making: An Evaluation of the Performance of ChatGPT Versus the Heart Team in Coronary Revascularization
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT revascularization recommendations with Heart Team decisions
evidence.effect: Agreement with the Heart Team was low (Cohen's kappa: 0.17 for o1 and 0.03 for 4o); no correct predictions for medical therapy.
evidence.quote: Agreement with the Heart Team was low (Cohen's kappa: 0.17 for o1 and 0.03 for 4o).

evidence.title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Comparison of five candidate open-source LLMs on same data
evidence.effect: Rombos significantly outperformed other LLMs with default prompt (72.9% vs 59.2–68.5%, p<0.0001) and with adapted prompts (85.3%).
evidence.quote: The overall accuracy of Rombos was significantly higher compared to each of the other LLMs ( p < 0.0001; see also Supplementary Table 4).

evidence.title: An end-to-end solution for out-of-hospital emergency medical dispatch triage based on multimodal and continual deep learning
evidence.outcome: F1-score of AI model versus existing in-house triage protocol for incident severity
evidence.effect: Absolute F1 gains over the existing protocol of 18.46% (life-threatening level), 25.96% (response delay) and 3.63% (jurisdiction); also beat non-continual learning baselines by 3.04%, 9.66% and 0.58%.
evidence.quote: Compared with the Valencian Region's existing in-house triage protocol, E2eDeepEMC<sup>2</sup> achieved absolute F1-score gains of 18.46% for life-threatening level, 25.96% for response delay and 3.63% for jurisdiction.

evidence.title: Head-to-Head Comparison of 2 Artificial Intelligence Computer-Aided Triage Solutions for Detecting Intracranial Hemorrhage on Noncontrast Head CT
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head sensitivity and specificity of two ICH triage AI vendors on same local CT scans
evidence.effect: Vendor A sensitivity 94.4%, specificity 97.4%; Vendor B sensitivity 59.5%, specificity 99.0%. Vendor A had 20 FNs and 97 FPs; Vendor B had 145 FNs and 36 FPs.
evidence.quote: Vendor A demonstrated a sensitivity of 94.4% and specificity of 97.4%, PPV of 77.7%, and NPV of 99.5%.

evidence.title: The clinical application potential assessment of the Deepseek-R1 large language model in lung cancer
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM versus junior oncologists on same guideline-based questions and cases
evidence.effect: Deepseek-R1 accuracy 92.3%, 87.5%, 85.1% vs junior oncologists 80.4%, 72.8%, 70.2% (P<0.05); overall diagnostic accuracy 94.6% vs 78.9% in 256 cases.
evidence.quote: In a sample of 256 cases evaluated formally, Deepseek-R1's overall diagnostic accuracy was 94.6%, compared to 78.9% for junior oncologists (P < 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: patients with newly diagnosed lung cancer

evidence.title: Dual site external validation of artificial intelligence-enabled treatment monitoring for neovascular age-related macular degeneration in England
evidence.outcome: AI-led assessments versus real-world clinician assessments against reading-centre reference standard
evidence.effect: AI R9 NPV 95.3% vs real-world 81.6%; rNPV 1.17 (1.11-1.23) and rPPV 1.39 (1.10-1.76), meeting superiority criteria.
evidence.quote: Applying the thresholds described in R9 to determine AI-led assessments produced a comparable rNPV of 1.17 (1.11–1.23) and an improved rPPV of 1.39 (1.10–1.76).

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Neurological Practice: Real-World Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus neurologists (concordance with discharge diagnoses)
evidence.effect: Neurologists achieved 75% diagnostic accuracy, outperforming ChatGPT (54%) and Gemini (46%); LLMs overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases.
evidence.quote: Neurologists achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 75%, outperforming ChatGPT (54%) and Gemini (46%).

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of a Medical Large Language Model in Answering Real-World Radiation Oncology Questions: Multicenter Observational Study
evidence.outcome: LLM answer quality and harmfulness compared with senior radiation oncology experts on same questions
evidence.effect: Quality not significantly different (3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); potentially harmful 16% LLM vs 13% experts (P=.63).
evidence.quote: The answers were deemed potentially harmful in 13% of cases for the clinical experts compared with 16% of cases for the LLM (P=.63; Fisher exact test).

evidence.title: Interpreting psychiatric digital phenotyping data with large language models: a preliminary analysis
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs on the same test cases for pattern identification accuracy
evidence.effect: GPT-4o 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) significantly outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).
evidence.quote: GPT-4o demonstrated 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) in identifying clinical patterns based on standard test cases, significantly outperforming GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).

evidence.title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
evidence.outcome: Comparison of five LLMs, LLM-alone, and pharmacists alone on same scenarios
evidence.effect: Claude 3.5 Sonnet best native model (accuracy 51%, F1 0.42) vs Gemini Flash 16%; co-pilot 61% vs pharmacist alone 46%.
evidence.quote: Of the native models, Gemini Flash scored the lowest while Claude 3.5 Sonnet performed the best on measures of recall (0.16 vs. 0.51), precision (0.15 vs. 0.35), F1 (0.16 vs. 0.42), and overall accuracy (16% vs. 51%).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of three general-purpose LLMs against pathologist reference standard for ABG interpretation
evidence.effect: Primary disorder agreement κ ≥ 0.88 for all LLMs; secondary disorder agreement varied by model and method (ChatGPT LLM-S κ = 0.91 vs Copilot/Gemini 0.81).
evidence.quote: Agreement for identifying the primary acid-base (APD) disorder was strong across all approaches (Cohen's κ ≥ 0.88).

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT provide responses to patients for orthopaedic-related questions? A comparison between ChatGPT and medical support staff
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT vs support staff response quality and empathy on the same patient questions
evidence.effect: No quality difference (p = 0.075); ChatGPT rated more empathetic (p < 0.001); no difference in risk of incorrect treatment (p = 0.377).
evidence.quote: No quality difference was found (p = 0.075) between ChatGPT and support staff, though ChatGPT was rated as more empathetic (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Quality assessment of artificial intelligence-generated versus human-written hospital summaries evaluating detail, usefulness, and continuity of care
evidence.outcome: Rubric-rated quality of LLM-drafted vs human-written discharge summaries on same hospitalizations
evidence.effect: LLM summaries outperformed human summaries across all nine criteria (p < .05); comprehensiveness median 0.62 vs -0.23. LLM performance was consistent across medical and surgical services.
evidence.quote: LLM-generated summaries outperformed human-written summaries across all criteria (p < .05), with the greatest difference observed in comprehensiveness (LLM median 0.62 vs. human -0.23).

evidence.title: Application of Large Language Models in TN Staging and Treatment Response Evaluation for Patients With Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Comparative Performance Analysis of ChatGPT-4o-Latest and DeepSeek-V3-0324
evidence.venue: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
evidence.outcome: Accuracy comparison of two LLMs against radiologist reference standard for NPC staging
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3-0324 outperformed GPT-4o-latest in TRE-1 (96.5% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.001); no significant difference for T staging, N staging, or TRE-2.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-V3-0324 significantly outperformed GPT-4o-latest in TRE-1 staging (96.5% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (831 reports) in test set; 68 cases in reader study

evidence.title: Large Language Models Versus Human Readers in CAD-RADS 2.0 Categorization of Coronary CT Angiography Reports
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Full CAD-RADS categorization accuracy of LLMs versus human readers on same reports
evidence.effect: O1 90.7% accuracy vs GPT-4o 73.8%, GPT-4 59.7%, GPT-3.5-turbo 25.8%, fellow 83.3%, resident 1 83.3%; no significant difference vs cardiac radiologist (86.1%; P = 0.12) and resident 2 (89.4%; P = 0.68).
evidence.quote: However, there was no significant difference in accuracy when compared to the cardiac radiologist (86.1%; P = 0.12) and resident 2 (89.4%; P = 0.68).

evidence.title: The Potential of AI in Nursing Care: Multicenter Evaluation in Fall Risk Assessment
evidence.outcome: AI fall risk model AUROC versus rule-based clinical systems on same data
evidence.effect: AI models consistently outperformed rule-based systems in all setups; AUROC 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) geriatric hospital, 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) university hospital.
evidence.quote: Our findings demonstrate that AI models consistently outperform rule-based systems across all experimental setups, with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) for the geriatric hospital, and 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) for the university hospital.

evidence.title: OphthoACR (Ophthalmology Automated Chart Review): An AI-Powered Tool for Complete Automation of Ophthalmology Chart Reviews and Cohort Data Analysis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI chart review versus manual review for extracting variables
evidence.effect: OphthoACR achieved 94% accuracy in extracting variables of interest, significantly outperforming manual review (83%); 97% specificity, 92% sensitivity, Cohen's κ 0.70.
evidence.quote: OphthoACR achieved 94% accuracy in extracting variables of interest, significantly outperforming manual review (83%).
