evidence.title: Novel Insights into the Application of Large Language Models in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Complex Cardiovascular Diseases: A Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Comparative accuracy, comprehensiveness, and safety of two LLMs on same cardiovascular cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o outperformed Kimi on treatment accuracy (P=0.004) and comprehensiveness (P<0.001); high-risk outputs 1.5% vs 4.5%; diagnostic accuracy similar (P=0.663).
evidence.quote: For treatment recommendations, ChatGPT-4o outperformed Kimi in both accuracy (P = 0.004, r = 0.321) and comprehensiveness (P < 0.001, r = 0.644).

evidence.title: Development of a multi-task deep learning system for classification of nine common knee abnormalities on MRI: a large-scale, multicentre, stepwise validation study
evidence.outcome: DLS accuracy compared with senior radiologists on the same data
evidence.effect: DLS showed comparable accuracy to senior radiologists for meniscal tear (79.6% vs 78.1%), ACL tear (89.3% vs 89.4%), and MCL injury (87.1% vs 85.7%).
evidence.quote: For step 1 of validation, the DLS demonstrated comparable accuracy to that of the senior radiologists in classifying meniscal tear (79.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.426), ACL tear (89.3% vs. 89.4%, p = 1.000), and MCL injury (87.1% vs. 85.7%, p = 0.565).

evidence.title: Multimodal large language models in ultrasound diagnosis of breast masses: a multicenter comparative analysis based on GPT-4o, radiologists, and convolutional neural network (CNN)
evidence.venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o versus radiologists and a CNN on the same breast ultrasound cases
evidence.effect: GPT-4o image-only 58% vs image+text 70% (P=0.031); image+text similar to moderately experienced radiologists 71% (P=0.450) and CNN 74% (P=0.701).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy improved when deploying the image-combined-text-strategy compared to only image [58% (46 of 80) vs. 70% (56 of 80), P=0.031], which resembled board-certified moderately experienced radiologists (70% [56 of 80] vs. 71% [57 of 80], P=0.450) and customized CNN [70% (56 of 80) vs. 74% (59 of 80), P=0.701].

evidence.title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
evidence.outcome: initial readability versus Google
evidence.effect: Initial GPT-4 vs Google: Flesch-Kincaid 13.06 vs. 12.24 (P=0.41); Reading Ease 36.87 vs. 40.05 (P=0.53).
evidence.quote: No significant differences were found in readability between GPT-4 and Google, displaying a similar Flesch-Kincaid grade level (13.06 vs. 12.24, P=0.41) and Flesch Reading Ease score (36.87 vs. 40.05, P=0.53).

evidence.title: Automated Esophageal Cancer Staging From Free-Text Radiology Reports: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Overall esophageal cancer staging accuracy of LLMs versus clinicians on same reports
evidence.effect: INF-72B+IR achieved 61.5% accuracy and F1 0.60 versus clinicians' 39.5% and 0.39 (P<.001); Qwen2.5-72B+IR 46%; LLaMA3.1-70B not significantly different from clinicians.
evidence.quote: INF-72B+IR achieved a superior overall staging accuracy of 61.5% and an F1-score of 0.60, substantially higher than the clinicians' accuracy of 39.5% and F1-score of 0.39 (all P<.001).

evidence.title: AI meets sleep surgery: assessing drug-induced sleep endoscopy interpretation with a large language model
evidence.outcome: LLM DISE interpretation concordance versus expert raters and clinical reference standard
evidence.effect: LLM matched expert performance in all domains except epiglottis (moderate agreement); human raters had perfect or near-perfect agreement for velum, oropharynx, tongue base, jaw thrust.
evidence.quote: The large language model matched expert performance for all domains except the epiglottis, where moderate agreement was observed.

evidence.title: Human vs. artificial intelligence: Physicians outperform ChatGPT in real-world pharmacotherapy counselling
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT compared against physicians on the same real-world pharmacotherapy queries
evidence.effect: ChatGPT responses were substantially inferior to physician-generated responses for information quality and factual correctness; all three evaluators preferred physician answers.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's responses to real-world pharmacotherapeutic queries were substantially inferior compared to conventional physician-generated responses with regard to quality of information and factual correctness.

evidence.title: In-Context Learning for Data-Efficient Diabetic Retinopathy Detection via Multimodal Foundation Models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy, F1, and calibration error of Gemini ICL versus fine-tuned RETFound on the same DR data
evidence.effect: Gemini ICL accuracy 0.841 vs RETFound 0.849, F1 0.876 vs 0.883 (P>0.3). Calibration error 0.129 vs 0.081, RETFound better (P=0.004).
evidence.quote: While accuracy and F1 scores were comparable (P > 0.3), RETFound's calibration was superior (P = 0.004).

evidence.title: An integrated and interpretable machine learning framework for Kawasaki disease diagnosis and risk prediction
evidence.outcome: Model accuracy versus pediatricians and ChatGPT for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, CAL prediction
evidence.effect: Model accuracies were 0.900, 0.800, and 0.757 for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, and CAL prediction, outperforming pediatricians with over 5 years of experience and ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: In a comparative study, our model achieved accuracies of 0.900, 0.800, and 0.757 for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, and CAL prediction, respectively, consistently outperforming pediatricians with over 5 years of experience and ChatGPT, highlighting its potential as a clinical decision support tool.
evidence.sample_unit: pediatric patients (typical and atypical Kawasaki disease cases)

evidence.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for accurate detection of wrong blood in tube errors in hospitalized patients
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of ML model versus multivariate Mahalanobis and univariate delta checks on same internal data
evidence.effect: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.
evidence.quote: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of GPT-4o Compared to Radiology Residents in Emergency Abdominal Tomography Cases
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o diagnostic accuracy versus radiology residents on same emergency abdominal CT cases
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy 76% for R1-R2, 89% for R3, 82% for R4-R5, 84% for R6, and 82% for GPT-4o; no statistically significant differences between GPT-4o and residents (p > 0.05).
evidence.quote: No statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy were found between GPT-4o and the residents, regardless of the experience level or case difficulty (p > 0.05).

evidence.title: AI-Enabled ECG Analysis Improves Diagnostic Accuracy and Reduces False STEMI Activations: A Multicenter U.S. Registry
evidence.outcome: AI ECG versus standard triage sensitivity, specificity, and false positive activation rate against angiographic reference
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 92.0% vs 71.0%; specificity 81.0% vs 29.0%; FPA rate 7.9% vs 41.8% (P<0.001 for all); AUROC 0.94.
evidence.quote: The AI ECG model outperformed standard triage, demonstrating higher index ECG sensitivity (553 of 601 [92.0%; 95% CI: 89.7%-94.1%] vs 427 of 601 [71.0%; 95% CI: 67.4%-74.6%]), reducing FPA rates (34 of 431 [7.9%; 95% CI: 6.4%-9.6%] vs 180 of 431 [41.8%; 95% CI: 38.9%-44.7%]), and improving specificity (431 of 531 [81.0%; 95% CI: 77.2%-84.5%] vs 154 of 531 [29.0%; 95% CI: 24.8%-33.4%]) (P < 0.001 for all).
evidence.sample_unit: patients with suspected STEMI triggering emergent CCL activation

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models in Analyzing Common Hypertension Scenarios
evidence.outcome: LLM responses compared against hypertension expert responses on same vignettes
evidence.effect: All three LLMs scored below the expert on accuracy and safety; GPT-4 was closest (83% vs 92% accuracy), MedLM far lower (35%).
evidence.quote: Despite their potential, current LLM versions are inferior to expert recommendations.

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: LLM agreement with heart team compared with a simple guideline-based non-LLM reference model
evidence.effect: Reference model outperformed LLMs on raw reports; only with summaries plus guideline text did GPT-4 models and DeepSeek-R1 draw level with it.
evidence.quote: The reference model outperformed the LLMs in the raw experiment regarding the metrics we assessed.

evidence.title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
evidence.outcome: Candidate model comparison
evidence.effect: TSB accuracy 0.89, Claude-2 0.86, and GPT-4 0.78; GPT-4 was significantly lower than TSB (P < .001).
evidence.quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

evidence.title: Accounting for inconclusive results and repeated testing: A framework for evaluating wearable electrocardiogram diagnostic performance with application to Apple Watch and artificial intelligence-enhanced interpretation
evidence.outcome: AI algorithm vs existing Apple Watch algorithm on identical recordings
evidence.effect: AI pragmatic 98.4%/96.1% and ITD 98.4%/96.6%, with 92% reduction in inconclusive outputs vs Apple Watch.
evidence.quote: The AI algorithm achieved pragmatic 98.4%/96.1% and ITD 98.4%/96.6%, with 92% reduction in inconclusive outputs vs Apple Watch.

evidence.title: Malignancy prediction for calcified thyroid nodules using deep learning based on ultrasound dynamic videos
evidence.venue: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
evidence.outcome: AI model performance compared against radiologists and 2D models on same data
evidence.effect: Optimized 3D model AUROC 0.916 versus radiologists 0.638 (p < 0.0001); outperformed four other 3D DL models on external test.
evidence.quote: Its AUROC was significantly higher than that of radiologists (0.916 versus 0.638; p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: [Lesion detection in optical coherence tomography based on lightweight convolutional neural networks]
evidence.venue: [Zhonghua yan ke za zhi] Chinese journal of ophthalmology
evidence.outcome: Model accuracy compared with ophthalmologists of different experience levels on external OCT images
evidence.effect: Model average accuracy 89.9% on external validation; junior physicians 74% (95% CI 61.84%-86.16%); mid-level physicians 88% (95% CI 78.99%-97.01%); model approached mid-level physicians.
evidence.quote: The model achieved an average accuracy of 89.9% on the external validation set, whereas junior physicians demonstrated an accuracy of 74% (95%CI: 61.84%~86.16%) in interpreting OCT images, and that of mid-level physicians was 88% (95%CI: 78.99%~97.01%), indicating the model's performance approached that of mid-level physicians.

evidence.title: Clinical-Grade Interpretable Artificial Intelligence Tool for Automated Detection of Lymph Node Metastasis in Prostate Cancer
evidence.venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
evidence.outcome: Micrometastasis miss rate and slide examination time of AI versus pathologists
evidence.effect: Pathologists had a 9% micrometastasis miss rate versus 3% for the AI model; the AI reduced slide examination time versus general and genitourinary pathologists (P < .001).
evidence.quote: Although pathologists exhibited a 9% miss rate in micrometastasis detection, the AI model demonstrated a significantly lower miss rate of 3% using the institutional data set, highlighting its potential for clinical deployment.

evidence.title: Application of AI-assisted magnifying colonoscopy system in the diagnosis of colorectal tumors: a multicenter exploratory diagnostic study
evidence.outcome: AI model diagnostic accuracy compared with endoscopists of varying experience on same images
evidence.effect: AADM accuracy 0.938 was superior to junior endoscopists (0.866, P<0.05) and comparable to senior endoscopists (0.937, P>0.05).
evidence.quote: The diagnostic performance of the AADM was superior to that of junior endoscopists (accuracy: 0.938 vs. 0.866, P < 0.05) and comparable to senior endoscopists (accuracy: 0.938 vs. 0.937, P > 0.05).

evidence.title: Can general purpose large language models assist pediatricians in predicting infants with serious bacterial infection?
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy for infant SBI versus pediatricians, ML models, and rule-based methods
evidence.effect: LLMs performed comparably to ML models, rule-based methods, and pediatrician majority vote (MCC 0.41-0.43 vs 0.43); best individual pediatrician sensitivity 0.74, specificity 0.68, MCC 0.33.
evidence.quote: In comparison, the best-performing individual pediatrician achieved a higher sensitivity (0.74) but lower specificity (0.68), with an MCC of 0.33, while the pediatricians’ majority vote yielded sensitivity of 0.69, specificity of 0.81, and MCC of 0.43 — comparable to the top-performing LLMs.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (infants under 90 days admitted to the emergency department)

evidence.title: Exploring the prognostic utility of large language models versus traditional clinical models in heart failure: a pilot study
evidence.outcome: AUC of LLMs versus conventional logistic regression model on same data
evidence.effect: Zigong: ChatGPT AUC 0.59, DeepSeek 0.56 vs clinical model 0.63. MIMIC-IV: ChatGPT 0.72 vs clinical model 0.74 (P=0.31); DeepSeek 0.67.
evidence.quote: In the MIMIC-IV cohort, ChatGPT achieved higher discrimination (AUC 0.72) than DeepSeek (AUC 0.67, P < 0.001) and comparable performance to the clinical model (AUC 0.74, P = 0.31).

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
evidence.outcome: quality versus author-written summaries
evidence.effect: High-quality: extended prompt 79.4%, simple prompt 54.9%, original summaries 5.4%; P<.001.
evidence.quote: The proportion rated as high-quality was 79.4% for the extended prompt, 54.9% for the simple prompt, and 5.4% for original summaries (P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

evidence.title: Performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Models in Guideline-Concordant Prostate-Specific Antigen Testing: Comparative Study With Junior Clinicians
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate AI against junior clinicians on the same scenarios
evidence.effect: RAG-LLM 95.5% accuracy vs junior clinicians 62.3% (closed-book) and 74.1% (open-book); differences significant (P<.001).
evidence.quote: The difference was statistically significant for both closed-book (P<.001) and open-book (P<.001) formats.
evidence.sample_unit: case scenario responses (44 fictional scenarios x 5 runs/clinicians)

evidence.title: Real-world application of large language models for automated TNM staging using unstructured gynecologic oncology reports
evidence.outcome: LLM T/N staging accuracy versus existing manual registry entries
evidence.effect: Gemini 1.5 T- and N-stage accuracy 0.994 and 0.993; Qwen2.5 72B 0.971 and 0.923; both outperformed manual entries, which had error rates of 5.5-17.0%.
evidence.quote: Both a cloud-based LLM (Gemini 1.5; T- and N-stage accuracy: 0.994 and 0.993, respectively) and the top-performing local model (Qwen2.5 72B; T- and N-stage accuracy: 0.971 and 0.923, respectively) outperformed existing manual entries in extracting pathological T and N classifications.

evidence.title: Evaluating the potential of ChatGPT for patient identification in clinical breast cancer trials
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity/specificity of ChatGPT-4.0 versus clinicians for trial eligibility identification against reference standard
evidence.effect: Both AI and clinicians had high specificity, but sensitivity varied. ChatGPT-4.0 was especially ineffective for neoadjuvant trials; clinicians performed better but heterogeneously; team-based assessment identified nearly all eligible patients.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.0 proved especially ineffective at screening for neoadjuvant trials, whereas medical professionals showed better, but heterogeneous performance.

evidence.title: Comparative feasibility of reasoning and non-reasoning large language models for gynecologic cancer emergency care
evidence.outcome: LLM vs physician (fellows, residents) scores on same gynecologic oncology emergency cases
evidence.effect: GPT-4o total score higher than physicians (MD 3.55; 95% CI 2.98-4.10; P<0.001); o3-mini-high also outperformed physicians in total scores (MD 3.05; 95% CI 1.98-3.88), but not with speed metrics.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o achieved higher total scores than physicians (MD, 3.55; 95% CI, 2.98-4.10; P < 0.001) and maintained superiority when speed metrics were excluded (MD, 1.27; 95% CI, 0.80-1.79; P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Performance of large language models in interventional cardiology: the ILLUMINATE blinded model-comparison study
evidence.outcome: performance differences among candidate LLMs
evidence.effect: Performance varied across LLMs (P less than .001); ChatGPTi 7.8 [7.5-8.0] and ChatGPT-gl 7.7 [7.4-7.9] outperformed others.
evidence.quote: Performance significantly varied across LLMs (P less than .001), with ChatGPTi (7.8 [7.5-8.0]) and ChatGPT-gl (7.7 [7.4-7.9]) outperforming others.
evidence.sample_unit: blinded expert evaluations (20 cases x 6 models x 5 raters)

evidence.title: Evaluating Locally Run Large Language Models (Gemma 2, Mistral Nemo, and Llama 3) for Outpatient Otorhinolaryngology Care: Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM recommendations with treating doctors' recommendations on medical adequacy and other ratings
evidence.effect: ORL doctors achieved superior ratings compared with all three locally run LLMs across all categories (P<.0005).
evidence.quote: Over all categories, ORL doctors achieved superior (P<.0005) ratings compared to locally run LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral Nemo, and Gemma 2).

evidence.title: An Explainable AI Framework for Corneal Imaging Interpretation and Refractive Surgery Decision Support
evidence.outcome: Early keratoconus detection AUC versus baseline CNN and ViT models on same data
evidence.effect: Framework AUC 0.95 ± 0.03 vs. 0.88 (CNN) and 0.90 (ViT), p < 0.05.
evidence.quote: Comparative benchmarking against baseline CNN and ViT models demonstrated superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.95 ± 0.03 vs. 0.88 and 0.90, p < 0.05), confirming the added value of the neuro-symbolic reasoning layer.

evidence.title: Validation of an AI-Based platform for structured diagnosis of headache disorders using ICHD-3 criteria
evidence.outcome: Top-diagnosis accuracy of Head.AI versus other LLM platforms on the same vignettes
evidence.effect: Head.AI identified the top diagnosis in 89.5% of cases vs. 74-80% for comparators; ORs vs. comparators 2.04-2.86, all p < 0.01.
evidence.quote: The algorithm correctly identified the top diagnosis in 89.5% of cases (vs. 74-80% in comparators), with a citation rate >97% and calibration (Brier score 0.153).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence versus human expertise: reliability of ChatGPT and the London atlas for dental age estimation using panoramic radiographs
evidence.outcome: Accuracy (MAE, RMSE) of ChatGPT versus London Atlas method on same images
evidence.effect: ChatGPT had higher MAE and RMSE than the London Atlas, indicating lower accuracy and greater variability; errors were largest in 6-, 12-, and 13-year-olds.
evidence.quote: Compared with the LA, ChatGPT exhibited higher MAE and RMSE values, indicating lower predictive accuracy and greater variability.

evidence.title: Chat, Gemini and Claude at the dinner table: assessing general-purpose AI tools for carbohydrate counting in the context of type 1 diabetes
evidence.outcome: AI carbohydrate estimate error compared with expert dietitians on same meals
evidence.effect: Errors significantly higher for Gemini and Claude than dietitians, but not for ChatGPT (MAE 20±18 g vs 13±10 g).
evidence.quote: Errors were significantly higher for Gemini and Claude, but not for ChatGPT.

evidence.title: Risk Factor Assessment and Predictive Modeling for Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia: Design and Clinical Implementation of an Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Early Detection Framework Using Multisource Data Analytics
evidence.outcome: Model AUC compared against clinical pulmonary infection score (CPIS) for VAP prediction
evidence.effect: MM-HNN AUC 0.86 (95% CI 0.80-0.91), outperforming CPIS (p = 0.021).
evidence.quote: The model achieved an area under the curve of 0.86 (95% confidence interval: 0.80-0.91), outperforming the clinical pulmonary infection score (p = 0.021).
evidence.sample_unit: adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation >48 h

evidence.title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
evidence.outcome: AI CAD vs radiologists diagnostic yield and PPV on same CXRs
evidence.effect: CAD DYD 229/273 (83.9%) vs radiologists 70/273 (25.6%); CAD PPV 1.7% vs radiologists 10.3%; CAD captured all 70 radiologist-detected cases.
evidence.quote: Among the 273 patients with confirmed PTB, CAD achieved DYD of 83.9% (229/273), which was substantially higher than that of radiologists (70/273, 25.6%).

evidence.title: Using generative AI for the objective assessment of language in healthcare
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 predictions versus simpler benchmark linguistic features in explaining VABS-II variance
evidence.effect: GPT-4 predictions accounted for significantly more variance than benchmark linguistic features; correlation with VABS-II scores r > 0.65.
evidence.quote: The model's predictions also accounted for significantly more variance than that explained by the benchmark linguistic features.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models in rare maculopathy
evidence.outcome: MLLM diagnostic accuracy compared against retinal specialists on same cases
evidence.effect: Human specialists' accuracy 0.571-0.714 (broad list) and 0.804-0.839 (limited list) vs best MLLM 0.298 and 0.561; MLLMs performed poorly versus specialists.
evidence.quote: However currently, in rare diseases such as the maculopathies studied in the present paper, MLLMs perform poorly when compared to retinal specialists, and their use is unlikely to aid clinical assessment.

evidence.title: Performance of gastroenterologists and multimodal LLMs in endoscopic EREFS scoring of Eosinophilic Esophagitis
evidence.venue: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: EREFS scoring accuracy of multimodal LLMs versus GI specialists and fellows against anchor-rater
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy: fellows 72.4%, specialists 65.3%, LLMs 58.9% (p<0.001). LLMs beat specialists on edema (83.3% vs 49.3%) but were worse on rings (30% vs 58%). After few-shot prompting LLMs matched specialists (62.7% vs 65.3%, p=0.3).
evidence.quote: Overall assessment accuracy was significantly higher among GI fellows (72.4 %) compared to specialists (65.3 %, p = 0.004) and LLMs (58.9 %, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
evidence.outcome: AI performance compared against original pathologist sign-out at CIN2+ threshold
evidence.effect: Using P1 as reference, EagleEye sensitivity 93.3% (56/60), specificity 71.8% (28/39); agreement with P1 κ=0.67.
evidence.quote: Against P1 as reference, EE identified 56/60 CIN2+ cases (sensitivity 93.3%) with specificity 71.8% (28/39), corresponding to 11 false positives (P1 <CIN2) and 4 false negatives.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models Against Multidisciplinary Tumor Boards in Urological Oncology: Results from the Blinded, Prospective CONCORDIA Study
evidence.outcome: LLM treatment recommendation quality (mSCS) versus real multidisciplinary tumor boards, noninferiority margin 0.15
evidence.effect: MTB mean mSCS 0.849; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.731 (95% CI 0.697-0.765) narrowly missed noninferiority margin of 0.699; ChatGPT-4 0.660 (95% CI 0.623-0.696) clearly below.
evidence.quote: The mean mSCS score of the MTBs was 0.849 (standard deviation [SD] = 0.157), setting the noninferiority margin at 0.699.

evidence.title: Performance of a deep learning-based algorithm for automated measurements of Cobb angles on preoperative spine radiographs in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
evidence.outcome: Cobb angle mean absolute error of AI versus radiology residents against expert consensus ground truth
evidence.effect: Overall AI MAE 4.57° (95%CI 3.85–5.29), significantly higher than residents (P=0.0017); no significant difference for moderate and severe scoliosis per the conclusion.
evidence.quote: Overall, the AI's MAE was 4.57° [95%CI 3.85°, 5.29°], significantly higher than that of the residents' (P=0.0017).
evidence.sample_unit: Cobb angles on preoperative whole spine radiographs

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of BI-RADS Classification, Clinical Management, and Diagnostic Performance in Breast Ultrasound Reports Using ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3
evidence.venue: Seminars in ultrasound, CT, and MR
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity of LLMs versus experienced radiologist on the same breast ultrasound reports
evidence.effect: Radiologist sensitivity 0.989, DeepSeek-V3 0.968, ChatGPT 0.927; specificity 0.735-0.753 and PPV 0.403-0.436 comparable across models.
evidence.quote: The radiologist recorded the highest malignancy detection sensitivity (0.989), followed by DeepSeek-V3 (0.968) and ChatGPT (0.927).

evidence.title: Deep Learning for Coronary Stenosis Detection in Heavily Calcified Plaques at Coronary CT Angiography: A Stepwise, Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: Model AUC versus clinical reports on prospectively collected CCTA examinations
evidence.effect: Model demonstrated 53% specificity and a higher AUC versus clinical reports (0.91 vs 0.76; P < .001).
evidence.quote: In external testing dataset 3, the model demonstrated 53% specificity and a higher AUC versus clinical reports (0.91 vs 0.76; P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: CCTA examinations (development); external tests 442, 120, and 150 examinations

evidence.title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
evidence.venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
evidence.outcome: Extraction error rate of LLM versus manual abstraction against adjudicated ground truth
evidence.effect: LLM error rate 7.0% vs manual abstraction 14.2% (P<0.001) across 8708 datapoints for 28 variables
evidence.quote: Across 8708 datapoints for 28 variables with only one correct answer, the LLM achieved a 7.0% error rate, outperforming manual abstraction (14.2%, P <0.001).

evidence.title: An AI-powered tongue image model for home-based monitoring of liver fibrosis
evidence.outcome: AUC for liver fibrosis detection versus state-of-the-art image models on same data
evidence.effect: TongVMoe AUC 0.8061 versus DiffMIC-v2 0.6929, HorNet 0.7018, InceptionNeXt 0.7012, LSNet 0.6971, TransXNet 0.7062.
evidence.quote: The model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8061, outperforming State-of-the-Art methods such as DiffMIC-v2 (0.6929), HorNet (0.7018), InceptionNeXt (0.7012), LSNet (0.6971), and TransXNet (0.7062).

evidence.title: Retrospective validation study of a large language model approach to screening for intraabdominal surgical site infections for quality and safety reporting
evidence.outcome: LLM screening PPV and NPV versus current EHR-based screening workflow for intra-abdominal SSI
evidence.effect: LLM flagged 104 cases high risk, PPV 53.8%, NPV 100%; EHR-based workflow flagged 288 cases, PPV 19.4%, NPV 100%.
evidence.quote: In contrast, the EHR-based workflow identified 288 cases for further review, with a PPV of only 19.4% and the same NPV of 100%.

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence models in childhood exanthematous diseases: a comparative analysis against clinical diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models vs consultant and resident physicians against definitive diagnosis
evidence.effect: Consultant 96.6%; ChatGPT with clinical data 86.9%, Copilot 81.4%, Gemini 78.7%; resident 72.5%. Consultant superior to all other interpreters and models (p < .001).
evidence.quote: The consultant's diagnostic performance was significantly superior to all other interpreters and models (p < .001 for all comparisons).

evidence.title: ARTEMIS: a pilot study comparing AI-based and expert therapeutic decisions in simulated clinical cases of neuroendocrine neoplasms
evidence.outcome: Agreement with expert systemic therapy benchmark
evidence.effect: GPT 60.0%; GPTs 70.0%; RAG 70.0%; GPTs/RAG met –10% but not –5% non-inferiority.
evidence.quote: Against this benchmark, baseline GPT achieved 60.0% (95% CI 44.4–76.9), GPTs 70.0% (95% CI 54.5–85.7), and the retrieval-augmented model (RAG) 70.0% (95% CI 54.5–84.6).

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models for antimicrobial classification: implications for antimicrobial stewardship programs
evidence.outcome: Comparison of four LLMs against manual reference standard on same medication data
evidence.effect: Phase 1 accuracy: Claude 99.1%, Gemini 98.7%, ChatGPT-3.5 75.4%, Copilot 74.7%; Gemini and Claude significantly outperformed ChatGPT-3.5 and Copilot (all P < .001).
evidence.quote: Both Gemini and Claude significantly outperformed ChatGPT-3.5 and Copilot (all P < .001).

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, and DeepSeek-R1 in BI-RADS Category 4 Classification and Malignancy Prediction From Mammography Reports: Retrospective Diagnostic Study
evidence.outcome: LLM vs junior and senior radiologists diagnostic performance (AUC) on BI-RADS 4 malignancy prediction
evidence.effect: LLM AUCs 0.61-0.64 vs junior 0.72 and senior 0.75; all three LLMs significantly worse than both radiologist groups (all P<.05); accuracy 60.8-63.5% vs 72.0-74.5%.
evidence.quote: DeLong testing confirmed that all three LLMs performed significantly worse than both junior and senior radiologists (all P<.05), and no significant difference was observed between the two radiologist groups (P=.55).

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Specialist Physicians in Breast Care Triaging: A Real-World Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ML triage model versus specialist physicians on same cases
evidence.effect: ML model accuracy 100% vs physicians 83.9%; sensitivity 0.947 vs 0.826; PPV 0.500 vs 0.442; AUC 0.91 vs 0.83 for first prediction.
evidence.quote: The ML model demonstrated superior diagnostic accuracy (100%) compared to physicians (83.9%), with higher sensitivity (0.947 vs. 0.826) and PPV (0.500 vs. 0.442).

evidence.title: Secretary or SecretarAI: assessing the triage performance of AI vs human staff in a specialized dental clinic
evidence.venue: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology
evidence.outcome: Agreement with expert gold-standard triage ranking, LLMs versus secretaries and dental assistants
evidence.effect: AI agreement with expert gold standard Fleiss' κ = 0.572 vs dental assistants κ = 0.249 and secretaries κ = 0.227; GPT-o3 highest weighted κ = 0.681.
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) models demonstrated significantly higher agreement with the expert gold standard (Fleiss' κ = 0.572) compared to dental assistants (κ = 0.249) and secretaries (κ = 0.227).

evidence.title: Evaluating the appropriateness and safety of generative AI in delivering lifestyle guidance for atrial fibrillation patients
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM responses against electrophysiologist responses on ten dimensions
evidence.effect: GPT-4o had lower error rates and higher specialized content (OR 10.80), empathy (OR 5.55), and helpfulness (OR 6.74) than the electrophysiologist; RAG models were comparable.
evidence.quote: For Evidence of Incorrect Comprehension, GPT-4o demonstrated a significantly lower error rate compared with the electrophysiologist (OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.40–8.30), whereas DB GPT and PubMed GPT showed comparable performance (OR 1.06 [0.49–2.29] and 0.64 [0.30–1.37], respectively).

evidence.title: Does DeepSeek Provide Clinically Acceptable Intraocular Lens (IOL) Power Predictions in Cataract Surgery? A Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Prediction error of DeepSeek-R1 vs Barrett Universal II formula against measured postoperative refraction
evidence.effect: Barrett MedAE 0.36 D and MAE 0.43 D vs DeepSeek-R1 MedAE 0.76 D and MAE 0.77 D; Barrett better (Wilcoxon p<0.0001); within ±0.50 D 71.7% vs 25.9%.
evidence.quote: The paired comparison of per-eye absolute errors favored Barrett (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Detecting Suicidal Ideation in Adolescence Using Self-Reported Emotional and Behavioral Patterns: Comparing Machine Learning and Large Language Model Predictions
evidence.outcome: Suicidal ideation detection performance of LLM-based versus SDQ-trained ML models on the same data
evidence.effect: SDQ-trained ML models consistently outperformed LLM-prediction models across all SIQ-JR thresholds. Best SDQ-based model: sensitivity .85, specificity .72. Best LLM-based model: sensitivity .80, specificity .74.
evidence.quote: Notably, ML models trained directly on SDQ responses consistently outperformed those incorporating LLM predictions across all SIQ-JR thresholds.

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of AI language models in educating patients on women's sexual health
evidence.outcome: LLM response accuracy and relevance versus existing Prosayla patient education website, rated by two experts
evidence.effect: No significant accuracy differences across four sources (Physician A p=0.558; Physician B p=0.052); ChatGPT more accurate than Prosayla per Physician B (p=0.044); Physician B rated all AI models more relevant (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: No significant differences in accuracy scores were observed across the four sources for Physician A (p = 0.558) or Physician B (p = 0.052), although ChatGPT was rated significantly more accurate than Prosayla in post hoc analysis by Physician B (p = 0.044).

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy compared with neuroradiologists, residents, and machine learning baselines on the same cases
evidence.effect: GPT-4o matched expert neuroradiologist with expert features (94.3% vs 92.5%) and beat resident (79.2%); with raw images all LLMs were significantly worse than radiologists (p<0.05).
evidence.quote: Performance was moderate with resident-derived structured features (71.7-73.6%), significantly better than raw image input (p < 0.05), but declined markedly with raw images alone (18.9-52.8%), where all LLMs performed significantly worse than radiologists (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Automated Protocoling of Abdominal and Pelvic CT Scans: The Power of Context
evidence.outcome: Optimal protocol selection by LLM versus radiologists' human-selected protocols on the same cases
evidence.effect: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more often than humans (96.2% [527/548] vs 88.3% [484/548]; P < .001); inappropriate protocols 1.3% vs 2.4%, P = .21.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more frequently than humans (96.2% [527 of 548 patients] vs 88.3% [484 of 548 patients]; P < .001), but there was no evidence of a difference in inappropriate protocols (1.3% [seven of 548 patients] vs 2.4% [13 of 548 patients]; P = .21).

evidence.title: A Large Language Model Assistant for Summarizing Hepatology Referral Documents
evidence.outcome: Time to triage AI summary files versus original referral files
evidence.effect: 60% reduction in triage time; adjusted mean 37.2 seconds for AI files vs 94.2 seconds for original files, P < 0.001.
evidence.quote: Use of the AI summaries led to a 60% reduction in triage time (adjusted mean triage time of 37.2 seconds for AI files vs 94.2 seconds for original files, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-5 for drug-drug interaction detection in the intensive care unit: A real-world cohort study on large language model advances and implications for clinical pharmacists
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT pDDI detection versus standard interaction checkers, discrimination and clinical utility
evidence.effect: ChatGPT identified fewer interactions than standard databases (8 and 10 vs. 22 total; 1 and 2 vs. 4 significant per patient); none outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.
evidence.quote: None of the versions outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.

evidence.title: Retrospective modeling study of ChatGPT (GPT 4) warfarin dose adjustment in patients with INRs outside the therapeutic range
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 warfarin dose recommendations compared with physician dosing and modeled INR normalization
evidence.effect: Doses within ±1 mg/week of physician in 74% and ±2 mg/week in 84%; mean 27.5 vs 28.0 mg/week (p=.12); modeled therapeutic INR 69% vs 72% (p=.15).
evidence.quote: Seventy-two percent of patients achieved therapeutic INR under physician-managed dosing, while the model suggested a 69% success rate for ChatGPT-guided dosing (p = .15).

evidence.title: Identifying Volar Locking Plates on Plain Radiographs: Can Artificial Intelligence Models 'Beat' Clinicians?
evidence.outcome: Manufacturer identification accuracy of ChatGPT 5 versus five hand consultants on the same radiographs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 5 correctly identified 3 of 52 (5.8%); consultants 13.5-46.2% (mean 30.8%); humans had 7.26 times higher odds of correct identification (OR 7.26, 95% CI 2.27-23.18, p<0.001).
evidence.quote: In a standard logistic regression with clustered standard errors, the human cohort had 7.26 times higher odds of correct identification compared with the AI (OR 7.26, 95% CI 2.27-23.18, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Enabled Editing of Patient Audio Interviews From "This Is My Story" Conversations: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Blinded expert ratings of AI-edited vs expert- and novice-edited audio summaries
evidence.effect: Expert audio 4.84/content 4.83; novice 3.84/3.63; AI 3.49/3.20. AI and novice rated significantly lower than expert (P<.001) but not significantly different from each other.
evidence.quote: Novice and AI edits were rated significantly lower than the expert edits (P<.001), but not significantly different from each other.

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of five AI platforms for mandibular canal segmentation on CBCT images
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy compared across five competing AI platforms against expert reference on same scans
evidence.effect: Significant differences among platforms (p < 0.001); Relu Creator and 3D Slicer most accurate (≈0.5 mm, no >2.0 mm deviations); Atomica and BlueSkyPlan more variable with more deviations >2.0 mm.
evidence.quote: Significant performance differences were observed among platforms (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: AI Decision-Making Performance in Maternal-Fetal Medicine: Comparison of ChatGPT-4, Gemini, and Human Specialists in a Cross-Sectional Case-Based Study
evidence.outcome: LLM vs MFM specialist accuracy ratings on same hypothetical cases, blinded evaluation
evidence.effect: No significant difference between ChatGPT-4 and clinicians in median accuracy (Wilcoxon p = 0.18); Gemini significantly lower accuracy (p < 0.01).
evidence.quote: No significant difference was found between ChatGPT-4 and clinicians in median accuracy scores (Wilcoxon p = 0.18), while Gemini showed significantly lower accuracy (p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Bridging the analog divide: a comparison of printed X-ray films and digital images when using computer-aided detection software for tuberculosis screening
evidence.outcome: Genki specificity versus 10 human readers at matched sensitivity for TB screening
evidence.effect: At matched sensitivity (79.0%), Genki specificity was 95.2% (DICOM) and 92.1% (JPEG) versus 84.8% for human readers, p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: The corresponding specificity for the Genki software is significantly higher than the human readers, whether using the DICOM (84.8% vs 95.2%, p < 0.001) or JPEG files (84.8% vs 92.1%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Foundation models enable wearable signal screening for cardiovascular disease among people living with HIV
evidence.outcome: CVD detection AUROC and average precision
evidence.effect: The AI approach achieved AUROC 0.769 and average precision 0.489, outperforming simpler PCA features (0.651; 0.208) and supervised clinical models (0.744; 0.433).
evidence.quote: Here we show that the PaPaGei-embedding approach achieves area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.769 (95% confidence interval: 0.70, 0.84) and average precision 0.489 (0.37, 0.61) in this pilot cohort, numerically higher than zero-shot NormWear (0.610; 0.226), principal component analysis features (0.651; 0.208), and supervised clinical models (0.744; 0.433).

evidence.title: Human-AI collaboration enhances the performance of large language models in risk of bias assessment
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two candidate LLMs on risk-of-bias classification accuracy
evidence.effect: DeepSeek V3 outperformed Qwen-plus in four of seven domains (PB, AB, RB, OB); Qwen-plus slightly better in SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, DB.
evidence.quote: The results shown in Fig. 3 indicate that DeepSeek V3 outperforms Qwen-plus in the tasks of PB, AB, RB, and OB, whereas Qwen-plus performs slightly better in the tasks of SB-IRSG, SB-IAC, and DB.
evidence.sample_unit: domain-level RCT risk-of-bias assessments (300 per domain across 7 domains; 60 per domain in human-AI collaboration round)

evidence.title: Direct deep learning analysis of three-dimensional automated breast ultrasound videos with reading mode optimization for breast cancer diagnosis
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with experienced and novice radiologists on same data
evidence.effect: AI vs experienced: AUC 0.82 vs 0.83 (P=0.230); vs novice: AUC 0.82 vs 0.68 (P<0.001), specificity 81.5% vs 57.4% (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Compared with novice radiologists in independent-reading mode, DL-3DABUV showed significantly higher AUC (0.82 vs. 0.68, P<0.001) and specificity (81.5% vs. 57.4%, P<0.001), while maintaining comparable sensitivity (82.1% vs. 79.2%, P=0.590).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (test set; 547 total, read by 6 radiologists)

evidence.title: PREDICTING POSTOPERATIVE OUTCOMES IN FULL-THICKNESS MACULAR HOLE REPAIR SURGERY: ChatGPT Versus Clinical Decision
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-5 versus retina specialists in predicting FTMH surgery outcomes on same cases
evidence.effect: Anatomical accuracy 72-86% (specialists) vs 90% (ChatGPT-5); functional accuracy 42-44% (specialists) vs 66% (ChatGPT-5), but ChatGPT missed all nonclosure cases and worsened cases (optimism bias).
evidence.quote: The anatomical prediction accuracy was 72% to 86% (specialists) and 90% (ChatGPT-5).

evidence.title: A comparative study on DeepSeek and ChatGPT for bone and soft tissue tumor clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head accuracy of two LLMs on bone and soft tissue tumor questions versus expert answers
evidence.effect: DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT in overall accuracy (74.7% vs 55.4%, p < 0.001); single-choice 86.9% vs 64.9%; Pathology & Genetics 72.5% vs 40.0%; Treatment 71.3% vs 51.2%.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT in overall accuracy (74.7% vs 55.4%, p < 0.001), excelling in single-choice questions (86.9% vs 64.9%, p < 0.001) and two key domains: Pathology & Genetics (72.5% vs 40.0%, p = 0.006) and Treatment (71.3% vs 51.2%, p = 0.015).

evidence.title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity for high-severity patients, LLM versus initial nurse triage and baseline LLM
evidence.effect: MECR-RAG sensitivity for R1+R2 124/130 (95.4%) vs nurses 117/130 (90.0%) (P=.02) and baseline LLM 122/130 (93.8%); specificity similar to nurses.
evidence.quote: When high-severity outcomes were defined as R1+R2 (n=130) and triage “positive” as categories 1 - 3 versus 4 - 5, MECR‑RAG achieved the highest sensitivity for high-risk courses at 124/130 (95.4%), compared with 117/130 (90.0%) for initial nurse triage and 122/130 (93.8%) for the baseline LLM.

evidence.title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
evidence.outcome: Net benefit of recalibrated models versus treat-all and operative severity proxy in decision curve analysis
evidence.effect: For any morbidity, no incremental benefit over treat-all or proxy; major morbidity exceeded treat-all in 76.3% of thresholds and proxy in 46.1%; mortality exceeded proxy in 85.2%.
evidence.quote: Compared with the operative severity proxy (mean net benefit 0.173), the recalibrated model was higher in 46.1% of the thresholds, suggesting a modest and threshold-dependent incremental advantage (Fig. 4 B).

evidence.title: Cross specialty evaluation of large language model responses on intentional replantation
evidence.venue: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
evidence.outcome: Specialist-perceived accuracy and completeness of two LLMs on intentional replantation questions
evidence.effect: LLM type had a significant main effect on perceived accuracy and completeness (p < 0.001), with OpenEvidence scoring higher than ChatGPT 4.0 on both.
evidence.quote: The LMM analyses demonstrated that LLM type had a significant main effect on both perceived accuracy and completeness (p < 0.001), with OpenEvidence receiving higher scores than ChatGPT 4.0 for both outcomes.

evidence.title: Can ChatGPT compete with emergency medicine specialists? A two-stage assessment of ECG interpretation supported by clinical information
evidence.outcome: AI ECG interpretation compared against emergency medicine specialists on same ECGs
evidence.effect: Specialists outperformed ECG Reader-GPT in all diagnostic subgroups and both stages (77% vs 24%; 79% vs 27%), so the AI would not have been selected over clinicians.
evidence.quote: EMSs consistently outperformed ECG Reader-GPT under all conditions, indicating that the model is currently insufficient for real-world ECG interpretation.

evidence.title: Benchmark evaluation of deepseek AI models in antibacterial clinical decision-making for infectious diseases
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Concordance and performance of DeepSeek and ChatGPT o1 antibacterial regimens versus ID specialists' effective regimens
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3 had the highest concordance with ID specialists, exceeding DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT o1. DeepSeek-R1, R1+WS, and ChatGPT o1 escalated to higher AWaRe tiers significantly more than ID specialists (P<0.005). DeepSeek was comparable to ChatGPT o1.
evidence.quote: Moreover, DeepSeek's antibacterial clinical decision-making is comparable to that of ChatGPT o1, with DeepSeek-V3 surpassing it in certain performance metrics.

evidence.title: A comparative evaluation of large language models for simplifying prostate cancer pathology reports: ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.outcome: model comparison across simplification metrics
evidence.effect: Across 228 reports, GPT-4o (Few-Shot) had highest pathologist accuracy/comprehensiveness, while Gemini had best understandability; no numeric scores reported.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o (Few-Shot) achieved the highest accuracy and comprehensiveness scores from pathologists, while Gemini demonstrated the best understandability.

evidence.title: Translating evidence into practice: adapting TrialGPT for real-world clinical trial eligibility screening
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity in identifying truly eligible patients: adapted TrialGPT versus manual screening
evidence.effect: System identified more than twice as many truly eligible patients than manual screening (81.8% vs 36.4%) with equivalent specificity, n = 55.
evidence.quote: Compared with manual screening, it identified more than twice as many truly eligible patients (81.8% vs 36.4%) while preserving equivalent specificity.
evidence.sample_unit: patient-trial eligibility determinations in expert-adjudicated gold corpus (plus 55 in manual screening comparison)

evidence.title: Association of echocardiographic findings with mortality: human assessment vs. automated deep learning analysis
evidence.outcome: AI vs human expert echo analysis association with 1-year mortality (AUC)
evidence.effect: Multivariable AI and human mortality prediction were comparable (AUC 0.67 vs 0.66, P=0.86); adding AI automated strain analysis, AI model was superior (AUC 0.73 vs 0.66, P=0.048). AI LVEF was 5.8% higher than human.
evidence.quote: Incorporating automated strain analysis resulted stronger association with mortality of the AI analysis compared to standard human analysis.

evidence.title: Multimodal large language model versus emergency physicians for burn assessment: a prospective non-inferiority study
evidence.venue: Scandinavian journal of trauma, resuscitation and emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: Model versus emergency physicians on TBSA error and burn depth agreement against expert panel
evidence.effect: TBSA: model MAE 1.40 vs physician median 0.89 pp; non-inferior (HL median Δ 0.25, upper bound 0.50). Depth: model kappa 0.14 vs physicians 0.65.
evidence.quote: In contrast, depth agreement versus the panel was slight for the model (quadratic-weighted kappa 0.14), with systematic underestimation of deeper burns, while physician consensus showed substantially higher agreement (quadratic-weighted kappa 0.65).

evidence.title: Estimated impact of model-guided venous thromboembolism prophylaxis versus real-world practice
evidence.outcome: Total VTE and major bleeding events per 1000 patients, model-guided vs real-world clinician prophylaxis
evidence.effect: Model-based strategies produced 14.0-16.1 events per 1000 vs 14.3 for real-world practice; best model reduced prophylaxis by 55% and total events by 0.14%. Padua & IMPROVE caused the most total events.
evidence.quote: Overall, per 1000 patients, model-based strategies produced 14.0-16.1 events compared with 14.3 for real-world practice.

evidence.title: Large Language Models and Surgical Decision-Making: Evaluation of Generative Unimodal AI in Facial Traumatology Practice
evidence.venue: Journal of maxillofacial and oral surgery
evidence.outcome: LLM vs maxillofacial surgery residents on QAMAI quality scores across 30 cases
evidence.effect: Human surgery residents consistently scored higher than the LLMs across all QAMAI parameters (accuracy, clarity, relevance, completeness, references, usefulness); ChatGPT-4 outperformed Bard on additional examinations and treatment plans.
evidence.quote: Compared to LLMs, human surgery residents consistently scored higher across all parameters of the QAMAI tool, indicating superior accuracy, clarity, relevance, completeness, quality of references, and overall usefulness.

evidence.title: Development of BERT-based large language models for emergency department triage using real-world conversations
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy of developed models versus GPT-4o and ClinicalBERT on same test data
evidence.effect: Hierarchical model accuracy 75.94% vs ChatGPT 56.68% and fine-tuned ClinicalBERT 69.42%; urgent-case recall 0.9610 vs ChatGPT 0.5352.
evidence.quote: Our model with hierarchical structure achieved accuracies of 75.94%, significantly outperforming ChatGPT (56.68%) or fine-tuned ClinicalBERT (69.42%).

evidence.title: Large language models for predicting one-year major adverse cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome
evidence.outcome: LLM ROC performance compared with GRACE and TIMI scores for one-year MACE
evidence.effect: None of the LLMs outperformed traditional clinical scores; ChatGPT 4o performed below both GRACE and TIMI score.
evidence.quote: ROC analysis indicated that none of the LLMs outperformed traditional clinical scores, with ChatGPT 4o performing below both GRACE and TIMI score.

evidence.title: Colon-Pilot: A Generative AI Tool for Automated Colonoscopy Surveillance Recommendations and 2024 ACG/ASGE Quality Benchmarking
evidence.outcome: Guideline-concordant surveillance accuracy of AI versus original endoscopist recommendations
evidence.effect: Guideline-concordant accuracy 97.5% (κ = 0.970) for AI versus 69.7% (κ = 0.781) for original endoscopist recommendations.
evidence.quote: For automated cases, guideline-concordant accuracy was 97.5% (Cohen κ = 0.970) versus 69.7% (κ = 0.781) for original endoscopist recommendations.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-5 Matches Surgeon-Level Assessment of Facelift Candidacy: A Pilot Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT-5 with board-certified surgeon consensus on facelift candidacy and aging features
evidence.effect: Facelift candidacy agreement 95.5% (21/22; κ=0.91; McNemar P=1.00); binary aging features 81.8-90.9% (κ≈0.61-0.81); ordinal severity exact agreement 77.3%, weighted κ 0.74-0.86.
evidence.quote: For facelift candidacy, agreement was 95.5% (21/22; Cohen's κ = 0.91; McNemar P = 1.00).

evidence.title: Prompt Engineering for Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Status Extraction: Comparing Large Language Model Techniques
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM prompting methods against rule-based NLP for ECOG extraction
evidence.effect: CoT and DFT achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the rule-based method (91%) and simple prompting (86%).
evidence.quote: Both CoT and double filtering technique (DFT) achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the rule-based method (91%) and simple prompting (86%).

evidence.title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
evidence.outcome: AI sensitivity and NPV compared with working radiologist reports on same data
evidence.effect: At 0.125, sensitivity 90.10% vs 80.7% and NPV 89.01% vs 81.66% for radiologist, with non-overlapping CIs.
evidence.quote: At threshold 0.125, Lunit-enabled workflow demonstrates superior performance compared with the radiologist report, with significantly higher sensitivity (90.10% (95% CI 87.19% to 92.86%) vs 80.7% (95% CI 76.83% to 84.42%)) and NPV (89.01% (95% CI 85.71% to 92.05%) vs 81.66% (95% CI 77.95% to 85.24%)), with non-overlapping CIs in both metrics confirming the statistical significance of these differences.

evidence.title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
evidence.outcome: GPT-5 and GPT-5-assisted radiologists compared against unassisted and expert abdominal radiologist
evidence.effect: Abdominal radiologist accuracy 92% exceeded unassisted juniors (P<0.001) but did not differ from assisted juniors; assisted juniors outperformed the abdominal radiologist on differentials (P=0.002, 0.001).
evidence.quote: Comparatively, AR achieved an accuracy of 92% (79/86; 95% CI: 85%–97%), which was superior to the accuracy of R1 and R2 without GPT-5 assistance ( P < 0.001) but not significantly different from their performances with both browser-based GPT-5 and GPT-5 with the optimal settings ( Table 4 ).

evidence.title: AI-assisted interpretation of bone scans: Performance comparison between ChatGPT-4o and a TFDA-approved bone scintigraphy platform in AI-driven nuclear imaging interpretation
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-4o vs domain-specific platform vs physician gold standard on same bone scans
evidence.effect: Binary accuracy 84.6% (ChatGPT-4o) vs 82.7% (platform); regional precision 32.5% vs 80.3%; regional sensitivity 13.3% vs 64.9%.
evidence.quote: In binary classification, ChatGPT-4o achieved an accuracy of 84.6%, similar to the performance of the BS platform's accuracy of 82.7%.

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
evidence.venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
evidence.outcome: Comparison of 9 LLMs against each other on NVAF anticoagulation tasks
evidence.effect: Models varied substantially across 6 tasks; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research ranked first overall, DeepSeek-V3 lowest; no single model best across all tasks.
evidence.quote: The results showed that no single model performed optimally across all tasks.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

evidence.title: Diagnosing growth in low-grade gliomas with and without artificial intelligence-measured longitudinal volume measurements: A retrospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Time to tumor growth detection by AI volumetry versus radiologist visual inspection
evidence.effect: AI with human review detected growth a median of 21 months earlier than visual inspection in the clinical progression group, and 23 months earlier than last MRI in 13/22 clinically stable cases.
evidence.quote: The results demonstrate that volumetric analysis calculated by AI segmentation followed by human review detects tumor growth significantly earlier than traditional visual inspection by radiologists (median of 21 months, Table 1 , and Figure 1 ).

evidence.title: Vision transformer-based diagnosis of psoriasis and eczema in whole-slide histology
evidence.venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
evidence.outcome: AI accuracy versus dermatopathologists and baseline CNNs on same external cohort
evidence.effect: Virchow + CLAM 85% accuracy on external cohort vs individual readers 47.5-70.0%, consensus 62.5%, baseline CNNs 61%.
evidence.quote: In a reader study on the same external cohort, individual dermatopathologist accuracies ranged from 47.5 to 70.0%, with a majority-vote consensus accuracy of 62.5%; our method outperformed both the average individual reader and the consensus under histology-only conditions.

evidence.title: Explainable and evidence-linked recommendations for spine surgery via a retrieval-augmented LLM agent
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated overall score comparing four LLM agents on same spinal cases
evidence.effect: Gemini 2.5 Flash 49.25 ± 2.88 vs DeepSeek 47.49 ± 3.34, GPT-4o 45.59 ± 3.89, GPT-4o-mini 41.23 ± 5.96 (all P < 0.001), showing substantial inter-model variability.
evidence.quote: Gemini 2.5 Flash achieved the highest overall score (49.25 ± 2.88), significantly outperforming DeepSeek (47.49 ± 3.34, P < 0.001), GPT-4o (45.59 ± 3.89, P < 0.001), and GPT-4o-mini (41.23 ± 5.96, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of GPT-5 for Esophageal Cancer Staging Using Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography Maximum-Intensity Projection Images: Comparative Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Staging accuracy of LLMs versus physicians on the same FDG-PET images
evidence.effect: LLM accuracy 34% to 78% versus physicians 60% to 85%; physicians significantly higher (P<.05) for thoracic LN, abdominal LN, and cN stages; LLM kappa -0.07 to 0.25.
evidence.quote: The average accuracy was 41/120 (34%) to 94/120 (78%) for LLMs and 72/120 (60%) to 102/120 (85%) for physicians, with significantly higher accuracy for physicians (P<.05) in the thoracic LN, abdominal LN, and cN stages.

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning vs. human raters for detecting osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures in routine CT scans
evidence.outcome: Fracture detection accuracy of DL models versus human raters of varying expertise on same data
evidence.effect: DL models showed comparable accuracy as residents in detecting moderate/severe fractures (0.988 vs. 0.991, p > 0.05); SpineQ v1.1 had comparable AUROC and higher accuracy than experts; students lowest.
evidence.quote: DL models showed comparable accuracy as residents in detecting moderate/severe fractures (0.988 vs. 0.991, p > 0.05) on vetebral level.

evidence.title: Automatic acromegaly detection using deep learning on hand images: a multicenter observational study
evidence.venue: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
evidence.outcome: Model performance versus endocrinologists (F1-score) for acromegaly detection on hand images
evidence.effect: Model achieved sensitivity 0.89, specificity 0.91, AUC 0.96, outperforming specialists (F1-score range: 0.43-0.63).
evidence.quote: The model achieved a sensitivity of 0.89, specificity of 0.91, positive predictive value of 0.88, negative predictive value of 0.93, F1-score of 0.89, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.96, outperforming specialists (F1-score range: 0.43-0.63).

evidence.title: Improving reliability and accuracy of structured data extraction using a consensus large-language model approach-a use case description in multiple sclerosis
evidence.outcome: LLM consensus extraction accuracy compared with neurology specialists and trained medical personnel on same reports
evidence.effect: LLM consensus true-error rate 1.48% vs NSP ~2%; difference not significant (p=0.6447; OR 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).
evidence.quote: The difference between the LLM consensus evaluation and the NSPs was not significant ( p = 0.6447; odds ratio = 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).

evidence.title: Advancing trauma scoring through large language models: automated estimation of injury severity
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three candidate LLMs against human-assigned ISS on the same data
evidence.effect: GPT-4 and Grok-3 showed high agreement (weighted Kappa 0.88, 0.91) while Perplexity was lower (0.54); ICCs 0.97, 0.92, 0.84.
evidence.quote: ICCs were 0.97 (GPT-4, CI 95% = 0.94–0.98), 0.92 (Grok-3, CI 95% = 0.86–0.95), and 0.84 (Perplexity, CI 95% = 0.73–0.91), demonstrating near-expert-level consistency.

evidence.title: Large language models for structuring knee ultrasound reports-A comparative evaluation of DeepSeek R1, gemini 2.5 flash, and GPT-4o
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three candidate LLMs on the same reports for extraction, impression, recommendation
evidence.effect: GPT-4o had the best diagnostic F1 (0.79 vs 0.54 DeepSeek R1 and 0.45 Gemini 2.5 Flash), highest balanced accuracy and MCC; Gemini 2.5 Flash consistently underperformed.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o consistently outperformed DeepSeek R1 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, supporting its potential to improve knee ultrasound report consistency and clinical utility.

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models against human experts in rehabilitation medicine: a multidimensional evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM-generated rehabilitation plan quality versus senior physiatrist plans, blinded expert ratings
evidence.effect: Grok-4 (mean 4.31), Gemini-2.5-pro (4.14) and Deepseek-r1 (3.69) significantly outperformed human benchmark (3.56); Claude-opus-4 (3.50) did not differ significantly.
evidence.quote: Quantitative analysis revealed that Grok-4 (mean 4.31) and Gemini−2.5-pro (mean 4.14) significantly outperformed the human benchmark (derived from standardized expert solutions) (mean 3.56; [Formula: see text]).

evidence.title: Should we leave paediatric emergency triage to artificial intelligence? A comparison of ChatGPT 4o and Grok 3
evidence.outcome: ESI triage accuracy of LLMs versus nurses, against paediatric specialist gold standard, on same patients
evidence.effect: Accuracy: nurses 53.1%, ChatGPT 4o 76.1%, Grok 3 47.0% (Cochran's Q = 275.68, p < 0.001). ChatGPT 4o outperformed nurses; Grok 3 did not.
evidence.quote: Nurses achieved 53.1% (95% CI: 50.6-55.6) accuracy in triage assessments, while ChatGPT 4o achieved 76.1% (95% CI: 73.9-78.2) and Grok 3 achieved 47.0% (95% CI: 44.5-49.6) accuracy (Cochran's Q = 275.68, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Benchmarking a deep learning model against healthcare practitioners for hip fracture detection in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: DL model performance compared with radiographers and junior doctors on same radiographs
evidence.effect: Radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (P<0.001; sensitivity 99% vs 85%); no significant difference between DL model and ED junior doctors.
evidence.quote: On original high-resolution images, radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (McNemar's test: P < 0.001), achieving a sensitivity of 99% compared to the model's sensitivity of 85%.

evidence.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of tumor size measurement using a deep-learning-based CDSS in resected lung cancer
evidence.outcome: Tumor size measurement agreement of CDSS versus radiologists against pathologic size
evidence.effect: CDSS and radiology reports both showed ICC 0.869 with pathology; no significant difference between radiologists and CDSS; CDSS detected 162/176 (92%) tumors; interobserver ICC 0.907 vs CDSS 1.000
evidence.quote: No significant differences were found in the measurement of tumor size between radiologists and the CDSS.

evidence.title: RAPID CTA versus JLK LVO for large vessel occlusion detection: a pragmatic comparison of performance and common pitfalls
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head LVO detection performance of two commercial AI tools versus neuroradiologist consensus
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.93 for both tools (p = 0.64); at matched 83% sensitivity, JLK LVO specificity 0.96 vs RAPID CTA 0.89.
evidence.quote: Both tools demonstrated high and comparable overall performance (AUROC 0.93 for both, p = 0.64).

evidence.title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Competing transcription tools' word error rates
evidence.effect: NotebookLM: 96 errors, 4.0%; AssemblyAI: 252, 10.4%; Otter.ai: 448, 18.5%.
evidence.quote: Across the two interactions with a mean 2416 target words, NotebookLM demonstrated substantially lower overall word error rates (96 total word errors; 4.0% of target words) compared with AssemblyAI (252; 10.4%) and Otter.ai (448; 18.5%).

evidence.title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Comparison of five LLMs against each other on TCM knowledge and case analysis for model selection
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 had 96.7% knowledge accuracy vs 50.6-66.3% for others, and 17.31/20 case score vs 10.02-16.16; chosen as optimal model (P<.001).
evidence.quote: Based on superior performance across both evaluation domains and a significant advantage of 15.89 points over the second-ranked model, DeepSeek-R1 was selected as the optimal model for phase 4 clinical application and human-AI collaboration assessment.
evidence.sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-powered tiered early warning framework addressing high false alarm rates for in-hospital mortality prediction
evidence.outcome: Compared LLM-based direct risk assessment against ML-based stratification
evidence.effect: LLMs used as standalone classifiers had lower PPV and weaker risk separation than ML risk stratification.
evidence.quote: A direct comparison of the ML-based risk stratification with an LLM-based direct risk assessment (Supplementary Fig. S7 ) revealed that LLMs used as standalone classifiers exhibit lower PPV and weaker risk separation, reinforcing their optimal role as complementary reasoning tools rather than independent prognostic models.

evidence.title: Guideline-based benchmarking of large language models in otorhinolaryngology using 250 real-world cases
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Composite decision-quality scores comparing five LLMs on the same 250 cases
evidence.effect: Composite scores differed among models (p < 0.001); ChatGPT highest (5.72 ± 0.21), outperforming Gemini, DeepSeek, LLaMA and Grok (all p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Composite decision-quality scores (mean of five 6-point Likert domains; 1 = very poor, 6 = excellent) differed among models (p < 0.001), with ChatGPT achieving the highest overall performance (5.72 ± 0.21), outperforming Gemini (p < 0.001), DeepSeek (p < 0.001), LLaMA (p < 0.001), and Grok (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Dosimetric Impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Based Autocontouring Software, OncoStudio, in High-Risk Prostate Cancer Treatment Planning: A Three-Group Comparative Study on the Slice Ranges of Seminal Vesicles
evidence.outcome: Dosimetric parameters of AI autocontours versus manual contours on the same patients
evidence.effect: No significant DVH differences among manual, adjusted AC and unadjusted AC (all p>0.05); CTV Dmean difference -58.7 cGy (p=0.077) for unadjusted AC; differences <1% of prescription; underpowered (n=15).
evidence.quote: No statistically significant differences were observed among the three groups in any dose volume histogram parameters.

evidence.title: The performance boundaries of knowledge prompts: A study on injection strategies and scale effects for ICD coding tasks in large language models
evidence.outcome: Comparing five LLMs and five prompt strategies on the same coding data
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3 significantly outperformed other models across all three tasks (P<0.002); Doubao-1.5 was lowest at 61.0% primary diagnosis accuracy.
evidence.quote: Overall, DeepSeek-V3 significantly outperformed the other models across all three coding tasks, demonstrating comprehensive and consistent superiority.

evidence.title: Automated Flow and local LLM-Driven clinical Context Engineering: Precision colorectal cancer recurrence registry
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of rule-based LLM versus standard Taiwan Cancer Registry process against manual reference
evidence.effect: Rule-Based LLM achieved 90.7% accuracy, comparable to standard TCR processes (92.0%), with 77.2% sensitivity.
evidence.quote: Under a strict 60-day temporal tolerance, the Rule-Based LLM achieved 90.7% accuracy, comparable to standard TCR processes (92.0%), and 77.2% sensitivity.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (20% manual reference standard subset of 3053 CRC patients)

evidence.title: Advancing clinical utility of artificial intelligence: lessons from developing a model to predict cochlear implant eligibility
evidence.outcome: Model sensitivity and PPV versus existing referral heuristics for CI candidacy
evidence.effect: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).
evidence.quote: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o as a text-based clinical decision support tool for junior otolaryngology residents: A randomized controlled trial
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: AIPI scores of ChatGPT-4o versus board-certified otolaryngologist on same PGY1 consultation outputs
evidence.effect: Mean AIPI score for ChatGPT-4o was higher than otolaryngologist (14.20 ± 2.24 versus 12.34 ± 1.91; p = 0.001); comparable on history, clinical presentation, primary diagnosis, management plan.
evidence.quote: The mean AIPI score for ChatGPT-4o was significantly higher than the otolaryngologist score (14.20 ± 2.24 versus 12.34 ± 1.91; p = 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: PGY1 resident consultation outputs (40 per group)

evidence.title: Performance validation of large language models for drug-drug interaction consultations: Potential pharmacist assistant in outpatient pharmaceutical services
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: LLM responses compared against pharmacist answers on the same queries
evidence.effect: Four LLMs compared with pharmacists' answers; consistency 84.85%-89.09%; DeepSeek R1 achieved 3-4-point scores in 137 queries.
evidence.quote: In scored evaluations, DeepSeek R1 achieved the highest score, achieving 3-4-point scores in 137 queries by integrating multi-perspective drug analysis and actionable administration strategies.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of fetal hypoxia: a multicenter model development and nationwide AI-human comparison
evidence.outcome: AUROC of AI models versus human experts on same held-out CTG cases
evidence.effect: All CAP models achieved higher AUROC than 10,571 expert responses (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, DeLong P < 0.05).
evidence.quote: In comparison with 10,571 expert responses, all CAP models achieved higher AUROC (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, P values in Delong test < 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: CTG cases in nationwide AI-human comparison (held-out; 10,571 expert responses)

evidence.title: From Guidelines to Clicklists: GPT-5-Generated ERAS Checklists Improve Guideline Coverage for Bariatric and Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery-A STROBE-Compatible Cross-Sectional Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Guideline-item coverage and clarity of GPT-5 checklists versus guideline-derived traditional checklists
evidence.effect: AI coverage 97.0% ± 2.1% vs 89.0% ± 3.2% for traditional; clarity 4.8 ± 0.2 vs 4.2 ± 0.3 (p = 0.021).
evidence.quote: AI-generated checklists demonstrated higher mean guideline-item coverage than traditional checklists (97.0% ± 2.1% vs. 89.0% ± 3.2%) and higher clarity scores (4.8 ± 0.2 vs. 4.2 ± 0.3; p = 0.021).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Powered Diagnostic Co-Pilot ("CapyEngine") for Mental Disorders: Development, Evaluation, and Future Optimization Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of candidate LLM tools versus clinicians and general LLM on same questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o outperformed CapyEngine and clinicians at top 10 and top 5 (all P<.03); clinicians beat CapyEngine at top 5 (OR 0.26, P=.02); top 1 no significant differences.
evidence.quote: Across diagnostic accuracy thresholds, ChatGPT-4o consistently outperformed both CapyEngine and clinicians in broader rankings (top 10 and top 5 benchmarks; all P<.03).

evidence.title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
evidence.outcome: AI compared with radiologists on the same data for PE detection
evidence.effect: AI alone AUC 0.807-0.810 was lower than manual reading AUC 0.888-0.914; AI had 43 errors versus 29 for radiologists.
evidence.quote: The findings of our comprehensive analysis reveal a persistent performance gap between standalone AI systems and experienced radiologists in PE detection.

evidence.title: Clinical Summaries of Social Media Timelines for Mental Health Monitoring: Human Versus Large Language Model Comparative Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM-generated clinical summaries versus human clinician-written summaries, rated on clinical criteria
evidence.effect: Human summaries scored highest for factual consistency (3.75) and usefulness (3.63); TH-VAE 3.35 and 3.28; 2-step LLM models comparable to humans on interpersonal/intrapersonal patterns and changes over time.
evidence.quote: Human summaries scored highest for factual consistency (3.75) and general usefulness (3.63).

evidence.title: Structural error asymmetry and harm-weighted analysis of ChatGPT versus ICU Physicians in acid-base interpretation: a prospective observational study
evidence.outcome: Overall categorical accuracy and agreement of ChatGPT versus ICU physicians against expert reference diagnosis
evidence.effect: Accuracy 82% ICU physicians vs 72% ChatGPT; kappa 0.73 vs 0.63; paired difference not significant (p = 0.267), power 0.22.
evidence.quote: Paired comparison did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in overall classification (p = 0.267), and post-hoc power analysis indicated limited ability to detect modest effect sizes (power = 0.22).
evidence.sample_unit: consecutive ICU patients' arterial blood gas interpretations

evidence.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Professional Expertise in Adapted Physical Activity Prescription for Orthopedic Rehabilitation
evidence.venue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
evidence.outcome: overall perceived APA protocol quality
evidence.effect: Overall scores: scoliosis EP 4.35 vs AI 3.38; LBP 4.67 vs 3.73; osteoporosis 4.58 vs 3.78; falls 4.54 vs 3.88; osteoarthritis 4.42 vs 3.48.
evidence.quote: Across all investigated pathologies, the APA protocols designed by the EP consistently achieved the highest overall evaluation scores, followed by the protocols developed by the NAI, while the AI protocols received the lowest scores.

evidence.title: Potential Cost-Effectiveness of Machine Learning-Enabled Primary Care Identification of Hepatitis C Virus Patients in the US
evidence.outcome: QALYs and costs versus conventional testing
evidence.effect: At 30% recall, costs increased $1.20/person and QALYs increased 0.000013/person versus conventional testing.
evidence.quote: At 30% recall, the algorithm required additional per-person costs of $1.20 [95% CI: $1.07, $1.31], yielding a 0.000013 [95% CI: 0.000010, 0.000016] increase in QALYs per person over conventional testing practices.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated patients in Markov model cohort

evidence.title: Adaptive AI for Cardiovascular Event Adjudication: Cardiovascular Event Adjudication Across Different Definitions in the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID Trials
evidence.outcome: Comparison of AI strategies against human adjudication and each other on the same data
