evidence.effect: ADAPT-CEC, hybrid, and GPT-4o correctly classified 86.4%, 95.6%, and 76.3% of end points versus human adjudication; ADAPT-CEC bleeding F1 0.78 superior to GPT-4o.
evidence.quote: ADAPT-CEC was compared via F1 score with direct Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) 4o adjudication and a hybrid approach where the 30% of suspected events with the lowest AI prediction certainty used human adjudication.
evidence.sample_unit: suspected EUCLID primary end point events
evidence.country: International (ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and EUCLID multinational trials)

evidence.title: Automated identification of radiotherapy treatment sites from unstructured physician notes
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: LLM treatment-site identification accuracy benchmarked against two human observers
evidence.effect: Weighted accuracy 94.2% [95%CI: 89.4%-98.1%] versus sites isolated by either observer; 92.3% versus delivered plans.
evidence.quote: Llama 3.3 achieved a weighted accuracy of 94.2% [95%CI: 89.4%-98.1%] when compared to sites isolated by either observer.

evidence.title: A prospective multicenter trial of deep learning auto-segmentation for organs at risk in thoracic radiotherapy
evidence.outcome: Comparative accuracy against alternative models
evidence.effect: The iCurveE model (mean vDSC 0.896) significantly outperformed competing models nnU-Net (0.850) and TotalSegmentator (0.781).
evidence.quote: The iCurveE model achieved a significantly superior performance, with a mean volumetric Dice similarity coefficient (vDSC) of 0.896 and a 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 5.62 mm, compared to both the nnU-Net (vDSC, 0.850; HD95, 12.05 mm; p < 0.0001) and TotalSegmentator (vDSC, 0.781; HD95, 19.07 mm; p < 0.0001) models.

evidence.title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and specialist recommendations in urogynecology case management: a blinded assessment
evidence.venue: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
evidence.outcome: Blinded expert ratings of ChatGPT-4 versus urogynecologist management recommendations on 12 vignettes
evidence.effect: Median scores did not differ between human (5.8) and AI (6.1; p = 0.39). GPT-4 outperformed in guideline-based cases; humans generally outperformed in clinical reasoning cases.
evidence.quote: Median scores did not differ between human (5.8; 95% CI, 4.4-9.0) and AI-generated responses (6.1; 95% CI, 4.0-9.4; p = 0.39).

evidence.title: Multidisciplinary expert evaluation of large language models on questions regarding bariatric surgery: a comparative analysis of ERNIE Bot 4.0, ChatGPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini Pro
evidence.outcome: Accuracy differences between LLMs
evidence.effect: Good ratings differed: ChatGPT-4 90.0%, ERNIE Bot 84.0%, Claude 80%, Gemini Pro 48.0%; all p≤0.05.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 received “good” ratings for 90.0% of its responses, which were significantly higher than those of ERNIE Bot 4.0 (84.0%), Claude 3 Opus (80%), and Gemini Pro (48.0%; all p ≤ 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses to bariatric surgery questions

evidence.title: Comparative performance of LLMs and machine learning in predicting complications after percutaneous kyphoplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures
evidence.outcome: LLM predictive performance versus traditional ML models and surgeons on same data
evidence.effect: LLMs comparable to TML for BCL (F1 0.857-0.871 vs 0.758-0.867) but worse for NVF zero-shot (F1 0.309 vs RBF-SVM 0.536); LLMs did not outperform TML models.
evidence.quote: The LLMs did not outperform the TML models in the domain-specific tasks.
evidence.sample_unit: prospective test samples for BCL prediction (116 for NVF)

evidence.title: Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Comparative Analysis of Chat-GPT and Breast Radiologists on ACR Appropriateness Criteria
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT versions versus breast radiologists agreement with ACR criteria
evidence.effect: Radiologists had lowest mean bias (0.2438, p=0.489) and smallest slope bias; all ChatGPT versions had significant bias (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Radiologists had the lowest overall mean bias (0.2438) relative to the ACR (p = 0.489).
evidence.sample_unit: imaging decisions rated (10 ACR breast imaging clinical variants)

evidence.title: Precision Risk Model Using Quantitative Assessment of Vascular Severity in Telemedicine-Based Screening
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of model with vascular severity versus gestational age alone for 2-week TR-ROP
evidence.effect: Adding vascular severity improved AUROC vs GA alone: difference 0.13 (95% CI 0.06-0.19) in i-ROP and 0.08 (95% CI 0.03-0.14) in SUNDROP.
evidence.quote: Adding vascular severity improved discrimination vs GA alone (AUROC difference 0.13 [95% CI, 0.06-0.19] in i-ROP; 0.08 [95% CI, 0.03-0.14] in SUNDROP).
evidence.sample_unit: infants (559 i-ROP training; 1544 SUNDROP external validation)

evidence.title: Comparison of AI-generated radiology impressions: a multi-stakeholder evaluation
evidence.outcome: Comparison of custom AI, generic LLM and radiologist impressions on completeness, correctness, and utility
evidence.effect: Custom model achieved near parity with human impressions; generic LLM impressions were less preferred by radiologists (h 1.04-1.22 original; 0.66-0.69 independent, p < 0.001) and less concise (r = 0.85-0.87).
evidence.quote: Custom model impressions achieved near parity with human impressions; original radiologists rated their own impressions slightly more complete (r = 0.22, p = 0.0016).

evidence.title: Machine learning to predict ureteral access sheath placement failure in flexible ureteroscopy: development and prospective validation
evidence.outcome: Model AUC versus senior urologists' prediction of UAS placement failure in prospective cohort
evidence.effect: Simplified RF model achieved an AUC of 0.872 in prospective validation, significantly surpassing the predictive accuracy of senior urologists.
evidence.quote: During prospective validation, the simplified RF model achieved an AUC of 0.872, significantly surpassing the predictive accuracy of senior urologists.

evidence.title: Initial Insights Into an Institutional Secure Large Language Model for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Examination Requests: Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: Protocol accuracy of sLLM versus board-certified radiologists against consensus reference standard
evidence.effect: Overall protocol accuracy 93.1% (566/608) for sLLM vs 91.4% for Rad 3 (P=.23) and 92.1% for Rad 4 (P=.40); contrast accuracy 94.4% vs 92.1% for Rad 3 (P=.027).
evidence.quote: Overall protocol accuracy was 93.1% (566/608; 95% CI 89.6-96.6) for the sLLM, 91.4% (556/608; 95% CI 87.6-95.3) for Rad 3, and 92.1% (560/608; 95% CI 88.4-95.8) for Rad 4 (sLLM vs Rad 3 P=.23 vs Rad 4 P=.40).

evidence.title: Publicly available multimodal large language models for ocular surface infections: benchmarking against corneal specialists in triage, diagnosis and treatment
evidence.outcome: Multimodal LLM diagnosis, treatment and triage compared with corneal specialists on same cases
evidence.effect: Image+text near-human accuracy (Perplexity 96.7%; GPT-5 91.7%) without consistently surpassing specialists; text-only and image-only were below specialists; treatment accuracy lower.
evidence.quote: Combined image+text achieved near-human accuracy without consistently surpassing corneal specialists (Perplexity 96.7%; κ=0.95; GPT-5 91.7%; κ=0.87).
evidence.sample_unit: microbiologically confirmed infectious keratitis and conjunctivitis cases

evidence.title: Toward Automating the Summarization of Cancer Pathology Reports Using Large Language Models to Improve Clinical Usability
evidence.outcome: LLM summary vs physician summary completeness and correctness against original pathology reports
evidence.effect: LLM summaries scored higher on all objective metrics (P<.0001) vs physician summaries; DeepSeek, Mistral, Llama 3.1, 3.2 rated more complete (P=.017, <.0001) with comparable correctness (P=1.000).
evidence.quote: Using the original pathology reports as the ground truth, the LLM-generated summaries achieved higher scores across all objective evaluation metrics compared with physician pathology summaries (P < .0001).

evidence.title: Validation of the safety, empathy and utility of a large language model conversation agent for parents of autistic and neurodivergent children
evidence.outcome: Blind-rated comparison of LLM and clinician responses to 50 parent/carer questions
evidence.effect: Ratings for LLM and clinician responses were highly correlated. The evaluator identified response provenance 74% of the time.
evidence.quote: The ratings for LLM and clinician’s responses were highly correlated and the evaluator was able to distinguish which the provenance of the responses (74%).

evidence.title: Benchmarking of large language models to determine candidacy for spine surgery and comparison with conventional machine learning
evidence.outcome: LLM versus conventional random forest accuracy for spine surgery recommendation on same vignettes
evidence.effect: Zero-shot ChatGPT3.5 RMSE 0.37, AUROC 0.79; random forest RMSE 0.12, AUROC 0.96; fine-tuned LLMs AUROC 0.81-0.90, all below random forest.
evidence.quote: The random forest model, trained on the structured data, achieved superior performance (RMSE = 0.12, AUROC = 0.96).

evidence.title: A hybrid large language model framework for structured data entry from code-switched persian clinical speech
evidence.outcome: Field detection accuracy of proposed pipeline versus rule-based and simulated commercial baselines
evidence.effect: Medium forms FDA: rule-based 76%, simulated Dragon 83%, proposed auto with annotations 94%, hybrid with annotations 98%. Large forms: 68%, 75%, 92%, 92% respectively.
evidence.quote: The proposed hybrid with metadata and normalization substantially outperformed both baselines, as detailed in Tables 6 and 7 .

evidence.title: Evaluating AI in leukocyte classification: performance of the AI system against 15 morphology experts
evidence.outcome: AI leukocyte classification accuracy compared with 15 morphologists against a senior-expert gold standard
evidence.effect: AI overall accuracy 95.97% (ranked second among AI and 15 morphologists); abnormal subsets 91.38% (ranked fifth).
evidence.quote: The AI achieved an overall accuracy of 95.97% (ranked second) and 91.38% accuracy for the abnormal subsets (ranked fifth).

evidence.title: RadTranslateGPT: An Improved AI-Based System for Translation and Simplification of Structured Radiology Reports
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: Translation accuracy of GPT-o1 versus Google Translate rated by medical interpreters
evidence.effect: GPT-o1 achieved significantly higher translational accuracy (median 4.0 vs 3.0; P < .001), higher language register scores, and higher comprehensibility than Google Translate in all languages tested.
evidence.quote: GPT-o1 achieved significantly higher translational accuracy (median, 4.0 vs 3.0; P < .001) and higher language register scores and was rated more comprehensible than Google Translate in all languages tested.

evidence.title: Error Detection in Emergency Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model: Multistage Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Error detection rate of LLM versus radiologists of different seniority on same reports
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 few-shot 84.4% vs residents 51.6% and 53.1% (both P<.05); no significant difference vs senior/attending radiologists (68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
evidence.quote: Its performance exceeded that of radiology residents (84.4% vs 51.6% and 53.1%, respectively; both P<.05) and showed no statistically significant difference compared with senior radiologists and attending radiologists (84.4% vs 68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
evidence.sample_unit: emergency radiology reports (dataset 1); 200 reports stage 1, 100 stages 2-3, 800 stage 4

evidence.title: Evaluation of the reliability of large language models for ASA-PS classification in cardiovascular surgery: a pilot study
evidence.outcome: Exact-match agreement with specialist consensus, LLMs versus residents on same cases
evidence.effect: Exact-match to five-specialist consensus was 42.2% for residents versus 59.4–75.0% for LLMs; LLM–specialist ICC 0.61–0.65.
evidence.quote: Exact-match to a five-specialist consensus was 42.2% for residents versus 59.4–75.0% for LLMs; classifications outside the range of ratings assigned by individual specialists were rare (0–3.1%).

evidence.title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy compared against physicians and across models/prompts on same cases
evidence.effect: Best configuration (GPT-4.1 Guidance-Self-Consistency, 91.3%) matched top physicians (92.7%) and exceeded community physicians; zero-shot DeepSeek 62.6%.
evidence.quote: Overall, GPT-4.1 with the Guidance-Self-Consistency prompt proved to be the most effective model-prompt configuration, achieving the optimal accuracy of 91.3% across the main decision-making dimensions; thus, it was selected as the optimal model.

evidence.title: Large language models as clinical decision-support tools in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and neurologists
evidence.venue: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
evidence.outcome: AI versus neurologist correct responses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT higher overall: without context 72.9% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.038); with context 80.5% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.001).
evidence.quote: When analyzing results across all studies combined, ChatGPT-4o demonstrated a significantly higher percentage of correct responses than neurologists in both conditions: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001) ( Figure 1A ).
evidence.sample_unit: neurologists (responses to 21 clinical vignettes; ChatGPT-4o run 10 times per case)

evidence.title: Evaluating open-source LLMs for dental EMR generation
evidence.outcome: Between-model EMR quality differences
evidence.effect: Automated metrics differed significantly; expert 7DI found no significant between-model differences: F = 0.21, p = .957, η² = 0.009.
evidence.quote: ANOVA detected no statistically significant differences among models (F = 0.21, p = .957, η² = 0.009), and all post-hoc Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons were non-significant (all p > .05).
evidence.sample_unit: de-identified dental EMRs converted to synthetic Mandarin dialogues (50-case expert-rated subset)

evidence.title: Prompt engineering enables open-source large language models to match proprietary models in diagnostic accuracy for annotation of radiology reports
evidence.outcome: Overall diagnostic accuracy across candidate models
evidence.effect: GPT-4o 97.9%; Qwen3-8b 97.8%; Llama3.1-405b 97.1%; GPT-4o-mini, Ministral-8b, and Llama3-8b each 96.9%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy at 97.9% (95%; CI: 97.3%-98.5%), followed by Qwen3-8b (97.8%; 95% CI: 97.4%-98.1%), Llama3.1-405b (97.1%; 95% CI: 96.4%-97.8%), GPT-4o-mini (96.9%; 95% CI: 96.2%-97.6%), Ministral-8b (96.9%; 95% CI 96.4%-97.2%) and Llama3-8b (96.9%; 95% CI: 95.9%-97.3%).

evidence.title: Comparison of Drug Information Questions' Responses Between Drug Information Pharmacists and Artificial Intelligence Technologies: A Real-World Analysis in a Tertiary Care Hospital
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
evidence.outcome: AI tool responses compared against drug information pharmacists on same questions
evidence.effect: GPT-4o and Medical Chat comparable to pharmacists; Gemini and Copilot lower; GPT-4o outperformed Gemini and Copilot in pairwise comparisons.
evidence.quote: Welch's analysis of variance (ANOVA) demonstrated a significant difference in composite scores among groups (p < 0.001), with GPT-4o outperforming Gemini and Copilot in pairwise comparisons.

evidence.title: Multi-modal large language models for paediatric tele-ophthalmology: A blinded real-world evaluation of diagnostic accuracy and safety
evidence.outcome: Composite score of advanced LLMs versus GPT-4o baseline on the same cases
evidence.effect: Multi-modal arm: Grok 4.1 15.06 ± 0.68, GPT 5.1 Thinking 14.52 ± 1.19, Gemini 2.5 Pro 14.30 ± 1.08 versus GPT-4o 11.20 ± 0.72.
evidence.quote: Grok 4.1 led with the highest overall score in the multi-modal arm (15.06 ± 0.68), followed by GPT 5.1 Thinking (14.52 ± 1.19) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (14.30 ± 1.08), while GPT-4o lagged significantly at 11.20 ± 0.72.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language model performance and reliability in scoring picture description tasks for neuropsychological assessment
evidence.outcome: LLM scoring error versus three-human-rater consensus on Cookie Theft content units
evidence.effect: No significant differences in MAE between best-performing models and human raters; LLMs showed significantly higher interrater reliability than human raters.
evidence.quote: LLMs demonstrated comparable accuracy to human raters in scoring the Cookie Theft task, with no significant differences in mean absolute error (MAE) between the best performing models and human raters.
evidence.sample_unit: participants (Cookie Theft picture description transcripts from DementiaBank)

evidence.title: Clinical relevance of AI-based PD-L1 scoring in non-small cell lung cancer
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI PD-L1 scoring with expert pathologist reference
evidence.effect: Binary concordance 95.2% (κ=0.89); three-tier concordance 94.5% (weighted κ=0.93); category changes in 6% (20/333) of cases.
evidence.quote: The overall concordance of PD-L1 status (cutoff ≥1%) between the uPath algorithm and the pathologist was 95.2% (κ = 0.89), while the concordance for the three-tier categorization was 94.5% (weighted κ = 0.93).

evidence.title: Trial emulation for validating the clinical efficacy of a foundational AI model in embryo selection
evidence.outcome: Comparative efficacy of FEMI high-risk score versus other scoring mechanisms on implantation treatment effect
evidence.effect: High-risk FEMI score carried significantly stronger ITE penalty on implantation than other scoring mechanisms (p < 0.0001), persisting after adjusting for maternal age.
evidence.quote: Comparative efficacy using S-Learner models demonstrated that a high-risk FEMI score carried a significantly stronger individual treatment effect (ITE) penalty on implantation compared to other scoring mechanisms (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of four large language models (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet-4, and DeepSeek-R1) for diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making in real-world otolaryngology scenarios
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Therapeutic accuracy compared across four competing LLMs on same 100 cases
evidence.effect: Therapeutic accuracy: Gemini 2.5 Pro 86%, DeepSeek-R1 and Claude Sonnet-4 69% each, ChatGPT-5 64% (p = 0.0001); Gemini significantly better than others.
evidence.quote: Overall differences in therapeutic performance among the four models were statistically significant (p = 0.0001).

evidence.title: Prognostic Prediction of Avulsed Permanent Teeth Using Conversational AI Models Versus Expert Dentists: Influence of Prompt Structure and Temporal Stability
evidence.venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
evidence.outcome: comparison with expert dentists
evidence.effect: Gemini and ChatGPT-4o were most balanced; Claude deviated more in absolute severity; DeepSeek had lower categorical concordance.
evidence.quote: Gemini and ChatGPT-4o showed the most balanced performance, whereas Claude preserved relative risk ordering with greater deviation in absolute severity, and DeepSeek demonstrated lower categorical concordance.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic avulsion scenarios (each in 4 prompt formats, evaluated twice by 4 models)

evidence.title: Large Language Model Recommendations for Empiric Antibiotics Versus Clinician Prescribing: A Non-Interventional Paired Retrospective Antimicrobial Stewardship Analysis
evidence.outcome: Guardrail violation rate of LLM vs clinician empiric antibiotic regimens on same admissions
evidence.effect: Violations in 17.0% of clinician regimens vs 4.9% of LLM regimens (paired RD -12.2%; matched OR 0.216, 95% CI 0.127-0.367; McNemar exact p = 1.60 × 10^-10).
evidence.quote: Guardrail violations occurred in 17.0% of clinician regimens vs. 4.9% of LLM regimens (paired RD -12.2%; matched OR 0.216, 95% CI 0.127-0.367; McNemar exact p = 1.60 × 10-10).

evidence.title: External validation of ECG artificial intelligence for emergency and cardiac assessment across a large-scale U.S. healthcare system
evidence.outcome: ECG-AI AUC versus initial troponin T for AMI and STEMI equivalents in paired subset
evidence.effect: In paired subset (N = 1368), ECG-AI AUC 0.920 vs 0.878 for AMI and 0.932 vs 0.736 for STEMI equivalents (all P < 0.001).
evidence.quote: In a paired subset (N = 1368), ECG-AI outperformed initial troponin T for AMI (AUC 0.920 vs. 0.878) and STEMI equivalents (AUC 0.932 vs. 0.736; all P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Clinical validation and implementation of mSTOP, a machine learning-based, longitudinal prediction model for the early identification of non-small cell lung cancer patients who not benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment
evidence.outcome: mSTOP predictive performance compared with CT imaging for identifying non-responders
evidence.effect: mSTOP identified 35.1% of nonresponding patients with PPV 84.8%, comparable to CT-imaging; combined with CT, PPV rose to 95.7% identifying 19.8% of non-responders.
evidence.quote: mSTOP identified 35.1 % of nonresponding patients, with a positive predictive value (PPV) of 84.8 %, which was comparable to CT-imaging.

evidence.title: Open-Source Large Language Models Distilled DeepSeek-R1 Pose Challenges for On-Premises Clinical Deployment in Medical Diagnosis: A Comparative Study of Performance
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of reasoning models versus their base models on the same cases
evidence.effect: R1-671B beat DeepSeek-V3 (95.45% vs 88.18%; p=0.008); R1-8B underperformed Llama3.1-8B (47.27% vs 64.54%; p=0.003); no significant differences for mid-sized models.
evidence.quote: The study concludes that the DeepSeek-R1-671B shows potential for medical diagnosis, but distilled models do not exceed their base models.

evidence.title: Fluoroscopic image-driven deep learning model for predicting intussusception irreducibility during air enema in children
evidence.outcome: AI model AUC compared with radiologists and other methods on same data
evidence.effect: Model AUC 0.89 vs intermediate radiologist 0.804 (P < 0.001) and senior radiologist 0.842 (P = 0.108); outperformed comparative methods (AUC ranges 0.823-0.877 and 0.634-0.826).
evidence.quote: The model demonstrated superior performance compared with that of the intermediate radiologist (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.804; P < 0.001) and comparable performance to that of a senior radiologist (AUC: 0.89 vs. 0.842; P = 0.108).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (real-world test set: 46 irreducible and 802 reducible)

evidence.title: Ai-generated personalized informed consent for elective spinal surgery: a comparative study using retrieval-augmented generation
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
evidence.outcome: Consent document content quality
evidence.effect: 14.75 ± 0.35 vs. 10.17 ± 0.69 out of 15; p < 0.001; 75% achieved maximum score.
evidence.quote: AI-generated documents scored significantly higher than standard forms on the modified Spatz instrument (14.75 ± 0.35 vs. 10.17 ± 0.69 out of 15; p < 0.001), with 75% achieving the maximum score.

evidence.title: MARTP: a multi-agent simulation framework for automated radiation therapy planning based on LLMs
evidence.outcome: Dosimetric metrics of AI-generated plans versus expert-crafted clinical plans
evidence.effect: No statistically significant differences in dosimetric metrics between MARTP and expert-crafted clinical plans, with substantially improved planning efficiency.
evidence.quote: Statistical analysis reveals that the dosimetric metrics of plans generated by MARTP exhibit no statistically significant differences compared with expert-crafted clinical plans, while the planning efficiency is substantially improved.

evidence.title: Deep learning models for acute kidney injury prediction: multi-center external validation and evaluation under simulated continuous monitoring conditions
evidence.outcome: Comparing deep learning models against XGBoost and logistic regression baselines on same data
evidence.effect: Deep learning outperformed baselines externally (AUROC 0.956-0.963 vs. 0.630-0.686).
evidence.quote: Deep learning substantially outperformed baselines externally (AUROC 0.956-0.963 vs. 0.630-0.686).

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence versus 263 pediatric clinicians for childhood exanthems
evidence.outcome: AI model diagnostic accuracy compared with pediatric residents and specialists on the same cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 53/61 (86.9%), Gemini 50 (82.0%), Copilot 44 (72.1%); ChatGPT and Gemini exceeded the specialist median 95% CI upper bound (47.17); all three exceeded resident bound (42.76).
evidence.quote: Both ChatGPT and Gemini exceeded the upper bound of the specialist population median 95% CI (47.17).
evidence.sample_unit: pediatric clinicians (107 residents, 156 specialists) and 61 cases

evidence.title: Combining Machine Learning Models and Screening to Enhance Suicide Risk Identification for American Indian Patients: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity of ML model versus ASQ screening on same data for suicide attempt/death within 90 days
evidence.effect: ML medium-risk threshold sensitivity 0.782 (95% CI 0.648-0.915) vs ASQ alone 0.178 (95% CI 0.073-0.282); NPV 0.999 vs 0.997.
evidence.quote: The ML model outperformed ASQ screening on sensitivity and NPV at the evaluated thresholds; however, because the model included prior screening and ideation features, this comparison reflects the incremental value of longitudinal EHR information rather than a contemporaneous head-to-head assessment of the index screening alone.

evidence.title: A TyG-UHR-based machine learning model for screening lean MAFLD: development and external validation
evidence.outcome: candidate algorithm comparison
evidence.effect: XGBoost best: AUC 0.995, F1 0.955, accuracy 0.992, precision/specificity 1.000, sensitivity 0.914; RF second AUC 0.990.
evidence.quote: XGBoost demonstrated the best discrimination (AUC 0.995) and, at the F1-max threshold, the strongest overall classification performance with an F1 score (F1) of 0.955, accuracy (ACC) of 0.992, precision (PRE) of 1.000, specificity (SPE) of 1.000, and sensitivity (SEN) of 0.914.

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models in breast cancer care: agreement with radiology-led multidisciplinary tumor board decisions
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: LLM treatment recommendation concordance with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions as comparator
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o 83.2%, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 79.7%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 79.4% overall concordance; Luminal A ~66%; mastectomy F1 <58; axillary dissection F1 ≤23.5.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated the highest overall concordance with MDTB decisions (83.2%), followed by Claude 3.7 Sonnet (79.7%) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (79.4%).

evidence.title: Automatic Speech Recognition and Large Language Models for Multilingual Pathology Report Generation: Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three candidate LLMs on the same transcripts via automated metrics and pathologist ranking
evidence.effect: Qwen2:72b outperformed Llama3.1:70b and Gemma2:27b across all 5 automated metrics (all P<.001) and had the lowest error rate, showing large differences between candidates.
evidence.quote: Pairwise Wilcoxon tests showed that Qwen2:72b outperformed Llama3.1:70b and Gemma2:27b across all 5 automated metrics (all P <.001).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated mixed Chinese-English pathology dictation audio recordings

evidence.title: Safety and diagnostic accuracy of large-language model application of PECARN head injury algorithm
evidence.outcome: LLM NPV and accuracy versus ED clinicians on PECARN head injury risk classification
evidence.effect: Optimized Features Model NPV 0.98, accuracy 0.89 versus ED clinicians NPV 0.99, accuracy 0.92; all models had high NPV comparable to PEM physicians.
evidence.quote: The GPT model with the highest combination of NPV and accuracy was the prompt-engineered "Optimized Features Model" (NPV = 0.98, accuracy = 0.89), which performed similarly to that of the ED clinicians in both NPV (0.99) and accuracy (0.92).

evidence.title: Comparative accuracy of a predictive algorithm versus cardiologist assessment for 90-day readmission in decompensated chronic heart failure
evidence.outcome: 90-day readmission prediction: algorithm versus three cardiologists on same patients
evidence.effect: PRED'IC AUC 0.81, sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 69.7%; cardiologists sensitivity 90.9%, specificity 35.8%. Algorithm flagged 35% high risk versus 67% by cardiologists.
evidence.quote: Cardiologists demonstrated higher sensitivity (90.9%) but lower specificity (35.8%).

evidence.title: Vision-weighted diagnostic gain (VWDG) in the diagnosis of oral malignant and potentially malignant lesions: A multimodal comparative analysis
evidence.venue: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multimodal LLMs compared with board-certified oral medicine experts on same lesions
evidence.effect: Experts had highest Top-1 accuracy (65.3%); ChatGPT-5 multimodal (Top-1 50.0%) approached expert-level performance at Top-3 and Top-5; Gemini showed limited benefit from images.
evidence.quote: Experts achieved the highest Top-1 accuracy (65.3%), but ChatGPT-5 multimodal outputs approached expert-level performance at Top-3 and Top-5.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Role of ChatGPT in the Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage on Non-contrast Computed Tomography: A Retrospective Case-Control Study
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic performance compared with radiologist diagnoses for intracranial hemorrhage on NCCT
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 84.8%, accuracy 87.3%; kappa 0.75 with radiologists; McNemar p = 0.31, no significant difference. Subtype sensitivity was lower for subdural (61.5%) and epidural (66.7%).
evidence.quote: McNemar's test showed no statistically significant difference between ChatGPT and radiologist diagnoses (p = 0.31).

evidence.title: An Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Instructor
evidence.outcome: AI agent adherence to CPR instruction criteria compared with 911 dispatchers on real calls
evidence.effect: Agent achieved 100% minimally viable and 98.9% maximally effective adherence, absolute improvements of 15.5 points (P = .02) and 36.1 points (P < .001) over dispatchers (84.5% and 62.8%).
evidence.quote: In a retest using 911 calls, the agent achieved 100% (95% CI, 88.6%-100%) adherence to minimally viable and 98.9% (95% CI, 94.0%-99.8%) adherence to maximally effective criteria, representing absolute improvements of 15.5 percentage points (95% CI, 2.1-27.4 percentage points; P = .02) and 36.1 percentage points (95% CI, 27.2-44.3 percentage points; P < .001) over dispatchers (84.5%; 95% CI, 73.1%-91.6% and 62.8%; 95% CI, 55.0%-70.0%, respectively).
evidence.sample_unit: simulated OHCA scenarios and 911 dispatcher-assisted calls

evidence.title: Evaluating reasoning models for therapy recommendations in gastrointestinal stromal tumors: expert and LLM-based evaluations of OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1
evidence.venue: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
evidence.outcome: Concordance of LLM therapy recommendations with MDT decisions, compared across two reasoning models
evidence.effect: OpenAI o1 achieved higher concordance with MDT decisions than DeepSeek-R1 (76.9% vs. 53.8%, p < 0.001); aligned with either MDT or guidelines 80.0% vs. 63.1%, p = 0.005.
evidence.quote: OpenAI o1 achieved higher concordance with MDT decisions than DeepSeek-R1 (76.9% vs. 53.8%, p < 0.001) and more recommendations aligned with either MDT or guidelines (80.0% vs. 63.1%, p = 0.005).

evidence.title: Independent Head-to-Head Comparison of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Devices for Lung Cancer Detection on Chest Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head diagnostic accuracy of competing commercial AI devices on same local dataset, incl. versus radiologist reporting
evidence.effect: AUC varied 0.80-0.94 (P<.05 for 9 of 15 pairwise comparisons); sensitivity 20.8%-77.8%, specificity 58.9%-98.4%; additional false positives vs radiologist reporting ranged 10 to 2039.
evidence.quote: There was clinically and statistically significant variability in the diagnostic accuracy of commercial AI devices for lung cancer detection at chest radiography.

evidence.title: Qualified prediction system for allograft failure in real world settings: extended validation study
evidence.outcome: Predictive ability of iBox versus eGFR slope and anti-HLA donor specific antibodies
evidence.effect: iBox C index 0.81 vs eGFR slope 0.62 and vs donor specific antibodies 0.57.
evidence.quote: The iBox was also superior to eGFR slope (C index 0.81 v 0.62) and circulating anti-HLA donor specific antibodies (C index 0.81 v 0.57) in its predictive ability.
evidence.country: France, other European countries, United States/Canada, South America (multinational)

evidence.title: LuminaConsent: AI-driven standardization and quality enhancement of urological informed consent documentation
evidence.outcome: Blind expert-rated consent document quality of AI versus society standard forms and specialist documents
evidence.effect: LuminaConsent 82.33 (SD 4.2) vs society standard 78.77 (SD 6.1) and specialist documents 57.43 (SD 3.8); +4.5% over standards (p<0.05), +43.3% over specialists (p<0.001)
evidence.quote: LuminaConsent achieved higher performance with mean scores of 82.33 points (SD±4.2) versus 78.77 points (SD±6.1) for professional society standards and 57.43 points (SD±3.8) for specialist documentation, representing statistically significant improvements of 43.3% over specialist practices (p<0.001) and 4.5% over professional society standards (p<0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: urological procedures (consent documents per arm, blind-rated by 3 urologists)

evidence.title: Reliability of Multimodal LLMs for Sinusitis with Polyps vs. Sinusitis Without Polyps Classification from Paranasal Sinus CT Slices
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Compared three multimodal LLMs against each other on the same CT cases
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o accuracy 0.89, kappa 0.77; ChatGPT-5 accuracy 0.67, kappa 0.33; Gemini 2.5 Pro accuracy 0.56, kappa 0.11; ChatGPT-4o significantly better (p<0.001 each).
evidence.quote: Multimodal LLMs showed significant differences in CT-based polyp detection under the same inputs, depending on the version and vendor.

evidence.title: Patient-friendly simplification and translation of neuroradiology impressions using artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: LLM Spanish translation quality vs manual bilingual translations rated by certified interpreters
evidence.effect: Interpreter scores not significantly different: brain MRI 4.6 vs 4.4/4.7 (p=0.29); head CT 4.6 vs 4.6/4.7 (p=0.63); spine MRI 4.5 vs 4.3/4.5 (p=0.28).
evidence.quote: Machine generated translations were not significantly different from either reference translation, and reference translations were not significantly different from each other (Brain MRI mean scores 4.6, 4.4, and 4.7, p = 0.29; Head CT mean scores 4.6, 4.6, and 4.7, p = 0.63; and Spine MRI mean scores 4.5, 4.3, and 4.5, p = 0.28 for Hypothesis, Reference 1, and Reference 2, respectively; p s from Kruskal-Wallis test).
evidence.sample_unit: neuroradiology reports (brain MRI, head CT, spine MRI); 60 impressions translated to Spanish

evidence.title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
evidence.outcome: AI segmentation compared with manual contouring by physicists/technologists on accuracy, dose and time
evidence.effect: AI-seg median DSC liver 0.988, spleen 0.965, kidneys 0.994 vs manual 0.955, 0.929, 0.929; AI with correction faster (47.0 vs 54.3 min, p=0.014).
evidence.quote: Further, the total required time for the reference contour, including the corrections after AI segmentation, was significantly shorter than that for manual contouring ( p = 0.014).

evidence.title: Performance evaluation of large language models in the diagnosis of emergency internal medicine diseases: a retrospective study
evidence.outcome: Main diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus emergency junior physicians on same real cases
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-V3 (90.0%), ChatGPT-4o (86.0%), Grok3 (86.0%) significantly higher than EDJP (77.5%, p<0.05); LLM comprehensiveness scores all higher than EDJP; LLMs faster (6.3-14.0 s vs 360.2 s).
evidence.quote: Main diagnostic accuracy: DeepSeek-V3 (90.0%), ChatGPT-4o (86.0%), and Grok3 (86.0%) were significantly higher than that of EDJP (77.5%, p < 0.05); in the subgroup of respiratory system diseases, Gemini-2.0 and DeepSeek-V3 performed better (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Application of large language models in clinical decision-making for dry eye disease
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: LLM versus junior ophthalmologists on DED classification and treatment necessity accuracy on same cases
evidence.effect: Treatment necessity accuracy LLMs 96-99% vs junior ophthalmologists 97%; DeepSeek-V3 classification 92% (kappa 0.80) outperformed ChatGPT-4o and juniors (71%, kappa ≈ 0.53; p < 0.01).
evidence.quote: For DED classification, DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest accuracy (92%) and agreement with experts (kappa = 0.80), outperforming ChatGPT-4o and junior ophthalmologists (71%, kappa ≈ 0.53; p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Clinical validation of an artificial intelligence model for thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy indication: comparison with TI-RADS systems and human specialists in a Chilean public hospital
evidence.outcome: AI FNA recommendation sensitivity/specificity versus specialists using ACR and Horvath TI-RADS on same patients
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.41; Horvath TI-RADS by expert radiologist sensitivity 0.82, specificity 0.69; concordance between AI and TI-RADS methods moderate.
evidence.quote: The AI model showed a sensitivity of 0.88 and a specificity of 0.41.

evidence.title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
evidence.outcome: Comparison of AI (SVM, Gemini) against clinician-in-the-loop on same scans
evidence.effect: On same 86 scans, HITL accuracy 94% vs SVM 84% and Gemini 90%; sensitivity 98% vs 83% and 86%.
evidence.quote: While advanced reasoning models like Gemini exhibit powerful contextual capabilities, the direct integration of human domain knowledge proved superior, firmly establishing the value of HITL over fully autonomous “models-only” pipelines.
evidence.sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

evidence.title: Multimodal GPT-5 for Predicting Poor Functional Outcomes After Intracerebral Hemorrhage in the Emergency Department: Validation Study
evidence.outcome: GPT models vs conventional ML model on same data: discrimination, calibration, overall performance, net benefit
evidence.effect: Zero-shot GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 AUROC 0.84 and 0.85 vs ML 0.85, but lower scaled Brier scores, low or negative Nagelkerke R², and no superior clinical utility on decision curve analysis.
evidence.quote: Zero-shot GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 demonstrated discrimination comparable to the ML model (AUROC 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.91 and 0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.91, respectively) with high reproducibility (ICC 0.91 and 0.95, respectively) but inferior overall performance, as reflected by lower scaled Brier scores and low or negative Nagelkerke R² values.

evidence.title: Adaptive Fast-Slow Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional Classification of Prenatal Ultrasound Reports: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: candidate model comparison for severity
evidence.effect: On test set, V3.2-R 86% vs V3.2-B 57%; minor anomalies V3.2-B F1=0 vs V3.2-R F1=0.83.
evidence.quote: On the test set, V3.2-R achieved an accuracy of 86%, significantly outperforming V3.2-B, which achieved only 57%.

evidence.title: Large language models approach clinician performance in ESC cardiovascular risk stratification: a vignette-based benchmark study
evidence.outcome: LLM performance compared with clinicians on the same vignettes for ESC risk classification
evidence.effect: Eight clinicians pooled κw 0.52 (0.28-0.67); best LLM GPT-4o κw 0.69 (0.44-0.84); clinicians made no major two-class errors whereas several LLMs did.
evidence.quote: Notably, five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded this pooled clinician benchmark, suggesting that top-performing models reach the performance level of the average individual physician on this task.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical vignettes (each in Portuguese and English)

evidence.title: LLM-Generated Transplant Algorithms: Comparing GPT and Gemini in Producing Step-Wise Diagnostic and Management Pathways
evidence.outcome: Clinical concordance of LLM transplant algorithms, compared across two candidate models on identical prompts
evidence.effect: Gemini 2.5 Pro achieved a higher median Clinical Concordance score than GPT-4 (4.5 vs 3.8, P < .01) and higher Logical Flow and Completeness scores.
evidence.quote: Gemini 2.5 Pro achieved a higher median Clinical Concordance score than GPT-4 (4.5 vs 3.8, P < .01) and higher Logical Flow and Completeness scores.
evidence.sample_unit: post-transplant clinical scenarios (algorithms scored by 3 transplant specialists)

evidence.title: Human expertise or artificial intelligence? A prospective study on nail disorder diagnosis
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multimodal LLMs versus dermatologists on the same nail images (SD and SD+DD)
evidence.effect: Dermatologists correct in 70.6% (SD) and 80.3% (SD+DD); AI models correct in 25.0% (SD) and 35.0% (SD+DD), p<0.001.
evidence.quote: In comparison, AI models were correct in 25.0% (95% CI: 16.8-35.5) and 35.0% (95% CI: 25.5-45.9) of cases, respectively (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical images of nail disease cases

evidence.title: Performance of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Image-Based Electrocardiogram Interpretation: Exploratory Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Comparison of generalist versus ECG-specialized LLMs on same ECG images
evidence.effect: Specialized models achieved overall balanced accuracy of 56.5% (ECG-Instruct) and 64.4% (PULSE-7B) versus 50.1%-61.8% for generalist models; PULSE-7B better on rhythm and ectopic beats.
evidence.quote: Specialized models achieved overall balanced accuracy of 56.5% (ECG-Instruct-Llama-3.2-11B-Vision) and 64.4% (PULSE-7B), with PULSE-7B showing higher task-specific balanced accuracy in rhythm classification and ectopic beats detection (up to 86.3% and 89.2%, respectively).

evidence.title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
evidence.outcome: AI versus chart-review recovery
evidence.effect: LLM-enhanced roadmaps recommended 83-89 (20%-22%) versus expert chart reviews 49 (12%).
evidence.quote: The expert chart reviews recovered 49 (12%), while the algorithms using LLMs-enhanced roadmaps recommended almost twice as many (83-89, 20%-22%).

evidence.title: Automated Triage for New Keratoconus Referrals Using Multimodal Deep Learning
evidence.outcome: Progression prediction AUROC of multimodal versus conventional ML and unimodal models on same data
evidence.effect: Multimodal AS-OCT, Placido and tabular model gave best single-visit AUROC 0.84 (95% CI 0.83-0.85); adding sequential visits via LSTM raised it to 0.93 (95% CI 0.91-0.96).
evidence.quote: The multimodal model of AS-OCT, Placido, and tabular data yielded the best single-visit prediction (AUROC 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.83-0.85); adding sequential visits via long short-term memory boosted this to 0.93 (95% CI: 0.91-0.96).
evidence.sample_unit: eyes (internal dataset; 963 eyes in external validation)

evidence.title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
evidence.outcome: model comparison performance
evidence.effect: XGB was best overall; RF was slightly lower except 1-month AUC 0.74 versus XGB 0.72.
evidence.quote: In accordance with the results from the original development of the models, the best performance overall was from the XGB model, with the exception of the AUC for 1-month mortality.

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of generative AI models for chest radiograph report generation in the emergency department
evidence.outcome: VLM-generated CXR report quality versus radiologist-written reports on same cases
evidence.effect: AIRead had lower RADPEER 3b rate (5.3% vs 13.9%) and higher acceptability (84.5% vs 74.3%) than radiologists; other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%) and lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%).
evidence.quote: Other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%; p < 0.05), lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%; p < 0.05), and more frequent hallucinations (5.4-17.4%; p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of GPT-5 and Gemini Models in Decision Support for Bariatric Surgery: A Simulation-Based Study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two candidate LLMs on the same vignettes
evidence.effect: GPT-5 outperformed Gemini on composite score (6.92±0.61 vs 5.43±0.88; P<0.001); Gemini 4 times more likely to produce an unsafe action (RR 4.0; 95% CI 2.2-7.3).
evidence.quote: Gemini was 4 times more likely to produce an unsafe action than GPT-5 (risk ratio, 4.0; 95% CI, 2.2-7.3).

evidence.title: Performance of GPT-based large language models in hepatocellular carcinoma stratification: liver function assessment, BCLC staging, and treatment recommendations
evidence.outcome: GPT recommendations compared against tumor board decisions and expert consensus, plus time and cost versus staff
evidence.effect: In 9-14% of cases GPT suggestions were retrospectively more guideline-concordant than tumor board decisions; GPT reduced costs approximately 300- to 1300-fold versus clinical staff.
evidence.quote: In 9-14% of cases, GPT suggestions were retrospectively more guideline-concordant than tumor board decisions.

evidence.title: General-purpose large language models outperform specialized clinical AI tools on medical benchmarks
evidence.outcome: Specialized clinical AI tools versus frontier LLMs on same benchmarks and real clinical queries
evidence.effect: Frontier LLMs outperformed clinical AI tools in all three evaluations (MedQA, HealthBench, RCQ); clinical AI tools performed comparably to Google Search AI Overview on the RCQ.
evidence.quote: Frontier LLMs outperformed clinical AI tools in all three evaluations.
evidence.sample_unit: model-question annotations by clinicians (RCQ benchmark; plus 500 MedQA and 500 HealthBench items)

evidence.title: Comparing clinical decision-making between colposcopists and large language models in cervical dysplasia management: a pilot prospective multicenter study
evidence.outcome: Concordance with guideline-author gold standard, LLMs versus board-certified colposcopists, cervical dysplasia management
evidence.effect: Overall concordance 69.6% clinicians, 69.6% ChatGPT-4o, 65.2% ChatGPT-5. ChatGPT-5 beat clinicians in precancerous lesions (81.8% vs 66.4%); clinicians better in unspecific histopathology (86% vs 60%).
evidence.quote: Clinicians and LLMs achieved similar overall concordance rates compared to the gold standard (69.6% for clinicians, 69.6% for ChatGPT-4o, and 65.2% for ChatGPT-5).
evidence.sample_unit: anonymized real-life patient cases with multiple-choice questions

evidence.title: Configuring large language models to deliver patient-facing explanations of pathology reports
evidence.outcome: LLM configurations compared with pathologist-written explanations on same questions
evidence.effect: GPT-5_p_rag met noninferiority (Δ=1.5) and was significantly preferred over pathologist responses (58% win rate, P=.04); GPT-5-n_p performed worse (36% win rate, P<.001).
evidence.quote: Among all configurations, GPT-5_p_rag achieved the highest ability estimate and was the only model statistically significantly preferred over pathologist-written responses (difference, 0.33; P = .04; 58% win rate).

evidence.title: Performance of the Techcyte AI-based image analysis system for coproparasitological diagnosis in clinical stool specimens: a retrospective evaluation study
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted diagnosis compared with conventional microscopy on same specimens
evidence.effect: AI plus operator review detected additional parasites in 74/178 (41.57%) specimens versus microscopy; kappa 0.865.
evidence.quote: After data analysis, there were a total of 74/178 (41.57%) specimens with additional parasite etiologies detected respect to conventional microscopy examination.

evidence.title: An expert-level vision-language model for multitask diagnostic morphology in clinical laboratories
evidence.outcome: Overall accuracy on national EQA compared with human expert group and general models
evidence.effect: Lingjian 93.0% overall accuracy vs human expert group 78.1% and Gemini-3 Pro 75.3%.
evidence.quote: On China's National Center for Clinical Laboratories External Quality Assessment (EQA, 2021-2025), it reached 93.0% overall accuracy, outperforming a human expert group (78.1%) and strong general models (e.g., Gemini-3 Pro, 75.3%).

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of GPT-4o as a representative multimodal large language model and human fitters in orthokeratology lens fitting: Assessing accuracy, efficiency and cost-effectiveness in initial lens parameter selection
evidence.outcome: Parameter-matching accuracy of GPT-4o versus human fitters on same cases
evidence.effect: GPT-4o 78% accuracy (196/250), comparable to human fitters (experienced ophthalmologist 83%, optometrists 85%, general ophthalmologists 76%); kappa 0.18-0.60.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o achieved 78% accuracy (196/250), comparable to human fitters (experienced ophthalmologist: 83%, optometrists: 85%, general ophthalmologists: 76%).

evidence.title: Evaluating accuracy and reasoning capabilities of large language models for acute ischemic stroke management
evidence.outcome: Treatment decision accuracy of LLMs versus stroke experts on the same vignettes
evidence.effect: DeepSeek R1 had highest MT accuracy (87%) and IVT accuracy of 78%; neurologists 81% MT and 80% IVT; neuroradiologists 84% MT and 76% IVT.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek R1 achieved the highest MT accuracy among all models and clinicians (MT 87%), with IVT accuracy of 78%.

evidence.title: Evaluation of six cutting-edge large language models in answering a set of open-ended questions in dental case reports
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality of six candidate LLMs compared on identical dental case questions
evidence.effect: Significant differences across all metrics; DeepSeek median 4.5/5 vs GPT 4.0, Gemini 4.0, Copilot 4.0, MedGemma 3.75, Llama 3.5.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek achieved the highest expert ratings, with a median score of 4.5/5, outperforming other models such as GPT (4.0/5), Gemini (4.0/5), Copilot (4.0/5), MedGemma (3.75/5), and Llama (3.5/5).

evidence.title: Performance of multivariable risk prediction algorithms in predicting COPD exacerbations: a population-based study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of ACCEPT versus exacerbation history (standard of care) for predicting moderate/severe exacerbations
evidence.effect: ACCEPT 2.0 AUC 0.77 outperformed any and frequent exacerbator categories (AUC 0.69 and 0.67); ACCEPT 3.0-UK net beneficial and superior to exacerbation history across wide range of thresholds.
evidence.quote: ACCEPT 2.0 achieved an AUC of 0.77 for predicting moderate/severe exacerbations, outperforming both any and frequent exacerbator categories (AUC: 0.69 and 0.67, respectively).

evidence.title: Automatic diagnosis of osteonecrosis of the femoral head and segmentation of necrotic regions using deep learning at computed tomography: a real-world multicenter study
evidence.outcome: Model diagnostic and segmentation performance compared against three orthopaedic surgeons
evidence.effect: Model outperformed surgeons in diagnosis and matched a 10-year-experienced attending in segmentation.
evidence.quote: It outperformed surgeons in diagnosis and matched a 10-year-experienced attending in segmentation.

evidence.title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two candidate LLMs against tumor board decisions on the same cases
evidence.effect: Gemini 2.5 (guideline-integrated) outperformed MedGemma 27B on concordance and safety (p<0.001); full concordance 81.7% vs 57.0% (T=0) and 62.3% (T=1).
evidence.quote: Comparisons of the three-category concordance distributions showed significant differences between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 0.0) ( p < 0.001) and between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 1.0) ( p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

evidence.title: Prompt Architecture as a High-Impact Design Factor in Expert-Rated Clinical Documentation Quality: A Controlled Comparative Study in Inpatient Rehabilitation
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated quality of LLM discharge reports versus human-authored reports on same cases
evidence.effect: Friedman χ2(3)=23.93, p<0.001; human reports scored significantly lower than SP (p=0.003), SBP (p=0.003), SBP+W (p=0.025) after Bonferroni correction.
evidence.quote: Post hoc pairwise comparisons using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction showed that Strategy A yielded significantly lower scores than Strategy B ( p = 0.003), Strategy C ( p = 0.003), and Strategy D ( p = 0.025).
evidence.country: Not reported (national public hospitals; likely Spain)

evidence.title: Large-language-models for pediatric diagnosis: Performance evaluation using real-world clinical notes from common and rare cases
evidence.outcome: Top-1 diagnostic accuracy of LLMs compared with pediatric clinicians on the same cases
evidence.effect: o1-preview and Claude-3.5 Sonnet achieved mean Top-1 accuracies of 60.0% and 59.0% versus clinicians' 48.2% (ORs 2.99 and 2.75, both P < 0.001).
evidence.quote: o1-preview and Claude-3.5 Sonnet achieved mean Top-1 accuracies of 60.0% and 59.0%, respectively, compared to clinicians' 48.2% (odds ratios [ORs]: 2.99 and 2.75, both P < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: real clinical cases (each queried three times per LLM; compared with 78 pediatric clinicians)

evidence.title: Leveraging transformer-based artificial intelligence for enhanced anesthetic decision-making in orthopedic surgery
evidence.outcome: Comparison against classical and neural baselines and clinician behavior
evidence.effect: Improved discrimination and precision-recall versus baselines; off-policy estimators show higher counterfactual utility than clinician behavior and behavior cloning.
evidence.quote: Off-policy estimators indicate higher counterfactual utility than clinician behavior and behavior cloning while ensuring zero-guardrail violations.

evidence.title: Clinical decision support in hematological malignancies using a case-grounded AI agent
evidence.outcome: expert ratings of recommendation quality
evidence.effect: mean score of 4.22 with HemaGuide versus 3.21 as a plain model without the agent framework
evidence.quote: The highest-capacity open-weight model (gpt-oss-120b) achieved the strongest overall ratings through HemaGuide (mean 4.22 ± 0.063) versus substantially lower and more variable scores as a plain model (3.21 ± 0.39; P = 0.0015) (Fig. 2b ).

evidence.title: Automated generation of structured breast ultrasound reports using BreastViT and ChatGPT
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Rater scores comparing BreastViT+GPT-4o against GPT-4o alone and BreastViT alone on external cases
evidence.effect: Combined BreastViT + GPT-4o scored highest across all categories (7.31, 7.61, 8.03, 8.02), significantly superior to standalone models (all P < 0.05).
evidence.quote: These scores were significantly superior to those of the standalone models (all P < 0.05).

evidence.title: Radiologist-Large Language Model Collaboration in Dermatologic Ultrasound Reporting: Evaluating the Clinical Utility of ChatGPT
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: LLM versus radiologist comparison
evidence.effect: Diagnostic accuracy differed across same-data comparators: Condition 3 83.2%, radiologist 55.4%, image-only LLM 26.2% (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic accuracy was highest in Condition 3 (83.2%), compared with Condition 1 (55.4%) and Condition 2 (26.2%) (p<0.001).

evidence.title: AI-enabled clinical decision support in breast cancer care: a blinded multicenter benchmarking study comparing medically specialized with a general-purpose system
evidence.outcome: Rated quality of breast cancer treatment plans across specialized versus general-purpose AI systems by blinded specialists
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5 Thinking rated significantly higher in all categories; ranked top in 96.4% of rater-case combinations vs 3.6% OpenEvidence; Prof. Valmed never ranked first.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-5 Thinking achieved significantly higher ratings across all evaluation categories, with no significant differences between the two medically specialized systems.

evidence.title: A comparative study of four large language models in treatment decision-making for Hip impingement syndrome based on real-world data
evidence.venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
evidence.outcome: Comparison of four LLMs' treatment decision accuracy against real-world treatment outcomes on same cases
evidence.effect: With structured records (Group B), GPT-5 accuracy 88%, Gemini 2.5 Pro 62%, DeepSeek-R1 58%, Grok-4 42%.
evidence.quote: Under the same conditions, the other models showed inferior performance (Gemini 2.5 Pro: 62% accuracy; DeepSeek-R1: 58%; Grok-4: 42%).

evidence.title: Initial Experience With a Deep Learning Algorithm for Detecting Posterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion on Noncontrast Computed Tomography
evidence.outcome: DL algorithm versus neuroradiologist on noncontrast CT for PC-LVO detection
evidence.effect: Algorithm sensitivity 55.4%, specificity 80.9%, AUC 0.72; neuroradiologist sensitivity 27.4%, specificity 91.8%.
evidence.quote: The neuroradiologist achieved a sensitivity of 27.4% and specificity of 91.8%.

evidence.title: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-5 in evaluating root canal treatment and periapical pathosis on periapical radiographs
evidence.outcome: Overall diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-5 versus general dentists on periapical radiographs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5 overall accuracy 54.0%-63.2% was significantly lower than general dentists 76.0%-85.6% (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Overall accuracy (54.0%-63.2%) was significantly lower than that of general dentists (76.0%-85.6%) (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language models against practicing clinicians on psychopathological assessment
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy versus early-career clinicians on AMDP item-level psychopathological assessment
evidence.effect: GPT-5.1 and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview accuracy 0.72 (64th percentile of clinicians); GPT-5.1 per-scenario 0.81/0.76/0.60 vs clinician means 0.79/0.68/0.58.
evidence.quote: GPT-5.1, selected for a marginal advantage, showed per-scenario accuracies of 0.81 (depression), 0.76 (mania), and 0.60 (schizophrenia) versus clinician means of 0.79, 0.68, and 0.58.
evidence.sample_unit: early-career clinicians (benchmark comparators); 10 LLMs rated transcripts of 3 simulated interviews across 100 AMDP items

evidence.title: From Gram Stain to Decision Support: Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models in Blood Culture Microscopy
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy versus expert microbiologists and reference standard on Gram stain interpretation
evidence.effect: Experts achieved 100% concordance for Gram type and major morphology; LLM combined accuracies were 82-84%, with morphology 84-85% and Gram type 95-98%.
evidence.quote: LLM accuracy was high for Gram-type classification (95-98%) but lower for cellular morphology (84-85%), resulting in combined accuracies of 82-84%.

evidence.title: Exploring the Role of AI in Enhancing Nuclear Medicine Report Impressions Generated by Trainees and ChatGPT-4o: Comparative Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Correctness, completeness, clarity of AI vs trainee PET/CT impressions rated blindly by physicians
evidence.effect: Correct 92% AI vs 91% trainee (P=.80); completeness higher for AI (mean 4.52 vs 4.09, P<.001); clarity, organization, satisfaction similar; AI more often criticized for excess length (33% vs 0%).
evidence.quote: AI-generated impressions were rated as correct in 92% of reports (mean 0.92, SD 0.27) and trainee-generated impressions rated as correct in 91% of reports (mean 0.91, SD 0.29; P=.80, negligible effect size).

evidence.title: Large language model-generated clinical summaries in emergency departments: A blinded comparison study
evidence.outcome: Blinded physician ratings of LLM vs physician-authored ED one-liner summaries on accuracy, completeness, utility
evidence.effect: LLM summaries rated higher: accuracy 4.18 vs 3.40 (β=0.78; 95% CI 0.50-1.07); completeness 3.69 vs 3.25 (β=0.44); clinical utility 3.88 vs 3.21 (β=0.67).
evidence.quote: We found that across all dimensions, LLM-generated summaries received higher ratings than physician-authored summaries.

evidence.title: Treatment effects prediction and clinical decision-making system for retinal vein occlusion by artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: AI retreatment prediction accuracy compared with retinal specialists on same data
evidence.effect: AI system achieved higher predictive accuracy than retinal specialists while substantially reducing image interpretation time.
evidence.quote: In the reader study, the AI system achieved higher predictive accuracy than retinal specialists while substantially reducing image interpretation time.

evidence.title: Automating clinical history extraction for flow cytometry panel selection using an EHR-integrated large language model
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM against current CLS workflow on same cases
evidence.effect: ChatEHR matched CLS on history extraction (78% vs 78%) but was worse on panel selection (47% vs 78%); processing time 20.3 s vs 41 s.
evidence.quote: ChatEHR achieved comparable accuracy to CLS in extracting and categorizing prior hematologic diagnoses (78% vs. 78%).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in the Clinical Management of Patients With Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Insights From Real-World Patient Data
evidence.outcome: LLM risk stratification performance versus clinical risk scores and ML models on same patients
evidence.effect: GBS had the best clinical-score AUROC (0.73). LLMs were inferior to clinical scores, especially GBS. Hybrid LLM-score models did not outperform GBS alone (best GBS+GPT-5 AUROC 0.670).
evidence.quote: LLMs showed moderate performance in UGIB risk stratification and endoscopic prediction but were inferior to clinical scores, especially GBS.

evidence.title: Skyer: a novel benchmark for evaluating the effectiveness of large language models in emergency department triage
evidence.outcome: LLM triage accuracy and weighted score compared with human triage experts on same scenarios
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4.5-preview (77% accuracy, mean weight 377.5/550) and Gemini-2.5_05-06 (74%, 365/550) outperformed human experts (64%, 253.5/550); p<0.05, Cohen's D 2.18 and 1.98.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4.5-preview (77% accuracy, mean weight 377.5 out of 550) and Gemini-2.5_05-06 (74% accuracy, mean weight 365/550) significantly outperformed human-triage-experts accuracy (64% accuracy, mean weight 253.5/550) and other models.

evidence.title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of candidate LLM configurations (fine-tuned, RAG, hybrid) compared against baseline LLM on same queries
evidence.effect: Overall accuracy baseline 68% vs FT 92.7%, RAG 91.3%, hybrid 97.3% (P<.001); pairwise all enhanced significantly better than baseline.
evidence.quote: Pairwise comparisons demonstrated that all 3 knowledge-enhanced approaches significantly outperformed the baseline model.
evidence.sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

evidence.title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
evidence.outcome: ANN and XGBoost versus best traditional NTCP model (LKB) discrimination on hold-out test set
evidence.effect: ANN AUC 0.93 vs LKB 0.89 (p=0.420) parotid; 0.95 vs 0.91 (p=0.380) oral cavity; 0.91 vs 0.88 (p=0.150) larynx; no significant differences; XGBoost overfit (test AUC 0.67-0.82).
evidence.quote: No statistically significant differences were observed between ANN and the best traditional model (LKB) for any organ.

evidence.title: Comparative Interpretation of Pediatric Electrocardiograms by Large Language Models and a Pediatrician
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs against a pediatrician on same ECG data
evidence.effect: Pediatrician outperformed all three LLMs (accuracy 78.7% vs 71.9%, 66.9%, 50.0%); accuracy varied markedly across models.
evidence.quote: The clinician outperformed the LLMs in pediatric ECG interpretation.

evidence.title: ConLymphNet: A Generalizable Region-Constrained Deep Learning Architecture for Precise Abdominal Lymph Node Segmentation Across Cancer Types
evidence.outcome: AI model detection rate and processing time compared with radiologists
evidence.effect: Model detection rate 89.6% comparable with experienced residents (89.2%); processing time 28.7 ± 12.4 s vs 165.3 ± 47.8 s.
evidence.quote: The model's detection rate (89.6%) was comparable with experienced residents (89.2%) but with reduced processing time (28.7 ± 12.4s v 165.3 ± 47.8 s).
evidence.sample_unit: contrast-enhanced CT scans (training); external validation n=54 GBC, 81 public lymph node, 606 multicancer

evidence.title: Real-world evaluation of medication recommendation workflows: Retrieval augmentation, physician-RAG collaborative workflow, and prescribing quality
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLM workflows against physicians on same cases using reference standard
evidence.effect: Stand-alone LLM showed lower agreement and weaker structured prescribing accuracy than supervised workflows; Physician-RAG had the highest agreement with the expert reference.
evidence.quote: In this retrospective expert-reference-based evaluation, stand-alone LLM output showed lower agreement and weaker structured prescribing accuracy than supervised workflows.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Reasoning Models Versus Human Multidisciplinary Teams in Lung Cancer Decision-Making: Real-World Study
evidence.outcome: LRM recommendation quality versus human MDT decisions and versus each other, graded by oncologists
evidence.effect: GPT-5-Thinking avg_rec exceeded MDT grade in both phases (retrograde 4.90 vs 4.14, P<.001; anterograde 4.79 vs 4.34, P<.001); Deepseek-v3-r1 exceeded MDT only in retrograde phase (4.56 vs 4.14, P<.001; anterograde P=.15).
evidence.quote: The mean (95% CI) GPT-5-Thinking avg_rec exceeded MDT grade in both phases (retrograde: 4.90, 4.84-4.95 vs 4.14, 3.96-4.33; P<.001; anterograde: 4.79, 4.69-4.89 vs 4.34, 4.16-4.52; P<.001); Deepseek-v3-r1 exceeded MDT in the retrograde phase (4.56, 4.40-4.72 vs 4.14, 3.96-4.33; P<.001) but not the anterograde phase (4.54, 4.41-4.67 vs 4.34, 4.16-4.52; P=.15).

evidence.title: DETERIO-LLM: enhancing traditional deterioration risk scores with clinical context and advanced reasoning
evidence.outcome: PPV and F1 of DETERIO-LLM versus comparators including eCART on same cohort
evidence.effect: DETERIO-LLM achieved PPV 30.6% and F1 37.3%, outperforming eCART and all comparators, with comparable sensitivity.
evidence.quote: DETERIO-LLM significantly improved predictive precision over all comparators.

evidence.title: Multi-centre generalisability of deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck radiotherapy using DAHANCA real-world data
evidence.venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
evidence.outcome: Deep learning dose prediction versus a simpler median-based model on the same data
evidence.effect: The deep learning model outperformed the median model. OAR Dmean difference was 1.1 Gy [-0.6, 3.7] versus -4.6 Gy [-14.6, 3.9] for the median model, which had larger interquartile ranges.
evidence.quote: The dose prediction model outperformed the median-based model, with prediction-plan differences within interquartile ranges observed across cohorts, supporting generalisability.
evidence.sample_unit: treatment plans (42 internal test plans plus 560 national DAHANCA plans)

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in Approximating Clinically Confirmed Diagnoses From Structured Numerical Pure-Tone Audiogram Data
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of two LLMs versus expert clinical diagnosis on same audiogram data
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o accuracy 60.8% (kappa 0.578) vs Gemini 1.5 Pro 86.1% (kappa 0.848); Gemini significantly higher, showing candidate performance differs on the same data.
evidence.quote: The findings suggest that Gemini 1.5 Pro demonstrated stronger performance, achieving an accuracy of 86.1%, whereas ChatGPT-4o achieved 60.8% in interpreting real-world pure-tone audiograms.

evidence.title: A multimodal evidence-driven framework for clinical decision support in cognitive impairment
evidence.outcome: mHC versus flat multimodal baselines
evidence.effect: mHC outperformed flat multimodal baselines across 15 diagnostic labels.
evidence.quote: Across 15 diagnostic labels, mHC outperformed flat multimodal baselines, supporting hierarchical diagnostic modeling.

evidence.title: Comparative performance of chatgpt and gemini in diagnostic classification and clinical reasoning for open-angle glaucoma: a standardized scenario-based study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two LLMs on diagnostic accuracy, classification and reasoning on the same cases
evidence.effect: Accuracy 85.4% GPT-5.3 vs 75.0% Gemini (P=0.306); reasoning 4.4±0.6 vs 3.9±0.7 (P=0.011); kappa 0.675 vs 0.628.
evidence.quote: GPT-5.3 scored higher than Gemini in overall clinical reasoning (4.4 ± 0.6 vs. 3.9 ± 0.7, P = 0.011).

evidence.title: Large language models as a screening tool for the qualification of patients with Parkinson's disease for device-aided therapies
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM screening versus MANAGE-PD with specialist decisions for device-aided therapy eligibility
evidence.effect: Kappa about 0.575 (LLM) vs 0.567 (MANAGE-PD); no significant difference in kappa (p = 0.81) or discordant classifications (McNemar p = 1.0).
evidence.quote: Agreement with specialist decisions was similar for LLM-based screening and MANAGE-PD (κ ≈ 0.575 vs. 0.567), with no significant differences in Cohen's kappa (p = 0.81) or discordant classifications (McNemar p = 1.0).

evidence.title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
evidence.outcome: Stroke outcome model discrimination
evidence.effect: TabPFN AUROC 0.816 vs CatBoost 0.789 and logistic regression 0.700.
evidence.quote: While all models exhibited acceptable discrimination, the TabPFN model demonstrated the highest AUROC (0.816; 95% CI, 0.784 to 0.847), followed by CatBoost (0.789; 95% CI, 0.756 to 0.822) and logistic regression (0.700; 95% CI, 0.665 to 0.735).

evidence.title: Diagnostic Ambiguity in Appendicitis: Comparing Failure Modes of Large Language Models and Surgeons
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus surgeon specialists on same vignettes
evidence.effect: GPT-5 accuracy 95.3% vs specialist consensus 92.7% and GPT-4o 82.0% (P<0.001); in pediatric/geriatric vignettes GPT-5 93.8%, specialists 90.0%, GPT-4o 71.2%.
evidence.quote: GPT-5 achieved the highest accuracy (95.3%), exceeding GPT-4o (82.0%; P < 0.001) and slightly surpassing specialist consensus (92.7%).

evidence.title: Bigger Is Not Always Better: Computational Efficiency in Lexical Prehospital Triage Modeling
evidence.outcome: Compared simple ML model versus transformer models on the same data for predicting lifesaving intervention
evidence.effect: AUROC .793 for MLM vs .803 for BioBERT and DistilBERT; AP .670 vs .674 and .673. Performance was equivalent, and the LLMs needed far more computation, so the simpler model was sufficient.
evidence.quote: MLMs and LLMs produced broadly equivalent performance in predicting LSI (MLM: AUROC = .793 [.776, .810]; AP = .670 [.643, .695] vs. BioBERT: AUROC = .803 [.796, .816]; AP = .674 [.649, .698]) vs. DistilBERT: AUROC = .803 [.785, .811]; AP = .673 [.651, .688]).

evidence.title: AI-assisted VMAT planning incorporating deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck cancer: feasibility of quality standardization and human intervention for irregular cases
evidence.venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted plan quality versus experienced planner's clinical plans on the same cases
evidence.effect: Comparable PTV coverage and Paddick CI (0.478 vs 0.479); spinal cord PRV Dmax 23.97 vs 27.50 Gy (p<0.01); contralateral parotid worse with AI (20.16 vs 16.82 Gy).
evidence.quote: Regarding the OARs, the AI‐assisted plans significantly reduced doses to the spinal cord PRV, with lower values observed for both Dmax (27.50 ± 1.65 vs. 23.97 ± 2.12 Gy, p <0.01), and Dmean (17.69 ± 2.03 vs. 12.92 ± 1.65 Gy, p <0.01).

evidence.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbot Compared to Orthopedic Trauma Surgeons in Evaluating Indication for Surgery for Isolated Lateral Malleolar Fractures: a Retrospective Study
evidence.venue: Acta chirurgiae orthopaedicae et traumatologiae Cechoslovaca
evidence.outcome: AI chatbot versus three orthopedic trauma surgeons on surgical indication accuracy and AUC
evidence.effect: Agreement with actual outcome ranged 67.3-86% for all raters, AI within same range. AUC 0.63-0.67 comparable for all raters. AI measurements differed systematically on five of six parameters.
evidence.quote: ROC analysis showed comparable AUC values (0.63-0.67) for all raters.

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-5 for CT Imaging in Canadian CT Head Rule-Positive Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT-5.1 accuracy versus consultants, residents, CCHR and logistic model for predicting CT findings
evidence.effect: Probabilistic model accuracy 74.0%, consultants 69.3%, residents 66.9%; rule-based ChatGPT sensitivity 91.8%, specificity 22.2%; ER-simulation ChatGPT accuracy 54.3%; consultants outperformed ER simulation (p = 0.01).
evidence.quote: Consultants outperformed the ER simulation model (p = 0.01), while their performance was similar to that of the probabilistic model (p = 0.44).

evidence.title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Emergency Treatment Recommendation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Treatment recommendation accuracy of multiagent framework versus baseline LLMs on same cases
evidence.effect: Model-level accuracy ranges increased from 0.546-0.737 to 0.687-0.851 in group A, 0.587-0.698 to 0.671-0.813 in group B, and 0.507-0.646 to 0.667-0.750 in group C.
evidence.quote: Model-level accuracy ranges increased from 0.546-0.737 to 0.687-0.851 in group A, from 0.587-0.698 to 0.671-0.813 in group B, and from 0.507-0.646 to 0.667-0.750 in group C.
evidence.sample_unit: cases (1055 group A, 721 group B, 144 group C, 161 group D)

evidence.title: Real World Evaluation of AI-Based Tumor Cell Content Quantification for Molecular Tumor Profiling
evidence.venue: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
evidence.outcome: concordance with molecular quantification
evidence.effect: AI-based digital quantification showed stronger concordance (Rs = 0.63) than pathologists' visual quantification (Rs = 0.38).
evidence.quote: Agreement was lowest between VQ and MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38) and between VQ and DQ (Rs = 0.44), while DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63).

evidence.title: Validation of an AI-based automated Knee Inflammation MRI Scoring System for assessing bone marrow lesions
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI scoring with manual expert readers and human-human agreement on the same cases
evidence.effect: Human-to-iKIMRISS baseline ICC mean 0.72 vs human-to-human 0.76; agreement with 2 manual readers ICC 0.75 and 0.85.
evidence.quote: The inter-reader reliability analysis (see Supplementary Table S2-S9 ) highlights that human-to-iKIMRISS agreement in baseline KIMRISS BML scoring across the 3 scoring subregions (mean ICC = 0.72) was comparable to human-to-human agreement (mean ICC = 0.76), suggesting that iKIMRISS agreed with human readers to a similar degree as human readers did with each other ( Supplementary Table S8 ).
evidence.sample_unit: patients (2-time-point knee MRI cases) read by 11 readers

evidence.title: Real-world assessment of a deep learning neural network algorithm for prostate cancer detection in MRI using true de novo data
evidence.outcome: AI versus clinical radiologist PI-RADS discrimination on the same cases
evidence.effect: Heat map AUC 0.76 versus PI-RADS 0.73 (difference 0.03, p=0.38). ROI AUC 0.71 (difference -0.02, p=0.43). Neither AI output differed significantly from radiologists.
evidence.quote: Neither the XProstate Heat Map (AUC difference = 0.03, 95% CI: -0.04, 0.10, p = 0.38) nor the XProstate ROI (AUC difference = -0.02, 95% CI: -0.09, 0.04, p = 0.43) was significantly different from the radiologist PI-RADS score.
