evidence.title: Assessing a reduced-channel algorithm for end-to-end seizure detection on multiday EEG using inter-rater agreement with epileptologists
evidence.outcome: VED and Persyst 15 sensitivity and false positives per day versus expert epileptologists on same EEG records
evidence.effect: VED averaged sensitivity 77.0% [69.4-83.2] with 4.79 FPs/day; P15 65.4% [56.0-74.0] with 1.30 FPs/day; VED non-inferior in sensitivity but not FPs/day at Low confidence.
evidence.quote: VED at the official Low confidence level demonstrated non-inferiority in sensitivity (p < 0.01), while not meeting statistical non-inferiority for FPs/day.
evidence.sample_unit: EEG records (mean 67 hours each; 4,036 hours total)

evidence.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Auditing: Workflow-Error Detection, False-Positive Burden, and Limits of Key-Image Interpretation
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: Comparison of LLMs against physician reader and physician-interpreted findings input
evidence.effect: Key-image input underperformed physician-interpreted findings input for malignancy (AUC 0.879 vs 0.971) and BI-RADS (AUC 0.887 vs 0.984).
evidence.quote: In the full cohort, key-image input underperformed physician-interpreted findings input for malignancy classification (AUC, 0.879 vs 0.971) and BI-RADS risk classification (AUC, 0.887 vs 0.984).
evidence.sample_unit: breast ultrasound examinations (300-report error-enriched subset for report auditing)

evidence.title: Large language model treatment-pathway outputs based on structured clinical text in mid- and low rectal cancer: Concordance with multidisciplinary team decisions and features associated with discordance
evidence.venue: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
evidence.outcome: LLM concordance with MDT compared against majority-class baseline
evidence.effect: Preoperatively the LLM had the same crude concordance as the majority-class baseline but higher κ and balanced category-specific concordance; postoperatively it exceeded the baseline across these metrics.
evidence.quote: Compared with the majority-class baseline, the LLM had the same preoperative crude concordance but higher κ and balanced category-specific concordance; postoperatively, it exceeded the majority-class baseline across these metrics.

evidence.title: AI-Driven vision large language framework for pediatric pain assessment
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of AI pain scoring versus expert consensus, compared with senior experts and ML methods
evidence.effect: PA-VLLF-ChatGPT achieved 86.36% accuracy on expert-labeled pain scores, comparable to senior experts (84.69%, p > 0.05) and outperforming machine-learning approaches.
evidence.quote: In this dataset, PA-VLLF-ChatGPT successfully aligned with the collective expert consensus, achieving 86.36% accuracy on expert-labeled pain scores, performing comparably to senior experts (84.69%, p > 0.05) and outperforming machine-learning approaches in our comparisons; precision of pain-level assessment was evaluated using complementary metrics (MAX agreement and Z-Score).

evidence.title: Feasibility of LLM-assisted post-discharge tuberculosis care: A comparative study of medication counseling, patient education, and follow-up planning
evidence.outcome: LLM vs TB physician responses on precision, recall, F1 and subjective ratings
evidence.effect: Patient education: LLM precision 0.86 vs 0.50 (P<.001), recall 0.53 vs 0.14, F1 0.65 vs 0.22. No significant objective differences for medication counseling and follow-up planning (all P>.050). LLMs rated higher on suitability, understandability, empathy.
evidence.quote: Conversely, no statistically significant differences were observed in objective metrics for medication counseling and follow-up planning (all P > .050), although LLMs demonstrated a tendency toward broader but more discordant coverage.

evidence.title: Measuring Depression Severity With Clinical Global Impression-Severity Scale Scores From Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models: Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs and prompting strategies against psychiatrist ratings on the same notes
evidence.effect: GPT-4o zero-shot had highest agreement with average human ratings (κ=0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.90); few-shot did not improve; Llama-4 zero-shot lower (κ=0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.80).
evidence.quote: GPT-4o with zero-shot prompting demonstrated the highest agreement with average human ratings (κ=0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.90), and few-shot prompting did not improve performance.

evidence.title: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Clinicians in Evidence-Based Cardiovascular Disease Management for People Living With HIV: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: AI model versus clinician ratings on accuracy, completeness, readability, reliability for HIV-CVD guideline questions
evidence.effect: All AI models scored higher than clinicians across all dimensions (P<.001); AI mean 3.44-3.68 vs clinicians mean 1.78-2.05; DeepSeek-R1 best.
evidence.quote: All AI models achieved significantly higher scores than clinicians across all dimensions (P<.001).

evidence.title: Critical Care-Specific vs General-Purpose Large Language Models in Emergency Intensive Care Unit Diagnosis: Single-Center Retrospective Paired Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Top-1 diagnostic accuracy of critical care-specific LLM versus general-purpose LLMs on same EICU data
evidence.effect: Final-stage top-1: Qiyuan 64.1% (118/184), GPT-5.1 59.2%, DeepSeek V3.1 57.1%, Qwen3-32B 51.6%; no significant gaps between Qiyuan and top 2 general models.
evidence.quote: Corrected pairwise comparisons (α=.0083) confirmed Qiyuan 3.0.1, GPT-5.1, and DeepSeek all outperformed Qwen3-32B significantly (all adjusted P<.008), while no statistical gaps were detected between Qiyuan 3.0.1 and the 2 top-performing general models.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o in delirium recognition: a pilot study
evidence.outcome: Delirium identification of ChatGPT-4o versus comparator model DeepSeek-V2 on same vignettes
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% (independent sessions) and 90% (consecutive run) of cases, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% of cases in both independent sessions and 90% in the consecutive-session run, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.

evidence.title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
evidence.outcome: Simpler-model comparison
evidence.effect: Adding clinical variables changed AUC by +0.015, +0.008, -0.009, and -0.029 across cohorts.
evidence.quote: Compared with the B-mode score-only model, adding clinical-ultrasound variables changed the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) by +0.015 in development, +0.008 in temporal validation, -0.009 in Center 2, and -0.029 in Center 3.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Computer-aided Detection for Identifying Missed Gastric Cancer After Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
evidence.outcome: Per-lesion sensitivity for missed gastric cancers, CADe versus 10 endoscopists on same images
evidence.effect: Per-lesion sensitivity 15.0% (9/60) for CADe vs 13.8% (83/600) for endoscopists (p = 0.538); per-image specificity 88.5% vs 94.8% (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: The per-lesion sensitivity for MGCs was 15.0% (9/60) and 13.8% (83/600) for CADe and endoscopist detection, respectively (p = 0.538).
evidence.sample_unit: endoscopic images (60 missed gastric cancer lesions; 10 endoscopists)

evidence.title: A Multidisciplinary Team-Based Large Language Model Framework for Predicting Postoperative Neurological Complications in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: Model Development and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: LLM configurations compared against traditional ML models and single-agent LLMs on same data
evidence.effect: Best GPT-5 MDT+ICL AUC 0.8419 vs random forest AUC 0.7857 internal validation; difference not significant (P=.18).
evidence.quote: The AUC of GPT-5 with MDT and in-context learning was also not significantly higher than that of the random forest model (P=.18).

evidence.title: Sequential vancomycin trough and dosing interval prediction in ICU patients using general purpose large language models: a head-to-head comparison of ChatGPT and GROK AI
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two LLMs on vancomycin trough and dosing interval prediction accuracy
evidence.effect: ChatGPT outperformed Grok for trough (MAE 4.07 vs 5.08 mg/L; ±2 mg/L accuracy 37.0% vs 29.0%); Grok better for interval (MAE 1.36 vs 1.61 h). Neither compared with pharmacist TDM.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT outperformed Grok in trough prediction (MAE 4.07 vs 5.08 mg/L; RMSE 5.55 vs 7.53 mg/L; ±2 mg/L accuracy 37.0% vs 29.0%), with greater advantage at T1/T2 and in renal dysfunction.
evidence.sample_unit: predictions (239 ICU admissions, 3 sequential vancomycin troughs each)

evidence.title: Large language models for MoCA-defined cognitive risk screening in obstructive sleep apnea using polysomnography and brain MRI reports: A retrospective single-center pilot study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of LLMs versus AHI rule and structured/TF-IDF baselines for MoCA<26
evidence.effect: AHI rule AUC 0.456; age-and-education model 0.759; GPT-5.2 0.698 (98.6% sensitivity, 47.4% specificity); Gemini 3 Pro 0.884, exceeding baselines after Holm correction.
evidence.quote: Gemini 3 Pro achieved the highest discrimination (AUC 0.884, 95% CI 0.822-0.934), exceeding the age-and-education model, the full structured model, the gradient-boosted structured model, and the input-matched TF-IDF model after Holm correction within their respective comparison families.

evidence.title: Development of an LLM pipeline exceeding physician-documented cardiovascular risk scores under routine clinical conditions
evidence.outcome: Agreement and deviation of AI pipeline scores vs treating physicians and other LLM configurations against expert ground truth
evidence.effect: Pipeline mean Krippendorff's α 0.78 vs 0.32 standalone LLMs, 0.39 RAG, 0.31 treating physicians; mean RMSE 0.89 vs 5.81, 1.85, 1.34.
evidence.quote: Pipeline-generated scores showed substantially higher agreement with expert adjudication than standalone LLMs, LLMs with RAG, and treating physicians (mean Krippendorff's α: 0.78 vs. 0.32 vs. 0.39 vs. 0.31) and lower deviation from ground truth (mean RMSE: 0.89 vs. 5.81 vs. 1.85 vs. 1.34).

evidence.title: Error Detection and Correction in Chinese Radiology Reports Using Large Language Models: Real-World Clinical Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of eight LLMs and eight human readers on identical error-detection reports
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 had the highest test-set detection rate at 89% (P=.001-.007 vs other 7 models) and matched radiologists (83% vs 80% and 78%).
evidence.quote: On the test set, DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest overall detection rate at 89% (95% CI 87%-90%), significantly better than the other 7 models (P=.001-.007).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Prompt Design and Internal Reasoning in Chatbot-Based Medical History Taking: Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: History coverage of LLM chatbot configurations versus rule-based baseline on same cases
evidence.effect: DT coverage 72.3% vs choice baseline 51.1% (Hedge g 1.53, P<.001); MN did not differ significantly from choice (P>.99).
evidence.quote: Post hoc pairwise t tests with Bonferroni correction ( Table 2 ) showed that the DT mode significantly outperformed all other configurations.

evidence.title: Multidisciplinary dental treatment planning by artificial intelligence: A comparative evaluation
evidence.venue: Journal of prosthodontics : official journal of the American College of Prosthodontists
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate AI tools on identical cases against expert reference standard
evidence.effect: Four AI tools compared on the same 10 cases; scores varied meaningfully: OpenEvidence 7.7±1.4, ChatGPT-5 7.6±1.1, Gemini 5.1±1.2, Copilot 4.7±3.1.
evidence.quote: Mean total scores were highest for OpenEvidence (7.7 ± 1.4) and ChatGPT-5 (7.6 ± 1.1), followed by Google Gemini (5.1 ± 1.2) and Microsoft Copilot (4.7 ± 3.1).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical cases (intraoral photo plus periapical radiograph)

evidence.title: Reproducibility of Tear Ferning Test Classification by Human Examiners and Artificial Intelligence Models: A Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI platforms versus human examiners on tear ferning grading against consensus
evidence.effect: Claude agreed best with consensus (4-grade weighted kappa 0.84; binary kappa 0.87), within interhuman range; ChatGPT and Gemini weighted kappa 0.48 each and underclassified abnormalities.
evidence.quote: Claude best matched the human benchmark, whereas ChatGPT and Gemini were less reproducible and systematically underclassified abnormalities.

evidence.title: Comparative diagnostic agreement of a supervised machine learning model and a general-purpose, zero-shot, non-domain-adapted large language model for classifying headache disorders using structured questionnaires
evidence.venue: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic agreement (Cohen's kappa) with specialist diagnosis, ML classifier vs zero-shot LLM on same data
evidence.effect: ML classifier kappa 0.46 vs LLM 0.26 (95% CI of difference 0.15-0.25); ML had higher macro precision, specificity, F-value; LLM higher macro sensitivity.
evidence.quote: The machine learning classifier showed significantly higher diagnostic agreement with the specialist than the LLM (Cohen's κ: 0.46 vs. 0.26; 95% confidence interval of the difference: 0.15-0.25).

evidence.title: Large Language Models as a New Tool for Therapists in Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: Blinded Clinician Rating Pilot Experiment
evidence.outcome: Clinician-rated quality of LLM vs human therapist responses across five quality dimensions
evidence.effect: Ratings were similar on a 1-5 scale, e.g. overall quality LLM 4.00 vs human 3.96 (d=0.06); empathy LLM 4.31 vs human 4.08 (d=0.42); helpfulness LLM 3.85 vs human 3.93.
evidence.quote: LLM-generated responses were judged to be of comparable quality to those written by human therapists, though qualitative feedback indicated they were at times generic and insufficiently challenging.

evidence.title: Transient Ischemic Attack Diagnosis using Explicit Criteria Outperforms Artificial Intelligence: a Prospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of AI versus explicit diagnostic criteria for TIA, against neurologist reference standard
evidence.effect: AI sensitivity 98.5%, specificity 11.7%; EDCT v1-3 sensitivities 95.5%, 91.0%, 91.0% with specificities 23.3%, 43.3%, 46.7%. AI labelled 119/127 patients as TIA.
evidence.quote: Structured clinical criteria (EDCT) outperformed an advanced AI model in distinguishing TIA from mimics in an emergency setting.

evidence.title: Improvement of Clinical Practice Guideline Appraisal by Human Experts and AI Agents by Using Structured Guidance: Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Validation Study
evidence.outcome: AI agent appraisal compared against human experts on the same guidelines (agreement and time)
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 ICC 0.711 vs reference, close to expert 1 (0.734) and above expert 2 (0.651); 5.44 min per guideline vs 14.97 and 7.39 min for experts.
evidence.quote: In contrast, DeepSeek-R1 completed appraisals in a mean of 5.44 (SD 0.16) minutes per guideline while maintaining reliability comparable to the more time-intensive human approach.

evidence.title: Assessing the feasibility of ChatGPT in predicting outcomes after intracerebral hemorrhage
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o mini vs two neurologists in predicting 3-month mRS after ICH
evidence.effect: GPT r=0.64 vs averaged clinician r=0.68; AUC for favorable outcome 0.86 vs 0.85; GPT mean difference -0.99 vs clinicians -0.35, so comparable discrimination but greater underestimation.
evidence.quote: GPT's accuracy in predicting favorable 3-month outcomes (defined as mRS 0-3) was comparable to clinician-averaged scores (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.85), with high sensitivity (88%) and moderate specificity (67%).

evidence.title: An interpretable data-driven approach to optimizing clinical fall risk assessment
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of recalibrated CSO vs existing JHFRAT and XGBoost benchmark against proxy labels
evidence.effect: CSO AUC-ROC 0.91 vs JHFRAT 0.86 (augmented); XGBoost higher at 0.96; augmented CSO sensitivity at threshold 13 was 0.57 vs 0.29 for JHFRAT.
evidence.quote: The CSO model demonstrated significant improvements over the current JHFRAT in classification alignment with the proxy labels (CSO AUC-ROC = 0.91, JHFRAT AUC-ROC = 0.86).

evidence.title: Streamlined TI-RADS Reporting From Bilingual Speech Recognition to LLM-Assisted Conclusion Generation Using a Two-Stage Workflow
evidence.outcome: ASR word error rate versus commercial model
evidence.effect: LLM ASR WER 1.0 [IQR 0-2.0] vs commercial 3.0 [IQR 2.0-3.0], P < 0.001.
evidence.quote: In stage 1, the LLM-based ASR model demonstrated a significantly lower overall word error rate compared to the commercial ASR model (1.0 [IQR 0-2.0] vs 3.0 [IQR 2.0-3.0], P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Rethinking Pediatric Asthma Education Through Large Language Model Generation and Simplification: Randomized Double-Blind Study
evidence.outcome: AI materials versus expert-authored responses
evidence.effect: AI-GRs vs PEARs total scores: professionals 76.17 vs 72.97 (Holm P=.53); families 68.77 vs 64.18 (Holm P=.15); AI-SRs vs PEARs adjusted P>.99.
evidence.quote: After Holm correction, none of the prespecified comparisons between either AI group and PEARs was statistically significant for the overall score or its 4 dimensions.

evidence.title: From zero-shot to fine-tuning: optimize large language models for error detection of ultrasound reports
evidence.outcome: Error detection performance of fine-tuned open-source LLMs versus proprietary LLMs and radiologists
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned Qwen3-14B reached accuracy 0.931 and Macro-F1 0.739, approaching senior radiologists (0.764) and outperforming most proprietary LLMs.
evidence.quote: Some fine-tuned open-source LLMs maintained performance despite smaller parameter sizes and outperformed most proprietary LLMs with vastly larger parameter counts.

evidence.title: A two-stage evaluation of large language models for guideline-based Q&A and draft rehabilitation planning in stroke care
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of candidate LLMs on the same questions and cases
evidence.effect: Four LLMs compared on 100 questions; top two compared on Q&A with no significant differences and on 60 cases where ChatGPT-o3 outperformed DeepSeek across all five domains.
evidence.quote: In Stage 2b, ChatGPT-o3 significantly outperformed DeepSeek across correctness, completeness, readability, helpfulness, and safety in the GEE analysis.
evidence.sample_unit: de-identified stroke cases (Stage 2b); also 100 questions in Stage 1 and 20 guideline-derived questions in Stage 2a

evidence.title: Validation of ST-RADS calculator: AI web tool for soft tissue-RADS implementation in de novo non-operated tumors and tumor-like lesions
evidence.outcome: AI calculator versus four MSK radiologists on ST-RADS sensitivity and specificity
evidence.effect: Sensitivity similar (85% radiologists, 86% image-only, 81% text-only, 86% combined). Specificity 76.5% radiologists vs 69.4% text-only (p=0.46), 61.2% combined, 25.5% image-only.
evidence.quote: Text features-only did not differ significantly from radiologists (p = 0.46).

evidence.title: Large Language Models Approximate Inter-Expert Agreement in Glaucoma Suspect and Glaucoma Classification from Multimodal Data
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic agreement versus glaucoma specialists on same data against consensus reference standards
evidence.effect: Specialist accuracy 71.3%-83.9% (κ 0.46-0.68); GPT-5 Pro long prompt 80.4%-85.7% (κ 0.61-0.71); Gemini 3 Pro long prompt 80.9%-84.3% (κ 0.62-0.68); Grok 2.2 near chance.
evidence.quote: Glaucoma specialist accuracy ranged from 71.3% to 83.9% (κ = 0.46-0.68).

evidence.title: Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement
evidence.outcome: candidate-model performance comparison
evidence.effect: Local CatBoost AUC-ROC 0.92; F1 0.74; Brier 0.04 vs SafeNET Brier 0.055.
evidence.quote: Locally trained CatBoost models outperformed SafeNET (AUC-ROC, 0.92; F1, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.72-0.78) and demonstrated improved calibration (Brier 0.04 vs. 0.055).

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of AI enhancements to rules-based clinical triage chatbot: Convergent mixed-methods study
evidence.outcome: Triage accuracy of AI-enhanced chatbots versus existing rules-based chatbot on same vignettes
evidence.effect: Rules-based 71.8% (95% CI 56.2-83.5%) vs Dialogflow 30.8% (p = 0.002) and Gemini 41.0% (p = 0.031); Dialogflow, ChatGPT, Gemini statistically indistinguishable.
evidence.quote: The rules-based chatbot was most accurate (71.8%, 95% CI 56.2-83.5%), outperforming Dialogflow (30.8%, p = 0.002) and Gemini (41.0%, p = 0.031).

evidence.title: Multimodal artificial intelligence-based decision support for stroke classification in medical emergency calls using call transcripts and patient health records: A retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
evidence.outcome: Stroke-class F1 of AI models versus EMCC operator baseline on same calls
evidence.effect: Multimodal model stroke F1 0.77 vs operator baseline 0.73 and transcript-only model; about 26 false alerts per 1,000 calls vs 36 for operators at assumed 1.2% prevalence.
evidence.quote: The multimodal classification model achieved a stroke-class F1-score of 0.77, exceeding that of both the transcript-only model and the operator baseline (0.73).

evidence.title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
evidence.outcome: AI-human double reading compared with conventional human-human double reading on the same images
evidence.effect: Comparable accuracy for DR and RVO with about 46-49% fewer human reads; AMD sensitivity higher in two of three configurations, with lower specificity (≥0.978).
evidence.quote: Accordingly, human–human double reading required 2.00 to 2.10 human reads per image, whereas AI–human double reading required 1.02 to 1.11, corresponding to a 46% to 49% reduction in human reading events ( Table 2 ).

evidence.title: Comparison of OneChoice AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Recommendations with Infectious Disease Specialists and Non-Specialists for Empirical Urinary Tract Infection Therapy in Lima, Peru
evidence.outcome: Concordance of AI antimicrobial recommendations with physicians and blinded expert preference in discordant cases
evidence.effect: First-choice concordance was 50.9% and general concordance 62.5%. ID specialists showed higher concordance than non-ID physicians (72.9% vs. 57.8% general). The panel preferred the CDSS in 90.5-93.2% of discordant cases.
evidence.quote: Among discordant evaluations, the external panel judged the CDSS recommendation to be preferable in 90.5-93.2% of cases.
evidence.sample_unit: evaluations (by 194 physicians across 42 real UTI cases)

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Large Language Models for Four-Class Benchmark of Oral Autoimmune Blistering Diseases: A Multicenter Paired Study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head diagnostic accuracy of two candidate multimodal LLMs on same cases
evidence.effect: Claude achieved higher accuracy than Gemini (92.0% vs. 86.0%, p = 0.012), kappa 0.893 vs. 0.813, macro-AUC 0.998 vs. 0.965.
evidence.quote: Claude achieved significantly higher diagnostic accuracy than Gemini (92.0% vs. 86.0%, p = 0.012), stronger agreement with the reference standard (κ = 0.893 vs. 0.813), and superior discrimination (macro-AUC 0.998 vs. 0.965).

evidence.title: External Validation of Clinical Risk Scores and Machine Learning Models for Predicting 30-Day Cardiovascular Risk After Noncardiac Surgery: The PERICARE Study
evidence.outcome: ML models' AUROC compared with established clinical risk scores (AUB-HAS2, RCRI) on external validation data
evidence.effect: No ML model showed statistically significant AUROC superiority over AUB-HAS2 (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed RCRI; Naive Bayes highest AUROC 0.738.
evidence.quote: However, in external validation, no ML model demonstrated statistically significant AUROC superiority over the AUB-HAS2 score (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed the RCRI.

evidence.title: Retrospective comparison of three commercial artificial intelligence algorithms for detection of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in the emergency radiology department
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of three commercial AI algorithms versus radiologists on the same CT exams
evidence.effect: Aidoc performed best, with 90.3% sensitivity and 99.0% specificity; AI performance varied substantially, and only one system showed clinically relevant accuracy.
evidence.quote: Aidoc performed best, with 90.3% sensitivity and 99.0% specificity.

evidence.title: A Flexible-Horizon Clinical Decision Support Model for Dementia Early Detection and Risk Prediction in Secondary Care: A Responsible AI Approach
evidence.outcome: Flexible-horizon ML model versus Cox proportional hazards baseline: G-mean, sensitivity, specificity
evidence.effect: ML had higher G-mean at four of five horizons and higher specificity from 48 months; Cox had greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.
evidence.quote: Compared with a Cox proportional hazards model, our flexible-horizon ML model achieved a higher G-mean at four of the five evaluated horizons and higher specificity from 48 months onwards, whereas Cox achieved greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.

evidence.title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
evidence.outcome: AI-assisted negative-screening workflow versus human-only reading on same images: sensitivity, specificity, workload
evidence.effect: Workload cut to 7.3%-8.0% (DR), 11.7%-11.9% (RVO), 13.5%-16.8% (AMD); sensitivity lower for DR and AMD, unchanged for RVO; specificity not significantly changed.
evidence.quote: Thus, the MRMC analysis showed a significant sensitivity trade-off for DR and AMD, with no statistically significant specificity gain, while RVO performance was preserved.

evidence.title: Large language models fail to reliably predict emergent catheterization laboratory activation from prehospital electrocardiograms
evidence.venue: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
evidence.outcome: LLM performance compared against existing ECG machine algorithm on same ECGs
evidence.effect: ECG machine algorithm had sensitivity 67.7% and higher specificity (64.2%) than all LLMs; LLMs did not outperform the existing software.
evidence.quote: The ECG machine algorithm demonstrated more balanced performance, with sensitivity of 67.7% (95% CI 61.4-73.4) and higher specificity (64.2%) than all LLMs.

evidence.title: Clinical implementation and evaluation of an artificial intelligence-driven one-click automatic planning system for functional lung avoidance radiotherapy
evidence.outcome: Automatic FLART plan quality versus manual FLART and conventional plans, including blinded clinician review
evidence.effect: 87.9% of automatic plans clinically acceptable without modification; 68.7% rated comparable (38.4%) or superior (30.3%) to manual FLART plans; high-function lung mean dose reduced 15.1% versus manual ConvRT.
evidence.quote: Blinded reviews indicated that 87.9% of automatic FLART plans were clinically acceptable without modification, and 68.7% were rated as comparable (38.4%) or superior (30.3%) to manual FLART plans.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Data Abstraction Demonstrates Accuracy and Reliability for NSQIP
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
evidence.outcome: Abstraction accuracy of LLM versus human abstractors against a plastic surgeon reference standard
evidence.effect: LLM accuracy 99.33% (61 errors) vs human 98.19% (164 errors); McNemar p<0.001; Chi-square p<0.001
evidence.quote: Overall abstraction accuracy was 99.33% (61 errors) for the LLM versus 98.19% (164 errors) for human abstraction (McNemar p<0.001; Chi-square p<0.001).

evidence.title: Concordance between GPT-4 and a multidisciplinary tumor board in pancreatic cancer: A prospective pilot study
evidence.outcome: Concordance of GPT-4 treatment recommendations with multidisciplinary tumor board (standard of care) decisions
evidence.effect: Overall concordance 73.3% (33/45), κ = 0.64; lowest with diagnostic workup (50.0% discordance) and complex cases.
evidence.quote: The observed agreement before literature-based prompting was 73.3% (33 cases, κ = 0.64, p < 0.0001, Fig. 1 ).

evidence.title: Fine-tuning a compact large language model on real-world cases yields diagnostic performance comparable to flagship models in rheumatology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic hit1 of fine-tuned compact model versus flagship and other LLMs on the same test cases
evidence.effect: Fine-tuning raised Qwen3-8B hit1 from 68.41% to 79.84%, highest among evaluated models; physician-adjudicated Hit1 91.6% versus 93.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol (1000 cases).
evidence.quote: Fine-tuning increased Qwen3-8B's hit1 from 68.41% to 79.84%, the highest among the evaluated models on the internal test set.

evidence.title: Comparison of Multimodal Large Language Models and Oral and Maxillofacial Radiologists in the Detection of Incidental Findings on Panoramic Radiographs: A CBCT-Referenced Diagnostic Accuracy Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance of multimodal LLMs versus expert radiologists on same radiographs against CBCT reference
evidence.effect: Expert sensitivity 89.5-91.6%, specificity 92.0-93.0%, accuracy 91.8-92.9% versus LLMs 75.1-83.1%, 88.0-90.0%, 86.8-89.0%; reader effect significant (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Under the consumer-interface conditions and access period tested, the LLMs performed below the experts, particularly for high-risk findings, and should not be used independently to evaluate panoramic radiographs.
evidence.sample_unit: panoramic radiographs (4500 finding-level decisions per reader)

evidence.title: Locally deployed large language model for real-world lecanemab eligibility pre-screening.
evidence.outcome: Eligibility classification accuracy of LLM pipeline versus rule-based extractor comparator on hold-out set
evidence.effect: LLM-based pipeline achieved 94% accuracy and Cohen's kappa 0.90, significantly surpassing the rule-based comparator (80% accuracy).
evidence.quote: The LLM-based pipeline achieved 94% accuracy and a Cohen's kappa of 0.90 on the hold-out set, significantly surpassing the rule-based comparator (80% accuracy) and demonstrating performance comparable to human experts.

evidence.title: Development of a ChatGPT-based assistant in multidisciplinary team discussions in oncological urology: the UroMDT Advisor study
evidence.outcome: Agreement of GPT recommendations with urologists, oncologists, radiation oncologists, and final MDT decision
evidence.effect: Exact agreement 61.7%, 66.7%, 63.3%, 66.7%; Cohen's kappa 0.401, 0.489, 0.441, 0.482 (moderate agreement).
evidence.quote: Exact agreement between UroMDT Advisor and urologists, oncologists, radiation oncologists, and final MDT decisions was 61.7%, 66.7%, 63.3%, and 66.7%, respectively; the corresponding unweighted Cohen's kappa values were 0.401, 0.489, 0.441, and 0.482.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a deep learning-based clinical decision support model.
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric orthopedics. Part B
evidence.outcome: Model diagnostic performance versus board-certified emergency physicians on same radiographs
evidence.effect: Model test accuracy 90.34%, sensitivity 93.5%, specificity 86.8%; physicians accuracy 87.6%, sensitivity 90.5%, specificity 84.7%; differences not statistically significant (P > 0.05).
evidence.quote: Diagnostic performance differences between the model and physicians were not statistically significant (P > 0.05).

evidence.title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
evidence.outcome: Zero-shot LLM insulin dosing performance versus trained RL agents in simulator
evidence.effect: Carefully prompted smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) achieved comparable or superior clinical performance versus trained SRAs, particularly in stable cohorts; limitations in other settings.
evidence.quote: Our results indicate that carefully designed zero-shot prompts enable smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) to achieve comparable or superior clinical performance relative to extensively trained SRAs, particularly in stable patient cohorts.

evidence.title: Is ChatGPT-5 Ready for Mammogram VQA?
evidence.outcome: GPT-5 mammogram performance compared with human experts and domain-specific fine-tuned models
evidence.effect: GPT-5 was best among GPT models but lagged human experts and fine-tuned models; sensitivity 63.5% and specificity 52.3% versus human expert estimates.
evidence.quote: Compared with human expert estimations, GPT-5 exhibited lower sensitivity (63.5%) and specificity (52.3%).
evidence.sample_unit: mammography images/questions across four public datasets (EMBED, InBreast, CMMD, CBIS-DDSM)

evidence.title: A Comparison and Evaluation of Fine-tuned Convolutional Neural Networks to Large Language Models for Image Classification and Segmentation of Brain Tumors on MRI
evidence.outcome: Glioma classification and segmentation performance of a general LLM versus custom 3D CNNs on the same BraTS data
evidence.effect: CNN reached 80% accuracy on LGG vs HGG; base LLM 76% accuracy with 18% specificity; fine-tuned LLM 72% accuracy and 55% specificity. LLM segmentation clustered near image center with no spatial accuracy.
evidence.quote: Overall, CNNs outperformed LLMs in both tasks.

evidence.title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE): Benchmarking Frontier Multimodal AI Against Human Experts and a Taxonomy of Visual Reasoning Errors in Radiology
evidence.outcome: Frontier AI diagnostic accuracy compared against radiologists and trainees on same cases
evidence.effect: Radiologists 83%, trainees 45%, all AI models lower (best GPT-5 30%).
evidence.quote: Board-certified radiologists achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (83%), outperforming trainees (45%) and all AI models (best performance shown by GPT-5: 30%).

evidence.title: Cross-Representation Benchmarking in Time-Series Electronic Health Records for Clinical Outcome Prediction
evidence.outcome: Comparative performance of complex pre-trained models versus simpler count-based baselines on same EHR data
evidence.effect: Pre-trained CLMBR was highly sample-efficient in few-shot settings, but simpler count-based models were competitive given sufficient data; event stream models performed best overall.
evidence.quote: Pre-trained models like CLMBR are highly sample-efficient in few-shot settings, though simpler count-based models can be competitive given sufficient data.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark tasks (MIMIC-IV ICU tasks and EHRSHOT longitudinal tasks)

evidence.title: Identifying Imaging Follow-Up in Radiology Reports: A Comparative Analysis of Traditional ML and LLM Approaches
evidence.outcome: Compared LLMs against simpler traditional ML baselines on same follow-up imaging classification data
evidence.effect: GPT-4o (Advanced) F1 = 0.832 and GPT-OSS-20B (Advanced) F1 = 0.828; LR and SVM performed strongly (F1 = 0.776 and 0.775), so simpler models remain valuable baselines.
evidence.quote: LR and SVM also performed strongly (F1 = 0.776 and 0.775), underscoring that while LLMs approach human-level agreement through prompt optimization, interpretable and resource-efficient models remain valuable baselines.

evidence.title: Balancing Natural Language Processing Accuracy and Normalisation in Extracting Medical Insights
evidence.outcome: accuracy versus simpler rule-based methods
evidence.effect: Rule-based methods had higher accuracy for information retrieval, especially age and sex; LLMs excelled in drug name recognition.
evidence.quote: Results demonstrate that rule-based methods provide higher accuracy in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction.

evidence.title: MEDSYN: Benchmarking Multi-EviDence SYNthesis in Complex Clinical Cases for Multimodal Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: MLLM versus expert clinician performance on differential diagnosis generation and final diagnosis selection
evidence.effect: Top models often match or outperform human experts on DDx generation, but all MLLMs show a much larger DDx-FDx performance gap than expert clinicians.
evidence.quote: While top models often match or even outperform human experts on DDx generation, all MLLMs exhibit a much larger DDx--FDx performance gap compared to expert clinicians, indicating a failure mode in synthesis of heterogeneous CE types.

evidence.title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Understand Pathologic Movements? A Pilot Study on Seizure Semiology
evidence.outcome: Zero-shot MLLM feature recognition versus fine-tuned CNN and ViT baselines on seizure videos
evidence.effect: MLLMs outperformed fine-tuned CNN and ViT baseline models on 13 of 18 features without task-specific training.
evidence.quote: MLLMs outperformed fine-tuned Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) baseline models on 13 of 18 features without task-specific training, demonstrating particular strength in recognizing salient postural and contextual features while struggling with subtle, high-frequency movements.

evidence.title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral
evidence.outcome: Comparison of zero-shot LLMs against task-adapted encoders on same data
evidence.effect: Zero-shot LLMs were substantially less effective than task-adapted encoders for closed-set classification, with language-dependent instability; IndicBERT-HPA Macro-F1 0.8792.
evidence.quote: The evaluated zero-shot LLMs remain substantially less effective than task-adapted encoders for closed-set classification, with language-dependent instability.

evidence.title: Physiology-Aware CNN and Zero-Shot Multimodal LLMs for ECG Image Classification: A Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of zero-shot multimodal LLMs against CNN baselines on the same ECG normal/abnormal task
evidence.effect: CNN models reached average internal ROC-AUC 0.92-0.94 and external 0.85-0.86, while zero-shot LLMs were near chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).
evidence.quote: In contrast, zero-shot LLM discrimination remained near-chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).

evidence.title: Locally Deployable Small Language Models for Emergency Department Decision Support: A Systematic Benchmark of Fine-Tuning Strategies
evidence.outcome: Comparison of fine-tuned open-source SLMs against commercial LLM baselines on ED triage, referral, and diagnosis tasks
evidence.effect: LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperformed Claude Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 baselines on triage level and specialist referral; diagnosis prediction remained challenging for open-source SLMs.
evidence.quote: Using 2,083 MIMIC-IV-ED cases and Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 as baselines, we found that LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperform commercial baselines on triage level prediction and specialist referral recommendation, while diagnosis prediction remains challenging for open-source SLMs.

evidence.title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss
evidence.outcome: LLM F1 for de-identification compared with purpose-built systems on same notes
evidence.effect: Best LLM F1=0.918±0.001 vs. Stanford TiDE 0.779; advantages concentrated in contextual categories.
evidence.quote: LLMs outperformed the purpose-built systems (best F1=0.918$\pm$0.001 vs.\ TiDE 0.779), with advantages concentrated in contextual categories.
evidence.sample_unit: annotated pediatric oncology notes (5,322 PHI spans)

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT for Disease Prediction: A Comparative Study on Heart Disease and Diabetes
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy versus best traditional ML/DL models on disease prediction
evidence.effect: ChatGPT did not outperform traditional machine learning and deep learning models; GPT-4o 5-shot reached 77.07% (Pima diabetes), 75.85% (Frankfurt diabetes), 83.65% (heart disease).
evidence.quote: Even though ChatGPT does not outperform traditional machine learning and deep learning models, these findings highlight its potential as a complementary tool in disease prediction.
evidence.sample_unit: records from public datasets (Pima Indian Diabetes, Frankfurt Hospital Diabetes, heart disease)

evidence.title: Benchmarking transformer-based models for medical record deidentification: A single centre, multi-specialty evaluation
evidence.outcome: PII redaction model selection
evidence.quote: The best performing redaction tool was the Microsoft Azure de-identification service: F1 0.939 (0.934-0.944), precision 0.928 (0.922-0.934), recall 0.950 (0.943-0.958).

evidence.title: Empirical Review of LLM-driven Classification of Multidimensional Sleep Health Mentions from Free-Text Clinical Notes
evidence.outcome: Classification accuracy, latency and span identification of fine-tuned discriminative vs generative LLMs
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned discriminative models consistently gave higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.
evidence.quote: Our experiments demonstrate that fine-tuned discriminative models consistently provide higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than either prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.

evidence.title: From Rule-Based to DeepSeek R1 – A Robust Comparative Evaluation of Fifty Years of Natural Language Processing (NLP) Models To Identify Inflammatory Bowel Disease Cohorts
evidence.outcome: F1 and compute cost of simple vs. complex NLP models for IBD cohort identification on the same data
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT F1 94.06%; BOW F1 93.38% at 1.63g CO2; LLMs F1 86.65% to 91.58% with higher compute cost (938.5 to 33884.4g CO2) and more bias.
evidence.quote: Older NLP approaches, such as BOW, can outperform modern LLMs in clinical cohort detection when properly trained.

evidence.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Binary Classification of Pediatric Chest X-Rays: A Comparative Evaluation Using a Public Pneumonia Dataset
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of five multimodal LLMs compared on the same pediatric chest X-ray dataset
evidence.effect: GPT-4.1 had 84% sensitivity and 76% specificity; GPT-4o 99%/18%; Gemini 2.5 Pro 97%/25%; Claude 4 Sonnet 100%/0%; Grok 2 Vision 82%/56%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4.1 demonstrated the most balanced performance with 84% sensitivity and 76% specificity.

evidence.title: A Comparative Performance Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in Gynecologic Oncology
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head model performance
evidence.effect: Thirteen RAG architectures were compared with a non-RAG baseline; RAG systems generally outperformed baseline, with domain-dependent gains.
evidence.quote: Across domains, RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline.

evidence.title: From Notebook to Real World: Design and Deployment of a Web-Based Machine Learning System for PCOS Risk Screening
evidence.outcome: candidate classifier performance
evidence.effect: Logistic Regression test accuracy was 86.76% and weighted F1-score 0.8684, but differences were within sampling variability.
evidence.quote: Evaluated on a 75/25 stratified split with 5-fold cross-validation, Logistic Regression achieves the highest test accuracy of 86.76% and weighted F1-score of 0.8684 achieves the highest test F1 among the five classifiers evaluated, though differences are within sampling variability at this test set size.

evidence.title: Clinical Note Comparison and Data Retrieval Via Embedding Vectors: Model Selection, Metrics, and Convergence
evidence.outcome: Performance differences between candidate embedding models on the same clinical tasks
evidence.effect: Qwen3-Embedding-8B outperformed multilingual-E5-large in retrieval; sufficiency 3.25 vs 3.17 for first query and 2.25 vs 1.15 out of 5 for second query.
evidence.quote: Our results show that the choice of embedding model is important: performance differences between models can be large enough to determine whether clinically relevant information reaches the end user, and model weaknesses can be both task-specific and context-dependent.
evidence.sample_unit: synthetic discharge summaries and patient record retrieval queries

evidence.title: Extraction of Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) Concepts from Clinical Notes Utilizing Large Language Models (LLM) with Model Context Protocol (MCP)
evidence.outcome: Tool-augmented LLM HPO extraction performance compared with a commercial EHR-based HPO extraction tool
evidence.effect: Tool-augmented LLMs achieved higher F1-scores than the commercial benchmark and substantially greater recall for inferred phenotypes.
evidence.quote: Compared with the commercial benchmark, tool-augmented LLMs achieved higher F1-scores and substantially greater recall for inferred phenotypes.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM extraction runs (>2,000 total, across 4 synthetic clinical genetics notes)

evidence.title: Agent Role Structure and Operating Characteristics in Large Language Model Clinical Classification: A Comparative Study of Specialist and Deliberative Multi-Agent Protocols
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two multi-agent protocols (GD vs FS) on same data
evidence.effect: Cleveland FS higher accuracy (0.72 vs 0.65) and macro-F1 (0.71 vs 0.65); Pima GD higher accuracy (0.68 vs 0.51) and macro-F1 (0.64 vs 0.49). Winner depends on dataset.
evidence.quote: Under the primary configuration (  llama3.1:8b ), Cleveland FS achieves higher accuracy (0.72 vs. 0.65) and macro-F1 (0.71 vs. 0.65), with a specificity-favoring operating point, whereas Pima GD achieves higher accuracy (0.68 vs. 0.51) and macro-F1 (0.64 vs. 0.49), while FS induces pronounced class asymmetry.
evidence.sample_unit: benchmark cases (UCI Cleveland Heart Disease and Pima Indians Diabetes)

evidence.title: DentaCoPilot, a Large Language Model-Augmented Next-Procedure Recommender for General Dentistry: Development and Comparative Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Top-1 accuracy of LLM variants versus classical baselines on same synthetic data
evidence.effect: Classical baselines reached 0.567 top-1; pure LLM variants reached 0.267 to 0.467; Sonnet to Opus backbone did not help.
evidence.quote: On an apples-to-apples synthetic evaluation, classical baselines reach 0.567 top-1 while pure LLM variants trail at 0.267 to 0.467, and moving the backbone from Sonnet to Opus does not help.

evidence.title: A Breakeven Recall Framework for LLM Candidate-Set Narrowing in P300 BCIs: Derivation and Cross-Dataset Validation
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM-assisted decoding versus simpler static-vocabulary and unconstrained decoding on same data
evidence.effect: Static vocabulary 48.1% vs 30.6% unconstrained on BigP3BCI (p = 0.001, dz = 1.24); LLM-assisted mode did not beat unconstrained (SV > UC ≥ LLM in all three datasets).
evidence.quote: Current small LLMs (Qwen2.5 1.5B, GPT-2) operate below both necessary conditions in all three datasets, explaining the consistent ordering SV > UC ≥ LLM.
evidence.sample_unit: spelling rounds (across three public P300 datasets)

evidence.title: LLM-based reconstruction of longitudinal clinical trajectories in chronic liver disease
evidence.outcome: accuracy across extraction tasks
evidence.effect: Llama-3.3-70B exceeded 90% accuracy on 59/70 tasks and outperformed three other LLMs.
evidence.quote: Llama-3.3-70B performed best, exceeding 90% accuracy on 59/70 tasks, outperforming Llama-3.1-8B (a smaller variant), OpenBioLLM-70B (a medically fine-tuned model), and DeepSeek-R1-8B.

evidence.title: Beyond AUC: The Clinical Impact of Threshold Optimization in COVID-19 Mortality Prediction
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of logistic regression versus decision tree and neural network
evidence.effect: Logistic regression AUC 0.697 vs decision tree 0.654 and neural network 0.654; differences not statistically significant by DeLong's test.
evidence.quote: Logistic regression achieved the highest discrimination (AUC 0.697), followed by decision tree (AUC 0.654) and neural network (AUC 0.654) models, although differences were not statistically significant according to DeLong’s test.

evidence.title: Detection without calibration: benchmarking domestic and international large language models for quality control of Mandarin  18  F-FDG PET/CT reports
evidence.outcome: LLM error detection versus human physicians and between competing domestic and international models on same reports
evidence.effect: Missed-diagnosis detection best 0.467, the one category where human physicians outperformed every model; domestic vs international detection did not differ (Δmacro-F1 = −0.011, P = 0.84).
evidence.quote: Missed-diagnosis detection was the universal weakness (best 0.467) and the one category where the human physicians outperformed every model.

evidence.title: Solving Emergency Department Triage with Small Language Models: Why Large Commercial Models Fail and How Specialized Training Achieves Clinical Accuracy
evidence.outcome: Exact ESI triage accuracy of competing large commercial models versus specialized small-model pipeline on same cases
evidence.effect: Off-the-shelf large models reached 45–55% exact ESI accuracy; BiomedBERT pipeline reached 88.9% exact and 97.2% adjacent accuracy on a 50-case set.
evidence.quote: Off-the-shelf large models achieve only 45–55% exact ESI accuracy while being impractical for clinical deployment due to privacy constraints, cost, and latency.

evidence.title: One Size Fits All? Comparing Foundation and Task-specific Models for Retinal Fluid Segmentation
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy of task-specific model versus foundation model on same benchmark data
evidence.effect: Task-specific RetiFluidNet achieved higher pixel-level segmentation performance than the VisionFM foundation model on 4,248 OCT images using three-fold cross-validation.
evidence.quote: The task-specific model achieved higher segmentation performance and more consistent fluid quantification across devices.

evidence.title: Decision Curve Analysis for Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Next-Day Transfer Out of ICU
evidence.outcome: decision utility versus baseline strategies
evidence.effect: Model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule across thresholds.
evidence.quote: Across thresholds, model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule.

evidence.title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
evidence.outcome: external performance by complexity
evidence.effect: Across N =550 academic and N =511 community samples, increasing model complexity did not improve external performance.
evidence.quote: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance, whereas training on pooled data substantially improved both discrimination and calibration.

evidence.title: A clinic-updated digital twin for Parkinson’s disease progression: Governed Bayesian forecasting with uncertainty-gated reporting
evidence.outcome: coverage versus baseline
evidence.effect: 95% coverage was 94% to 96% across endpoints versus 64–69% for linear mixed-effects baselines.
evidence.quote: Predictive interval coverage at the 95% level ranged from 94% to 96% across all three endpoints, compared with 64–69% for linear mixed-effects baselines.

evidence.title: The Independence of Discrimination and Calibration in Clinical Risk Prediction: Lessons from a Multi-Timeframe Diabetes Prediction Framework
evidence.outcome: Comparison of new framework against QDiabetes-2018 on same synthetic cohort
evidence.effect: QDiabetes-2018 had comparable AUC (0.831 vs 0.844) with better calibration (O:E 0.89 vs 0.66).
evidence.quote: QDiabetes-2018 achieved comparable discrimination (AUC = 0.831) with better calibration (O:E = 0.89).
evidence.country: Not reported (synthetic data based on UK/Finnish/US parameters)

evidence.title: When AI Meets the FDA: An Evaluation of Large Language Models Performance in Regulatory and Clinical Trial Data Extraction, Synthesis, and Analysis
evidence.outcome: Comparative accuracy across candidate LLMs on the same regulatory extraction task
evidence.effect: Accuracy differed significantly across models (p<0.001): Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.7%, ChatGPT-4o 51.9%, DeepSeek R1 37.0%.
evidence.quote: Among 324 responses, accuracy differed significantly across models (χ², p <0.001) with Gemini 2.5 Pro achieving the highest accuracy (66.7%), followed by ChatGPT-4o (51.9%) and DeepSeek R1 (37.0%).

evidence.title: Data leakage inflates reported accuracy of deep learning for kidney stone detection on CT: a leakage-free, calibrated and uncertainty-aware reassessment across three centers
evidence.outcome: performance versus comparator architectures
evidence.effect: Plain ResNet-18 performed comparably to hybrid model; convolution-free Transformer performed near chance.
evidence.quote: A plain ResNet-18 performed comparably to the hybrid model, while a convolution-free Transformer performed near chance, and performance held up reasonably well across held-out hospitals.

evidence.title: Evaluating Clinical Concept Extraction and Evidence-Bounded Terminology Linking: Multisite Model Comparison and Pilot Ablation Study
evidence.outcome: side-by-side extraction model ranking
evidence.effect: MedGemma embedding F1 0.55; Gemma 0.53; sci_md/SciBERT 0.43; Llama 3.3 0.32.
evidence.quote: Automated exact-match F1 scores ranged from 0.07 to 0.17; embedding-match F1 was highest for MedGemma (0.55), followed by Gemma (0.53),  sci_md and SciBERT (each 0.43), and Llama 3.3 (0.32).
evidence.sample_unit: deidentified clinical notes (Study 1); 56 clinical spans (Study 2); 84 terms (Study 3)

evidence.title: Occam’s Razor in AI-assisted complex diagnosis: a comparative effectiveness study of single large language models versus multi-agent systems in resource-constrained primary care settings
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic recall of single LLMs and multi-agent systems compared with each other and physicians on same cases
evidence.effect: Single GPT-oss-20b scored 4.68 vs Adaptive multi-agent 4.13 (p<0.001); Adaptive system did not outperform median physician score of 4.22 (p=0.432).
evidence.quote: The Adaptive System, despite utilising dynamic routing, failed to outperform the median score of human physicians (4.22 [SD 3.62]; p = 0.432).

evidence.title: Performance drift is a major barrier to the safe use of machine learning in cardiac surgery
evidence.outcome: comparative model performance
evidence.effect: Xgboost CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729 and Random Forest CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728 were best overall.
evidence.quote: Xgboost (CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729) and Random Forest (CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728) were the best overall performing models both temporally and non-temporally.

evidence.title: Spot the Difference: Can ChatGPT4-Vision Transform Radiology Artificial Intelligence?
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of GPT4V versus trained U-Net and ViT on MS progression detection
evidence.effect: Both U-Net and ViT had 94% accuracy while GPT4V had 85%; GPT4V gave overly cautious non-answers in 6 cases.
evidence.quote: Both U-Net and ViT had 94% accuracy while GPT4V had 85%.

evidence.title: Enhancing Precision in Rectal Cancer Radiotherapy: Localized Fine-Tuning of Deep-learning based Auto-segmentation (DLAS) Model for Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-risk
evidence.outcome: LFT versus pretrained model accuracy
evidence.effect: LFT outperformed VPM for CTV target volume, DSC, 95HD and specificity; bladder and femoral heads were adequate for both.
evidence.quote: Both models exhibited adequate accuracy for bladder and femoral heads, and LFT demonstrated significant enhancement in segmenting the more complex small intestine.

evidence.title: Enhancing Early Detection of Cognitive Decline in the Elderly: A Comparative Study Utilizing Large Language Models in Clinical Notes
evidence.outcome: Compared LLMs (GPT-4, Llama 2) against traditional models on same test data for cognitive decline detection
evidence.effect: GPT-4 outperformed Llama 2 but did not outperform traditional models (hierarchical attention network, XGBoost); ensemble achieved precision 90.3%, recall 94.2%, F1 92.2%.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency compared to Llama 2, but did not outperform traditional models.

evidence.title: 40 years of actigraphy in sleep medicine and current state of the art algorithms
evidence.outcome: Sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome accuracy of complex vs simple algorithms against PSG on the same dataset
evidence.effect: Simple regression-based and heuristic algorithms showed slightly superior performance to recent complex ML/DL algorithms in sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome estimation.
evidence.quote: Despite the inclusion of recently published complex algorithms, simple regression-based and heuristic algorithms demonstrated slightly superior performance in sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome estimation.

evidence.title: Machine learning-based automatic proton therapy planning: Impact of post-processing and dose-mimicking in plan robustness
evidence.outcome: KBP-generated IMPT plan quality compared with manually generated dosimetrist plans on same patients
evidence.effect: Nominal doses from the four KBP pipelines achieved comparable target coverage and improved dose to organs at risk compared to manual plans; NPP-RSM gave best robustness/OAR sparing trade-off.
evidence.quote: Nominal doses from the four KBP pipelines showed promising results achieving comparable target coverage and improved dose to organs at risk (OARs) compared to the manual plans.

evidence.title: Increased confidence of radiomics facilitating pretherapeutic differentiation of BRAF-altered pediatric low-grade glioma
evidence.outcome: Simpler model discrimination
evidence.effect: Linear model AUC 0.916 was comparable despite lower complexity; combined RF AUC 0.925 reported.
evidence.quote: The linear model had a comparable AUC (0.916), despite its lower complexity.

evidence.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head LLM readability and conversion time
evidence.effect: ChatGPT had easier FRE/FKGL/GFI/SMOGI than Bard and was faster: 5.38 s ± 0.67 s vs 8.57 s ± 1.29 s.
evidence.quote: Compared to Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly easier readability after conversion as per FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 66.5 ± 5.2 [Bard], p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 6.9 ± 0.8 [Bard], p = 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 9.3 ± 1.0 [Bard], p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 10.0 ± 0.8 [Bard], p < 0.001) scores (Fig. 1 ).

evidence.title: Evaluating the ChatGPT family of models for biomedical reasoning and classification
evidence.outcome: LLM prompting performance versus simple BoW and fine-tuned BioBERT baselines on same classification and reasoning data
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned BioBERT best (classification F1 0.800-0.902; reasoning 0.851). Best LLM few-shot CoT F1 0.671-0.770 and 0.682, comparable to BoW (0.602-0.753; 0.675). LLM took 78 h vs 0.078 h BioBERT and 0.008 h BoW.
evidence.quote: The simple BoW model performed similarly to the most complex LLM prompting.

evidence.title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Conformal Predictor to Predict Sepsis Mortality Risk: Retrospective Cohort Study
evidence.outcome: AUC versus comparator models
evidence.effect: External AUC was 0.800 (95% CI 0.789-0.811) for CPMORS versus 0.693 to 0.786 for comparators.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, CPMORS still showed the best performance with AUC 0.800 (95% CI 0.789-0.811) versus other models ranging from 0.693 (95% CI 0.680-0.706) to 0.786 (95% CI 0.775-0.798).

evidence.title: Assessment of the CLOT (children's likelihood of thrombosis) real-time risk prediction model of hospital-associated venous thromboembolism in children with congenital heart disease
evidence.outcome: AUROC comparing feature-expanded model
evidence.effect: Updated cardiac-specific model AUROC = 0.859 [0.813–0.898], a marginal non-significant improvement versus refit, P = .269.
evidence.quote: This updated cardiac specific model has an AUROC of 0.859 [0.813–0.898] ( Figure 2 ) demonstrating a marginal, but non-significant, improvement from the refit model ( P = .269).

evidence.title: Preoperative risk prediction models for acute kidney injury after noncardiac surgery: an independent external validation cohort study
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of nine candidate prediction models on the same validation data
evidence.effect: Performance varied widely across models; only three showed fair discrimination and positive net benefit after recalibration.
evidence.quote: We identified three models with fair discrimination and potential clinical utility after recalibration for assessing the risk of acute kidney injury after noncardiac surgery.

evidence.title: Calibrating Deep Learning Classifiers for Patient-Independent Electroencephalogram Seizure Forecasting
evidence.outcome: CNN versus XGBoost benchmark and calibration gains
evidence.effect: CNN outperformed traditional ML pipelines under RCV; calibration also helped XGBoost but with lower gains (ACC +6%/+10% CHB-MIT, +8%/+13% Conegliano) than CNN.
evidence.quote: It turns out that our calibration method is also effective with XGBoost, although the performance gains are slightly lower compared to the CNN.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (19 CHB-MIT, 22 Conegliano; 16 eligible for leave-out validation and calibration)

evidence.title: Comparing generative and retrieval-based chatbots in answering patient questions regarding age-related macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy
evidence.outcome: Response accuracy of generative chatbots versus retrieval-based chatbot on same patient questions, graded by specialists
evidence.effect: Median scores 6 (1) for ChatGPT-4 and ChatGPT-3.5 vs 4.5 (2) Google Bard and 2 (1) OcularBERT; 'Good' ratings 83.3%, 86.7%, 50%, 10%.
evidence.quote: Based on the consensus approach, 83.3% of ChatGPT-4's responses and 86.7% of ChatGPT-3.5's were rated as 'Good', surpassing Google Bard (50%) and OcularBERT (10%) (all p ≤1.4×10<sup>-2</sup>).

evidence.title: Evaluating the accuracy of a state-of-the-art large language model for prediction of admissions from the emergency room
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 admission prediction versus traditional ML models on the same data
evidence.effect: Ensemble ML AUC 0.88, AUPRC 0.72, accuracy 82.9%; naive GPT-4 AUC 0.79, AUPRC 0.48, accuracy 77.5%; GPT-4 with RAG and ML probabilities AUC 0.87, AUPRC 0.71, accuracy 83.1%.
evidence.quote: The Ensemble ML model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.88, an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.72 and an accuracy of 82.9%.

evidence.title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: Comparison of ML models against EuroSCORE II on same data
evidence.effect: XGBoost CEM 0.728 and RF 0.727 vs EuroSCORE II 0.541; EuroSCORE II performed worst across all comparisons (CEM difference to XGBoost 0.1876).
evidence.quote: Furthermore, EuroSCORE II substantially underperformed against all ML models across all comparisons; this presents an urgent need to understand the drift effects of this score and is not limited to calibration drift.

evidence.title: A comparative study of large language model-based zero-shot inference and task-specific supervised classification of breast cancer pathology reports
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Macro F1 of zero-shot LLMs versus supervised models on the same pathology report classification tasks
evidence.effect: GPT-4 performed either significantly better than or as well as the best supervised model, LSTM-Att (average macro F1 0.86 vs 0.75); other LLMs performed poorly.
evidence.quote: Across all 12 tasks, the GPT-4 model performed either significantly better than or as well as the best supervised model, LSTM-Att (average macro F1-score of 0.86 vs 0.75), with advantage on tasks with high label imbalance.

evidence.title: A multi-center study on the adaptability of a shared foundation model for electronic health records
evidence.outcome: performance versus locally trained baselines
evidence.effect: Across 8 tasks, adapted FM SM matched GBM and provided a 13% improvement with few labels.
evidence.quote: Evaluations on 8 clinical prediction tasks showed that adapting the off-the-shelf FM SM matched the performance of gradient boosting machines (GBM) locally trained on all data while providing a 13% improvement in settings with few task-specific training labels.

evidence.title: Adaptation of risk prediction equations for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes in real-world settings: a cross-institutional study using common data model approach
evidence.outcome: Performance of competing risk equations
evidence.effect: UKPDS-OM2 all and RECODe stroke were AUROC < 0.7; all CHIME equations were AUROC ≥ 0.7.
evidence.quote: Overall, all the CVD risk equations from UKPDS-OM2 and the stroke risk equation from RECODe demonstrated unsatisfactory discrimination (AUROC < 0.7) for Taiwanese type 2 diabetes populations, and all the CVD risk equations from the CHIME model yielded acceptable discrimination (AUROC ≥ 0.7).

evidence.title: The potential and pitfalls of using a large language model such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, or LLaMA as a clinical assistant
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: LLM F1 versus disease-specific traditional machine learning models for patient identification
evidence.effect: GPT-4 had near similar or better performance compared to disease-specific ML models (F1 ≥ 85%) on COPD, CKD, PBC; 4.23% higher F1 on PBC. ChatGPT and LLaMA3 lower than GPT-4.
evidence.quote: In patient identification, GPT-4 had near similar or better performance compared to the corresponding disease-specific Machine Learning models (F1-score ≥ 85%) on COPD, CKD, and PBC.

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Ophthalmology
evidence.outcome: Human ranking score of candidate LLMs compared on the same 300 questions
evidence.effect: Ten LLMs benchmarked; ChatZOC scored 0.60 vs baseline 0.48 (difference 0.12; P=.02) and GPT-4 0.61 (P=.89).
evidence.quote: Evaluation using 300 questions sampled from the COD showed that the human ranking score of our ophthalmic LLM had achieved a score of 0.60, different from the baseline model of 0.48 (difference = 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02) and not different from GPT-4 with a score of 0.61 (difference = 0.01; 95% CI, −0.11 to 0.13; P = .89), as shown in Table 2 .

evidence.title: Computer-aided detection of tuberculosis from chest radiographs in a tuberculosis prevalence survey in South Africa: external validation and modelled impacts of commercially available artificial intelligence software
evidence.outcome: Accuracy differences among CAD products
evidence.effect: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9; qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye had AUCs 0·8-0·9.
evidence.quote: Diverse accuracy was noted: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9, followed by qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye (AUCs 0·8-0·9).

evidence.title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
evidence.outcome: Comparison of complex models (LSTM, GBM) with simpler logistic regression on same data
evidence.effect: Complex models did not outperform LR locally or transported; on KHIN LSTM AUROC 0.759 vs LR 0.787; LSTM HIDD to KHIN 0.595.
evidence.quote: More complex models, particularly deep long short-term memory neural network models, did not outperform simpler regularized logistic regression models in terms of both local and transported performance.

evidence.title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
evidence.outcome: accuracy differences between candidate LLMs
evidence.effect: On the same 19 questions, RAG had highest accuracy 2.46/relevance 2.61, GPT-4 highest readability 2.88; hallucinations ranged from RAG 3/19 to GPT-3.5 13/19.
evidence.quote: Results here demonstrated that the RAG model performed better on biomedical-specific tasks than the other LLMs evaluated, specifically with respect to accuracy and relevance of results.

evidence.title: Large-scale identification of social and behavioral determinants of health from clinical notes: comparison of Latent Semantic Indexing and Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) models
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Macro-F1 for SBDH detection of LSI versus GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and ICD-9 on gold standard sets
evidence.effect: Macro-F1 for LSI 0.74 was better than ICD-9 (0.71) and GPT-3.5 (0.54) but lower than GPT-4 (0.80); on common subsets, ICD-9 combined with LSI, GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 did not differ significantly.
evidence.quote: Using manually curated gold standard (GS) sets for nine SBDH categories, the macro-F1 score of LSI (0.74) was better than ICD-9 (0.71) and GPT-3.5 (0.54), but lower than GPT-4 (0.80).

evidence.title: Large language models in pathology: A comparative study of ChatGPT and Bard with pathology trainees on multiple-choice questions
evidence.outcome: LLM accuracy compared with pathology trainees on the same questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT scored 82.2% versus Bard 49.5%, junior trainees 45.1%, senior trainees 56.0%; ChatGPT stronger on difficult questions (63.4%-68.3%).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT significantly outperformed Bard and trainees, achieving an average total score of 82.2% compared to Bard's 49.5%, junior trainees' 45.1%, and senior trainees' 56.0%.
evidence.sample_unit: multiple-choice pathology questions (plus 16 pathology trainees as comparators)

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Improved Understanding of Communications With Patients With Cancer in a Call Center Setting: Proof-of-Concept Study
evidence.outcome: Intent classification accuracy of GPT-4 versus LSTM and BERT on same test sentences
evidence.effect: GPT-4 few-shot accuracy 85.2% versus LSTM 73.7% and BERT 71.3%; GPT-4 over 15% better on ambiguous categories.
evidence.quote: GPT-4, which uses only a few examples (a few shots), attained a remarkable accuracy of 85.2%, considerably outperforming the LSTM and BERT models, which achieved accuracies of 73.7% and 71.3%, respectively.

evidence.title: External validation of predictive models for antibiotic susceptibility of urine culture
evidence.outcome: Adequacy of empiric oral antibiotic coverage, algorithm-suggested vs clinician-prescribed
evidence.effect: The drug agent suggested by the algorithms more frequently resulted in adequate empiric coverage than clinician prescriptions for oral antibiotics.
evidence.quote: When algorithms' performances were tested against clinicians in a contemporary cohort for the empiric prescription of oral antibiotics, the drug agent suggested by the algorithms more frequently resulted in adequate empiric coverage.

evidence.title: Uncertainty estimation in diagnosis generation from large language models: next-word probability is not pre-test probability
evidence.outcome: LLM-based diagnostic probability estimation compared with a traditional ML classifier on the same EHR data
evidence.effect: The XGB classifier outperformed the LLM-based methods across all three tasks (Sepsis, Arrhythmia, CHF).
evidence.quote: The XGB classifier outperformed the LLM-based methods across all tasks.

evidence.title: Guidance on selecting and evaluating AI auto-segmentation systems in clinical radiotherapy: insights from a six-vendor analysis
evidence.venue: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
evidence.outcome: Performance of six competing auto-segmentation vendors compared on the same patient data
evidence.effect: Vendors varied widely from excellent to poor on raw performance metrics (Dice, Hausdorff Distance, Average Surface Distance, Surface Dice, Added Path Length); no vendor performed exceedingly well overall.
evidence.quote: In terms of raw performance, vendors varied widely from excellent to poor.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (20 head and neck, 20 thoracic, 19 male pelvis)

evidence.title: Research on a traditional Chinese medicine case-based question-answering system integrating large language models and knowledge graphs
evidence.outcome: Candidate LLM response-generation comparison
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5-Turbo scored highest on RAGAS: faithfulness 0.9375, answer relevance 0.9686, context recall 0.9500; it was selected for response generation.
evidence.quote: The evaluation results indicate that the GPT-3.5-Turbo model achieved the highest scores in three dimensions: fidelity, answer relevance, and context recall, with scores of 0.9375, 0.9686, and 0.9500, respectively.

evidence.title: The Potential Clinical Utility of the Customized Large Language Model in Gastroenterology: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: LLM scores compared with gastroenterology fellow and expert on the same 15 questions
evidence.effect: Customized LLM 8/15, fellow 10/15, conventional GPT-4o 14/15, expert 15/15.
evidence.quote: While the customized LLM correctly answered 8 out of 15 questions, the fellow answered 10 correctly.

evidence.title: An interpretable machine learning tool for in-home monitoring of agitation episodes in people living with dementia: a proof-of-concept study
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity versus alternative models
evidence.effect: LightGBM sensitivity was significantly higher than logistic regression (p-value < ×10−3) and other tree-based models (p-value < 5 × 10−3).
evidence.quote: The LightGBM yielded significantly higher sensitivity than logistic regression ( p − value < ×10 −3 ) and the other examined tree-based models ( p − value < 5 × 10 −3 ) (see Table S5 ).
evidence.sample_unit: people living with dementia (512 labelled weeks; 32,896 person-days)

evidence.title: Characterization of artificial intelligence performance for lesion detection using synthetic lesions in PET imaging
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two lesion detection AIs on same synthetic lesion library by sensitivity and precision
evidence.effect: One AI consistently outperformed the other in number of reported lesions, sensitivity, and precision. 10 mm lesions detected at 90% sensitivity at 8:1 vs 16:1 lesion-to-background ratio for the two algorithms.
evidence.quote: One AI consistently outperformed the other in terms of number of reported lesions, sensitivity, and precision.

evidence.title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
evidence.outcome: ML models compared against baseline biomarkers and prior ML models on same internal test data
evidence.effect: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed MDW, CRP, Sepsis Index, COMPOSER, and Mindray SVM baselines across all decision thresholds.
evidence.quote: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed all the baseline comparison methods (ie, MDW [ 37 ], CRP [ 44 ], Sepsis Index [ 45 ], COMPOSER [ 25 ], as well as the SVM model developed in the study by Aguirre and Urrechaga [ 31 ]; Figures 1 and 2 ; Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ) and did so across all possible decision thresholds.

evidence.title: Large language models are less effective at clinical prediction tasks than locally trained machine learning models
evidence.outcome: AUROC and Brier score of LLMs versus locally trained gradient-boosting ML on same EHR prediction tasks
evidence.effect: ML AUROC 0.847/0.894 (VUMC/MIMIC) vs GPT-3.5 0.537/0.517 and GPT-4 0.629/0.602; Brier ML 0.134 vs GPT-3.5 0.384 vs GPT-4 0.251 (VUMC).
evidence.quote: Traditional ML [AUROC: 0.847, 0.894 (VUMC, MIMIC)] substantially outperformed GPT-3.5 (AUROC: 0.537, 0.517) and GPT-4 (AUROC: 0.629, 0.602) (with and without in-context learning) in predictive performance and output probability calibration [Brier Score (ML vs GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4): 0.134 vs 0.384 vs 0.251, 0.042 vs 0.06 vs 0.219)].
evidence.sample_unit: EHR-based clinical prediction tasks (VUMC and MIMIC IV)

evidence.title: Enhanced Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer Management: A Comparative Analysis and Optimization Study of Multiple Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of six LLMs on 100 bladder cancer guideline questions, compared across models
evidence.effect: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 89.33% ± 1.53%, ChatGPT-4 85.67%, Grok-beta 84.33%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 82.00%, Mistral-Large-2 81.00%, GPT-3.5-Turbo 74.33% ± 3.06%; accuracy varied across candidate models.
evidence.quote: In the initial evaluation, Claude-3.5-Sonnet demonstrated the highest accuracy (89.33% ± 1.53%), followed by ChatGPT-4 (85.67% ± 1.15%).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-driven forecasting and shift optimization for pediatric emergency department crowding
evidence.outcome: Comparison of advanced deep learning forecasting models against traditional models on the same data
evidence.effect: TCN R2 73%, TiDE-RIN 75%, N-BEATS 72%, N-HiTS 57% outperformed ARIMA 16%, LSTM 32%, RNN 40%.
evidence.quote: It was observed that advanced deep learning architectures such as TCN (R 2 : 73%), TiDE-RIN (R 2 : 75%), N-BEATS (R 2 : 72%), and N-HiTS (R 2 : 57%) outperformed traditional time-series models like ARIMA (R 2 : 16%), LSTM (R 2 : 32%), and RNN (R 2 : 40%).

evidence.title: Improving the Precision of Deep-Learning-Based Head and Neck Target Auto-Segmentation by Leveraging Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model
evidence.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 versus Llama-3-8B for tumor information extraction from reports
evidence.effect: GPT-4 extracted 40 primary tumors and 106 LNs vs RadOnc 40/111; Llama-3-8B gave 48 primary tumors and 127 LNs with extra false positives; Llama-3 inferior.
