evidence.quote: Our study found that Llama-3 is inferior to the GPT-4 model in terms of tumor information extraction.
evidence.sample_unit: head and neck cancer cases (institutional external test set)

evidence.title: From text to data: Open-source large language models in extracting cancer related medical attributes from German pathology reports
evidence.outcome: Candidate model extraction performance
evidence.effect: Mistral Small 24B with RAG achieved nearly equivalent performance to Llama 70B on most entity types with fewer resources.
evidence.quote: However, when combined with the RAG pipeline, Mistral Small 24B achieved nearly equivalent performance, matching Llama 70B on most entity types while requiring significantly fewer computational resources.

evidence.title: Language Models for Multilabel Document Classification of Surgical Concepts in Exploratory Laparotomy Operative Notes: Algorithm Development Study
evidence.outcome: Multilabel classification F1 of Llama 3.3 versus BoW, tf-idf, Clinical-Longformer on same notes
evidence.effect: Llama 3.3 micro F1 0.88 (HL 0.11) vs BoW 0.68, Clinical-Longformer 0.73, tf-idf 0.57 on the same 388 notes.
evidence.quote: Off-the-shelf autoregressive LLMs outperformed fined-tuned, encoder-only transformers and traditional natural language processing techniques in classifying operative notes.

evidence.title: Large-scale deep learning for metastasis detection in pathology reports
evidence.outcome: Recall of task-specific deep learning model versus general-purpose LLM on the same data
evidence.effect: Task-specific model recall 0.894 versus 0.824 for the general LLM.
evidence.quote: Our deep learning architecture trained on task-specific data outperforms a general-purpose LLM, with a recall of 0.894 compared to 0.824.

evidence.title: Specialized AI and neurosurgeons in niche expertise: a proof-of-concept in neuromodulation with vagus nerve stimulation
evidence.outcome: Specialized RAG LLM score versus neurosurgeons on VNS knowledge questionnaire
evidence.effect: AI scored 0.75, exceeding the highest individual clinician score (0.68; median 0.50), p < 0.001. AI better on anatomical/technical items; clinicians better on practical judgment.
evidence.quote: The AI achieved a score of 0.75, exceeding the highest individual clinician score (0.68; median: 0.50), with statistical significance (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: A Multimodal Large Language Model as an End-to-End Classifier of Thyroid Nodule Malignancy Risk: Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three candidate multimodal models (open-source, fine-tuned, commercial) against expert ratings on same data
evidence.effect: o3 had highest validity (98.6% vs 91.5% LLaVA vs 75% LLaVA-Med) and best accuracy for most components; overall accuracy up to 57.3%.
evidence.quote: The OpenAI o3 model produced the highest proportion of valid responses (2273/2304, 98.6%), followed by the LLaVA model (2108/2304, 91.5%), then the LLaVA-Med model (1729/2304, 75%, P <.001 for overall comparison).

evidence.title: DeepSeek-R1 vs OpenAI o1 for Ophthalmic Diagnoses and Management Plans
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic and next-step accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 compared head-to-head with OpenAI o1 on same cases
evidence.effect: DeepSeek-R1 diagnostic accuracy 70.4% vs 63.0% for o1 (7.3% difference, P=.02); next-step 82.7% vs 75.8% (6.9% difference, P=.01); intermodel agreement moderate (κ=0.422).
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-R1 achieved a higher diagnostic accuracy of 70.4% (297 of 422 cases) compared with 63.0% (266 of 422 cases) for OpenAI o1, a 7.3% difference (95% CI, 1.0%-13.7%; P = .02).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records
evidence.outcome: Comparison of candidate GPT model configurations against expert physician labels on same data
evidence.effect: GPT 4 Turbo precision 90.6%, sensitivity 100%, kappa 0.95; GPT 3.5 precision 44.9%, kappa 0.59; GPT 3.5+4 precision 81.0%, kappa 0.88.
evidence.quote: The best results came using configuration 3, the GPT 4 Turbo.

evidence.title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
evidence.outcome: AUC of CNN versus simple MAP threshold for predicting intraoperative hypotension across datasets
evidence.effect: CNN beat MAP threshold in the ambiguous Karolinska data (64.41 vs 61.92) but only marginally in VDB datasets (80.29 vs 78.46; 80.64 vs 79.80); threshold metrics were comparable at 80% specificity.
evidence.quote: In the Karolinska dataset, characterized by narrow class separation ( = 2.44 mmHg), the CNN model performed better than MAP threshold method (MAPthr), achieving a higher (64.41 vs. 61.92 ).

evidence.title: Comparative Diagnostic Performance of a Multimodal Large Language Model Versus a Dedicated Electrocardiogram AI in Detecting Myocardial Infarction From Electrocardiogram Images: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: MI detection accuracy/AUC of general LLMs versus dedicated ECG AI on same ECG images
evidence.effect: ECG Buddy accuracy 96.98%, AUC 98.8% vs ChatGPT accuracy 65.95%, AUC 57.34%; Gemini accuracy 29.63%, AUC 51.63%; DeLong test P<.001 vs ChatGPT.
evidence.quote: DeLong test confirmed that ECG Buddy significantly outperformed ChatGPT (all P<.001).
evidence.country: Pakistan (public dataset); study conducted elsewhere not stated

evidence.title: Robust comparative evaluation of 15 natural language processing algorithms to positively identify patients with inflammatory bowel disease from secondary care records
evidence.outcome: Comparison of 15 NLP algorithms, from simple to LLM, on the same labelled data
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT best (micro F1 93.54%), sBERT-Base 93.05%; LLMs 86.47-92.20% but slow (18-300 hours) and expensive; specificity 67.80-64.41% for top two.
evidence.quote: The fine-tuned DistilBERT_IBD model achieved the best performance overall (micro F1: 93.54%), followed by sBERT-Base (micro F1: 93.05%); however, specificity was an issue for both: (67.80-64.41%) respectively.

evidence.title: Exploring AI's Potential in Papilledema Diagnosis to Support Dermatological Treatment Decisions in Rural Healthcare
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o versus fine-tuned ResNet and human ophthalmologists on same test images
evidence.effect: GPT-4o accuracy 85.9% (Kappa 0.72), specificity 78.9%, PPV 73.7%; ResNet 99.5% (Kappa 0.99); ophthalmologists 96.0% (Kappa ≈ 0.92). GPT-4o underperformed both.
evidence.quote: GPT-4o achieved moderate diagnostic accuracy and substantial agreement with the ground truth, but it underperformed compared to both a domain-specific ResNet model and human ophthalmologists.
evidence.sample_unit: fundus images (test set from 1094 total; test set size not reported)

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Automating Clinical Trial Criteria Conversion to Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model Queries: Validation and Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Concept mapping accuracy of GPT-4 versus USAGI baseline on 357 clinical terms
evidence.effect: GPT-4 achieved 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001); llama3:8b had higher effective SQL rate (75.8%) than GPT-4 (45.3%).
evidence.quote: GPT-4 achieved a 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001), with domain-specific performance ranging from 72.7% (drug) to 38.3% (measurement).
evidence.sample_unit: SQL generation attempts (19 trials x 8 LLMs x 5 prompting strategies)

evidence.title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
evidence.venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
evidence.outcome: AI versus human plan quality
evidence.effect: Final iteration mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D98% and −0.01 for rectum V40Gy.
evidence.quote: PTV coverage and rectum sparing was almost identical between the two groups, with a mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D 98 % coverage and −0.01 for rectum V 40 G y .

evidence.title: Unlocking Potential of Generative Large Language Models for Adverse Drug Reaction Relation Prediction in Discharge Summaries: Analysis and Strategy
evidence.outcome: Generative LLMs vs in-house fine-tuned model on ADR relation prediction F1 and recall
evidence.effect: On MIMIC-Unrestricted, Gemini 1.5 Pro F1 0.724 to 0.863 and recall 0.675 to 0.943; Llama 3.1 405B F1 0.724 to 0.814 and recall 0.675 to 0.948 versus BioM-ELECTRA-Large.
evidence.quote: Notably, on the MIMIC-Unrestricted dataset, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Llama 3.1 405B outperform our in-house fine-tuned BioM-ELECTRA-Large, with Gemini 1.5 Pro showing a 19.2% (0.724-0.863) improvement in F1 score and a 39.7% (0.675-0.943) increase in recall, while Llama 3.1 405B exhibits a 12.4% (0.724-0.814) improvement in F1 and a 40.4% (0.675-0.948) boost in recall.

evidence.title: AgentMD: Empowering language agents for risk prediction with large-scale clinical tool learning
evidence.outcome: Risk prediction accuracy of AgentMD compared with GPT-4 baseline
evidence.effect: AgentMD outperformed GPT-4 for risk prediction, 87.7% vs. 40.9% accuracy.
evidence.quote: Our evaluations show that AgentMD significantly outperforms GPT-4 for risk prediction (87.7% vs. 40.9% in accuracy).

evidence.title: Can a Natural Image-Based Foundation Model Outperform a Retina-Specific Model in Detecting Ocular and Systemic Diseases?
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head AUC comparison of candidate foundation models on same ocular and systemic disease tasks
evidence.effect: DINOv2-Large DR AUCs 0.850-0.952 vs RETFound 0.823-0.944 (all P≤0.007); RETFound better for systemic incidence prediction (AUC 0.796 HF, 0.732 MI, 0.754 stroke vs DINOv2 0.663-0.771, P<0.001).
evidence.quote: Conversely, for systemic disease incidence prediction, RETFound achieved superior AUCs of 0.796 (heart failure), 0.732 (myocardial infarction), and 0.754 (ischemic stroke), outperforming DINOv2's best models' AUC (0.663-0.771, all P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Detecting Laterality Errors in Combined Radiographic Studies by Enhancing the Traditional Approach With GPT-4o: Algorithm Development and Multisite Internal Validation
evidence.outcome: Comparison of the candidate ensemble against GPT-4o, ClinicalBERT and RoBERTa on the same test data
evidence.effect: On Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o had F1 0.780, versus 0.352 for GPT-4o, 0.088 for ClinicalBERT and 0.000 for RoBERTa.
evidence.quote: In experiment 2, on Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o (precision=0.696; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.780) outperformed GPT-4o (precision=0.219; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.352), ClinicalBERT (precision=0.047; recall=0.667; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.088), and RoBERTa (F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.000).

evidence.title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
evidence.outcome: Comparative transcription accuracy across 10 ASR systems on same data
evidence.effect: GPT4oTranscribeCorrected best (DWER 3.5%; WER 3.7%); Heidi Health best commercial (DWER 6.2%); Dragon Professional Anywhere worst (WER 33.9%).
evidence.quote: Heidi Health was the highest-performing commercial system (DWER = 6.2%; WER = 5.4%), with Dragon Professional Anywhere being the worst (WER = 33.9%).
evidence.sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

evidence.title: A comparative performance analysis of regular expressions and a large language model-based approach to extract the BI-RADS score from radiological reports
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM vs simple Regex baseline for BI-RADS extraction on same reports
evidence.effect: Accuracy 89.20% Regex vs 87.69% LLM (P = .56, not significant); Regex 28,120 times faster (0.06 s vs 1687.20 s).
evidence.quote: For structured, standardized data like BI-RADS, traditional NLP techniques seem to be superior, though future work should explore hybrid approaches combining Regex precision for standardized elements with LLM contextual understanding for more complex information extraction tasks.

evidence.title: Enabling Just-in-Time Clinical Oncology Analysis With Large Language Models: Feasibility and Validation Study Using Unstructured Synthetic Data
evidence.outcome: LLM extraction accuracy and time compared with human extraction on the same 40 letters
evidence.effect: >99% average accuracy, comparable to human extraction; LLM 3.7 min vs human 133.8 min
evidence.quote: For multiparameter extraction from 40 letters, the LLM achieved >99% average accuracy, comparable to human extraction, but in significantly less time (LLM: 3.7 min vs human: 133.8 min).

evidence.title: When Jack of All Trades Is a Master of None: Comparing the Performance of GPT-4 Omni against Specialised Neural Networks in Identifying Malignant Dermatological Lesions from Smartphone Images and Structured Clinical Data
evidence.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4o against specialised neural networks on skin lesion malignancy triage
evidence.effect: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons; GPT-4o balanced accuracies were 0.571, 0.602, 0.622 for clinical, image, multimodal inputs.
evidence.quote: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons.
evidence.sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

evidence.title: A vision-language model-based approach for lung cancer diagnosis using lossless 3D CT images: evaluation of GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o for patient-level malignancy assessment
evidence.outcome: GPT-4.1 compared with deep-learning baselines and radiologist readers for lung nodule malignancy
evidence.effect: GPT-4.1 maintained its competitiveness when compared to representative deep-learning baselines and radiologist readers.
evidence.quote: GPT-4.1 maintained its competitiveness when compared to representative deep-learning baselines and radiologist readers.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Models and Top-Decile Doctors on an Undergraduate Ophthalmology Examination
evidence.outcome: LLM versus top-decile doctors on 100-question ophthalmology MCQ exam
evidence.effect: Pooled LLMs 85.50% vs doctors 75.67%, p = 0.0533 (not significant); Claude Sonnet 4 91.00% significantly outperformed pooled doctors (p = 0.0268).
evidence.quote: A primary analysis revealed no statistically significant difference between these groups (p = 0.0533).

evidence.title: Predicting emergency mortality risk in traumatic brain injury: comparative analysis of machine learning and large language model GPT-5
evidence.outcome: Compared LLM prompting strategies against SVM machine learning model on same TBI dataset
evidence.effect: SVM achieved best overall performance (AUC = 0.920); after threshold adjustment all LLMs reached comparable AUCs (0.902-0.919).
evidence.quote: The SVM model achieved the best overall performance (AUC = 0.920).

evidence.title: Diagnostic performance of large language models on the NEJM image challenge: a comparative study with human evaluators and the impact of prompt engineering
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of top LLM versus medical students and attending physician on same questions
evidence.effect: o4-mini-high achieved 94% accuracy; human accuracies ranged from 38.5% (three medical students) to 70.5% (attending physician), all significantly lower than the LLM.
evidence.quote: The human accuracies in this cohort ranged from 38.5% for three medical students to 70.5% for an attending physician-all significantly lower than OpenAI o4-mini-high.

evidence.title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
evidence.outcome: pairwise candidate model differences
evidence.effect: Chinese without-prompt N-staging: DeepSeek-R1 outperformed GPT-4o OR = 4.64, Qwen3 OR = 2.43, Grok-3 OR = 5.86; all p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: For instance, in the Chinese without-prompt N-staging condition, DeepSeek-R1′s superiority was substantial against GPT-4o (OR = 4.64, 95% CI [3.20–6.74], p < 0.001), Qwen3 (OR = 2.43, 95% CI [1.52–3.89], p < 0.001), and Grok-3 (OR = 5.86, 95% CI [4.29–8.00], p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

evidence.title: Comparative diagnostic capability of large language models in neurosurgery
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of five LLMs compared on the same neurosurgical vignettes
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 74% correct, AtlasGPT 63%, ChatGPT-3.5 53%, Microsoft Copilot 48%, Gemini 36%; ChatGPT-4 more accurate than counterparts (p = 0.005).
evidence.quote: Chi-square comparisons demonstrated that ChatGPT-4 was more accurate in providing clinical diagnoses than its counterparts (p = 0.005).

evidence.title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
evidence.outcome: AI-ECG versus QRS duration model discrimination and net reduction in CMR
evidence.effect: AI-ECG AUROC 0.87 vs 0.78 for QRS duration; QRS model gave no net CMR reduction (-0.02) at 0.25 threshold.
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence analysis of electrocardiograms outperformed QRS duration (AUROC 0.87 vs. 0.78, see Supplementary material online , Figure S3 ).

evidence.title: Benchmarking large language model-based agent systems for clinical decision tasks
evidence.outcome: Agent system accuracy versus baseline LLMs on the same clinical benchmarks, plus token and latency cost
evidence.effect: Agent systems gave only modest accuracy gains over baseline LLMs (60.3% AgentClinic MedQA, 28.0% MIMIC, 30.3% MedAgentsBench, 8.6% HLE text), with >10x token usage and >2x latency.
evidence.quote: Despite access to advanced tools (e.g., web browsing, code development and execution, and text file editing) agent systems yielded only modest accuracy gains over baseline LLMs, reaching 60.3% and 28.0% in AgentClinic MedQA and MIMIC, 30.3% on MedAgentsBench, and 8.6% on HLE text.

evidence.title: Defining operational safety in clinical artificial intelligence systems
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two FDA-cleared mammography AIs on same data for operational safety
evidence.effect: AI #1 had higher AUC (0.928 vs 0.882), but at alpha=100% AI #2 ruled out 290 true negatives (29.0%) vs 167 (16.7%) for AI #1; difference 123 cases (95% CI 87.0–150.0).
evidence.quote: This represents a substantial improvement over AI #1, which cleared only 167 cases (16.7% of the cohort), with a difference of 123 cases in the Rule-out Safe Zone in favor of AI #2 (95% confidence interval: 87.0–150.0).

evidence.title: Humans and Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Study with Medical Calculators
evidence.venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
evidence.outcome: LLM versus human annotator accuracy on medical calculator selection questions
evidence.effect: Best LLM (o1) accuracy 66.0% (CI 56.7-75.3%) on 100 questions vs. two human annotators averaging 79.5% (CI 73.5-85.0%); LLMs not superior to humans.
evidence.quote: Ultimately, we evaluated medical trainees and LLMs in recommending medical calculators across clinical scenarios like risk stratification and diagnosis.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
evidence.venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
evidence.outcome: F1 of LLM approaches vs traditional LightGBM structured-data model on 30-day ED revisit prediction
evidence.effect: All LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed LightGBM on structured data (F1=0.4614, 95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]); benchmarking against simpler model showed no LLM advantage.
evidence.quote: Despite having access to comprehensive structured and unstructured clinical data, all LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]))).

evidence.title: Multimodal Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-4.o, Claude 3.7, and Gemini 2.5 on Real-World Retina Cases
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of competing multimodal LLMs compared on the same retina cases
evidence.effect: Full-context accuracy: GPT-4.o 78.4%, Claude 73.0%, Gemini 29.7% (P<.001). Image-only: Claude 73.7%, GPT-4.o 63.2%, Gemini 31.6% (P<.001).
evidence.quote: In full-context cases, GPT-4.o achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (78.4%), followed by Claude (73.0%) and Gemini (29.7%) (P < .001).

evidence.title: Comparison of proprietary and fine-tuned large language models for multi-label classification of billing codes from radiology reports
evidence.outcome: F1 of fine-tuned small model versus commercial and open-source LLMs on same report sets
evidence.effect: On 500 real-world reports, fine-tuned model F1 70.32% ± 1.54% vs best LLM Gemini 2.5 Flash 58.22% ± 1.50% (p<0.001); on 350 cleaned reports GPT-5 (89.51 ± 1.52%) outperformed fine-tuned models.
evidence.quote: On a subset of 500 real-world samples, our models outperformed the best-performing LLM, Gemini 2.5 Flash, with an F1-score of 70.32% ± 1.54% compared to 58.22% ± 1.50% (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of Advanced Reasoning Models for Clinical Decision Support in Urology
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs versus experienced urologists and medical students on the same urology questions
evidence.effect: All five AI models had significantly higher odds of correct answers than experienced urologists (all p < 0.001, Dunnett-adjusted); medical students did not differ significantly from urologists.
evidence.quote: In the model-adjusted analysis, all five AI models showed significantly higher odds of correct answers than experienced urologists (all p < 0.001, Dunnett-adjusted), while medical students did not differ significantly from urologists.

evidence.title: Augmenting Large Language Model With Prompt Engineering and Supervised Fine-Tuning in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Tumor-Node-Metastasis Staging: Framework Development and Validation
evidence.outcome: TNM staging accuracy of optimized GLM-4-Air versus GPT-4o on held-out test set
evidence.quote: It achieved higher staging accuracies on the black-box test set: 92% (95% CI 0.850-0.959) for T, 86% (95% CI 0.779-0.915) for N, 92% (95% CI 0.850-0.959) for distant metastasis status (M), and 90% for overall clinical staging; by comparison, GPT-4o attained 87% (95% CI 0.790-0.922), 70% (95% CI 0.604-0.781), 78% (95% CI 0.689-0.850), and 80%, respectively.

evidence.title: Comparative performance of large language models and Drugs.com versus Lexicomp for antiseizure medication drug-drug interactions: A cross-sectional study with iterative prompting analysis
evidence.venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
evidence.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of LLMs versus Drugs.com against Lexicomp reference for ASM interactions
evidence.effect: Drugs.com sensitivity 0.870, specificity 0.629, accuracy 0.709; ChatGPT sensitivity 0.842, specificity 0.358; DeepSeek sensitivity 0.877, specificity 0.200. LLMs overpredicted interactions.
evidence.quote: Drugs.com demonstrated the best overall performance, with sensitivity 0.870, specificity 0.629, and accuracy 0.709.

evidence.title: How DISCERNing is ChatGPT? An Evaluation of Models and Prompt Engineering in Assessing Patient Education Materials
evidence.outcome: Agreement with human DISCERN scores across three GPT models and four prompting strategies
evidence.effect: Agreement was weak to moderate; o3 consistently outperformed GPT-5.2 and GPT-4o, and combined prompting modestly improved agreement and reduced absolute error.
evidence.quote: Combined prompting modestly improved agreement and reduced absolute error, particularly for the o3 model, which consistently outperformed GPT-5.2 and GPT-4o.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models and Machine Learning for ASA Classification Using Structured Electronic Health Record Data
evidence.outcome: ASA classification accuracy of LLMs versus traditional machine learning on the same data
evidence.effect: GPT-4o Few Shot Feature LLM reached 66% accuracy, F1 0.65, AUROC 0.79, versus 54% accuracy for the best traditional method (LightGBM), a 12-percentage-point improvement.
evidence.quote: Large language models outperformed traditional machine learning for ASA classification in this dataset, particularly in intermediate-risk patients comprising most surgical cases.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Crisis Detection: A Real-World Benchmark from Psychological Support Hotlines
evidence.venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
evidence.outcome: LLM performance versus trained human operators on crisis assessment tasks
evidence.effect: LLMs comparable or superior on suicide plan identification and risk assessment; humans retained advantages on mood status recognition and suicidal ideation detection.
evidence.quote: Compared to trained human operators, LLMs achieved comparable or superior performance on suicide plan identification and risk assessment, while humans retained advantages on mood status recognition and suicidal ideation detection.

evidence.title: Glass-box agentic-style workflow for multiclass cine cardiac magnetic resonance imaging classification with a large language model
evidence.outcome: LLM workflow accuracy compared with supervised ML models on same biomarkers
evidence.effect: LLM V3 accuracy 0.925 comparable to supervised models: Random Forest 0.938; SVM/Logistic Regression 0.925.
evidence.quote: Performance was comparable to supervised models (Random Forest accuracy 0.938; SVM/Logistic Regression accuracy 0.925).
evidence.sample_unit: cases (cine cardiac MRI studies) in independent evaluation set

evidence.title: Calibration and evaluation of machine-learning algorithms for missense variant classification under ACMG/ClinGen recommendations
evidence.venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
evidence.outcome: comparative predictor performance
evidence.effect: REVEL had highest overall performance; AM outperformed other tools for autosomal dominant variants in haploinsufficiency genes.
evidence.quote: REVEL demonstrated the highest overall performance, particularly for autosomal recessive variants and autosomal dominant variants tolerant to loss-of-function.

evidence.title: Deep learning for freezing of gait assessment using inertial measurement units: a multicentre validation study
evidence.outcome: architecture selection by ICC
evidence.quote: LTContext was selected for further experiments, as it achieved the highest ICC for both %TF and #FOG across all external datasets.
evidence.country: Belgium (multicentre: Netherlands, USA, Brazil, China, Germany, Israel)

evidence.title: Beyond Diagnosis: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs for Pathology Localization in Chest Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Localization accuracy of MLLMs versus task-specific CNN and radiologist benchmark
evidence.effect: GPT-5 49.7%, GPT-4 39.1%, MedGemma 17.7%, all lower than task-specific CNN (59.9%) and radiologist benchmark (80.1%).
evidence.quote: Averaged across nine pathologies in the CheXlocalize dataset, GPT-5 exhibited a localization accuracy of 49.7%, followed by GPT-4 (39.1%) and MedGemma (17.7%), all lower than a task-specific CNN baseline (59.9%) and a radiologist benchmark (80.1%).

evidence.title: Performance and safety of a fine-tuned small language model for pediatric emergency triage: A benchmark study
evidence.outcome: Overall triage performance of fine-tuned LLM versus structured-data XGBoost comparator
evidence.effect: LLM accuracy 58.60%, macro-F1 0.417, QWK 0.535 vs XGBoost accuracy 69.40%, macro-F1 0.618, QWK 0.651; LLM had a safer error profile.
evidence.quote: The structured-data comparator showed higher overall performance, with an accuracy of 69.40%, a macro-F1 score of 0.618, and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.651.

evidence.title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
evidence.outcome: LLM strategies compared against each other and an exploratory nurse baseline
evidence.effect: Nurse achieved 93% MCQ and 90% open-ended; GraphRAG comparable on MCQ (96.89%) but nurse exceeded all LLM configurations on open-ended (best 66.44%).
evidence.quote: Her multiple-choice performance was comparable to the best-performing LLM strategy, whereas her open-ended performance exceeded all tested LLM configurations.

evidence.title: Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models in Detection and Position Assessment of Thoracic Devices on Chest Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Radiologist versus multimodal LLM performance on thoracic device assessment, paired comparison
evidence.effect: Radiologists numerically outperformed all three LLMs in 42/42 paired comparisons; significant after Bonferroni correction in 33/42 (32/42 at p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Radiologists numerically outperformed all three LLMs in 42/42 paired comparisons; the superiority was statistically significant after Bonferroni correction in 33/42 (32/42 at p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Bladder Cancer: Comparative Knowledge Retrieval and Clinical Reasoning of DeepSeek and ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: LLM performance compared against urologists on the same reconstructed clinical cases
evidence.effect: Human urologists significantly outperformed both AI models in diagnostic test appropriateness (P < 0.01); DeepSeek-R1 comparable to humans and ChatGPT-5 Pro on logical coherence (P > 0.05).
evidence.quote: Notably, human urologists significantly outperformed both AI models in diagnostic test appropriateness (P < 0.01), primarily because DeepSeek-R1 struggled with "test avoidance," tending to recommend redundant investigations (P < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Cross-Sensor and Cross-Population Generalization of Deep Learning Models for Digital Mammography: A Controlled Four-Country Benchmark of Five Backbone Architectures with Statistical Significance Testing
evidence.outcome: Foundation models compared to simpler ResNet-50 baseline on same data
evidence.effect: ResNet-50 (AUC 0.867) outperformed Mammo-CLIP (0.847), Mammo-FM (0.846), DINOv2 (0.813), Rad-DINO (0.703); all gaps p_adj<0.05.
evidence.quote: No foundation model beats the ResNet-50 baseline, and the gaps are statistically significant once predictions are stacked across seeds and run through a paired DeLong test.
evidence.sample_unit: validation images (CBIS-DDSM; external: CMMD 1032, DMID 509, MIAS 322)

evidence.title: Can Small Open-Source Language Models With Retrieval-Augmented Generation Match GPT-4 Performance in Breast Cancer Clinical Decision Support?
evidence.outcome: Comparison of small open-source RAG models against GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5 on same queries
evidence.effect: RAG-enhanced Qwen2.5-14B scored 3.77 vs 3.96 for GPT-4-turbo (pairwise 0.72 vs 0.81), and outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo across all metrics.
evidence.quote: Qwen2.5-14B outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo across all metrics, achieving a normalized pairwise score of 0.72 versus 0.81 for GPT-4-turbo.

evidence.title: Clinician expertise and prompt engineering enhance cancer information extraction in electronic health records by small language models
evidence.outcome: Model performance by model type
evidence.effect: General-purpose models, including LLaMA 3.1 8B, outperformed biomedical models in most tasks, particularly binary-feature extraction.
evidence.quote: We show that general-purpose models (e.g., LLaMA 3.1 8B) outperform biomedical models in most tasks, particularly in extracting binary features.

evidence.title: Strategies for Deploying Large Language Models for Ascertaining Clinical Outcomes and Sites of Metastases From Radiology Impressions in Patients With Cancer
evidence.outcome: Comparison of open-source LLMs against GPT4 models on the same data for radiophenotype extraction
evidence.effect: GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs zero/one-shot; fine-tuned Mistral0.2 had OR 0.27 (95% CI 0.20-0.36) versus best GPT4 for progression, favoring the fine-tuned models.
evidence.quote: In zero-/one-shot settings, GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs.

evidence.title: Transferring healthcare risk prediction models between Medicaid populations: a transfer learning evaluation
evidence.outcome: Comparison of complex transfer methods against simpler baselines on same data
evidence.effect: Meta-ensemble AUC 0.728 vs source-only 0.725 (p=0.454); Enhanced MAML 0.677 significantly below source-only (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: The AUC difference of 0.003 was not statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.454; bootstrap 95% CI for difference: −0.005 to 0.010).
evidence.sample_unit: Virginia Medicaid members in hold-out test set

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Classifying Usual Interstitial Pneumonia from Radiology Reports: Native Reasoning Versus Structured Prompting
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: candidate model comparison
evidence.effect: Llama 3.1 405B offered no advantage over Llama 3.3 70B; Qwen 397B underperformed Qwen 27B.
evidence.quote: Larger models did not consistently outperform smaller ones: Llama 3.1 405B offered no advantage over Llama 3.3 70B, and the Qwen 397B model underperformed the dense Qwen 27B.

evidence.title: Pediatric vs. Adult Pneumonia Detection: Quantifying Age-related Generalization Gaps in Zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Comparison of zero-shot LLMs against domain-trained CNN baseline on same test sets
evidence.effect: CNN outperformed all LLMs in pediatrics (MCC 0.799 vs 0.484, 0.470, 0.272) and remained best in adults (MCC 0.850).
evidence.quote: In adults, all models improved, but the CNN remained best (MCC 0.850, 0.816-0.882).

evidence.title: Improving the reliability of polygenic risk score-based prediction for cardiovascular and renal complications across ancestries in type 2 diabetes using Mondrian Cross-Conformal Prediction
evidence.outcome: MCCP versus LR-SP discrimination
evidence.effect: At α≈0.05 in WB, AUROC was 0.69 vs 0.68 for stroke, 0.75 vs 0.76 for MI, and 0.79 vs 0.78 for Low eGFR.
evidence.quote: Compared with coverage-matched LR-SP (top/bottom 5.1%, 5.2%, and 10.3%, respectively), the two methods showed comparable discrimination: stroke (MCCP: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.65–0.73; LR-SP: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.64–0.73), MI (0.75, 95% CI: 0.71–0.79 vs. 0.76, 95% CI: 0.73–0.79), and Low eGFR (0.79, 95% CI: 0.76–0.82 vs. 0.78, 95% CI: 0.76–0.81).
evidence.sample_unit: UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes (17,574 White British, 1,145 South Asian, 749 African/Caribbean) tested; 4,098 ADVANCE participants used for training

evidence.title: Multimodal Large Language Models and Dental Students in Radiographic Landmark Identification: A Novel Grid-Based Assessment
evidence.outcome: MLLM landmark localisation versus fourth-year dental student consensus on same radiographs
evidence.effect: Both models remained inferior to student consensus on all periapical and panoramic comparisons; GPT-5.4 matched students only on cephalometric landmarks; Gemini approached parity only on cephalometric points under guided prompting.
evidence.quote: Both models remained inferior to the student consensus on all periapical and panoramic comparisons, with Gemini 3.1 Pro approaching parity only on cephalometric points under guided prompting.
evidence.sample_unit: queries (200 dental radiographs, 12 landmarks, 3 repetitions; 10,800 API calls)

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Large Language Models in Retinal Fundus Photography
evidence.outcome: Comparison of four candidate multimodal LLMs on the same fundus images
evidence.effect: Accuracy varied widely between models on the same data: ChatGPT 75% vs Claude 18%, Grok 18%, Gemini 14%; agreement across models was low (kappa 0.11-0.16 with ChatGPT).
evidence.quote: Agreement across models was consistent low (κ = 0.11-0.16 with ChatGPT; κ ≈ 0.05 among Claude, Gemini, and Grok).

evidence.title: The Performance of Large Language Models in Extracting Intestinal Symptoms From Electronic Health Records: Retrospective Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of 12 candidate open-source LLMs on same annotated data to select configuration
evidence.effect: Qwen3-8b no-role macro F1 0.89 vs Llama3.1-8b 0.35-0.40 and Llama2-Chinese-7b 0.00-0.11; model choice greatly affected performance.
evidence.quote: Among all configurations, Qwen3-8b with no-role prompting achieved a macro F 1 -score of 0.89 and balanced accuracy of 0.95±0.06, with an inference time of 3.64 seconds per record, whereas Qwen3-1.7b under zero-shot prompting achieved a macro F 1 -score of 0.85 with a faster inference time of 1.61 seconds.

evidence.title: Performance and label efficiency of traditional deep-learning models and a retina-specific foundation model for ocular and systemic disease detection: a retrospective comparative study
evidence.outcome: AUC of retina foundation model versus supervised deep-learning models on same test data
evidence.effect: Similar ocular disease AUCs with full datasets (traditional 0.914-0.965 vs RETFound 0.938-0.966); RETFound outperformed on systemic disease and on glaucoma/DR with small fine-tuning sets.
evidence.quote: Under this specific study design, the performance of traditional deep-learning models is similar to that of RETFound for ocular disease detection when fine-tuned on large datasets.

evidence.title: DiagnosticXchange: an open-source framework for evaluating safety, efficiency, and diagnostic reasoning in clinical AI systems
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Comparison of AI systems against each other and neurologists on multiple dimensions
evidence.effect: Systems with near-identical accuracy differed significantly in cost (P<.001); pilot comparison captured multi-dimensional performance of 14 neurologists alongside AI systems.
evidence.quote: A pilot comparison captured multi-dimensional performance of 14 neurologists alongside AI systems.

evidence.title: Audited large language model triage for systematic review screening in national clinical guideline production: validation and prospective deployment
evidence.outcome: Retention of eligible records by AI versus blinded human consensus
evidence.effect: Across the completed 680-record audit, AI flagged all 38 final retained records, whereas locked blinded human consensus missed seven.
evidence.quote: Across 600 randomly sampled AI-excluded records from the migraine and dementia programmes, none was confirmed as a final false negative after post-unblinding adjudication; across the completed 680-record audit, all 38 final retained records had been AI flagged, whereas locked blinded human consensus missed seven.

evidence.title: Utilizing standardized nursing terminologies in implementing an AI-powered fall-prevention tool to improve patient outcomes: a multihospital study
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: AI model discrimination versus existing heuristic fall-risk tools
evidence.effect: AI models AUROC 0.8051-0.9851 versus heuristic tools alone AUROC 0.6491-0.7364.
evidence.quote: For both of these the performance was better than for the heuristic tools alone (AUROC = 0.6491–0.7364).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for characterization of colorectal polyps: Prospective multicenter study
evidence.outcome: AI vs expert endoscopist diagnostic performance for polyp histology prediction
evidence.effect: Sensitivity 80% (AI) vs 88% (endoscopists), P<0.05; specificity 83% for both; accuracy 81% vs 86%. AI classified 22 of 23 sessile serrated lesions as hyperplasia; endoscopists correctly classified 16 of 23.
evidence.quote: However, sensitivity was greater with endoscopists as compared with CAD EYE ( P <0.05).

evidence.title: Comparison of 21 artificial intelligence algorithms in automated diabetic retinopathy screening using handheld fundus camera
evidence.outcome: Variation in performance across competing AI algorithms on the same dataset
evidence.effect: Agreement for referable DR varied from 49.4% to 92.3% across 21 algorithms; ungradable rate ranged 0% to 28.2%.
evidence.quote: The AI algorithms achieved a mean agreement of 79.4% for referable DR, but the results varied from 49.4% to 92.3%.

evidence.title: Implementation and prospective performance evaluation of an intraoperative duration prediction model using high throughput real-time data
evidence.outcome: Prediction error compared with bias-corrected scheduled duration
evidence.effect: Mean CRPS was 27.19 mins (standard error 0.016 min) for the model versus 51.66 min (standard error 0.029 min) for bias-corrected scheduled duration.
evidence.quote: The mean CRPS across all predictions was 27.19 mins ( se , 0.016 min), compared with 51.66 min ( se , 0.029 min) for the bias-corrected scheduled duration.

evidence.title: Development, validation, and clinical evaluation of a machine-learning based model for diagnosing early infection after cardiovascular surgery (DEICS): a multi-center cohort study
evidence.outcome: Discrimination of candidate ML models versus traditional logistic regression for early postoperative infection
evidence.effect: XGBoost had the highest AUROC, 0.96 (95% CI 0.93-0.98), and was chosen over the other ML models and the logistic regression comparator; Brier score 0.02.
evidence.quote: The XGBoost model achieved the highest performance with an AUROC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.93-0.98).

evidence.title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
evidence.outcome: discrimination of AI versus traditional early warning scores
evidence.effect: AUROC 0.896 vs 0.797 (NEWS) and 0.722 (MEWS); AUPRC 0.336 vs 0.125 (NEWS) and 0.079 (MEWS)
evidence.quote: VC-MAES achieved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.896 using only vital signs and age, outperforming traditional EWSs, including the National Early Warning Score (0.797) and the Modified Early Warning Score (0.722).

evidence.title: Real-World Evaluation of AI-Driven Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in Public Health Settings: Validation and Implementation Study
evidence.outcome: Commercial algorithms' diagnostic performance against human grading
evidence.effect: Across three algorithms, sensitivity ranged from 60%-80% and specificity from 14%-96%, demonstrating substantial differences between candidate products.
evidence.quote: The three AI algorithms demonstrated variable diagnostic performance, with sensitivity (60%-80%) and specificity (14%-96%).

evidence.title: Accuracy and efficiency of artificial Intelligence-Assisted three-dimensional liver volumetry in living donor evaluation based on real world prospective data
evidence.venue: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
evidence.outcome: Graft-volume prediction accuracy versus conventional manual volumetry
evidence.effect: After exclusions, AI: R² = 0.818; median error 54.0 mL. Conventional methods: R² = 0.707; median error 65.0 mL.
evidence.quote: After exclusions, AI-based volumetry showed superior predictive performance (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.818; median error 54.0 mL) versus conventional methods (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.707; median error 65.0 mL).

evidence.title: Tele-ophthalmology-enabled and artificial intelligence-ready referral pathway for community optometry referrals of retinal disease: HERMES cluster randomised trial with a diagnostic accuracy study
evidence.outcome: AI referral decision accuracy versus hospital experts and community optometrists
evidence.effect: Octane showed inferior sensitivity and specificity versus human expert assessors (clinical reference standard); similar accuracy to community optometrists.
evidence.quote: Compared to hospital-based experts for referral decisions, Octane was less accurate at making routine and urgent referral decisions and of similar accuracy to community optometrists.

evidence.title: Predicting the Value of Radiology Artificial Intelligence Applications: Large-Scale Predeployment Evaluation of a Portfolio of Models
evidence.outcome: AI versus radiologist positive predictive value and sensitivity
evidence.effect: Radiologists generally had higher PPV, whereas AI generally had higher sensitivity; neither consistently outperformed the other across both metrics.
evidence.quote: Across tasks, radiologists generally had higher PPV, whereas AI generally had higher sensitivity.

evidence.title: Research on the generalization of a blood donor recruitment framework based on machine learning
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Recruitment success compared with conventional donor selection
evidence.effect: High-willingness donor recruitment success was 408.28%, 25.19%, and 47.31% higher than conventional methods in Nanjing, Suzhou, and Yangzhou, respectively.
evidence.quote: On average, the recruitment success rate for high-willingness donors was 408.28%, 25.19%, and 47.31% higher than that of conventional methods in Nanjing (χ 2 = 35.471, p = 0.000), Suzhou (χ 2 = 9.384, p = 0.009), and Yangzhou (χ 2 = 96.701, p = 0.000), respectively, as shown in Table 1 .
evidence.sample_unit: prospective SMS recruitment rounds (model development used 11,616 Nanjing SMS records)

evidence.title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
evidence.outcome: CDS screening performance versus human standard-of-care screening
evidence.effect: CDS sensitivity 81.7% (77.1–85.8%) vs human 80.2% (75.4–84.4%); specificity 67.3% vs 67.4%; no notable difference
evidence.quote: There was no notable difference between human performance and the CDS given overlapping CIs.

evidence.title: Using Optimal Feature Selection and Continuous Learning to Implement Efficient Model Arrays for Predicting Daily Clinical Radiology Workload
evidence.outcome: Workload forecasting performance compared with trivial estimates
evidence.effect: Average R² of 0.83 (IQR 0.13) across tested radiology divisions; the model array significantly outperformed trivial estimates.
evidence.quote: The model array had an average R<sup>2</sup> of 0.83 (IQR 0.13) across the tested radiology divisions; it significantly outperformed trivial estimates and provided an accurate daily prediction pattern.
evidence.sample_unit: days of radiology exam volume data

evidence.title: Implementation costs and cost-effectiveness of ultraportable chest X-ray with artificial intelligence in active case finding for tuberculosis in Nigeria
evidence.outcome: TB cases detected and implementation costs compared with symptom screening
evidence.effect: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 detected 76 cases at US$56589, versus 77 cases at US$48939 for any symptom screening; the AI-only algorithm was strictly dominated.
evidence.quote: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 algorithm was strictly dominated as it led to 1 fewer diagnosis but costed more than the any symptom algorithm.

evidence.title: Hemodialysis equipment malfunction incidence and risk profiling in clinical settings: a retrospective single-center cohort analysis
evidence.outcome: Discriminative performance compared with alternative models
evidence.effect: Random forest achieved AUC = 0.774, reported as superior to gradient boosting, support vector machines, and logistic regression. Comparator AUCs were not reported.
evidence.quote: A random forest algorithm was developed to predict alarm events, selected based on superior discriminative performance (AUC = 0.774) compared to gradient boosting, support vector machines, and logistic regression.

evidence.title: Development and Implementation of a Machine Learning Model for Prediction of Surgical Case Duration
evidence.venue: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
evidence.outcome: Surgical duration prediction accuracy compared with standardized existing scheduling practices
evidence.effect: Standardized workflow MAE = 20.1 min versus ORchestra MAE = 19.8 min; standardization approached ML-level accuracy for many procedures, while ORchestra decreased overscheduling outliers.
evidence.quote: Notably, workflow standardization alone approached ML-level accuracy for many procedures, highlighting human-factor variability as a dominant source of error.

evidence.title: Agentic Automation of BT-RADS Scoring: End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Standardized Brain Tumor Follow-up Assessment
evidence.outcome: BT-RADS classification accuracy versus expert reference standard, AI system compared with initial clinical assessments
evidence.effect: AI system 374/492 (76.0%; 95% CI 72.1%-79.6%) versus 283/492 (57.5%; 95% CI 53.1%-61.8%) for initial clinical assessments, +18.5 percentage points, P<.001
evidence.quote: The system achieved 374/492 (76.0%; 95% CI, 72.1%-79.6%) accuracy versus 283/492 (57.5%; 95% CI, 53.1%-61.8%) for initial clinical assessments (+18.5 percentage points; P<.001).

evidence.title: Preventive Care Recommendations by Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: LLM preventive care prioritization compared with historical physicians on the same survey (LYGPC, consistency, selectiveness)
evidence.effect: LLMs closely mirrored physicians (mean Spearman 0.83); several models exceeded physicians in LYGPC and consistency; lifestyle services underprioritized (8.8% vs 38% rated 4 or higher); augmentation effects varied by model.
evidence.quote: Several models exceeded physicians in LYGPC and consistency while being more selective.

evidence.title: Cost-effectiveness of an AI-based app compared to usual care for early skin cancer detection in Belgium
evidence.outcome: Skin cancer detection rate and cost of AI app versus usual care
evidence.effect: App detection rate lower than usual care: melanoma 0.601 vs 0.874, BCC 0.585 vs 0.912, SCC 0.706 vs 0.922, benign 0.820 vs 0.937; costs were lower or similar; unnecessary benign referrals.
evidence.quote: In its current diagnostic performance the AI-based app was associated with lower skin cancer detection rates and as a consequence, lower costs.
evidence.sample_unit: decision-tree model simulation (no patient sample reported)

evidence.title: Enhanced Language Models for Predicting and Understanding HIV Care Disengagement: A Case Study in Tanzania
evidence.outcome: Fine-tuned LLM performance versus supervised ML and zero-shot LLMs on same data
evidence.effect: Enhanced LLMs outperformed the supervised ML model and zero-shot LLMs across all outcomes in both internal and external validation datasets.
evidence.quote: The enhanced LLMs consistently outperformed the supervised ML model and zero-shot LLMs across all outcomes in both internal and external validation datasets.
evidence.sample_unit: people living with HIV (4,809,765 EMR records)

evidence.title: Evaluation of Gender Bias in the Evaluation of Synthetic Cardiovascular Disease Cases with Open Source LLMs
evidence.outcome: Variability between candidate LLMs in diagnostic confidence and test recommendations
evidence.effect: Substantial inter-model variability: Gemma-2b and Phi assertive, TinyLLaMA conservative.
evidence.quote: Substantial inter-model variability was observed, with Gemma-2b and Phi demonstrating assertive diagnostic patterns while TinyLLaMA showed conservative tendencies.
evidence.sample_unit: model responses (500 synthetic cases x 3 models)

evidence.title: From Clinical Judgment to Large Language Models: Benchmarking Predictive Approaches for Unplanned Hospital Admissions
evidence.outcome: Discrimination (AUROC/AUPRC) of physicians, structured ML model, and LLMs predicting 30-day ED visits/admissions on same cases
evidence.effect: CLMBR-T AUROC 0.79 (AUPRC 0.78), large LLMs AUROC 0.74, pooled physicians AUROC 0.65 (AUPRC 0.61). LLMs beat physicians but trailed the ML model.
evidence.quote: CLMBR-T achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.79, 95% CI: 0.75-0.83; AUPRC 0.78, 95% CI: 0.72-0.83), followed by large LLMs (DeepSeek V3, Claude 4.1 Opus, GPT-5; AUROC 0.74).

evidence.title: Ranking-optimized survival models can underperform fixed-horizon clinical prediction
evidence.outcome: Fixed-horizon AUROC of ML survival model versus physician estimates and 1995 model
evidence.effect: At 60 days AUROC was 0.750 for the survival model, 0.808 for physicians (matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model; gap reproduced across eight splits.
evidence.quote: The survival model achieved a competitive ranking concordance (0.705) but underperformed both comparators at fixed horizons: at 60 days its area under the ROC curve was 0.750, versus 0.808 for physicians (on the matched sample) and 0.827 for the 1995 model, a gap reproduced across eight independent splits and statistically reliable after multiplicity correction.

evidence.title: Data Extraction from Oncology Imaging Reports by Large Language Models: A Comparative Accuracy Study
evidence.outcome: LLM classification accuracy versus human accuracy on same reports, by task
evidence.effect: Metastasis status: all LLMs non-inferior to humans (gpt-oss:120b 97.6% vs human 98.4%). Treatment response: all LLMs inferior (best 78.3% vs human 86.0%, -7.7 pp).
evidence.quote: In this study, LLMs were non-inferior to human accuracy for classification of metastasis status but were inferior for response to treatment assessment.

evidence.title: Multi-Agent Dynamic Refinement Outperforms Static RAG in Clinical Reasoning for Complex Nephrology Cases
evidence.outcome: static RAG versus baseline LLM
evidence.quote: Static knowledge retrieval alone fails to enhance frontier LLM performance in longitudinal medical reasoning.

evidence.title: Contextual Cue Susceptibility in Clinical AI: A Randomized Controlled Clinician-Comparator Study
evidence.outcome: LLM versus clinician diagnostic susceptibility
evidence.effect: Baseline LLM lure selection was 84.9% vs clinicians 27.8%; extra cue effect 57.6 percentage points (95% CI 50.2-65.2); cue accuracy 12.4% vs 54.6%.
evidence.quote: Baseline LLMs selected the lure in 84.9% of matched cue responses versus 27.8% for clinician participants, an extra cue effect of 57.6 percentage points (95% CI 50.2-65.2); cue accuracy fell to 12.4% versus 54.6%.
evidence.sample_unit: usable LLM responses (plus 1,128 clinician responses from 47 clinicians)

evidence.title: Machine learning for elective caesarean section in Bangladesh: validation design, not model choice, determines the performance a deployed model would have
evidence.outcome: discrimination of machine learning models compared to logistic regression
evidence.effect: AUROC ranged from 0.724 to 0.736 under cluster-grouped validation, a spread of 0.012; no model improved on logistic regression by an actionable margin
evidence.quote: No model improved on logistic regression by a margin worth acting on: the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranged from 0.724 to 0.736 under cluster-grouped validation, a spread of 0.012.

evidence.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using Lumbar Spine Imaging: Diagnostic Performance, Reproducibility, Effects of Few-Shot Prompting, and Comparison with Physicians
evidence.outcome: radiographic diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus physicians
evidence.effect: Claude achieved 73.3% accuracy, Gemini 64.4%, specialists 57.4%, ChatGPT 55.6%, and non-specialists 44.0%
evidence.quote: Claude achieved the highest radiographic accuracy (73.3%), followed by Gemini (64.4%), specialists (57.4%), ChatGPT (55.6%), and non-specialists (44.0%).
evidence.sample_unit: images (45 lateral lumbar radiographs and 45 sagittal CT images)

evidence.title: ChatGPT in Occupational Medicine: A Comparative Study with Human Experts
evidence.outcome: performance versus professional doctors
evidence.effect: On a 5-point likert score, physicians performed better for accurate questions; ChatGPT with legislative context was comparable for complete answers.
evidence.quote: Occupational physicians perform better than ChatGPT in generating accurate questions on a 5-point likert score, while ChatGPT with access to legislative context is comparable to professional doctors in providing complete answers.

evidence.title: Real-World Performance of Large Language Models in Emergency Department Chest Pain Triage
evidence.outcome: ACS diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus human experts on same retrospective chest pain data
evidence.effect: Human experts 86.37% accuracy and 89.26% specificity vs Lingyi Zhihui 76.40%/70.15%, Tongyi Qianwen 61.11%/47.95%, MediGuide-14B 84.52% accuracy; LLMs had higher sensitivity.
evidence.quote: Human experts achieved higher accuracy (86.37%) and specificity (89.26%) but lower sensitivity compared to the LLMs.

evidence.title: Multimodal Image Dataset for AI-based Skin Cancer (MIDAS) Benchmarking
evidence.outcome: Model-to-clinician diagnostic performance comparison for malignant vs benign
evidence.effect: Dermatologists were 79% accurate with top-1 diagnosis differentiating malignant from benign; used as comparative baseline for the models.
evidence.quote: As a comparative baseline, the dermatologists performing biopsies were 79% accurate with their top-1 diagnosis at differentiating a malignant from benign lesion.

evidence.title: Unmet Needs in Acute Hepatic Porphyria Diagnosis: A Comparative Big Data Analysis of an AI-based Human-in-the-Loop Screening Versus Standard of Care
evidence.outcome: clinically plausible cases compared to standard of care
evidence.effect: 74 (38.74%) vs 28 (27.72%) clinically plausible cases for HAI vs SOC; 46 de-novo cases found by HAI; difference not statistically significant
evidence.quote: In our study, our proposed HAI screening approach showed a higher plausibility rate in suspected cases compared to the SOC and statistical testing could not find a statistically significant difference between the screening methods.

evidence.title: Using an artificial intelligence tool incorporating natural language processing to identify patients with a diagnosis of ANCA-associated vasculitis in electronic health records
evidence.outcome: Patient identification performance compared with ICD-10 coding
evidence.effect: The AI identification method outperformed ICD-10 coding, mainly for MPO+ and organ-limited AAV patients.
evidence.quote: Our identification method outperformed ICD-10-coding predominantly in identifying MPO+ and organ-limited AAV patients.
evidence.sample_unit: AAV patients in training (n=203) and validation (n=84) sets

evidence.title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
evidence.outcome: Costs versus current care
evidence.effect: Observed referral had the lowest average cost, €5890/patient; prediction-model scenarios ranged €5954–€6742/patient.
evidence.quote: The decision tree analysis shows that the observed probabilities of referral led to the lowest costs with average patient costs of €5890.

evidence.title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic performance versus clinicians
evidence.effect: Overall F1: ophthalmologists 89.35%, interns 82.69%, ChatGPT English prompts 76.76%, Chinese prompts 73.04%.
evidence.quote: Although ChatGPT performed better than experts for some disease types (eg, Direct-English and Step-English prompts for the normal and CRVO categories and all prompts for the BRVO category), the overall performance of ophthalmologists was the best (89.35%), followed by ophthalmology interns (82.69%), ChatGPT with Direct-English and Step-English prompts (76.76%), and ChatGPT with Direct-Chinese and Step-Chinese prompts (73.04%).

evidence.title: Large-Scale assessment of ChatGPT's performance in benign and malignant bone tumors imaging report diagnosis and its potential for clinical applications
evidence.outcome: diagnostic performance of AI compared with physicians
evidence.effect: Physicians significantly outperformed few-shot ChatGPT (accuracy 0.88 vs 0.87, specificity 0.81 vs 0.73, AUC 0.92 vs 0.83; t = 3.42, P = 0.0008), while direct ChatGPT had 0.73 accuracy and 0.58 specificity.
evidence.quote: Additionally, the comparison between physicians and few-shot enhanced ChatGPT showed a T-statistic of 3.42 with a P-value of 0.0008, underscoring the physicians' statistically superior performance.( Table 2 ).

evidence.title: Diagnosis and prognosis of abnormal cardiac scintigraphy uptake suggestive of cardiac amyloidosis using artificial intelligence: a retrospective, international, multicentre, cross-tracer development and validation study
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with five physicians on the same 200 cases
evidence.effect: Physicians' mean AUC 0·946 (0·924-0·967) was inferior to AI AUC 0·997 (0·991-1·000), p=0·0040; physicians disagreed in 22 (11%) of 200 cases.
evidence.quote: In the multicase multireader study, five physicians disagreed in 22 (11%) of 200 cases (Fleiss' kappa 0·89), with a mean AUC of 0·946 (95% CI 0·924-0·967), which was inferior to AI (AUC 0·997 [0·991-1·000], p=0·0040).

evidence.title: Machine learning models' assessment: trust and performance
evidence.outcome: Performance (geometric mean) of candidate models versus the GRACE score on the same dataset
evidence.effect: The rule-based approach outperformed the GRACE model's performance while providing a high level of trust. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: It provides a high level of trust in the respective operation while outperformed the GRACE model's performance, enhancing the required physicians' acceptance.

evidence.title: Automated remote sleep monitoring needs uncertainty quantification
evidence.outcome: AI versus human expert performance
evidence.effect: Machine learning approach outperformed the human expert; no human accuracy reported.
evidence.quote: Remarkably, the machine learning approach outperformed the human expert in interpreting these wearable data.

evidence.title: AI-integrated Screening to Replace Double Reading of Mammograms: A Population-wide Accuracy and Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: cancer detection accuracy of AI replacing second reader versus standard double reading
evidence.effect: sensitivity −1.58% (P < .001), NPV −0.01% (P < .001), recall rate −0.06% (P = .04), and arbitration rate +1.22% (P < .001)
evidence.quote: Integrated AIsecond had lower sensitivity (−1.58%, P < .001), negative predictive value (NPV) (−0.01%, P < .001), and recall rate (−0.06%, P = .04) but a higher positive predictive value (PPV) (+0.03%, P < .001) and arbitration rate (+1.22%, P < .001).

evidence.title: Deep Learning Algorithms for Breast Cancer Detection in a UK Screening Cohort: As Stand-alone Readers and Combined with Human Readers
evidence.outcome: DL algorithms combined with human readers compared with double reading
evidence.effect: Combining DL with human readers achieved noninferior sensitivity (67.0%, 65.6%, 65.4% vs 67.4%; P<.001 for all) and superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, 97.6% vs 97.1%; P<.001 for all) compared with double reading.
evidence.quote: Combining the DL algorithms with human readers achieved noninferior sensitivity (67.0%, 65.6%, and 65.4% for DL-1, DL-2, and DL-3, respectively; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (67.4%), and superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, and 97.6%; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (97.1%).

evidence.title: Efficacy of Early Warning Scores as the Prediction Tool for Detecting Patients With Acute Deterioration in a High Dependent Unit
evidence.outcome: predictive accuracy of AI versus simpler score for composite outcome
evidence.effect: NEWS was superior to VSI for composite outcome (AUC 0.701 vs 0.647, p=0.014) and unexpected ICU transfer (AUC 0.834 vs 0.767)
evidence.quote: The AUC for NEWS was significantly superior to that of VSI for the composite outcome (p=0.014).

evidence.title: Development, validation and recalibration of a prediction model for prediabetes: an EHR and NHANES-based study
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: prediabetes discrimination of 23-variable LASSO versus 8-variable approximation model
evidence.effect: optimism-corrected C-statistic was 0.760 for 23-variable LASSO versus 0.763 for 8-variable approximation model
evidence.quote: Both the LASSO and approximation models demonstrated similar discrimination in the EHR cohort, with optimism-corrected C-statistics of 0.760 and 0.763, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (EHR development cohort); 2,348 NHANES participants for external validation

evidence.title: Development and Evaluation of a GPT4-Based Orofacial Pain Clinical Decision Support System
evidence.outcome: GPT4 diagnostic accuracy versus clinical experts, medical students, and general practitioners on the same 24 cases
evidence.effect: GPT4 was comparable to non-expert evaluators but surpassed by clinical experts, who correctly diagnosed 54% of cases at ICOP level 3; GPT4 reached level 3 in 38% of the 100 cases.
evidence.quote: In the subset of 24 cases, the model's performance was comparable to non-expert human evaluators but was surpassed by clinical experts, who correctly diagnosed 54% of cases at level 3.
evidence.sample_unit: anonymized orofacial pain patient case descriptions

evidence.title: Smart Pharmaceutical Monitoring System With Personalized Medication Schedules and Self-Management Programs for Patients With Diabetes: Development and Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: medication schedule and self-management program performance compared to software and clinicians
evidence.effect: DUMS and pharmacist refinement scored significantly higher than GPT-4 in schedule accuracy (4.43 and 4.49 vs 3.84), safety (4.44 vs 3.91), and total scores (37.96 and 39.52 vs 36.35; all P<.001).
evidence.quote: Reliability analysis demonstrated that the DUMS group outperformed the GPT-4 group in medication schedule accuracy and safety, as well as comprehensiveness and richness of the self-management program (P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

evidence.title: Multi-Center Benchmarking of a Commercially Available Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) Score Assignment and Lesion Detection in Prostate MRI
evidence.outcome: AI versus radiologist sensitivity and specificity for csPCa on same MRI exams
evidence.effect: Patient level sensitivity/specificity 92%/64% radiologists vs 91%/57% AI; lesion level 90%/70% vs 81%/78% (PI-RADS ≥4). AI sensitivity comparable to radiologists.
evidence.quote: Sensitivity and specificity for clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa, defined as ISUP ≥ 2) were 92%/64% for radiologists vs. 91%/57% for AI detection on patient level and 90%/70% vs. 81%/78% on lesion level, respectively (cut-off PI-RADS ≥ 4).

evidence.title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
evidence.outcome: Performance versus OrthoInfo benchmark
evidence.effect: OrthoInfo scored 5.0 ± 0.0 versus standard ChatGPT 4.7 ± 0.47 accuracy and 4.5 ± 0.57 appropriateness.
evidence.quote: OrthoInfo responses were rated markedly more accurate (5.0 ± 0.0 vs. 4.7 ± 0.47; P = 0.004) and appropriate (5.0 ± 0.0 vs. 4.5 ± 0.57; P = 0.016) compared with standard ChatGPT responses.

evidence.title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated total PEM quality versus physician PEM
evidence.effect: ERNIE Bot 4.0 was comparable to physician-sourced PEM; other LLMs generally had lower total scores.
evidence.quote: In terms of the total scores, the PEMs generated by ERNIE Bot 4.0 are comparable to the physician-sourced PEM, the PEMs generated by other LLMs generally had lower scores than the physician-sourced PEM( Figure 2A ).

evidence.title: Human-AI collectives most accurately diagnose clinical vignettes
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
evidence.outcome: Model performance versus physicians
evidence.effect: Four of five LLMs outperformed the average physician; one did not.
evidence.quote: Comparing the individual LLM performance with that of the human users showed that four of the five LLMs outperformed the average physician.
evidence.sample_unit: text-based medical case vignettes (40,762 physician differential diagnoses)

evidence.title: The evaluation of artificial intelligence in mammography-based breast cancer screening: Is breast-level analysis enough?
evidence.outcome: AI AUC versus human reader AUC on the same mammograms at breast and lesion level
evidence.effect: AI AUC 0.942 (breast) and 0.929 (lesion) versus mean human AUC 0.878 and 0.851; AI outperformed humans at both levels (ps < 0.01).
evidence.quote: AI outperformed human readers at the breast and lesion level (ps < 0.01, respectively) according to the AUC.

evidence.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model in Translating Patient Instructions to Spanish Using a Standardized Framework
evidence.outcome: Translation quality (MQM score) of GPT-4o versus professional human translators on the same instructions
evidence.effect: Mean difference 1.6 MQM points (90% CI, 0.7-2.5), within equivalence margin of ±5; LLM had fewer mistranslation errors; 52% (SE 6%) of ratings preferred the LLM.
evidence.quote: Equivalence testing showed no significant difference in translation quality between GPT-4o and human translations, with a mean difference of 1.6 points (90% CI, 0.7-2.5), falling within a predefined equivalence margin of plus or minus 5 MQM points.
evidence.sample_unit: source files of pediatric patient instructions

evidence.title: Large language models: unlocking new potential in patient education for thyroid eye disease
evidence.outcome: LLM FAQ performance versus Google
evidence.effect: For both standard and simplified TED FAQ responses, LLM performance outperformed Google.
evidence.quote: Additionally, a comparative analysis of FAQs about TED on Google using LLMs showed that, regardless of whether the response was standard or simplified, the LLM's performance outperformed Google, yielding results similar to those generated by the brochures.

evidence.title: Optimizing Thyroid Nodule Management With Artificial Intelligence: Multicenter Retrospective Study on Reducing Unnecessary Fine Needle Aspirations
evidence.outcome: AI benign-nodule identification compared with junior and senior radiologists on same cohort
evidence.effect: AI identified 81.4% (96/118) of benign nodules vs 40% (junior) and 55% (senior) radiologists; AUC 0.88 vs 0.43 (P=.002) and 0.63 (P=.003).
evidence.quote: It outperformed junior and senior radiologists, who identified only 40% and 55%, respectively.

evidence.title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools
evidence.outcome: Performance versus traditional scores
evidence.effect: AUC values for ELTS and Models 1–3 were all <0.68; Model 3 slightly better but not significant; ELTS performance was similar.
evidence.quote: This final score performed slightly better but was not clearly superior to the traditional one, and its performance was nowhere near that of the score used in the Chinese cohort.

evidence.title: Machine learning model for differentiating xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis and gallbladder cancer in multicenter largescale study
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance and time versus six radiologists on the same cases
evidence.effect: LIDGAX improved sensitivity by 1.2-8.5%, specificity by 0.0-4.6%, and balanced accuracy by 1.8-6.6% versus radiologists. It reduced diagnostic time by 30.44-35.76 s per patient.
evidence.quote: Compared to six radiologists, LIDGAX improved sensitivity (1.2-8.5%), specificity (0.0-4.6%), and balanced accuracy (1.8-6.6%), while reducing average diagnostic time per patient by 30.44-35.76 s.

evidence.title: Diagnosis and Triage Performance of Contemporary Large Language Models on Short Clinical Vignettes
evidence.outcome: LLM performance versus physicians
evidence.effect: Best LLM diagnosis reached 93.75% versus physician benchmark 96%; triage remained lower than physicians, who correctly classified 91%.
evidence.quote: However, triage accuracy for these models remained lower than that of physicians, with systematic tendencies toward over-triage.

evidence.title: Evaluating human-in-the-loop strategies for artificial intelligence-enabled translation of patient discharge instructions: a multidisciplinary analysis
evidence.outcome: Candidate LLM versus professional translation
evidence.effect: Armenian overall quality 2.4 (95% CI 2.1–2.7) vs professional 3.6 (3.4–3.9), p<0.001.
evidence.quote: Relative to professional translations, evaluators rated all domains for ChatGPT-4o most poorly for Armenian and Somali.
evidence.sample_unit: evaluators (12 linguists, 16 clinicians, 14 family caregivers) rating 20 discharge instruction texts translated into 6 languages

evidence.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for accurate detection of wrong blood in tube errors in hospitalized patients
evidence.outcome: discriminative performance compared with Mahalanobis approach and delta checks
evidence.effect: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.
evidence.quote: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.

evidence.title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
evidence.outcome: LLM decision performance compared with a simpler non-LLM reference model
evidence.effect: A simpler non-LLM guideline reference model outperformed all LLMs on raw medical reports, while LLMs only matched the reference model when given manually curated summaries.
evidence.quote: The reference model outperformed the LLMs in the raw experiment regarding the metrics we assessed.

evidence.title: Accounting for inconclusive results and repeated testing: A framework for evaluating wearable electrocardiogram diagnostic performance with application to Apple Watch and artificial intelligence-enhanced interpretation
evidence.outcome: AI diagnostic performance and inconclusive outputs compared with the native Apple Watch algorithm
evidence.effect: AI achieved pragmatic sensitivity/specificity of 98.4%/96.1% and ITD 98.4%/96.6%, with 92% reduction in inconclusive outputs vs Apple Watch.
evidence.quote: The AI algorithm achieved pragmatic 98.4%/96.1% and ITD 98.4%/96.6%, with 92% reduction in inconclusive outputs vs Apple Watch.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Decision-Making in Emergency Care
evidence.venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
evidence.outcome: RAG quality versus no-retrieval Mixtral
evidence.effect: Across 100 German clinical cases, semantic retrieval improved guideline selection, but physician-rated responses were not superior to Mixtral without retrieval.
evidence.quote: However, while the semantic retrieval enhanced the guideline selection process, physicians did not rate its responses as superior in terms of medical and content accuracy, case relevance, factual integrity, and overall usability when compared to those from the Mixtral model without a retrieval mechanism.

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models in rare maculopathy
evidence.outcome: MLLMs versus retinal specialists
evidence.effect: Human accuracy was 0.714/0.571 and 0.839/0.804; best comparable MLLM accuracy was 0.298 and 0.561.
evidence.quote: Human retinal specialists consistently outperformed MLLMs in diagnostic accuracy for Prompts 1 and 2, which corresponded to MLLM Prompts 2D and 4D, respectively.

evidence.title: Vision-based diagnostic gain of ChatGPT-5 and gemini 2.5 pro compared with human experts in oral lesion assessment
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multimodal LLMs versus board-certified oral medicine experts on same cases
evidence.effect: Experts outperformed both models in simple and benign cases; ChatGPT-5 gained +19/+18/+14 pp at Top-1/3/5 with images, Gemini 0/0/-2 pp.
evidence.quote: Human experts consistently outperformed both models in simple and benign presentations.

evidence.title: Can artificial intelligence models provide reliable medical counselling to fertility patients?
evidence.outcome: Expert-blinded ratings of AI versus physician replies to fertility counselling questions
evidence.effect: Physicians scored higher than AI (P < 0.001). Median scores: Doctor A 9.0, Doctor B 8.0, ChatGPT 7.0, Gemini 4.5. Responses scoring ≥8: 70.8%, 56.3%, 47.9%, 35.4%.
evidence.quote: The replies authored by physicians received significantly higher overall scores than those generated by AI models (P < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: clinical questions (each response rated by 8 blinded experts)

evidence.title: Publicly Available Large Language Models for Trichoscopy: A Head-to-Head Comparison with Dermatologists
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of public LLMs versus dermatologists on the same trichoscopic images
evidence.effect: LLM accuracy 18.2% for suspected diagnosis and 44.4% for SD + DD, versus dermatologists 58.1% and 68.3%; all human-AI differences p < 0.001. Best model Gemini 2.5 Flash reached 62.5% for SD + DD.
evidence.quote: In trichology, publicly available LLMs currently underperform compared to human experts, especially in providing a single correct diagnosis.
evidence.sample_unit: dermatologists (5 residents, 4 board-certified, 6 trichology experts) compared with 4 LLMs on trichoscopic images

evidence.title: Evaluating the clinical utility of large language models for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment recommendations: A nationwide retrospective registry study
evidence.outcome: Survival of patients whose treatment matched LLM recommendations versus mismatched, by BCLC stage
evidence.effect: BCLC-A concordance improved survival (ChatGPT 4o HR 0.743); BCLC-C concordance worse survival (HR 1.650, Gemini 1.586, Claude 1.483); BCLC-B modest or nonsignificant.
evidence.quote: In BCLC-A patients, treatment concordance with LLM recommendations was associated with significantly improved survival (ChatGPT 4o HR: 0.743, 95% CI [0.665, 0.831], P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Bridging the analog divide: a comparison of printed X-ray films and digital images when using computer-aided detection software for tuberculosis screening
evidence.outcome: Genki specificity compared with human readers at matched sensitivity
