evidence.effect: Genki specificity was significantly higher than human readers (84.8%) using DICOM (95.2%, p < 0.001) or JPEG (92.1%, p < 0.001) at matched sensitivity (79.0%).
evidence.quote: The corresponding specificity for the Genki software is significantly higher than the human readers, whether using the DICOM (84.8% vs 95.2%, p < 0.001) or JPEG files (84.8% vs 92.1%, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Characterising liver lesions from free-text computer tomography reports - A real-world multicentre analysis
evidence.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 vs medically fine-tuned Med-LM on same CT reports against radiologist LI-RADS reference
evidence.effect: Med-LMop had the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001); lesion-level LI-RADS accuracy 40.8%-61.3%.
evidence.quote: Med-LMop demonstrated the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001).
evidence.country: Multi-institutional (five institutions; country not stated in text)

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Stability of Multimodal Large Language Models for Hand Fracture Detection: A Multi-Run Evaluation on Plain Radiographs
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of MLLMs for hand fracture detection on plain radiographs
evidence.effect: Accuracy ranged from 33.8% to 64.3% (GPT-5 Pro highest at 64.3%); scaphoid fractures remained challenging; models not reliable standalone tools.
evidence.quote: At present, MLLMs should be regarded as experimental diagnostic reasoning systems rather than reliable standalone tools for clinical fracture detection.

evidence.title: Comparative assessment of quality, consistency, and reference accuracy of MIH-related clinical information generated by ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek R1
evidence.outcome: Head-to-head expert-rated quality (GQS) of two competing LLMs on MIH questions
evidence.effect: DeepSeek R1 scored 4.44 ± 0.54 versus ChatGPT-4o 3.99 ± 0.59 (t(23) = 11.83, p < 0.0001); DeepSeek higher across all categories and sessions.
evidence.quote: When overall scores were examined, DeepSeek R1 (4.44 ± 0.54) again outperformed ChatGPT-4o (3.99 ± 0.59) (t(23) = 11.83, p < 0.0001).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (20 questions x 2 models x 3 sessions), rated by 24 pediatric dentists

evidence.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Professional Expertise in Adapted Physical Activity Prescription for Orthopedic Rehabilitation
evidence.venue: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
evidence.outcome: APA protocol quality compared to clinicians
evidence.effect: EP protocols scored significantly higher than AI protocols across all conditions (p < 0.01; mean EP 4.35-4.67 vs AI 3.38-3.88), with largest differences in safety, appropriateness, and progression.
evidence.quote: Post hoc analyses showed that EP protocols received significantly higher rating than AI protocols in all conditions (p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Accuracy of AI-Based Nutrient Estimation from Standardized Hospital Meal Images: A Comparison with Registered Dietitians
evidence.outcome: AI vs registered dietitian accuracy for energy and macronutrient estimation against weighed ground truth
evidence.effect: For energy and carbohydrates, RDs and top AI models had r > 0.8, often within ±10%. Protein and lipid accuracy was significantly lower across all AI models, with lipid overestimation Mean Bias > +20%.
evidence.quote: For energy and carbohydrates, RDs and top-performing AI models (notably ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro) demonstrated practical accuracy (r > 0.8, frequently within ±10% range).

evidence.title: A prospective multicenter trial of deep learning auto-segmentation for organs at risk in thoracic radiotherapy
evidence.outcome: Segmentation accuracy compared with alternative models on the same cohort
evidence.effect: iCurveE: vDSC 0.896, HD95 5.62 mm; nnU-Net: 0.850, 12.05 mm; TotalSegmentator: 0.781, 19.07 mm; both comparisons p < 0.0001.
evidence.quote: The iCurveE model achieved a significantly superior performance, with a mean volumetric Dice similarity coefficient (vDSC) of 0.896 and a 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 5.62 mm, compared to both the nnU-Net (vDSC, 0.850; HD95, 12.05 mm; p < 0.0001) and TotalSegmentator (vDSC, 0.781; HD95, 19.07 mm; p < 0.0001) models.

evidence.title: Comparative performance of LLMs and machine learning in predicting complications after percutaneous kyphoplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures
evidence.outcome: predictive performance of LLMs compared to traditional machine learning models
evidence.effect: LLMs did not outperform TML models; RBF-SVM had highest F1 (0.514) and MCC (0.414) for NVF, while TML models had superior MCCs (0.384–0.416) for BCL
evidence.quote: The LLMs did not outperform the TML models in the domain-specific tasks.
evidence.sample_unit: prospective test samples for BCL prediction (116 for NVF)

evidence.title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
evidence.outcome: Ratings versus evidence-based online responses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT higher for 11/12 questions; r_rb=-0.46 to -1.00; all p<0.05; +0.824 units average.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT responses were rated significantly higher than the evidence-based responses for 11 of the 12 study questions, with moderate to large effect sizes (r r b  = -0.46 to -1.00; all p-values <0.05), with ChatGPT answers being rated on average 0.824 units higher.
evidence.country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT's Accuracy, Repeatability, and Reasoning Ability in Prosthodontics Education: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study with Prosthodontists
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical and experimental dentistry
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT accuracy compared with prosthodontists on prosthodontics questions
evidence.effect: Prosthodontists outperformed ChatGPT in overall accuracy (p < 0.05), notably on medium-difficulty and clinical questions; ChatGPT lacked consistency and clinical judgment.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT demonstrates moderate ability in delivering accurate theoretical information but lacks consistency and clinical judgment.
evidence.sample_unit: responses per group (36 questions, ChatGPT queried twice daily for 15 days)

evidence.title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
evidence.outcome: contouring accuracy of AI segmentation versus manual clinician contouring
evidence.effect: Manual contouring had significantly lower spleen HD (7.1 vs 12.5 mm, p=0.027), while AI had significantly higher kidney DSC (0.993-0.994 vs 0.926-0.935, p<0.001) and lower MDA
evidence.quote: For HD in the spleen, manual contouring showed significantly lower values than those of AI segmentation ( p = 0.027).

evidence.title: Large language models approach clinician performance in ESC cardiovascular risk stratification: a vignette-based benchmark study
evidence.outcome: Clinician benchmark comparison
evidence.effect: Five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded the pooled clinician benchmark.
evidence.quote: Notably, five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded this pooled clinician benchmark, suggesting that top-performing models reach the performance level of the average individual physician on this task.
evidence.sample_unit: simulated clinical vignettes (each in Portuguese and English)

evidence.title: Limits of Artificial Intelligence Models for Skin Cancer Diagnosis in Realistic Settings
evidence.outcome: Multiclass skin lesion diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus physician readers by experience level
evidence.effect: Experts with >10 years achieved 74.2% accuracy versus 56.7% CNN, 72.2% unimodal, 66.3% multimodal; AI did not beat the most experienced clinicians.
evidence.quote: With a mean (SD) accuracy of 74.2% (5.7%), experts with more than 10 years of experience achieved the highest multiclass diagnostic accuracy, outperforming all AI models on this primary end point, which included 56.7% (3.9%) for CNN, 72.2% (3.5%) for the unimodal model, and 66.3% (3.8%) for the multimodal model.
evidence.sample_unit: cases (clinical and dermoscopic images with metadata)

evidence.title: Large Language Model Chatbot Conversations vs Public Health Materials and Parental HPV Vaccination Intentions: A Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.outcome: Parental HPV vaccination intent, chatbot versus government public health materials, over 45 days
evidence.effect: Immediate intent: materials d=0.53, default chatbot d=0.48, conversational chatbot d=0.33 vs no intervention. At 45 days neither chatbot increased intent; materials kept modest effects.
evidence.quote: At 45 days, neither chatbot increased intent relative to controls, whereas public health materials maintained modest effects.

evidence.title: Edge-Hosted LLM-Assisted NICU Discharge Summary Generation: Field-Level Evaluation Using a Clinician-Defined Rubric
evidence.outcome: Rubric-based quality of AI vs clinician-authored NICU discharge summaries on same admissions
evidence.effect: AI scored higher than clinicians: accuracy 0.93 vs 0.75, completeness 0.91 vs 0.67, non-hallucination 0.95 vs 0.78; fewer omissions, unsupported assertions, and contradictions.
evidence.quote: Error taxonomy analysis demonstrated fewer omissions, unsupported assertions, and contradictions in AI-generated summaries than in clinician-authored summaries.

evidence.title: Assessing GPT-4o in cataract surgery decision-making: appropriateness, consistency, and clinical implications
evidence.outcome: GPT-4o IOL selection appropriateness versus high- and low-volume cataract surgeons
evidence.effect: Overall appropriateness of GPT-4o was significantly lower than that of human surgeons (37.84% vs. 72.14%, P = 0.001).
evidence.quote: The overall appropriateness rate of GPT-4o for IOL selection was significantly lower than that of human surgeons (37.84% vs. 72.14%, P = 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Infectious Disease Decision-Making: From Examination to Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: LLM versus infectious disease resident performance on exam questions
evidence.effect: LLMs comparable to doctors on low-order questions (87.4-92.3% vs 88.4%, p=0.54); doctors had higher high-order score rate (76.5% vs 54.5-66.5%, p=0.10).
evidence.quote: Doctors achieved the highest score rate (164.5/215, 76.5%), with numerically higher performance than all LLMs.

evidence.title: Zero-shot detection of apical periodontitis on periapical radiographs using multimodal large language models: diagnostic accuracy and error patterns
evidence.outcome: Comparison of three candidate MLLMs against each other and a clinician reference standard on same images
evidence.effect: Gemini 3.0 Pro accuracy 71.67%, significantly superior to Claude 4.5 Sonnet (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.0015); models differed in sensitivity and specificity trade-offs.
evidence.quote: This performance was significantly superior to that of Claude 4.5 Sonnet (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.0015).

evidence.title: Diagnostic capability of large language models in critically ill patients: a prospective single-centre study comparing ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini with emergency physicians
evidence.outcome: Reference diagnosis inclusion in preliminary and differential lists, LLMs versus emergency physicians
evidence.effect: Physicians included the reference diagnosis in 83.9% (top-5 preliminary) and 98.3% (top-3 differential) of cases, significantly exceeding every LLM (all p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Physicians contained the reference diagnosis within their top-5 preliminary and top-3 differential lists in 83.9% and 98.3% of cases, respectively, significantly exceeding every LLM (all p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
evidence.outcome: AI discrimination compared to simpler traditional radiobiological models
evidence.effect: ANN showed no statistically significant advantage over LKB (parotid ΔAUC +0.04, oral cavity ΔAUC +0.04, larynx ΔAUC +0.03; all p>0.05); XGBoost overfitted (training AUC 0.98–1.00; test AUC 0.67–0.82).
evidence.quote: When comparing ANN against the best-performing traditional model (LKB) for each organ, differences were modest across all endpoints: parotid glands (ΔAUC +0.04), oral cavity (ΔAUC +0.04) and mixed-architecture larynx (ΔAUC +0.03), no statistically significant advantage for ML was observed for any organ architecture.

evidence.title: The Performance of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 in Interpreting Thyroid Nodule Ultrasound Text Reports: Multicenter Study
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic performance versus senior radiologists on benign-malignant differentiation
evidence.effect: Senior radiologists (AUC 0.865, accuracy 0.804) outperformed DeepSeek-R1 (accuracy 0.729) and ChatGPT-4o (accuracy 0.644).
evidence.quote: However, both LLMs remained inferior to senior radiologists, suggesting their role as decision-support tools rather than stand-alone diagnostic systems.

evidence.title: Real World Evaluation of AI-Based Tumor Cell Content Quantification for Molecular Tumor Profiling
evidence.venue: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
evidence.outcome: Agreement of AI and pathologist tumor cell content estimates with molecular quantification
evidence.effect: AI DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63) than pathologist VQ with MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38); VQ–DQ agreement was Rs = 0.44.
evidence.quote: Agreement was lowest between VQ and MQ (Spearman Rs = 0.38) and between VQ and DQ (Rs = 0.44), while DQ showed stronger concordance with MQ (Rs = 0.63).

evidence.title: Prompt Configurations for Multimodal Large Language Models in Diagnosing and Staging Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Multimodel Retrospective Observational Diagnostic Study
evidence.outcome: MLLM performance compared with surgeons and commercial versus open-source models on same data
evidence.effect: Surgeons mean detailed grading accuracy 0.71 (SD 0.19) versus MLLM ID ARCO 0.56; no significant commercial versus open-source difference (P=.83).
evidence.quote: Consistent with the bootstrap analysis, no significant overall difference was found between commercial and open-source models, though some model-specific variations existed ( Figure 5 C,D).

evidence.title: Diagnostic performance and short-interval reproducibility of multimodal large language models in differentiating cholesteatoma from chronic otitis media using key-image temporal bone high-resolution computed tomography
evidence.outcome: Multimodal LLM diagnostic accuracy versus radiologist on same HRCT images
evidence.effect: Radiologist accuracy 96.0% (κ 0.921); GPT-5 43.6%/46.5% and Gemini 2.5 Pro 49.5%/47.5% in S1/S2, with specificity 1.9%-13.2%.
evidence.quote: The radiologist achieved an accuracy of 96.0% (95% CI: 90.3-98.4) with almost perfect agreement with the reference standard (κ: 0.921).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Prompt Design and Internal Reasoning in Chatbot-Based Medical History Taking: Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: Coverage versus rule-based baseline
evidence.effect: DT outperformed Choice (t65=9.71; P<.001; g=1.53), but MN and Choice did not differ (t65=1.48; P>.99).
evidence.quote: The MN and choice modes did not differ significantly ( P >.99).

evidence.title: Physician-revised AI-generated drafts are associated with higher ratings of written explanations in end-of-life care in the intensive care unit: a scenario-based single-center cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: AI-only versus physician-only ratings
evidence.effect: Primary comparisons: medical validity P=0.210; HCP empathy and non-HCP empathy P>0.999. Sensitivity: AI-only lower medical validity −0.17, higher non-HCP empathy 0.22.
evidence.quote: By contrast, comparisons between physician-only and AI-only responses varied across analytic approaches: no significant differences were observed for any outcome in the primary analyses, whereas a difference in medical validity was observed in both the sensitivity and exploratory analyses, and a difference in empathy rated by nonhealthcare professionals was observed only in the sensitivity analyses.

evidence.title: Balancing Natural Language Processing Accuracy and Normalisation in Extracting Medical Insights
evidence.outcome: accuracy of rule-based methods versus LLMs in information retrieval
evidence.effect: Rule-based methods provided higher accuracy than LLMs in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction
evidence.quote: Results demonstrate that rule-based methods provide higher accuracy in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction.

evidence.title: Generalist Large Language Models Outperform Clinical Tools on Medical Benchmarks
evidence.outcome: Comparative benchmark performance of clinical AI tools versus generalist LLMs on the same items
evidence.effect: Generalist LLMs consistently outperformed OpenEvidence and UpToDate Expert AI, with GPT-5 highest. Clinical tools showed deficits in completeness, communication quality, context awareness, and systems-based safety reasoning.
evidence.quote: Generalist models consistently outperformed clinical tools, with GPT-5 achieving the highest scores, while OpenEvidence and UpToDate demonstrated deficits in completeness, communication quality, context awareness, and systems-based safety reasoning.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
evidence.outcome: LLM versus conventional gait classifiers
evidence.effect: Supervised KNN MCC = 0.88; best LLM GPT-5 with reference grounding multiclass MCC = 0.70.
evidence.quote: The supervised KNN achieved the highest performance (multiclass Matthews Correlation Coefficient, MCC = 0.88).

evidence.title: MedRealMM: A Real-World Multimodal Benchmark for Chinese Online Medical Consultation
evidence.outcome: LLM next-response quality versus online physician responses on rubric criteria
evidence.effect: Frontier models remain below the online physician response. Some meet as many or more positive criteria than physicians but trigger more negative criteria.
evidence.quote: Our results show that image information is critical for reliable clinical performance and that current frontier models remain below the online physician response.

evidence.title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
evidence.outcome: Outcome agreement versus baseline
evidence.effect: Outcome agreement varied across models and showed no consistent advantage over the baseline.
evidence.quote: Outcome agreement varied across models and showed no consistent advantage over the baseline.

evidence.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generative AI Versus Human-Curated Expert Systems in Drug-Drug Interaction Screening
evidence.outcome: Agreement of generative AI with expert-curated DDI system on mechanism and severity
evidence.effect: Mechanism agreement over 99%; CKAI assigned higher severity than LexiDrug and often recommended 'avoid' over nuanced modifications; evidence categorization diverged.
evidence.quote: CKAI consistently assigned higher severity levels compared to LexiDrug and frequently recommended “avoid” actions rather than nuanced modifications.

evidence.title: A Breakeven Recall Framework for LLM Candidate-Set Narrowing in P300 BCIs: Derivation and Cross-Dataset Validation
evidence.outcome: P300 decoding accuracy of LLM compared to simpler alternatives
evidence.effect: Static vocabulary (48.1%) > unconstrained (30.6%) > LLM (24.4% observed) on BigP3BCI (p = 0.001), with consistent ordering SV > UC >= LLM across all three datasets
evidence.quote: Current small LLMs (Qwen2.5 1.5B, GPT-2) operate below both necessary conditions in all three datasets, explaining the consistent ordering SV > UC ≥ LLM.
evidence.sample_unit: spelling rounds (across three public P300 datasets)

evidence.title: Performance evaluation and benchmarking across 16 large language models on a comprehensive real-world emergency department triage data set
evidence.outcome: Agreement of LLM ESI predictions with nurse-assigned ESI levels
evidence.effect: Quadratic-weighted kappa ranged from 0.18 to 0.75 across models; only structured stepwise prompting reached substantial agreement (0.747).
evidence.quote: Only a structured stepwise prompting strategy achieved substantial agreement (κ_qw = 0.747), approaching reported human inter-rater reliability.

evidence.title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
evidence.outcome: external performance by model complexity
evidence.effect: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance compared to simpler models.
evidence.quote: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance, whereas training on pooled data substantially improved both discrimination and calibration.

evidence.title: Buyer Beware: confounding factors and biases abound when predicting omics-based biomarkers from histological images
evidence.outcome: Deep learning biomarker prediction versus simple pathologist-assigned grade baseline
evidence.effect: Because of biomarker correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages over pathologist-assigned grades for predicting certain biomarkers. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: We also show that, due to the presence of such correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages in predicting certain biomarkers in comparison to simply using pathologist-assigned grades for their prediction.

evidence.title: Evaluating the accuracy of a state-of-the-art large language model for prediction of admissions from the emergency room
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: ED admission prediction accuracy of GPT-4 versus traditional ensemble ML
evidence.effect: Naive GPT-4 (0.79 AUC, 0.48 AUPRC) and peak GPT-4 (0.87 AUC, 0.71 AUPRC) performed lower than ensemble ML (0.88 AUC, 0.72 AUPRC).
evidence.quote: Its peak performance, although slightly lower than the pure ML model, is noteworthy given its potential for providing reasoning behind predictions.

evidence.title: Computer-aided detection of tuberculosis from chest radiographs in a tuberculosis prevalence survey in South Africa: external validation and modelled impacts of commercially available artificial intelligence software
evidence.outcome: Comparative accuracy (AUC) of 12 commercial CAD products on same data
evidence.effect: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0.9; qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, ChestEye 0.8-0.9; XrayAME, RADIFY, TiSepX-TB under 0.8.
evidence.quote: Diverse accuracy was noted: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9, followed by qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye (AUCs 0·8-0·9).

evidence.title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of complex deep learning versus simpler regularized logistic regression models
evidence.effect: Logistic regression achieved comparable AUROC to LSTM on APCD (0.879 vs 0.901) and HIDD (0.831 vs 0.811), and outperformed LSTM on KHIN (0.787 vs 0.759); transported LSTM performance dropped substantially.
evidence.quote: More complex models, particularly deep long short-term memory neural network models, did not outperform simpler regularized logistic regression models in terms of both local and transported performance.

evidence.title: Summary Report of the SNMMI AI Task Force Radiomics Challenge 2024
evidence.venue: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
evidence.outcome: External-validation performance of radiomics ML models versus simple SUV and TMTV reference models for PFS prediction
evidence.effect: 6 of 19 continuous-outcome models performed similarly to the simple linear reference model; 1 of 12 binary-outcome models had higher but nonsignificant C-index than the simple logistic regression.
evidence.quote: This suggests that, for the challenge dataset, there was limited or no value seen from the addition of sophisticated radiomic features and use of machine learning when developing models for outcome prediction.
evidence.sample_unit: submitted models (19 continuous-outcome, 12 binary-outcome) from challenge teams

evidence.title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of CNN versus MAP threshold method across datasets
evidence.effect: In VDB cohorts, CNN was marginally better than MAPthr (AUC-ROC 80.29 vs 78.46, and 80.64 vs 79.80), but in Karolinska CNN was higher (64.41 vs 61.92); sensitivity, PPV, and F1 were comparable across all datasets.
evidence.quote: In contrast, for the VDB datasets–characterized by a wider class separation ( = 11.21–11.96 mmHg) and clearer hemodynamic patterns–the CNN model performed only marginally better than MAPthr ( = 80.29 vs. 78.46 for VDB Matched, and 80.64 vs. 79.80 for VDB Non-Matched).

evidence.title: Evaluating commercial multimodal AI for diabetic eye screening and implications for an alternative regulatory pathway
evidence.outcome: AUC for diabetic retinopathy detection versus retina specialists on Messidor-2
evidence.effect: GPT-4o AUC 0.83, Grok 0.63, Gemini AUC not calculable; retina specialists estimated at 0.94; OTSAIs do not approach FDA endpoints.
evidence.quote: The AUC of retina specialists on the same task was estimated at 0.94, so the emergent performance of OTSAIs does not match that of clinical experts, nor does it approach FDA endpoints for consideration as a medical device.

evidence.title: Assessing the Impact of the Quality of Textual Data on Feature Representation and Machine Learning Models: Quantitative Study Using Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Predictive performance of complex embedding models versus simpler models
evidence.effect: TF-IDF models outperformed neural network-based embedding models including word2vec, ClinicalBERT, and BioClinical ModernBERT across datasets, with logistic regression having comparatively higher ROC-AUC for most representations.
evidence.quote: In terms of the feature representation models, TF-IDF models outperformed neural network–based embedding models (word2vec, ClinicalBERT, and BioClinical ModernBERT).

evidence.title: Predicting emergency mortality risk in traumatic brain injury: comparative analysis of machine learning and large language model GPT-5
evidence.outcome: mortality prediction AUC of LLM versus simpler ML model
evidence.effect: SVM achieved the best overall performance with AUC 0.920, outperforming all LLM prompting configurations which reached AUCs between 0.902 and 0.919 after threshold adjustment.
evidence.quote: The SVM model achieved the best overall performance (AUC = 0.920).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
evidence.venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
evidence.outcome: 30-day ED revisit prediction F1 score compared to traditional LightGBM baseline
evidence.effect: All LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614, 95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])
evidence.quote: Despite having access to comprehensive structured and unstructured clinical data, all LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])).

evidence.title: Calibration and evaluation of machine-learning algorithms for missense variant classification under ACMG/ClinGen recommendations
evidence.venue: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
evidence.outcome: comparative performance of new ML variant predictors versus existing meta-predictor
evidence.effect: REVEL had highest overall performance (especially autosomal recessive and tolerant dominant variants); AM outperformed others in haploinsufficiency genes
evidence.quote: REVEL demonstrated the highest overall performance, particularly for autosomal recessive variants and autosomal dominant variants tolerant to loss-of-function.

evidence.title: Large language models for zero-shot procedure extraction in orthopedic surgery: a comparative evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM procedure extraction accuracy versus administrator-assigned coding labels, on the same notes
evidence.effect: LLMs consistently outperformed administrator-assigned labels, with macro-F1 above 0.6 and up to 10 points of improvement over administrative coding.
evidence.quote: We find that across models, LLMs consistently outperform administrator-assigned labels, achieving macro-F1 scores above 0.6 and improving over administrative coding by up to 10 points.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models for diagnostic reasoning from unstructured clinical narratives in epilepsy
evidence.outcome: LLM F1 for seizure onset zone localization compared with clinicians and naive baseline
evidence.effect: Zero-shot F1 of GPT-4 52.27% and Mixtral 51.66% versus clinicians 48.77% and 46.75%; naive classifier 38.21%.
evidence.quote: Exceptions are Mixtral-8 × 7B and GPT-4, which achieved substantially higher F1 scores than all other models of 51.66% and 52.27%, respectively (95% CI: [51.43, 51.90], [52.04, 52.50]), comparable to the clinician’s performance: Clinician 1 - 48.77% (95% CI: [48.53, 49.02]) and Clinician 2 - 46.75% (95% CI: [46.51, 46.99]).

evidence.title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
evidence.outcome: Concordance of three LLMs with CAP consensus for ER/PR scoring
evidence.effect: Claude 90-98%, Gemini 85-100%, Gemma 73-93% concordance across qualitative and semi-qualitative approaches; models compared with each other against CAP consensus, not against clinicians.
evidence.quote: Performance varied across models and scoring approaches, with Claude achieving the highest concordance (90-98%), followed by Gemini (85-100%) and Gemma (73-93%), reflecting differences in multimodal reasoning capacity that should be considered when selecting a model for implementation.

evidence.title: Cross-Sensor and Cross-Population Generalization of Deep Learning Models for Digital Mammography: A Controlled Four-Country Benchmark of Five Backbone Architectures with Statistical Significance Testing
evidence.outcome: in-distribution discrimination of foundation models versus simpler ResNet-50 baseline
evidence.effect: ResNet-50 outperformed all four foundation models on CBIS-DDSM (AUC 0.867 vs. 0.847, 0.846, 0.813, and 0.703; all gaps p_adj < 0.05).
evidence.quote: Within this single-source three-seed evaluation, ResNet-50 outperformed all four foundation models on CBIS-DDSM (AUC 0.867 vs. 0.847, 0.846, 0.813, and 0.703; all gaps p_adj < 0.05).

evidence.title: Moderate-to-substantial agreement of ChatGPT-5 for Kellgren-Lawrence grading on synthetic knee radiographs: a controlled cross-sectional observer agreement study
evidence.outcome: Comparison of two AI models against expert consensus
evidence.effect: Gemini 2.5 Flash weighted κ = 0.23 vs expert reference and 0.06 vs ChatGPT-5; ChatGPT-5 weighted κ = 0.680; Gemini specificity 0%.
evidence.quote: In the 112-image exploratory subset, Gemini 2.5 Flash showed limited agreement with the expert reference standard (weighted κ = 0.23, MAE = 0.66, exact agreement = 50.0%) and poor agreement with ChatGPT-5 (weighted κ = 0.06).

evidence.title: Improving the reliability of polygenic risk score-based prediction for cardiovascular and renal complications across ancestries in type 2 diabetes using Mondrian Cross-Conformal Prediction
evidence.outcome: Performance of complex machine learning vs linear models for polygenic risk score prediction
evidence.effect: Linear discriminant analysis, ridge classifier, and logistic regression achieved the best AUROC among 16 evaluated machine learning algorithms.
evidence.quote: Linear discriminant analysis (LDA), ridge classifier and logistic regression (LR) performed the best, with similar AUROC between the three ethnic groups ( S1 Fig ).
evidence.sample_unit: UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes (17,574 White British, 1,145 South Asian, 749 African/Caribbean) tested; 4,098 ADVANCE participants used for training

evidence.title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
evidence.outcome: Whether in-domain ranking of architectures predicts cross-domain ranking
evidence.effect: Best in-domain model (from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop; in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.
evidence.quote: The most accurate model in-domain (a from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop, and every pretrained estimate fell below every from-scratch estimate (family means 248% vs. 380%): in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.

evidence.title: Local adaptation of a chest radiograph AI model for pulmonary tuberculosis triage in Uzbekistan: Pooled and site-stratified internal validation and exploratory workstation integration
evidence.outcome: Adapted model versus public baseline AUC
evidence.effect: AUC difference from public baseline was 0.0054 (95% CI -0.0077 to 0.0230; p = 0.4864), showing no statistical superiority.
evidence.quote: The paired AUC difference from the public baseline was 0.0054 (95 % CI -0.0077 to 0.0230; p = 0.4864), showing no statistical superiority.

commentary.bottom_line: Head-to-head studies on shared data often find that candidate AI tools differ widely from one another and sometimes perform no better than clinicians, simpler scores, or symptom screening, which suggests pre-selection comparison can change purchasing decisions. No study compared organizations that ran such comparisons before selection with organizations that did not, so the benefit of the practice itself is inferred.

perspectives.view: Eleven of the listed tests are randomized, and most report AI against a comparator on the same data. They show that the comparison is feasible and that it changes the picture of performance. They measure tool performance, however, and not whether comparing before selection improves outcomes. Indirectness and results that point in different directions lower certainty to low.

Several comparisons found AI performing below or equal to existing care. AI sensitivity for polyp histology was 80% versus 88% for endoscopists. A CDS screen matched human screening at 81.7% versus 80.2%. A survival model trailed both physicians and a 1995 model. Comparison before selection may catch such tools before they reach patients.

Competing products tested on the same data showed wide spread. Agreement across 21 retinal algorithms ranged from 49.4% to 92.3%. One LLM matched community health workers at 97.9% referral accuracy while another reached 47.3%. A local sepsis model had an AUROC of 81.8% versus 57.5% for the vendor model in silent testing.

A few comparisons included low-income, rural, safety-net, or low-literacy groups outside the US. In India, the specificity of three commercial algorithms ranged from 14% to 96%. In Nigeria, symptom screening dominated AI-only TB screening on cost. No test drew on US Medicaid or US safety-net data.

FDA draft guidance expects device performance to be compared with a comparator tested on the same patients or data. CDRH has also raised clinician panels as a comparator for generative AI. These expectations apply to developers. No listed study examines whether a health system's own comparison adds value beyond cleared labeling.

Comparison has a cost, but it can inform spending. In Nigeria, AI screening found 76 TB cases at US$56589, and symptom screening found 77 cases at US$48939. In Taiwan, an intrinsic screening step ranked candidate models in the same order as full fine-tuning, which suggests lighter comparisons may work. Standardized scheduling came close to an ML tool's accuracy.

Patient-facing comparisons point in mixed directions. Patients rated psychiatrist-led interviews higher than chatbot or robot interviews. An AI agent answered in 0.5 minutes versus 358 for physicians, with accuracy of 93.9% versus 98.1%. Comparing tools with human care before selection may show where patients still need a clinician.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares organizations that ran same-data comparisons before selection with organizations that did not, whether on patient outcomes, cost, or later de-adoption of tools. Few studies explain which comparator they chose and why, and few use local US health-system data.
commentary.underserved_note: Some tests included limited English proficiency or non-English-speaking, rural, low-income, safety-net, and low-health-literacy populations, mostly in China, Rwanda, India, and Nigeria. None used US Medicaid or US safety-net data. Health systems serving those patients may therefore need to run comparisons on their own populations rather than rely on published rankings.
